Get Started
Introduction

Introduction

WHIP is a complete framework for FiveM servers. These docs are for developers building resources on it; server owners start with Quick Start.

Install WHIP on an empty server and players can make a character, carry and stash items, bank, buy and tune cars, own a home, and get hurt and revived. Admins run the server from inside the game with /whip. WHIP needs only FiveM and oxmysql: it replaces QBCore, ESX or ox_core, and the inventory, target, garage and banking resources they rely on.

What makes it different

  • Safe by default. A SecureEvent declares what it accepts (how often, which values, how close the player must be), and WHIP refuses everything else before your code runs.
  • Items are real things. Cash is banknotes that can be dropped, stolen or stashed. A bag weighs what's in it, and a car's boot works like any stash.
  • Nothing is half saved. Everything one action changes is saved in one transaction, so a crash never charges a player for something they didn't get.
  • Settings live in the game. Owners change settings in /whip → Settings, and your resource can add a page of its own.

What's in WHIP

whip_core plus the resources built on it. Each needs only whip_core, so you can leave out any you don't want.

ResourceWhat it is
whip_corePlayers, characters, inventory, money and banks, jobs, vehicles, garages, properties, prompts, the UI library, the Director, the admin panel and developer tools
whip_gunnyWeapons: magazines, calibers, melee, throwables and attachments
whip_fuelFuel tanks, pumps with a hose, and the jerry can
whip_ropeA physics rope to carry, tie and tow with
whip_phoneThe Duo phone, whose apps are modules from WHIP or any resource
whip_autos, whip_autos_shopWhiplash: customisation, turbos and nitrous, and the shop in Burton
whip_voice3D voice chat, on a voice server it runs itself
whip_chat, whip_loadingscreenChat and the loading screen
whip_media_* (in [assets]/[media])Clothing, furniture, vehicle, NPC and tattoo pictures, emote videos and the map
whip_homes_mirrorpark, whip_graphics (in [assets])Every Mirror Park house as a walk-in home, plus 25 garages; LED streetlights and WHIP's lighting and sky

Every resource runs on FiveM Legacy and GTA V Enhanced (Legacy and Enhanced). How the pieces fit: How WHIP is built.

Quick Start

Install WHIP as a new server with its txAdmin recipe, and check it works. The recipe builds the whole server (resources, database and server.cfg), so it can't be added to a server you already have.

Requirements

  • FiveM's server with txAdmin: FiveM Legacy (FXServer, artifact 38435 or newer) or GTA V Enhanced (cfx-server).
  • MariaDB 10.2.3+ or MySQL 8.0.16+, and a database login that can create a database.
  • About 1 GB of disk, and at least 10 Mbit/s to GitHub: txAdmin gives each download 150 seconds, and the largest is about 145 MB.
  • The voice ports open inbound, like 30120: UDP 7882-7893 and TCP 7881 (Setting up whip_voice).

Install

  1. Start the server and open txAdmin. On the setup page choose Remote URL Template and paste the recipe for your game: 
    Legacy:   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WHIPFX/txAdmin-recipe/main/whip-legacy.yaml
Enhanced: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WHIPFX/txAdmin-recipe/main/whip-enhanced.yaml
  2. Enter your server key (from portal.cfx.re) and your database login. txAdmin downloads WHIP and WHIPFX's oxmysql, creates an empty database, turns on OneSync, writes server.cfg and makes your txAdmin account an admin. There's no SQL to import: WHIP creates its own tables.
  3. Start the server.

The server.cfg it writes

sv_licenseKey "your key"
set mysql_connection_string "mysql://user:password@localhost/whip_1A2B3C"

# Legacy only: the game build WHIP is made for (or newer)
sv_enforceGameBuild 3889

# Players need a Steam account linked to their Cfx.re account
set sv_enforceSteamAuth true

ensure oxmysql
ensure whip_core
ensure whip_autos
ensure whip_autos_shop
ensure whip_chat
ensure whip_fuel
ensure whip_gunny
ensure whip_loadingscreen
ensure whip_phone
ensure whip_rope
# whip_voice starts its own voice server, which needs this permission
add_unsafe_child_process_permission whip_voice
ensure whip_voice
ensure [assets]    # the media packs and the map packs

# The admin tools (/w and /whip) for group.admin, which your txAdmin account is in
add_ace group.admin whip.devtools allow
add_principal identifier.fivem:1234567 group.admin

Only oxmysql has to come before WHIP's ensure lines; your own resources go after them. FiveM's stock chat, spawnmanager and basic-gamemode aren't installed: WHIP has its own.

On GTA V Enhanced, the recipe writes these two lines instead of sv_enforceGameBuild:

setr whip_platform enhanced                 # must be setr, so players' games get it too
set sv_resourceFileDownloadTimeout 600000   # time for slow connections to download the media packs

Check it works

  1. A few seconds after everything has started, the console prints the WHIP setup report. Each line marked FIX says what to change. When nothing needs fixing, Framework loaded successfully! follows it. Type whipsetup to see the report again.
  2. Join the server (your Cfx.re account needs a linked Steam account) and make a character.
  3. F2 opens the inventory, /w the quick tools and /whip the admin panel. To make someone else an admin, have them type /w: the console prints the add_ace line to add for them.

Updating

Each resource has its own releases on GitHub. Read the release's notes on its releases page, stop the server, and replace the resource's folder with the new release. Your database carries over: whip_core updates its tables on the next start.

First copy out what the server saved in the old folders: whip_core/pack_exports (exported Director packs), pictures taken in game (whip_media_props/img/props, whip_media_previews/img/vehicles) and whip_autos/engines.json.

Your First Resource

Build a coffee stand in about 30 minutes: a counter you walk up to, a purchase the server checks and charges for, and a coffee that takes four seconds to drink. Each step is something every WHIP resource does.

You need a server running WHIP (Quick Start) and the whip.devtools ACE, so /w and /whip open.

The finished stand is in whip_core/docs/examples/whip_cafe_example, line for line. Compare yours with it when a step doesn't work. It uses the same names as yours, so run one or the other.

1. The folder

Make a folder called mycafe in your resources, with fxmanifest.lua, shared.lua, server.lua and client.lua:

fx_version 'cerulean'
game 'gta5'
lua54 'yes'

dependency 'whip_core'
whip_requires '1.0'

shared_scripts {
    '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua',   -- WHIP's helper: gives you Whip.register and Whip.core
    'shared.lua',
}
server_script 'server.lua'
client_script 'client.lua'

Add ensure mycafe to server.cfg, below WHIP's lines. dependency 'whip_core' starts whip_core first, and restarts your resource whenever whip_core restarts. whip_requires makes the setup report flag an older whip_core.

Set up autocomplete first. Copy whip_core/types/luarc.template.json into mycafe as .luarc.json and open the folder in VS Code with the Lua extension (sumneko). Every export then shows its parameters and return values, and typos are underlined.

2. Where the counter is

Both sides need the counter's position: the client to show the prompt, the server to refuse anyone standing elsewhere. Put it in shared.lua:

Config = {
    Counter = vector3(-361.0, 49.0, 54.4),   -- just in front of where new characters spawn
    Price   = 15,
}

For your own spot, stand there in game, open /w → Coords and press G to copy vector4(x, y, z, heading).

3. The item, and the one rule

whip_core keeps everything you declare (items, use handlers, events, prompts) in memory, and forgets it when it restarts. So declare in Whip.register: it runs your function once whip_core is ready and again after every restart. In server.lua:

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItem('mycafe_coffee', {
        name     = 'Coffee',
        desc     = 'Hot and black. Quenches thirst.',
        weight   = 0.3,
        type     = 'consumable',
        stack    = true,
        maxStack = 10,
        usable   = true,
    })
end)

Running it twice is safe: registering the same thing again changes nothing (the registration rule). Every item field is under Item Definition. A refusal is printed in the server console, with the reason.

Call whip_core through Whip.core in there, so a refusal is printed for you. One function can hold every declaration, a loop over your Config too (The satellite helper).

Don't wait and hope. CreateThread(function() Wait(1000) … end) registers once, so a whip_core restart silently strips your items. Watching onResourceStart misses the first start. Use Whip.register.

4. Drinking it

Below it, say what using the coffee does. Passing RegisterUseHandler a table makes it a timed use: WHIP shows the bar, plays the animation and props, and times it on the server so a modified client can't skip it. When the bar ends, WHIP takes the coffee and runs onComplete.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterUseHandler('mycafe_coffee', {
        label    = 'Drinking coffee...',
        duration = 4000,
        anim     = { dict = 'amb@world_human_drinking@coffee@male@idle_a', clip = 'idle_c' },
        prop     = { model = 'p_amb_coffeecup_01', bone = 28422 },
        disable  = { move = false },

        -- Return AddStat's result: if it fails, WHIP gives the coffee back
        onComplete = function(source)
            return exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'thirst', 20, 'item:mycafe_coffee')
        end,
    })
end)

Thirst runs from 100 (full) down to 0, and new characters start full (Stats & Effects). Every field is on the timed use card.

Try it: in the server console, refresh then ensure mycafe (later, restart mycafe). In game, /whip → Economy → Items, give yourself a coffee, press F2, right-click it and choose Use.

5. Selling it

A SecureEvent is RegisterNetEvent with the checks built in. Also in server.lua:

-- The client sends nothing: not the price, not the item
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:SecureEvent('mycafe:buy', {
        rateLimit = 1000,   -- one purchase a second per player
        near = { at = Config.Counter, range = 3.0, message = 'Walk up to the counter' },
    }, function(source)
        local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, Config.Price, { reason = 'Coffee' })
        if not receipt then
            return false, err            -- couldn't pay: WHIP shows them why
        end

        local given, why = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'mycafe_coffee', 1)
        if not given then
            exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)   -- paid but got nothing: money back
            return false, why
        end

        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Enjoy your coffee', 'success')
    end)
end)
  • The client sends nothing. A client that could send the price could send 0.
  • near refuses anyone more than 3 m from the counter before your function runs.
  • rateLimit allows one call a second per player; extra calls are refused and logged.
  • ChargePlayer takes cash, or the bank if they don't carry enough, and returns a receipt for RefundPlayer (Charging a Player).
  • return false, why refuses: the player sees why, and the refusal is logged.

Inside a handler whip_core runs, call exports directly. In your own code (a thread, a command, a timer), use Whip.core:ChargePlayer(...), which returns false, why instead of erroring when whip_core isn't running (Calling whip_core).

6. The counter

In client.lua, put a prompt at the counter. Walk up and press E to send the event:

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:AddAction({
        id       = 'counter',
        at       = { coords = Config.Counter },
        label    = ('Buy coffee ($%d)'):format(Config.Price),
        icon     = 'cash',
        onSelect = function()
            TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:buy')
        end,
    })
end)

The same call puts an option on an entity, a car part or the F1 wheel (AddAction). It's removed automatically when your resource stops.

7. Try it

  1. restart mycafe, walk to the counter and press E. $15 goes, a coffee arrives.
  2. Open /whip → System → Monitor: each mycafe:buy is listed, accepted or refused, with the reason.
  3. Drink the coffee: the bar runs with the cup in your hand.

If nothing happens, check the server console and F8 for errors, and check each call's return values: a refusal returns false and a reason (Return values). To give the coffee a picture, add html/img/items/mycafe_coffee.webp and files { 'html/img/items/*.webp' } to the manifest (Item icons).

Your First Job

Add staff to the coffee stand from Your First Resource: a job, a counter with different options for customers and staff on duty, brewing under a bar the server times, and pay for each cup. About 30 minutes more, in the same four files.

1. The job

In server.lua, declare the job. The first start creates it; later starts find it again.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureJob('mycafe', {
        name  = 'Bean Machine',
        roles = {
            { name = 'Owner',   level = 100 },
            { name = 'Barista', level = 1 },
        },
    })
end)

Hire yourself in /whip → Economy → Jobs → Bean Machine → Change. (From code, use HirePlayer.)

2. One counter, several options

Customers buy; baristas clock on, brew and clock off. One prompt carries them all as options, and each option's require decides who sees it. In client.lua, replace the counter's AddAction:

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:AddAction({
        id      = 'counter',
        at      = { coords = Config.Counter },
        options = {
            { id = 'buy', label = ('Buy coffee ($%d)'):format(Config.Price), icon = 'cash',
              onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:buy') end },

            -- Staff only. whipJob is the job they're on duty at (false when off duty)
            { id = 'clockon', label = 'Clock on', require = { job = 'mycafe' },
              canInteract = function() return LocalPlayer.state.whipJob ~= 'mycafe' end,
              onSelect = function(ctx)
                  local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ClockOn('mycafe')
                  if not ok then ctx.refuse(why) end
              end },

            { id = 'brew', label = 'Brew a coffee', require = { job = 'mycafe', onDuty = true },
              onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:brew') end },

            { id = 'clockoff', label = 'Clock off', require = { job = 'mycafe', onDuty = true },
              onSelect = function() exports.whip_core:ClockOff('mycafe') end },
        },
    })
end)
require only decides what's offered. Anything that matters is checked again on the server, as the brew below is.

3. Brewing, and pay

Add BrewPay = 5 to Config in shared.lua. Then, in server.lua:

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:SecureEvent('mycafe:brew', {
        rateLimit = 2000,
        near = { at = Config.Counter, range = 3.0, message = 'Stand at the counter' },
    }, function(source, player)
        if not exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'mycafe') then
            return false, 'Clock on first'
        end

        local done, reason = exports.whip_core:Progress(source, {
            label    = 'Brewing...',
            duration = 6000,
            near     = { coords = Config.Counter, range = 3.0 },   -- still at the counter when it ends
        })
        if not done then return false, reason end

        -- Six seconds went by: still the same character?
        if not exports.whip_core:IsSessionCurrent(source, player.session) then return end

        local given, gwhy = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'mycafe_coffee', 1, nil, 'brewed')
        if not given then return false, gwhy end
        exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(source, Config.BrewPay, { reason = 'Brewed a coffee' })
    end)
end)
  • The server checks duty; the client's require only chose what to show.
  • Progress on the server times the bar itself, and its near checks they're still at the counter when it ends (the event's near is checked once, on arrival).
  • IsSessionCurrent checks the character is still the one playing after a wait, before giving anything.
  • PayPlayer pays cash; whatever doesn't fit their pockets lands at their feet.

4. Try it

  1. restart mycafe and hire yourself (step 1).
  2. At the counter, clock on, then brew: a six-second bar, a coffee, $5.
  3. Walk away during the bar: it stops with "too far", and nothing is given.
  4. /whip → System → Monitor shows each mycafe:brew and any refusal's reason.
