How WHIP talks to your resource

You want toUseExample
Hear that something happenedAn event: AddEventHandler('whip_core:…', fn). After the fact; it can't be stopped. On the server any resource can fire one, so check GetInvokingResource() where it matters (Server Events)whip_core:player:loaded
Hear a value changeA listener: OnStatChanged, OnVehicleStatChanged, WatchVehicleStat. Only WHIP calls it, and it's removed when your resource stopsA HUD that follows hunger
Act just before WHIP does something on the player's gameA client hook: RegisterClientHook. WHIP waits for it (up to a second) but it can't refusePut the phone away before a gun is drawn
Refuse something of your ownA check you pass in: canUse, canInteract, a panel's onValidateNo drinking in a car
Add something to WHIPRegister…, Add…, Ensure…, in Whip.registerRegisterItem, AddAction

Coming from QBCore, ESX or ox

WHIP is a framework of its own, with no bridge from QBCore, ESX or ox: a resource written for one of them won't run unchanged. Porting a small job means rewriting its glue code (about a day), and most of what it did by hand becomes one WHIP call.

Keep, replace, remove

ResourceWith WHIP
oxmysqlKeep: WHIP uses it. Ensure it before WHIP's resources
qb-core, es_extended, qbx_core, ox_coreRemove: one framework at a time. The setup report flags one that's running
ox_inventory, qb-inventoryRemove: WHIP has its own (F2)
ox_target, qb-targetReplace with AddAction
ox_libIts helpers (math, tables, lib.waitFor) are fine. For anything on screen, use WHIP's UI library: WHIP keeps one screen open at a time, and ox_lib's screens don't know about WHIP's
Garages, keys, fuel, banking, doorlock, housing, shops, multicharacter, spawn, HUDRemove: each is part of WHIP. Fuel is whip_fuel
pma-voice, mumble-voipRemove if you use whip_voice

Calls you know

QBCore / ESX / oxWHIP
GetCoreObject(), getSharedObject()Nothing to fetch: add dependency 'whip_core' and @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua to the manifest, then call Whip.core:… inside Whip.register and exports.whip_core:… anywhere else
QBCore.Functions.GetPlayer(src), ESX.GetPlayerFromId(src)GetPlayer(source): a plain table with no methods; act through exports
PlayerData.citizenid, xPlayer.identifierplayer.charId (a number; save this one)
PlayerData.job, xPlayer.jobOn duty: GetPlayerJob(source) (nil off duty). Has the job at all: GetPlayerRole(source, 'police')
PlayerData.gangNo gangs: make a gang a job with EnsureJob
PlayerData.metadataSetPlayerFlag or SetPlayerMetadata
AddMoney, xPlayer.addMoneyPayPlayer (cash, or method = 'bank')
RemoveMoney, xPlayer.removeMoneyChargePlayer, which returns a receipt for RefundPlayer
Cash as a number on the playerCash is an item (banknotes): it can be dropped, stolen or stashed
shared/items.lua, ox_inventory/data/items.luaRegisterItem in your resource, or /whip → Economy → Items
CreateUseableItem, ESX.RegisterUsableItemRegisterUseHandler; pass a table for a timed use
AddItem / RemoveItemAddItem, RemoveItem, GetItemCount
ox_inventory:RegisterStashEnsureContainer
RegisterNetEvent on the serverSecureEvent (side by side)
CreateCallback / TriggerCallback, lib.callbackSecureCallback / Callback: return the answer, no cb
qb-target:AddBoxZone, ox_target:addSphereZone, addLocalEntityAddAction with at = { coords }, { entity }, { model } or { vehiclePart }. job = 'police' becomes require = { job = 'police' }; distance becomes reach
qb-menu, lib.registerContextNo list menu: use options on a prompt (menus) or a select field in Input
QBCore:Notify, lib.notifyNotifyPlayer (server), Notify (client), or return false, 'why' from a SecureEvent
Progressbar, lib.progressBarProgress, on the server for anything handed out at the end
lib.skillCheck, lib.inputDialog, lib.alertDialogSkillCheck, Input, Alert / Confirm
lib.showTextUI, DrawText3DShowText (client), ShowPlayerText (server); usually a prompt says it already
PolyZone, lib.zonesZones (EnsureZone)
qb-vehiclekeys, SetFuel, qb-garagesGiveVehicleKey; the 'fuel' vehicle stat (whip_fuel); Garages; SpawnTempVehicle for a job car
SetVehicleProperties(veh, props)SetVehicleProperties({ entity = veh }, props) on the client: a bare number is a vehicleId. To keep the look, SetVehicleAppearance on the server
AddBlipForCoord + SetBlipRouteShowBlip from the server, with route = true
qb-doorlock, ox_doorlockEnsureDoors (Doors)
Lang:t(), localesNo locale system: your resource's text is your own

What will surprise you

  • Declarations go in Whip.register, not straight to whip_core at the top of a file (the one rule).
  • "Their job" means on duty. GetPlayerJob is nil off duty; GetPlayerRole is for "works there at all". Players clock on in the phone's Business app, or your resource calls ClockOn.
  • Pay with PayPlayer, charge with ChargePlayer. There is no lower-level cash call.
  • A receipt lasts 30 minutes. After that, give money back with PayPlayer.
  • A bar on the player's game is their word. For anything handed out at the end, use the server's Progress or a timed use.
  • Exports return false, 'why' instead of throwing (Return values).

A qb delivery job, call by call

The qb job doesThe WHIP version does
A job in shared/jobs.luaWhip.core:EnsureJob('delivery', { … }) in Whip.register
qb-target box at the depot, job = 'delivery'AddAction({ at = { coords = DEPOT }, require = { job = 'delivery', onDuty = true }, … })
Van deposit: RemoveMoney('bank', 500)ChargePlayer(source, 500, { method = 'bank' }); keep the receipt
CreateVehicle + vehiclekeys + SetFuelSpawnTempVehicle: the driver gets a key, and the van goes when you despawn it, after despawnAfter, or when your resource stops
Packages: AddItem + ItemBoxStoreGive into the van's boot, or AddItem
Blip and route to the drop-offShowBlip({ people = { source } }, 'drop', { coords = DROP, route = true })
Progressbar, then TriggerServerEvent('delivery:pay')A prompt at the door; a SecureEvent with near runs the server's Progress, takes the package and pays. near closes the classic exploit of firing the pay event from anywhere
Pay: AddMoney('cash', 120)PayPlayer(source, 120, { reason = 'Delivery' })
Van back: refund the depositRefundPlayer(receipt) within 30 minutes; after that PayPlayer

The whole job is in whip_core/docs/examples/whip_delivery_example, including what happens when the driver logs out or the van is taken back. Copy it into your resources and ensure it.

How WHIP works

Five ideas explain most of WHIP. Read this page alongside Your First Resource.

1. Accounts, characters and sessions

account        userId     made the first time they connect; staff permissions belong here
 └ character   charId     up to Config.MaxCharacters per account; kept forever: save this one
    └ loaded on a server id (source), for one session (player.session), until logout
IdNamesLastsUsed by
sourceA connected playerUntil they leave; the next player can get the same numberEverything about someone online: GetPlayer, AddItem, NotifyPlayer
{ charId = n }A character, online or notForeverCalls that can reach someone offline: PayPlayer, GiveOnLogin, the bank (naming a person)
userIdAn accountForeverStaff permissions (GrantPermission)
player.sessionOne load of a characterUntil logoutIsSessionCurrent, after your handler waited
vehicleIdA car WHIP knowsOwned: forever. Others: until the restartEvery vehicle export (vehicle references)

2. Every place items sit is a store

Pockets, a stash, a car's boot, glovebox or ignition, a shop, a wallet: each is a store, addressed as { kind, id, sub, slot }. One call moves items between any two (StoreMove), with the same checks, so code that fills a stash can fill a boot.

3. Memory first, the database catches up

WHIP changes its memory at once and writes the changes within about a second. Everything one player action changes is written in one transaction, so a crash never leaves half of it (Save System).

4. Declarations live in whip_core's memory

Items, use handlers, prompts and secure events are forgotten when whip_core restarts. So they go in Whip.register, which declares them again (the one rule).

5. The server decides

A player's game only asks. A SecureEvent checks who asked, how often, from where and every value before your handler runs. What the client is shown (an action's require) is a courtesy, never the check.

Where your data lives

Your dataPut it inSaved byVisible to
Items and cash a player carriesTheir pockets: AddItem, PayPlayerWHIP, with the actionThe player; admins
Something about one item: a serial, rounds, wearIts metadata: SetItemMetadataWHIP, with the itemThe holder's game too: never a secret
A fact about a character: a licence, quest progressSetPlayerFlag while they're online; SetPlayerMetadata, GiveOnLogin or the bank for someone offline tooWHIP, with the characterTheir game too: never a secret
Something about a car: a fitted part, a finance flagSetVehicleData; a gauge (fuel, boost) is a vehicle statWHIP, with the carGames near the car, for a stat
Items kept somewhere new: a mailbox, a vaultA container (EnsureContainer) or a store kind of your ownWHIPWhoever its rules let open it
Your resource's settingsA settings page: Whip.configPage (Settings pages)WHIP, in the databaseAdmins edit it in /whip; every game reads it unless the setting says sides = 'server'
A player's own choice: a volume, a toggleWhip.playerSetting (player settings)Their own PCThat player
Anything else: a ledger, a leaderboardA table of your own, made with EnsureTableYou; use CommitWithAction after an inventory changeWhoever your code shows it to
An item for a character who's awayGiveOnLoginWHIP, until their next loginThem, when it arrives
EnsureTable(name, createSql, migrations?)SERVER

Creates a table of your own the way WHIP creates its own, so nobody imports a .sql file. createSql is one complete CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; text sorts by utf8mb4_unicode_ci unless you name a COLLATE.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe table's name
createSqlstringThe table as it is now, complete
migrationstable?Changes made after release, in order, only ever appended. Each runs once per database, recorded as '<resource>:<id>'
Returns: true, or false, why: a bad name or statement, or the first migration that failed (later ones wait for the next start)
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureTable('mycafe_orders', [[
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `mycafe_orders` (
            `id`     INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
            `charId` INT          NOT NULL,
            `note`   VARCHAR(200) NULL,
            PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
        ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4]], {
        { id = '002_note', statements = {
            { sql = 'ALTER TABLE `mycafe_orders` ADD COLUMN `note` VARCHAR(200) NULL',
              unless = { column = { 'mycafe_orders', 'note' } } },
        } },
    })
end)
Put each change in both places. The CREATE for a new server, a migration for one that has the table. When this call creates the table, migrations are recorded as done without running. Guard a statement with unless or onlyIf and { column = { table, name } }, { index = … } or { constraint = … }; or give a migration a run function that returns false to be retried next start.
CommitWithAction(queries, opts?)SERVER

Runs your queries in one transaction with everything the player's current action changed that WHIP hasn't written yet: the item taken and your ledger row land together, or neither does. Outside an action, it runs the queries alone.

ParamTypeDescription
queriestable[]{ { query = '…', values = { … } }, … }
optstable?Called outside the handler that made the change? Name whose action with source (and vehicleId)
Returns: true, or false, why (nothing of the transaction landed; WHIP writes its own part again later)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RemoveItem(source, 'mycafe_coffee', 1)
if not ok then return false, why end
ok, why = exports.whip_core:CommitWithAction({
    { query = 'INSERT INTO `mycafe_orders` (`charId`, `note`) VALUES (?, ?)', values = { player.charId, 'coffee' } },
})
GiveOnLogin(who, item, amount?, metadata?, opts?)SERVER

Gives an item to someone who may not be playing: a prize, a refund owed. Online, they get it now, like AddItem. Offline, it's kept in the database and handed over at their next login (at their feet if their pockets are full), logged with your reason.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id or { charId = n }
itemstringItem key
amount, metadata, optsnumber?, table?, table?As for AddItem; opts.reason goes in the log
Returns: 'now' or 'login', or false, why (unknown item, bad amount, no such charId)
exports.whip_core:GiveOnLogin({ charId = winner }, 'mycafe_voucher', 1, nil, { reason = 'raffle prize' })

Return values

Every export follows one rule: the first value is the result or false; the second is why. Exports don't throw, and never return nil, 'reason', because an export's return values are cut off at the first nil.

local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RemoveItem(source, 'mycafe_coffee', 1)
if not ok then return false, why end
Kind of callSuccessFailure
Change somethingtrue, or something more useful (AddItem returns 'inventory' or 'ground', StoreGive the slot). Still truthy, so if not ok worksfalse, why
Read about a playerThe valueA list, count or yes/no returns its empty form and why: {}, why · 0, why · false, why. A single value (a stat, coordinates, the player sheet) returns nil
Check (may they?)truefalse, why: CanUseBankAccount, HasPropertyAccess, HasJobPermission, CanUseDoor
CreateThe new thing as a table; a vehicle returns its vehicleId (CreateOwnedVehicle, SpawnTempVehicle, AdoptVehicle)false, why
Deletetruefalse, why
Look upA tablenil when there's nothing; false, why when the question is wrong (a bad address)
Return an idThe id: AddAction, AddPoint, HoldMoney, WatchVehicleStatfalse, why. Where there's a third value (the warnings of AddAction, UpdateAction, AddPoint), the second is false on success so the third gets through

Codes and sentences

The reason isLooks likeFromDo
A code'busy', 'cancelled', 'too far', 'failed'Progress, SkillCheckBranch on it (if why == 'cancelled') and write your own words for the player
A sentence'Not enough cash'Everything elseShow it to the player, or return it from a SecureEvent. Don't compare it: the words may change

Naming a person

Wherever an export takes a person, a bare number is a server id (the source you already hold) and { charId = n } is a character, online or not. A bare number is never a charId, except in exports whose name says so (GetCharacterProperties(charId)).

exports.whip_core:GivePropertyKey(propertyId, source)              -- the player in front of you
exports.whip_core:GivePropertyKey(propertyId, { charId = 42 })   -- a character, online or not
A server id must be online. To reach someone who may be offline, pass { charId = n }. Some calls need the person online either way (a car key, TransferVehicle); their cards say so. A parameter named source is always a server id.

Finding one thing

A lookup is one call, GetX(ref): an id, or a table with one key that says what you hold. A list is GetXs(filter?).

exports.whip_core:GetVehicle({ plate = 'ABC123' })
exports.whip_core:GetShop({ key = 'burgershot' })
exports.whip_core:GetPlayer({ charId = 42 })          -- online players only
exports.whip_core:GetShops({ job = 'burgershot' })

Two export gotchas

Both come from FiveM, and neither errors where the mistake is.

1. A function passed through an export isn't type() == 'function'. It arrives as a callable reference. Calling it works; type-checking it rejects every caller. Matters when you write an export that takes a callback.

if type(fn) == 'function' then ... end   -- WRONG: false for every callback through an export
if fn ~= nil then pcall(fn, ...) end     -- RIGHT

2. A nil returned through an export arrives as no value at all. Nesting the call inside another call then passes no argument. Assign export results to a local first.

if type(exports.whip_core:GetVehicleData(id, 'key')) == 'table' then ... end   -- WRONG: errors when nil

local data = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleData(id, 'key')                       -- RIGHT
if type(data) == 'table' then ... end

Registering with WHIP

Items, stats, secure events, callbacks, actions, zones, store kinds: everything a resource registers with WHIP follows one rule, so running your registration twice is always safe.

You registerWhat happens
Something newIt's yours. Returns true
The same thing againNothing: no reset, no re-broadcast
A changed version of your ownIt replaces yours
Something another resource registeredRefused: false, 'item "x" belongs to other_resource', also printed once in the console (F8 on a client) and listed in the setup report
A name starting whip_core:Refused: those are WHIP's own

When your resource stops, what it registered is removed. Items are the exception, since players still carry them, but they stop being yours and another resource may take the name.

Prefix names with your resource's name

Item keys, right-click action names, stats, vehicle stats, server zone ids and permissions share one list per server, and the first resource to register a name owns it. Start each with your resource's name and an underscore: mycafe_coffee, mycafe_stress. Events and callbacks use a colon: mycafe:buy. An unprefixed name still works, but the console lists it once:

[whip_core] mycafe registers 3 items whose names do not start with "mycafe" (coffee, bagel, tea). ...
Names WHIP already uses. Items phone, sim_card, rope, radio, megaphone, nitro, whip_gunny's weapons, magazines and ammo (weapon_pistol and the like), and every item in whip_core's config.lua; vehicle stats nitro, boost and fuel. /whip → Economy → Items shows each key's owner.

Listing registrations, and run tags

GetRegistrations shows who holds a name that was refused. Run tags let a mission or heist clean up everything it made in one call: pass { tag = 'run:42' } in a registration's options (on modules that support it), then ReleaseTag.

GetRegistrations(resource?)CLIENTSERVER

Everything registered with WHIP on this side (events, callbacks, items, stats, actions, stat listeners, client hooks, settings, /w pages, debug tools, held props), or one resource's share.

ParamTypeDescription
resourcestring?Only this resource's registrations; everything when omitted
Returns: table[]: { { registry, key, owner }, … }
for _, r in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetRegistrations(GetCurrentResourceName())) do
    print(r.registry, r.key)
end
ReleaseTag(tag)CLIENTSERVER

Removes everything your resource registered under a run tag, in every WHIP module, and closes the tag: later registrations under it are refused with "… has ended". Use a new tag for each run; releasing one never touches another run or another resource's things.

ParamTypeDescription
tagstringYour run's label, e.g. 'run:42' (up to 100 characters)
Returns: true, count (how many things were removed), or false, why for an empty or over-long tag
local tag = 'heist:' .. jobId
exports.whip_core:SpawnNpc({ model = 's_m_m_security_01', coords = guardPos, behaviour = 'guard' }, { tag = tag })
exports.whip_core:SpawnTempVehicle('stockade', vanPos, { tag = tag })

-- The job is over: the guard and the van go
local ok, count = exports.whip_core:ReleaseTag(tag)
GetTagged(tag)CLIENTSERVER

What your resource holds under a run tag, across WHIP's modules.

ParamTypeDescription
tagstringYour run's label
Returns: table[]: { { registry, key }, … }; empty for an unknown or bad tag

The satellite helper

@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua is a file your resource loads, giving you Whip.register, safe calls to whip_core and a few tools. It runs inside your resource so it can remember your registrations across a whip_core restart.

-- fxmanifest.lua
dependency 'whip_core'
shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua'
CallWhat it does
Whip.register(fn)Runs fn once whip_core is ready (whichever started first) and again after every whip_core restart. Your declarations go in it, through Whip.core, and a refusal is printed (what it prints). Server and client.
Whip.core:Name(…)Calls an export safely, with its types in your editor: Whip.core:AddItem(source, 'cookie', 1). Returns what the export returns, or false, why when whip_core is down or the call errored. If whip_core stops during a wait it returns false, 'whip_core stopped', meaning "no answer", not "didn't happen": a charge already sent may still land.
Whip.call(name, …)The same, for a name built at run time: Whip.call(exportName, …). Otherwise use Whip.core, which your editor checks.
Whip.ready(timeoutMs?)Waits (in a thread) until whip_core is ready. false on timeout.
Whip.isReady()Is whip_core running and ready right now?
Whip.command(name, opts, fn) (server)A chat command behind a SecureEvent's checks: refused while the player is down (whileDead = true allows it), rate limited (three at once, then one a second; rateLimit = false for none), ace = 'my.perm', and dev = true for the console and whip.devtools with developer mode on. fn(source, args, raw) runs in its own thread. Use it instead of RegisterCommand with your own checks.
Whip.sayStarted() · Whip.startProblem(fmt, …) (server)One start line in the console instead of one per system. Once your Whip.register functions have run, it prints <your resource> started successfully!, unless something went wrong since your resource started (one of them threw, an error was caught, or something was printed in red); then those lines are all it prints. Whip.startProblem('engines.json is unreadable: %s', why) prints a problem in red with your resource's name. Call Whip.sayStarted() once, in a server file.
Whip.registry(name, opts) · Whip.caller()A registry of your own with WHIP's registration rule, for a resource others extend (phone apps, MDT plugins): local Apps = Whip.registry('app', { label = 'app' }), then in your export return Apps:add(Whip.caller(), id, def). Read Apps.entries, Apps:get(id), Apps:keysOf(owner).
Whip.registerWith(resource, fn)Runs fn now if resource is running and each time it starts, so registering with another resource's registry survives its restart.
Whip.requires('1.0') · Whip.has(name)Version checks. Put whip_requires '1.0' in your fxmanifest and the setup report flags an older whip_core; Whip.requires does the same from code. Whip.has('GetBalance') checks for one export. whip_updates 'you/myresource' there tells server owners when your GitHub repository has a newer release (Update checks).
Whip.onCoreLost(fn)Only for a resource without dependency 'whip_core': runs when whip_core stops, to let go of anything that needed it. Every player has been logged out by then with no whip_core:player:logout, so drop per-player state too.
Whip.voice(name, …) · Whip.voiceSystem()Calls whichever voice system runs (Voice for other resources).

Declaring in Whip.register

One function can hold every declaration: a loop over your Config, an answer you keep (an AddAction id), state of your own to reset. It runs again after each whip_core restart, so it reads Config as it is then, settings-page values included.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItem('mycafe_cup', { name = 'Cup', weight = 0.1 })
    for key, drink in pairs(Config.Drinks) do
        Whip.core:RegisterItem(key, drink)
    end
end)

While it runs, a declaring call that whip_core refuses prints one line in your console, naming your resource, the export and the reason: Register…, Ensure…, Add…, On…, Watch…, SecureEvent and SecureCallback, called through Whip.core or Whip.call. A call straight through exports.whip_core isn't printed: check its return yourself.

What else it does

  • With dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart stops and restarts your resource, so you start fresh and there's nothing to clean up. Without it, your resource keeps running: Whip.onCoreLost runs, then your Whip.register functions run again when whip_core is back.
  • It reports your errors to WHIP's tools (GetErrorLog, the Monitor) by wrapping CreateThread, SetTimeout, RegisterCommand, AddStateBagChangeHandler, RegisterNUICallback and print. They behave as before, at about half a microsecond per handler. Opt out with whip_error_tap 'no' in your fxmanifest.
  • Autocomplete: copy whip_core/types/luarc.template.json to your resource as .luarc.json. It finds WHIP's types next to your resource (../whip_core/types) or next to a [whip] folder; edit the path for any other layout.

Calling whip_core

Where the call isCallWhy
Inside a handler whip_core runs: SecureEvent, SecureCallback, a use handler, a right-click action, a hookexports.whip_core:Name(…)whip_core is up while it runs, and a payment and what it pays for are written together
Your own code: Whip.register, a thread, a command, a timer, an NUI callback, your own net event, a key pressWhip.core:Name(…)whip_core may not be ready yet (early in a start, or while a player's game loads); this returns false, why where a direct call would throw. In Whip.register, a refused declaration is printed
Code that runs every frameexports.whip_core:Name(…) behind Whip.isReady(), quick exports onlyWhip.core checks whip_core and guards every call, and an export that waits (WAITS) gets a thread of its own: too much at 60 a second

A card marked WAITS can wait on the database or the player. Call it from a thread or handler, never at file scope, and afterwards re-read anything that may have changed meanwhile. Your editor shows these as async.

The WHIP way

The rules WHIP's own resources follow. A resource that keeps them works on every WHIP server, survives a whip_core restart, and doesn't fight other resources.

RuleBecause
Declare in Whip.register: items, events, actions, jobswhip_core forgets them when it restarts (the one rule)
The server decides. Every message from a game is a SecureEvent or SecureCallback that names its values, with near where it mattersA modified game can send anything, from anywhere (Secure Events)
Return false, 'why'; never throw or return a bare nilCallers can tell a refusal from a bug, and players can read why (Return values)
Save a charId, never a server idServer ids are reused by the next player to join
Ask WHIP for what players share: the screen (SetScreenOpen), controls (BlockControls), hands (FreeHands)One owner each, released when your resource stops (Screens, input and controls)
React to events; don't poll with while true do Wait(0)A per-frame loop costs every player all the time (Timing your loops)
One call per action: StoreMove, not RemoveItem then AddItem; your own rows with CommitWithActionOne action, one transaction (Save System)
Prefix names with your resource's: mycafe_coffee, mycafe:buyNames are server-wide, first come first served (Registering)
Put a check where every path passes: in your export, not in each callerThe next caller can't forget it
Settings on a page, not in code: Whip.configPageOwners change it in /whip, and it survives your updates (Settings pages)

Glossary

Words these docs use in a sense of their own. Where QBCore, ESX or ox uses a different word, it's in italics.

WordMeans
ACEFiveM's permission system, set with add_ace in server.cfg. whip.devtools is the ACE for WHIP's admin tools (Dev Tools)
ActionSomething a player can do: a prompt in the world, an F1 wheel option, a choice on a car part. Made with AddAction. A target option.
AddressHow a store and slot are named: { kind, id, sub, slot } (Addresses)
AudienceWho something the server shows is for (a blip, a prop set, a point): 'everyone' or { people = { serverId | { charId = n } } } (Player)
CardOne step of a Director scenario: an NPC, a car, a goal, a line of talk (Director cards)
charIdA character's id. Saved, so it never changes; save this one (Naming a person)
Consume, liveThe two ways a client reports a vehicle stat only it can know: how much was used (fuel), or what it's worth now (boost). The server caps both (consume and live)
ContainerA storage box in the world; one kind of store. A stash. (Containers)
Developer modeA switch in /w. Off, an admin is treated as an ordinary player (Dev Tools)
DirectorWHIP's scenario builder in /whip: missions and stories made from cards, no code (Director)
DUIA web page drawn onto something in the world, like a screen or a sign (DUI)
Ensure…EnsureJob, EnsureShop, EnsureDoors and the rest: the first call creates the thing, later calls bring it in line with what you declare. Safe to declare at every start (Jobs)
F1 wheelThe radial menu (F1, or hold D-pad down). An action with at = { radial = true } (at). A radial menu.
Ground itemAn item lying in the world. Not a store: it has its own exports. A drop. (Ground Items)
HookA function of yours WHIP calls at a set moment and waits for, like a panel's onValidate (panel hooks) or a client hook (RegisterClientHook). Unlike an event, it can reply
Item keyThe name an item is registered under: 'mycafe_coffee' (Item Definition)
LayerA named change stacked on something, removed to restore what was under it: a weather layer (Layers), a handling layer (SetVehicleHandlingLayer)
Lore characterA story person the Director keeps, with a name, face, phone and voice lines (Director)
Managed doorA door owned by a resource (EnsureDoors) or a home. Admins can rename it but not change who opens it (Doors)
Monitor/whip → System → Monitor: every SecureEvent and SecureCallback call, accepted or refused, and Sentinel's detections
nearA SecureEvent rule: refuse unless the player is within range of a spot or the car named (near)
Owned, session vehicleOwned: someone's car, saved. Session: any other car WHIP knows, in memory only: street cars and SpawnTempVehicle cars (Vehicles)
PanelAn inventory-like window your resource opens beside the inventory, with OpenPanel. A secondary inventory. (Panels)
Panel itemAn item that holds items, like a wallet (RegisterPanelItem)
PermissionA WHIP staff role on an account, between player and full admin. Not an ACE (Permissions)
PersonA server id for someone online, or { charId = n } online or not (Naming a person)
Player sheetThe plain table GetPlayer returns: charId, fullName and so on, no methods. PlayerData, xPlayer. (Player)
PocketsA player's own stores: the main inventory (sub = 'player') and the accessory strip ('accessory')
PointAn interaction point added by server code (AddPoint)
Presencepersist = 'presence' on a vehicle stat: the database remembers the car has it, at its fitted value (RegisterVehicleStat)
ReceiptWhat ChargePlayer returns; pass it to RefundPlayer (Charging a Player)
Registry, registration ruleWhat whip_core holds of everything resources declared, forgotten on restart; same again changes nothing, another resource's name is refused (Registering)
Run tagA label like 'run:42' on what one mission makes, so ReleaseTag removes it all (Run tags)
SatelliteAny resource built on whip_core, loading @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua (The satellite helper)
SecureEvent, SecureCallbackRegisterNetEvent and a server callback, with checks built in (Secure Events)
SentinelWHIP's guard against a game changing the state bags WHIP writes (Sentinel)
SessionA number on the player sheet, new each time a character loads; check it with IsSessionCurrent after a wait. Not a session vehicle
Setup reportWhat whip_core prints at start: problems with the server's setup and the line that fixes each (Quick Start)
Server id, sourceFiveM's number for a connected player. Changes every join, so never save it
SnapshotThe copy of a car GetVehicle returns; it can be passed back to any vehicle export (Vehicle references)
Stat, effectA character's server-side numbers (health, hunger, your own) and timed changes to them (Stats & Effects)
StoreAnywhere items sit: pockets, a container, a boot, a shop, a panel item. Not a shop. An inventory. (Stores)
Store kindThe sort of store an address names: 'player', 'container', 'vehicle' or your own (Store Kinds)
Use handlerWhat using an item does: a function, or a table for a timed use. A usable item. (RegisterUseHandler)
userIdA player's account, holding up to Config.MaxCharacters characters (Characters)
Vehicle dataAnything stored on a car that isn't a gauge: SetVehicleData (Vehicle Data)
Vehicle reference{ id }, { entity }, { plate } or { netId }; a bare number is a vehicleId (Vehicle references)
Vehicle statA gauge on a car that WHIP keeps, syncs and saves: fuel, nitrous, boost (RegisterVehicleStat)
vehicleIdWHIP's id for a car: the database id when owned, 1,000,000,000 and up otherwise. Not the entity or netId
WatcherWatchVehicleStat / WatchVehicleData: your code runs while a car nearby has a stat (Watching stats)
Whip.registerThe function you hand declarations to, so WHIP can run it again after a restart (the one rule)

What a resource can change

Almost everything is done from your own resource, without editing whip_core, so WHIP's updates never undo your work. Here's where the line is.

Without touching whip_core

You canWith
Add items, stats, prompts, jobs, shops, stashes, store kinds, item windows, settings pages, Director cards, /w pages, skill check games, a voice systemRegister…, Add…, Ensure…, in Whip.register (The calls you'll use)
Change WHIP's own rules: the respawn wait, hospitals, hunger, the lockpick game, and some 200 more/whip → Settings → Config, or config.lua (Configuration)
Hold one of WHIP's things for a whileHoldRespawn (a dead player waits for a medic), HoldVehicleEngine, BlockControls, BlockHands, HoldPlayerPed
Refuse something of yourscanUse, canInteract, a panel's onValidate (How WHIP talks to your resource)
Hear what happenedServer Events, Client Events

What you can't change

  • WHIP's own items' uses (lockpick, bandage, food and drink). Register your own item, or change the item in /whip → Economy → Items.
  • The status HUD. Your stats can add gauges (RegisterStat with hud) and Config.HudSkin picks one of two looks, but it can't be turned off or redrawn.
  • The spawn picker's choices: last location, the presets in config.lua, and their homes.

Replacing a screen

ScreenHow
The look of every screenA theme: a resource with a theme.css, chosen by Config.Theme or SetActiveTheme (Theming)
InventorySet Config.InventoryRenderer to your resource, which then draws it (the renderer seat)
Death screenConfig.DeathScreen = false, and draw your own from whip_core:death:screenChanged (Death & Revive)
PhoneStop whip_phone and run your own, using SetScreenOpen, SetScreenArea and FreeHands
ChatAny chat resource that handles the stock chat's events
Loading screenAny FiveM loading screen; whip_core closes it when the player arrives
Status HUD, character select and creator, spawn picker, notifications, progress barA theme only

Testing and performance

Tools for trying your resource before players do, and for measuring what it costs on the player's game and the server.

Testing

To testUse
Your inventory screen, without the gamenode whip_core/dev/inventory-preview/preview.js my_inventory_ui runs it in Chrome with sample scenes (the renderer seat)
A Director card or scenarioTestDirectorCard(type, props, { player = source }), TestDirectorScenario (Director cards)
Something done to another player, alonePass { charId = n } for a second character of yours, then log in as them to see it
Two players at onceTwo FiveM clients on one PC, same account, different characters. Turn off Config.BlockOwnCharacterTransfers on a test server to move money between them
Dying, healing, a broken car/w → Kill Me, Restore Player Cores, Repair Vehicle (Dev Tools)
What your events did/whip → System → Monitor: each SecureEvent call, the reason for a refusal, and how long your handler took
Errors you missedwhiperrors in the server console (F8 in developer mode); GetErrorLog in code

Measuring

WhereToolTells you
Player's game/whipcost (developer mode)Microseconds per frame for each timed section, and each resource's memory. Time your own loops with WhipCost.start() / WhipCost.stop('my loop', t) (client_script '@whip_core/lib/cost.lua'), never with a Wait between them
Player's gameMeasureFrames({ seconds })FPS, the worst 1%, and frames over 33 and 50 ms: compare with your resource started and stopped
Serverwhipcost [seconds] in the consoleThe same for server sections marked with WhipCost (server_script '@whip_core/lib/cost.lua'), by CPU time
Server/whip → System → MonitorHow long each SecureEvent and SecureCallback handler took, database waits included
Eitherprofiler record 500, then profiler viewEvery resource's time per frame in Chrome's performance view. With setr whip_profiling 1, whip_core's handlers are named by event. Captures inflate costs about five times: compare captures, not budgets

The usual cost is a loop running every frame (Wait(0)). Wait on an event instead, and check the loops you must keep with /whipcost.

What an export costs

Cheapest first. Call the first two as often as you need; the rest when something happens, never every frame.

CostFor exampleMeans
MemoryHasItem, GetItemCount, IsPlayerClockedOn, GetPlayerJob, GetBalance after its first readMicroseconds
A copyGetPlayer, GetVehicle, StoreReadFrom memory, but the table is serialised on its way to you. Keep what you need rather than re-reading every frame
Sends to a gameNotifyPlayer, ShowBlip, ShowPlayerText, SetPlayerMetadataNetwork traffic: fine per action, wrong in a loop over every player
Waits on the databaseEnsure*, bank reads, ChargePlayer, PayPlayer, AddItem, SetVehicleDataMarked WAITS: milliseconds. Call from a thread or handler, and re-read after
Waits on the other side or the playerServer Progress, SkillCheck; client Callback, ResolveVehicle, InputWAITS too: a round trip (200 ms at 200 ms ping), or as long as the player takes

Legacy and Enhanced

WHIP runs on FiveM Legacy and GTA V Enhanced, and so can your resource. Almost everything is the same; these are the differences.

WhatOn EnhancedDo this
Models, maps, propsLegacy models must be convertedShip both: stream/ for Legacy and stream_enhanced/ for Enhanced, which is used instead when it exists
NPCs made at startAn NPC made before any character loads can lose its network idMake NPCs after whip_core:player:loaded, or in Whip.register once a player is on
Wide DUI pagesCreateDui refuses pages wider than 8192 pixelsPack an atlas into rows
Anything elseexports.whip_core:GetPlatform() returns 'legacy' or 'enhanced' on either side

A server says it's Enhanced with setr whip_platform enhanced (the server.cfg).

Selling on WHIP

Resources that use WHIP through its exports are your own work: open or closed, free or sold, under any licence. Here's what to keep in mind.

Licensing

  • WHIP is LGPL 3.0 (each resource's COPYING.LESSER, with the GPL 3.0 it builds on in COPYING; whip_core's emote list, shared/emote_list.lua, is GPL 3.0). A resource that calls its exports and loads @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua from whip_core's folder is yours. (That's WHIP's reading of its licence, not legal advice.)
  • Don't copy WHIP's files into your resource. A copied file stays LGPL, and buyers must be able to change it, which encryption prevents. Load the helper with shared_script; never paste it in. The example resources (names ending _example or _examples) are MIT: copy from them freely.
  • Don't call your resource WHIP. The licence doesn't cover WHIP's name or logo. "Works with WHIP" is fine. whip_core/NOTICE.md lists what the licence doesn't cover.

Escrow

FiveM's asset escrow encrypts your Lua. WHIP never reads your Lua files: it knows your resource by name, and your settings live in its database. A few files must stay readable:

FileWith escrow
Your config.luaAdd to escrow_ignore so owners can edit it, or use a Whip.configPage instead
A property pack as .luaAdd to escrow_ignore, or ship it as .json
Director scenario packsAlready .json: nothing to do
Your ui_page, images, soundsLeft as they are

WHIP is untested with escrowed resources. If something stops working once encrypted, send the console output.

What a buyer can copy

Escrow protects Lua and streamed models only. Your HTML, JavaScript, CSS, images, sounds, property packs and Director scenarios stay readable, and a shipped scenario can be duplicated and exported in the buyer's Director. Price scenario packs with that in mind.

Secure Events

Any player can send your server any event, with any values, as often as they like. With SecureEvent you write down what a call must look like, and WHIP checks it before your handler runs.

A call that fails never reaches your code, and the Monitor shows who sent it and why. SecureCallback does the same for a question the client waits on.

Before and after

A purchase with RegisterNetEvent, checked by hand:

local lastBuy = {}

RegisterNetEvent('myshop:buy', function(itemKey, amount)
    local source = source
    local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)
    if not player or player.isDead then return end                -- loaded, and alive

    local now = GetGameTimer()                                     -- a rate limit, and a table
    if lastBuy[source] and now - lastBuy[source] < 500 then return end  -- to clean up when they leave
    lastBuy[source] = now

    if type(itemKey) ~= 'string' or not itemKey:match('^[%w_]+$') then return end
    amount = tonumber(amount)
    if not amount or amount ~= math.floor(amount) or amount < 1 or amount > 100 then return end

    local pos = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source))              -- at the counter
    if #(pos - COUNTER) > 5.0 then return end

    buy(source, player, itemKey, amount)   -- every return above was silent: nobody sees why
end)

The same purchase as a SecureEvent:

exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myshop:buy', {
    rateLimit = 500,
    params = {
        {'itemKey', 'key', 60},       -- letters, digits, _ and -
        {'amount',  'amount', 100},   -- a whole number from 1 to 100
    },
    near = { at = COUNTER, range = 5.0 },
}, function(source, player, itemKey, amount)
    buy(source, player, itemKey, amount)   -- loaded, alive, checked, at the counter
end)

What WHIP checks for you

CheckWhat it stopsYou write
A loaded characterCalls from character select, or from someone logging outNothing: on by default
AliveA dead player buying, looting or using itemsNothing: on by default
How oftenA call fired hundreds of times a secondNothing (10 in a row, then one every 100 ms), or rateLimit
Every valueThe wrong type, a negative amount, text where a number goesparams
Where they areBuying from across the mapnear
What they ownNaming somebody else's slot, stash or carThe slot, addr and vehicle types
Who they areAdmin and staff actions from everyone elseace or permission

What your handler saves lands in one transaction (Save system), but return false or an error doesn't undo it: refund it yourself.

What it doesn't do. near trusts the position the player's game reports, so teleports, god mode and aimbots still need an anticheat. And never let a client handler decide anything that matters: a cheat can fire those too.

Writing one

Pass the event's name, its rules (the schema) and your handler. A tip jar for the coffee stand from Your First Resource:

-- server.lua
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:SecureEvent('mycafe:tip', {
        rateLimit = 2000,                                   -- one tip every 2 seconds
        params    = { {'amount', 'amount', 500} },          -- $1 to $500
        near      = { at = Config.Counter, range = 3.0 },
    }, function(source, player, amount)
        local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, amount, { reason = 'Tip' })
        if not receipt then return false, err end          -- refused: they are shown why
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, ('Thanks for the tip, %s'):format(player.firstName), 'success')
    end)
end)

-- client.lua: sent like any other event
TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:tip', 20)
  • Declare it in Whip.register, so it survives a whip_core restart (Your First Resource, step 3). Later examples show the call alone.
  • Start the name with your resource's and no other resource can take it.
  • The handler gets source, player, then your values in params order. Use this source, not the global. player is a copy of the player sheet.

Send TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:tip', -50) and /whip → System → Monitor shows it refused: amount: Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more. It keeps the last 500 accepted and 500 refused calls until whip_core restarts (Dev Tools). The console prints refusals too, unless Config.LogSecureRejections = false.

Checking the values: params

One line per value the client sends, in order: a name, a type, then its limits, as in {'amount', 'amount', 100}. Only listed values reach your handler; one you leave out arrives as nil.

  • Refused, never corrected: amount (counts and money), id and key (a thing named by a number or a word; they check the form, not that it exists), and slot, vehicle and addr (below).
  • Softer, for settings: number and int pull a value into range; enum, bool and string fall back to a default if you give one.
  • Shapes: list, record (a form's fields), and player (another player nearby).

Numbers sent as text count as numbers, except in an enum. Every rule is in the types table.

Checking what they own: slot, vehicle, addr

These check the player may use the thing, and hand your handler the thing itself.

  • slot: a slot in the caller's pockets, sent as a number or { sub = 'accessory', slot = 3 }. An empty slot is refused unless allowEmpty = true; with item, so is one holding something else. The handler gets { addr, item, amount, metadata }.
  • vehicle: a car they own, sent as its vehicleId (not the entity or netId). The handler gets a GetVehicle snapshot. anyOwner = true accepts anyone's owned car (for refuelling, with near); session = true also accepts unowned street cars.
  • addr: a slot in a store they can reach, like an open stash. Every item move in WHIP passes this gate (Addresses).
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('mykit:install', {
    params = { {'kit', 'slot', { item = 'mykit_turbo' }}, {'vehicle', 'vehicle'} },
    near = { at = 'vehicle', range = 5.0 },
}, function(source, player, kit, v)
    local taken, why = exports.whip_core:StoreTake(kit.addr, 1, { reason = 'fitted to ' .. v.plate })
    if not taken then return false, why end
    exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(v.vehicleId, 'mykit_turbo', { fittedAt = os.time() })
end)

Refusals a real player can meet ("That item is not there any more") are shown to them; forged values, like someone else's pocket, are refused silently.

Checking where they are: near

near refuses a call unless the player is within range metres (default 5) of at, which is a fixed vector3 or { x, y, z }; 'vehicle', the schema's vehicle value (sitting in it counts); or a function of the checked values:

near = {
    range = 15.0,
    at = function(source, player, shopId)
        local shop = exports.whip_core:GetShop(shopId)
        if not shop then return nil end          -- refused as too far
        return shop.x, shop.y, shop.z            -- or a vector3 or { x, y, z }
    end,
    message = 'You are too far from the shop', -- default 'Too far away'; false for timer calls
},

allowUnknown = true lets a call through when at finds no position, and range can be a function, to follow a setting.

How often: rateLimit and burst

You writeA player may send
nothing10 in a row, then one every 100 ms
rateLimit = 2000One, then one every 2 seconds: a cooldown
rateLimit = 2000, burst = 55 in a row, then one every 2 seconds
rateLimit = falseAny number

A pause earns calls back, up to the burst. Give a burst to anything done quickly by hand, and to anything that closes something: a refused close leaves it open.

Who may send it

  • Dead players are refused unless whileDead = true (closing a screen, respawn). The console line for that refusal names whileDead, and so does a toast with developer mode on.
  • ace = 'myresource.admin': that ACE only, dead or alive. whip.devtools also needs developer mode on.
  • permission = 'mygarage.manage': that permission only.
  • requirePlayer = false: also before a character loads; player is then nil.

Saying no

Your handler returnsThe player seesThe Monitor records
false, 'You need a wrench'The message, as an errorRefused, with the message
falseNothingRefused
anything else, or nothingOnly what you send themAccepted

To record a reason without showing one, call RecordEventRejection, then return.

Asking the server: SecureCallback

For a question the client waits on, register a SecureCallback and ask it with Callback. Your handler returns the answer.

local PRICES = { mycafe_coffee = 15, mycafe_muffin = 8 }   -- the server's prices, never the client's

-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
Whip.core:SecureCallback('mycafe:getPrice', {
    rateLimit = 500,
    params    = { {'itemKey', 'key', 60} },
}, function(source, player, itemKey)
    local price = PRICES[itemKey]
    if not price then return false, 'Not sold here' end   -- not nil: that would lose the why
    return price
end)

-- client.lua, in a command or event handler
local price, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('mycafe:getPrice', 'mycafe_coffee')
if not price then return exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error') end

The answer arrives up to its first nil, so refuse with false, why. With no answer, the client gets false and a reason:

The reasonWhen
'Rate limited', 'Player is dead', 'No player session', 'Too far away', 'itemKey: invalid key' …WHIP's checks refused the call
YoursYour handler returned false, 'Not sold here'
'Server error'Your handler errored (see the server console)
'Unknown callback'No callback has that name
'That is no longer available'Its resource has stopped
'No answer from the server'Nothing came back within 10 seconds

So answer an ordinary "no" with a word or a table, not false. The Monitor records every answer as accepted; RecordEventRejection records a refusal.

Less common options

ownerOf, onReject and sheet = 'light' are on the SecureEvent card. A handler that takes a lock can use TrackInvocationLock.

Common mistakes

  • Registering straight from the top of a file, not in Whip.register: it can run before whip_core is ready, and a whip_core restart forgets it.
  • Using the global source in a handler or its helpers.
  • int or number for money or a count: they pull -50 into range. Use amount with a max.
  • A callback returning nil to refuse: return false, 'why'.

Coming from ESX, QBCore or ox_lib

You use todayIn WHIP
RegisterNetEvent + AddEventHandlerSecureEvent
ESX.RegisterServerCallback, QBCore.Functions.CreateCallback, lib.callback.registerSecureCallback: return the answer, no cb
ESX.TriggerServerCallback, QBCore.Functions.TriggerCallback, lib.callback.awaitCallback: waits, and returns the answer

Moving an event over: swap the call, list its values in params, delete your own checks, declare it in Whip.register, and treat return false as "refused". You can move one event at a time. The rest: Coming from QBCore, ESX or ox.

SecureEvent & SecureCallback

Server exports for checked events and callbacks, and the client's Callback. New to them? Read Secure Events first.

Registering

SecureEvent(eventName, schema, handler)SERVER

Registers a net event whose every call is checked against schema before handler runs.

ParamTypeDescription
eventNamestringStarts with your resource's name ('myshop:buy'); up to 128 characters
schematableThe rules, below. {} takes every default and passes no values
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, ...values), values in params order; player lacks metadata. return false, 'why' refuses (Saying no)
Schema fieldDefaultDescription
params{}One {name, type, …} per value (types below). Only these reach the handler
rateLimit10 in a row, then one per 100 msLeast ms between calls, per player. false: no limit. 0 is refused (rate limits)
burst1 with a rateLimit, else 10Calls allowed back to back before rateLimit applies; a whole number, 1 or more
nearnone{ at, range = 5.0, message?, allowUnknown? } (near)
acenoneAn ACE the player must have. A dead player with it is let through
permissionnoneA WHIP permission, or a list (any one)
whileDeadfalsetrue lets a dead player send it
requirePlayertruefalse accepts players with no character loaded
ownerOfnoneNames an id value holding a netId: only that entity's network owner may send it (ownerOf = 'npcNet'). Refused quietly
onRejectnonefunction(source, reason, rawArgs), run when WHIP refuses before the handler. rawArgs are unchecked
sheet'full''light': player holds only source, session, userId, charId, firstName, lastName, fullName, dateOfBirth, gender, isDead
Value typeWrittenAccepts
amount{name, 'amount', max?}A whole number from 1 to max (no limit without one). Else refused
id{name, 'id', min?, max?}A whole number from min (default 1) to max. Else refused, never clamped
key{name, 'key', maxLen?}Letters, digits, _ and -, at most maxLen (default 60). Else refused, never cleaned
enum{name, 'enum', {values}, default?}One of the values, matched exactly ("1" is not 1)
bool{name, 'bool', default?}true, 1, "true", "1"; false, 0, "false", "0", "". Nothing sent is default (or false)
string{name, 'string', maxLen, default?}Text cut to maxLen, control characters but tab and newline removed. Empty is invalid
number{name, 'number', min, max, default?}Any number, pulled into min–max
int{name, 'int', min, max, default?}As number, rounded down. Never for a count, money or an id
slot{name, 'slot', opts?}A slot in the caller's pockets, as { addr, item, amount, metadata }. opts: item (a key or list), allowEmpty (slot)
vehicle{name, 'vehicle', opts?}A car the caller owns, as a GetVehicle snapshot. opts: anyOwner, session
addr{name, 'addr', opts?}A store address the caller may name, as for slot. opts.slotOptional accepts a whole store (Addresses)
list{name, 'list', entry, max?}Up to max entries (default 50), each checked against entry: one definition, or several for table entries ({ {'slot', 'id', 1, 50}, {'index', 'int', -1, 99} }). Refusals name the entry (basket[2].slot). No addr inside
player{name, 'player', { range?, notSelf? }}Another loaded player's server id, not in the creator, in the caller's routing bucket, within range m (default 3); not the caller unless notSelf = false. Passes their light sheet (source, charId, names, isDead …). "They are not here" and "They are too far away" are shown
record{name, 'record', fields}One table (a form), each field checked as a list entry's; only those fields are passed
any{name, 'any'}Anything, unchecked. Try record, list or slot first

With a default, enum, bool, string, number and int turn an invalid value into it; without one, they refuse it.

Returns: true, or false, reason (also printed; examples in Secure Events): the name is another resource's, starts whip_core: or cb:, or is a server lifecycle event such as playerDropped; or the schema is wrong (a rateLimit of 0, an unknown type, an enum with no values)
SecureCallback(name, schema, handler)SERVER

Registers a callback the client asks with Callback. Same checks as SecureEvent; the handler's return values are the answer.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringStarts with your resource's name
schematableAs SecureEvent's, without onReject
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, ...values), returning the answer (up to its first nil). Refuse with return false, 'why'
Returns: true, or false, reason, as SecureEvent. Example: Asking the server

Inside a handler

RecordEventRejection(eventName, src, reason?)SERVER

Records the call your handler is answering as refused in the Monitor. For a SecureCallback saying no (its false is an answer, recorded as accepted), or a SecureEvent refusing without a message on screen.

ParamTypeDescription
eventNamestringThe event or callback, as you registered it
srcnumberThe player whose request was refused
reasonstring?Why, as the Monitor shows it
Returns: nothing
exports.whip_core:RecordEventRejection('mycafe:getPrice', source, 'Not sold here')
return false, 'Not sold here'
TrackInvocationLock(releaseFn, eventName?, src?)SERVER

Calls releaseFn if your handler errors, so a lock it took isn't stuck until a restart. On a normal return, release it yourself.

ParamTypeDescription
releaseFnfunctionReleases the lock
eventNamestring?The event or callback your handler is answering
srcnumber?The source your handler was given
Returns: true, or false, reason outside a SecureEvent or SecureCallback handler
local release = acquireSafeLock(safeId)      -- yours: a release function, or nil if taken
if not release then return false, 'Someone is already at that safe' end
exports.whip_core:TrackInvocationLock(release, 'myheist:crackSafe', source)
crackSafe(safeId, source)                    -- if this errors, WHIP calls release
release()
Pass the event name and source, and keep burst at 1 (declare a rateLimit): two overlapping calls from one player can't be told apart.

Client: Callback

Callback(name, ...)CLIENT

Asks a server SecureCallback and waits for the answer. Commands and event handlers can wait; anywhere else (a RegisterNUICallback handler, say), call it inside CreateThread.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe callback's name
...anyThe values, in its params order
Returns: what the server's handler returned, or false, reason (the reasons, including 'No answer from the server' after 10 seconds)
local stock, why = exports.whip_core:Callback('myshop:getStock', 'corner')
if not stock then return exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error') end

Sentinel: Tamper Guard

The Sentinel stops a player's game from forging the facts WHIP shares through statebags: who is dead, on duty or escorted, damage taken, a car's stats. It's on out of the box, with nothing to write.

FiveM lets a player's game change the statebags about them and their car. When one changes a WHIP key, the Sentinel puts the right value back and strikes that player. Honest games never write these keys, so a detection is a modified client.

When it catches oneServer owners

The Monitor shows a red Tampered with <key> row and the console prints TAMPER. At 3 strikes the player is kicked, with a note signed Sentinel in the Player Manager as the lasting record. Strikes wear off after an hour, and reset when they rejoin. A kick isn't a ban: ban them from the Player Manager once you're sure.

A cheat, or a resource? A resource writing WHIP's keys looks exactly like a cheat. One player struck on a key that helps them is a cheat; several struck on one key at once (say, after an admin menu's revive) is a resource: turn kicking off and find it.
Config.SentinelDefaultWhat it does
enabledtruefalse turns the Sentinel off
autoKick3Strikes before a kick. false records them and kicks nobody
strikesForgetMinutes60Minutes without a strike before the count resets. false: never
logDebounceMs1000Repeats of one key by one player within this many ms count as one
bootSweeptrueAt start, put back values left wrong before the restart, with no strikes
damageModifierClamp{ min = 0.05, max = 4.0 }The range damage and melee modifiers are held to (0.05: 5% of the damage)

The first three can be changed live in /whip → Settings → Config → Server (changing a setting in game), where a saved value wins over config.lua and an empty Kick after box turns kicking off.

What it watches

Every WHIP key starts with whip:

  • Players: whipDead, whipJob, whipEscorted, whipEscortedBy, whipDamageMod, whipMeleeMod, whipMood.
  • Cars: whipVehicleId, whipVehicleSession, whipStats, whipLive, whipAppearance, whipVehData, whipVehDoors, whipEngineHold.
  • Object Viewer holds: whipOvHold.

For resource developers

  • On the server, read the player sheet or GetSentinelTruth, never the statebag. Names are never in one: use GetPlayerFullName.
  • Never write WHIP's keys with Player(src).state:set: the player is struck. Use WHIP's calls (its revive, for whipDead).
  • Guard your own statebag facts with the exports below, or send them as server events.
RegisterSentinelKey(def)SERVER

Puts one of your statebag keys under the Sentinel. A player key's truth is what you last wrote with SetSentinelPlayerKey; an entity key's comes from your truth function, since entities come and go.

FieldTypeDescription
def.keystringThe key. One another resource watches is refused
def.familystring'player' or 'entity'
def.truthfunction?Required for entity keys: function(entity) → value|nil, run when the key changes. nil removes the key: return it at the default, not {}
Returns: true, or false, reason. Watches go when your resource stops
Whip.core:RegisterSentinelKey({ key = 'mygang_tag', family = 'player' })   -- inside Whip.register
SetSentinelPlayerKey(src, key, value) / GetSentinelTruth(src, key)SERVER

Set records a value on the server, then writes the statebag. Truth reads that record, never the statebag: gate server checks on it. It reads WHIP's keys too.

ParamTypeDescription
srcnumberServer id; to set, they must be connected
keystringTo set: your keys or unwatched ones; another resource's and WHIP's are refused
valueanySet only. nil for "off", not false: an absent key costs nothing
Returns: set: true, or false, reason ('no such player', 'key "whipDead" is owned by whip_core') · truth: the value written (false and nil differ)
SetSentinelEntityKey(entity, key, value)SERVER

Writes one of your entity keys. Update the table your truth reads first; if they disagree, the console warns, nobody is struck, and the key is set back to your truth.

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumberThe entity (it must exist)
keystringYour keys or unwatched ones; another resource's and WHIP's are refused
valueanynil removes it
Returns: true, or false, reason ('no such entity', 'key "x" is owned by …')
tunes[plate] = t                                                -- your table, first
exports.whip_core:SetSentinelEntityKey(veh, 'mytune_data', t)   -- then the key
Not Entity(e).state:set. A bare write strikes whoever runs the entity: for a car, its driver.

Permissions

Staff roles between "everyone" and your full admins: a builder, a moderator, a garage manager. Your resource declares a permission, someone gives it to a player, and your events ask for it with permission = 'name'.

A grant works at once, with no restart. It's given to an account, so it's a staff role, not a job (for "police only", check the job). Full admins hold every permission: the whip.devtools ACE with developer mode on, and staff given dev tools in the Player Manager until the restart.

Permission or ACE?

ace = '…'permission = '…'
GivenIn server.cfg, with add_aceWith GrantPermission, or in the Player Manager
Best forFull adminsStaff roles given and taken while the server runs
A dead playerLet through: it's an admin toolRefused, unless whileDead = true

Using one

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterPermission('mygarage.manage', { label = 'Garage manager' })

    Whip.core:SecureEvent('mygarage:remove', {
        permission = 'mygarage.manage',     -- or a list: any one of them
        params     = { {'garageId', 'id'} },
    }, function(source, player, garageId)
        -- only a garage manager, or a full admin, gets here
    end)
end)

-- from a command or screen of yours
exports.whip_core:GrantPermission(targetSource, 'mygarage.manage')

A refused player shows in the Monitor with the permission they lacked.

Giving oneServer owners

Give and take any permission in /whip → Players → Player Manager → the player → Permissions. The Director's builders and admins can also be given in /whip → Director → Access.

RegisterPermission(name, def?)SERVER

Declares a permission; no other resource can take the name. The declaration goes when your resource stops, but grants stay in force.

FieldTypeDescription
namestring3 to 64 letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting with your resource's name
def.labelstring?Shown in the Monitor when someone lacks it
def.descriptionstring?A sentence for your own screens
def.impliesstring[]?Permissions this one includes (a Director admin is a builder too)
def.devtoolsboolean?false: full admins don't hold it automatically
def.grantedBystring?A permission whose holders may give and take this one. Full admins always may; temporary dev-tools admins need it
Returns: true, or false, reason
HasPermission(source, name)SERVER

Whether the player has it through a grant, an implying permission, or full admin. Read from memory.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer id
namestringThe permission
Returns: boolean
GrantPermission(who, name) · RevokePermission(who, name)SERVER

Gives an account a permission or takes it away, at once. whip_core:permission:changed fires on the server and on each of the account's online games (WHIP tells the player nothing); the activity log names your resource.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: an online server id, { charId = n } (online or not), or { userId = n }
namestringThe permission
Returns: true, or false, reason
GetPermissionHolders(name)SERVER

Everyone given it directly, named by their online or latest character. Full admins aren't listed.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe permission
Returns: { { userId, name, account, grantedBy, grantedAt, online }, … }, or false, reason

Character Lifecycle

A player connects, picks a character, plays, and logs out or leaves. Here's what your resource can rely on at each step, how WHIP saves, and the events it fires.

Connecting and loading

Joining needs a FiveM licence; banned players (by any identifier) are told the reason and when the ban ends. Everyone else gets an account (userId) and picks, makes or deletes a character, up to Config.MaxCharacters (4).

whip_core then loads the character, moves them to routing bucket 0, spawns the ped and syncs the world around them. The server's whip_core:player:loaded fires last: your "player ready" hook. The client's fires once the ped is in the world and the screen is back.

It isn't resent when your resource restarts, so also set up everyone already in from Whip.register (make setUp safe to run twice):

AddEventHandler('whip_core:player:loaded', function(e) setUp(e.source, e.player) end)

Whip.register(function()
    for source, player in pairs(exports.whip_core:GetPlayers()) do setUp(source, player) end
end)

Save system

Changes take effect at once in memory and reach the database within about a second (Config.FlushInterval, 1000 ms). You write no saving code.

  • One player action saves as one. A SecureEvent or SecureCallback handler is an action, and so is WHIP running your use handler, item action, onComplete, panel hook or AddAction callback. All it saves lands in one transaction.
  • Move an item between players in one call, StoreMove(fromAddr, toAddr); RemoveItem then AddItem can save as two.
  • Your own database writes join the transaction through CommitWithAction. Before a plain oxmysql write, call SavePlayer(source).
WhatWhen it's written
Pockets, stashes, boots, health and armour, activity logWithin Config.FlushInterval, or when the action ends; both halves of a move together
Position, hunger, thirst, your saved statsEvery Config.PlayerPositionSaveInterval (30 s), if changed
Car stats (fuel, nitro…) and positionEvery Config.VehicleStatsSaveInterval (15 s), or with the action
Car data, the bank, ground itemsImmediately, with the running action's other saves
Logout and disconnectAt once; the next login waits for anything still owed
restart whip_coreEvery owed write is sent as it stops
txAdmin restart or shutdownOn txAdmin's warning, most important first. Set its Shutdown Notice Delay to 15 seconds

A failed write isn't a failed action. The change stands and WHIP retries forever; after five failures it shows as stuck in /whipsaves, and that character can't load until it lands. If the database goes away, items lock until everything owed is written (BACK TO NORMAL in the console).

Health and armour aren't proof. They're what the player's game last reported, as on QBCore and ESX; only a report of 0 health is checked. To sell armour, give it with SetStat after payment and keep your own record. Hunger, thirst and your stats are the server's alone.

Logging out and leaving

Logout (back to the character screen) and disconnect both save the character and any stash or boot they had open, close their panels (yours gets onClose if they were its last viewer), clock them off, end any escort, and fire whip_core:player:logout with why = 'logout' or 'disconnect'.

New characters

A new character starts with full needs, the other stats at their starting values, and Config.StartingBalance ($1000) in the bank, and loads into the appearance creator. Only that first load has e.newCharacter (and e.player.isNewCharacter) set, even if the creator reopens later: the hook for a starter car.

A new character isn't a new player. Deleting one frees a slot for another, so a sellable gift can be farmed. Tie it to e.player.userId, or make it something that can't leave the character.

Deleting a character

Only from the character screen. Nothing the character held is thrown away:

WhatAfter the delete
Homes they ownedFor sale again with every key gone; furniture and stored items stay
Keys they heldRemoved
JobsLeft. A business they owned runs on unowned; reassign it in /whip → Economy → Jobs
Stashes locked to themContents stay; owner and lock are cleared
Cars and bank accountsUnchanged; an admin can reassign them

Clean up your own per-character data on whip_core:character:deleted, but any server resource can fire it, so first check if not exports.whip_core:IsCharacterDeleted(e.charId) then return end.

Events

Server eventWhenPayload
whip_core:player:loadedCharacter loaded and ready (same table on the client){ source, charId, name, newCharacter, player }
whip_core:player:logoutLogout or disconnect, after the save{ source, charId, player, why }
whip_core:character:createdNew character created{ source, charId }
whip_core:character:deletedCharacter deleted{ source, charId }
whip_core:character:renamedAn admin renamed a character (source nil if offline){ charId, source, firstName, lastName, name, oldName, by }

The renamed player's game gets whip_core:player:renamed with { charId, firstName, lastName, name }.

Player

Server exports for finding, reading and acting on players. Each takes a source and finds the player itself; for when players load and leave, see Character Lifecycle.

The player sheet

GetPlayer and the other lookups return a plain copy of the sheet, with no methods; change the player through exports.

local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)   -- nil until the character is fully loaded
if not player then return end

-- source (server id), session (this load, for IsSessionCurrent), userId (account), charId
-- firstName, lastName, fullName ("First Last"), dateOfBirth ("YYYY-MM-DD"), gender
-- cash (on hand), position ({ x, y, z, w }), health (0-200, 200 full), armour, isDead
-- metadata (not on the sheet a SecureEvent handler gets)

The client gets the same sheet, so identifiers stay off it (GetPlayerIdentifiers). Pockets and stats aren't on it either: use GetInventory and GetStats.

Finding players

IsReady()SERVER

Whether whip_core has finished starting. Whip.register doesn't need it (Your First Resource, step 3).

Returns: boolean
GetPlayer(who)SERVER

A copy of the whole sheet, appearance included, or nil until the character has loaded. Online players only. For one number, GetCharId is cheaper.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id, { charId = }, { userId = } (the account), or { identifier = 'license:…' } (license, steam, discord or fivem)
Returns: table|nil
local owner = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer({ charId = v.owner.charId })   -- nil when they are offline
GetCharId(source) · IsPlayerLoaded(source) · IsPlayerDead(source)SERVER

Their charId, whether a character is loaded, and whether they're down. They copy nothing: use them on hot paths.

Returns: integer|nil · boolean · boolean
IsSessionCurrent(source, session)SERVER

Whether the sheet's session (new each load) is still current. After a long wait, check it before giving or taking: a player who switched character mid-wait would be charged on one and paid on the other. (Logout waits up to two seconds for running handlers.)

Returns: boolean
Wait(4000)   -- after ChargePlayer
if not exports.whip_core:IsSessionCurrent(source, player.session) then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)
    return false, 'You left before the sale went through'
end
GetPlayers(opts?)SERVER

Every loaded player's sheet, keyed by server id. { light = true } returns light sheets (source, session, userId, charId, names, date of birth, gender, isDead): much cheaper.

Returns: table<number, table>
GetPlayerIdentifiers(source)SERVER

The platform identifiers the sheet leaves out.

ParamTypeDescription

Returns: { discord, fivem, license, steam }, or nil
GetPlayersInRange(coords, range?)SERVER

Players within network range of a point. Send news about a place to these, not to -1.

ParamTypeDescription

rangenumber?Metres; default Config.NetworkRange (424)
Returns: number[] server ids; empty for bad input
GetPlayerCoords(source)SERVER

The ped's position and heading now (the saved position until it spawns).

Returns: vector4|nil
IsCharacterDeleted(charId)SERVER

Whether a character is deleted or never existed. Ask before removing data on whip_core:character:deleted, which any server resource can fire.

Returns: true, 'deleted' or true, 'no such character'; false for a live one, or false, why when it can't tell

Messages, blips and props

A blip for 'everyone', { people = { serverId | { charId = n } } } or { job = 'police', onDuty = true }. The same id updates it; it goes when your resource stops or your tag is released. SetPlayerWaypoint sets one player's GPS waypoint.

Scenery each player's own game makes as they come near: crates, barriers, cash on a table. Not networked, frozen where placed, and can't be picked up. The same id replaces the set; it goes when your resource stops or your tag is released.

specTypeDescription
propstableUp to Config.PropSetMaxProps (256) of { model, coords, rot?, heading?, interior?, light?, collision?, weapon?, attach?, attachOffset?, attachRot?, drawDistance? }. rot: vector3(tiltForward, tiltSideways, heading), rotation order 2. collision = false: walk through. interior = true waits for an MLO and files it in its room; light = true lets a lamp light it. drawDistance (m, up to 500): each game makes and draws it that far out instead of 150 m, past its model's own draw distance (a speaker heard from afar). Costs a little drawing, nothing on the network
props[n].weaponstring?A firearm's world model ('WEAPON_RPG', or from Whip.weapons)
props[n].attachtable?Rides on { net = netId }, { set = id, index = n } or { index = n }, offset by attachOffset (m) and attachRot (°). Back in place when the parent goes
