Returns: true, or false, reason. A model a game lacks is skipped there

Metadata

GetPlayerMetadata(who, key?)SERVER

One metadata key, or the whole table. who is a person: a character who isn't playing is read from the database.

Returns: any; nil for nobody
SetPlayerMetadata(who, key, value)SERVER

Writes one key, saved with the character. who is a person: a character who isn't playing has their row written. Prefix yours ('myjob_licences'): the table is shared. WHIP's keys are refused: appearance, outfits, creatorPending, walk, mood, whipFlags, moneyHeldOwed, pourRefundOwed, lastSeat.

Returns: true, or false, reason: a WHIP key, no such person, unsaveable (a function, NaN), or a character logging in right now (try again)
Metadata isn't secret. The player's game gets every value: keep codes and cheat flags server-side.

Flags

Named facts about a character that outlive a restart ("met the fence", "jobs done: 3"), also used by Director scenarios. Kept in metadata: cheap, and visible to the player's game.

SetPlayerFlag(who, name, value) · GetPlayerFlag(who, name) · GetPlayerFlags(who)SERVER

Set, read or list an online character's flags. Each change fires whip_core:flag:changed { source, charId, name, value, was }.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|{ charId }A server id or an online character
namestringA letter, then letters, digits, _ . - :; at most 64. _ names are WHIP's
valuetrue|number|string|nilText up to 100 characters; nil or false clears. 256 flags per character at most
Returns: Set: true, or false, reason. Get: the value or nil. GetPlayerFlags: { [name] = value }, or nil when offline
local jobs = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerFlag(source, 'jobs_done') or 0
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerFlag(source, 'jobs_done', jobs + 1)

Saving and removing

SavePlayer(source)SERVER

Writes the character now, rarely needed (Save system): before your own write that follows an inventory change, or before something outside WHIP reads the rows.

Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
KickPlayer(source, reason)SERVER

Saves the character and drops the player with the reason.

Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
LogoutPlayer(source)SERVER

Saves, tears down the character's server state, and returns them to character select. Unless you're building your own character select, you want KickPlayer.

Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: false, 'Already leaving' while logging out or disconnecting

Appearance

SanitizeAppearance(appearance)SERVER

Runs an appearance through the character creator's validator, clamping every index. Optional tattoos ({ { collection, overlay }, … }, at most 40) and hairFade (one { collection, overlay }) are kept only if shared/tattoo_list.lua or shared/hair_fades.lua lists them for that body (once each, in the list's spelling); others are dropped, never refused.

ParamTypeDescription
appearancetableAppearance data to validate
Returns: boolean ok, table|string result: the cleaned appearance, or why it was refused
OpenCharacterEditor(who)SERVER

Opens a player's character editor on their own character, as /charedit does: Save keeps the new look and Cancel puts the old one back. It's refused for someone who isn't online, is still making their character or is down, and their game also refuses it while the editor is already open. A surgeon calls it once the player has paid; a store uses EditAppearance.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id, or { charId = n } for a character who is online
Returns: true, or false, why
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:OpenCharacterEditor(source)
if not ok then exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, why, 'error') end

A store (clothes, a barber, tattoos) opens the editor with EditAppearance on the player's game: only its tabs, the price of what changed on Save. Its server counts the changes with GetAppearanceChanges, charges, and keeps the look with SetPlayerAppearance. The tabs are the editor's category ids (heritage features eyes hair eyebrows beard makeup skin chestHair, mask tops undershirt arms legs shoes accessory armor decal bag, hat glasses ear watch bracelet, tatHead tatTorso tatLeftArm tatRightArm tatLeftLeg tatRightLeg, outfits) or their groups (face apparel props tattoos outfits). Any tattoo tab lets every tattoo change. Saved outfits only put clothes on, so offer outfits with apparel and props.

EditAppearance(opts)CLIENT

Opens the character editor on this character's own look, as a store. Save shows the price of what changed and calls onSave(look), which charges and keeps it (on the server) and returns true, or false, why: the reason is shown on Save and the editor stays open. Cancel puts the old look back. Refused while dead, in a vehicle or holding a weapon. Waits for the fade.

FieldTypeDescription
onlytable?The tabs offered: category ids or groups. Left out, all of them
pricestable?Dollars each, by category id, then group, then default: { apparel = 50, hat = 20 }. tattoos is per tattoo put on
methodstable?{ 'cash', 'bank' }: Save first opens a checkout, as whip_autos' basket: the total and a tile for each way to pay. One: no checkout, that way. Left out, Save pays your own way
wallettable?{ cash = n, bank = n }: shown on the tiles; one that can't cover the total is greyed out. Read it on your server (GetPlayerCash, GetBalance)
title / substring?The editor's heading
onSavefunction(look, method)Required. May wait. method is the tile chosen, or nil. Returns true, or false, why (60 characters)
onClosefunction(saved)?The editor shut: saved, or not (Cancel, a death, a logout)
Returns: true, or false, why
exports.whip_core:EditAppearance({
    only = { 'hair', 'beard', 'eyebrows' }, prices = { hair = 40, default = 15 }, title = 'Herr Kutz',
    methods = { 'cash', 'bank' }, wallet = exports.whip_core:Callback('mybarber:wallet'),
    onSave = function(look, method) return exports.whip_core:Callback('mybarber:buy', look, method) end,
})
GetAppearanceChanges(who, look, only?)SERVER

What changed between a playing character's saved look and look, counted as the editor prices it: one per category id changed (makeup counts each of its three overlays), and tattoos per tattoo put on. Taking off an accessory or a tattoo counts nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id, or { charId = n }
looktableThe look from the editor
onlytable?Count only these category ids or groups
Returns: { [id] = count, tattoos? }, or false, why
SetPlayerAppearance(who, look, opts?)SERVER

Keeps a look for a playing character, checked as the editor's Save is, and sends it to their game. opts.only takes only those tabs' parts from look and keeps the rest of their saved look, so a barber can't change a face.

Returns: true, look (as kept), or false, why
SecureCallback('mybarber:buy', { params = { { 'look', 'any' }, { 'method', 'enum', { 'cash', 'bank' }, 'cash' } } },
    function(source, player, look, method)
    local only = { 'hair', 'beard', 'eyebrows' }
    local changes, why = exports.whip_core:GetAppearanceChanges(source, look, only)
    if not changes then return false, why end
    local total = 0
    for id, n in pairs(changes) do total = total + (id == 'hair' and 40 or 15) * n end
    local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, total, { method = method, reason = 'Haircut' })
    if not receipt then return false, err end
    local ok, kept = exports.whip_core:SetPlayerAppearance(source, look, { only = only })
    if not ok then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) return false, kept end
    return true
end)

Client exports about the local player: their sheet, stats and effects, body state, emotes and voice. For the server side, see Player.

Stats and effects

Stats are read-only on the client: change them on the server with SetStat and AddStat.

One stat from the local cache: any stat registered with RegisterStat.

ParamTypeDescription

A copy of every stat the client knows.

Returns: { [name] = number }

Runs a function whenever a stat changes, instead of polling. The server has the same export, for every player.

    if new <= 20 and (old or 100) > 20 then exports.whip_core:Notify('You are starving.', 'error') end

Stats & Effects

Stats are a character's numbers: health, armour, hunger, thirst, oxygen, and any you register, such as stress or reputation. Effects are timed changes on top of them: a poison, a heal over time, a damage buff. WHIP saves and syncs them, so you write no table, save code or HUD.

Built-in stats

Every stat lives on the server and the player's game follows it, except combat damage: the hurt player's game sees the hit first and reports it, so a shot lands without waiting.

StatTypeRangeDecayThreshold
healthvital0–200——
armourvital0–100——
hungerneed0–100empty in Config.HungerMinutes (120)≤10 → health -1
thirstneed0–100empty in Config.ThirstMinutes (90)≤10 → health -1
oxygencustom0–100drains under water, refills above0 → drowns

Vital stats are synced to the GTA ped. Needs decay on the server, and their thresholds can damage other stats. Custom stats are yours (stress, tiredness).

Hunger and thirst are on by default: 100 is full, 0 is starving, and at 10 or below each costs 1 health per decay tick. Config.Hunger / Config.Thirst turn one off (also in /whip → Settings → Config → Hunger, thirst and breath). One that's off has no gauge, doesn't drain or save, and reads 100, so food and drink still work. Config.StatOrder sets the gauges' order.

Registering a stat

Declare RegisterStat from your server code, in Whip.register (why). Decay, thresholds, saving and client sync come with it. A hud block draws a ring on every player's HUD (HUD Framework); leave it out for a server-only stat such as reputation.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterStat('stress', {
        type = 'custom',
        default = 0, min = 0, max = 100,
        persist = true,
        decay = -0.5,          -- eases off half a point...
        decayInterval = 15,    -- ...every 15 seconds
        hud = { icon = 'M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12...', color = '#e879f9', order = 5 },
    })
end)

Reading and changing stats

Change stats on the server; the player's game follows. The client can only read.

-- server
local hunger = exports.whip_core:GetStat(source, 'hunger')
exports.whip_core:SetStat(source, 'hunger', 100)              -- full
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25, 'quest reward')  -- restore 25
local all = exports.whip_core:GetStats(source)             -- { health = 200, hunger = 74, ... }

-- client
local hunger = exports.whip_core:GetStat('hunger')

The setters return true, or false and a reason: an unregistered name is refused. The optional last reason shows in the debug change log and is passed to OnStatChanged.

A consumable item

The item's use handler calls AddStat. Return its refusal and the player keeps the item. whip_core's own food item (server/items/food.lua) works this way.

-- after RegisterItem('mycafe_sandwich', { type = 'consumable', usable = true, ... })
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterUseHandler('mycafe_sandwich', function(source, player, slotData)
        local ok, why = exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'hunger', 25, 'item:sandwich')
        if not ok then return false, why end   -- refused: they keep it
        return true                            -- consume one
    end)
end)

Listening for changes

OnStatChanged works on both sides and hears every change: decay, items, effects, combat damage and other resources' writes. On the server the callback gets the player's source first and the reason last. Declare it in Whip.register: running it again replaces it, and it goes when your resource stops.

-- server: every player
exports.whip_core:OnStatChanged('hunger', function(source, value, old, reason)
    if value <= 0 then --[[ starving ]] end
end)

-- client: the local player. old is nil for the first value after login.
exports.whip_core:OnStatChanged('reputation', function(value, old)
    if old and value >= 100 and old < 100 then
        exports.whip_core:Notify('Reputation: Trusted! New routes unlocked.', 'success')
    end
end)

Listen to '*' for every stat; the callback then gets the stat's name before the value. Options take one table instead of arguments (table = true) and a first call with the current value (now = true).

Effects

An effect runs your callbacks on a timer and removes itself when its duration runs out. It moves no stat by itself: the heal below is its onTick calling AddStat. Use one when a change must expire and clean up on its own; for a one-off change, call AddStat.

-- A bandage: 5 health every second for 10 seconds
exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'healing', {
    duration = 10,      -- seconds; nil = until RemoveEffect
    magnitude = 5,      -- any number your callbacks read
    tickRate = 1,       -- seconds between onTick calls
    onTick = function(src, player, effect)
        exports.whip_core:AddStat(src, 'health', effect.magnitude)
    end,
    onRemove = function(src)
        exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Healed!', 'success')
    end,
})

Any resource can end one early with RemoveEffect(source, 'healing'). Applying an active name replaces it: nothing stacks. Every field is on the ApplyEffect card.

Damage modifiers

Give an effect damageModifier (weapons) or meleeModifier to scale the damage the player takes: 0.5 takes half, 2.0 double. No other export or client code is needed. whip_core's own damage_reducer item (server/items/damage_reducer.lua) is a complete example.

-- In an item's use handler: half weapon damage for 20 seconds
return exports.whip_core:ApplyEffect(source, 'mydoc_iron_tonic', {
    duration = 20,
    damageModifier = 0.5,
    onRemove = function(src) exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(src, 'Damage reduction wore off', 'warning') end,
})
  • Effects under different names multiply. Two of 0.5 give 0.25; 0.5 and 2.0 cancel out. The result is kept between 0.05 and 4.0 (Config.Sentinel.damageModifierClamp), and GetDamageModifier returns that kept value.
  • The attacker's game applies them when it aims at or punches the player, so a hit lands right the first time. Shots fired from the hip without aiming do full damage.

Good to know

  • Spawn guard. For 10 seconds after a respawn or revive, low hunger and thirst cost no health and effects don't tick. Decay still runs.
  • Player Stats Debug (/w, the debug panel) shows live values, effects, decay rates, a change log with each hit's cause, and the ped's health and armour.
Hit causes are reported, not proven. The debug log's combat (reported): Carbine Rifle by John Smith (#3) comes from the hurt player's own game, so a modified game can make it say anything: never decide anything from it. For who killed a player, use killer on the server's whip_core:player:died (Death & Revive).

Stats API

Server exports for stats and effects. New to stats? Read Stats & Effects first. The client's read-only GetStat, GetStats, HasEffect, GetEffects and OnStatChanged are on Player & Status (Client).

Stats

RegisterStat(name, config)SERVER

Registers the stat name; a hud block puts a ring on every player's HUD as the call returns. The config is copied. Declare it in Whip.register: it's dropped when your resource stops, though values stay.

FieldTypeDescription
typestring?'need' or 'custom' (default). Vitals are WHIP's own; anything else is refused
defaultnumber?What a character starts on (default 0)
min / maxnumber?The range writes are clamped to (default 0–100)
persistboolean?Save with the character (default true). false: neither saved nor loaded, so it starts from default each login
decaynumber?Points added every decayInterval; negative drains. Omitted or 0: none
decayIntervalnumber?Seconds between decay ticks (default 10)
thresholdstable?Array of { stat, delta, value, below }: while past value (below = true for ≤, else ≥), add delta to stat each decay tick. Only on stats that decay
hudtable?{ color, icon, iconCritical, order, heartbeat, hideWhenEmpty, noCritical, showAboveZero, showBelowFull, glide }: see HUD Framework
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
Names are owned (the registration rule). health, armour, oxygen and another resource's stats are refused with the reason. Registering your own again is fine: the same definition changes nothing, a changed one replaces it.
GetStat(source, name) / GetStats(source)SERVER

One stat, or a copy of all, from the server's cache. Reported combat damage lands here too, so health is current without reading the ped.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringStat name (GetStat only)
Returns: number|nil / table. With no character loaded, GetStat returns nil and GetStats {}, 'Player not loaded'
SetStat(source, name, value, reason?)SERVER

Sets a stat, clamped to its range. The client gets it at once, and a persisting stat is queued for the next save. An unregistered name, such as a typo, is refused.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringA registered stat
valuenumberThe new value
reasonstring?What caused it ('quest reward'), for the debug change log and OnStatChanged. Default 'by <your resource>'
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: 'Player not loaded', 'no stat named "x" (RegisterStat it first)', 'value must be a number'
AddStat(source, name, delta, reason?)SERVER

Adds delta to the current value (or the default when unset) and sets it as SetStat does.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringA registered stat
deltanumberAmount to add; negative subtracts
reasonstring?As for SetStat ('item:food')
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: as SetStat, or 'amount must be a number'
OnStatChanged(name, callback, id?, opts?)SERVER

Calls you when any player's stat changes, by any path. Declare it in Whip.register: it's keyed by your resource and id, so running it again replaces it, and it goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringA stat name, or '*' for every stat
callbackfunction(source, value, old, reason), or (source, name, value, old, reason) for '*'. reason: 'decay', 'item:food', 'combat (reported): Pistol', 'by my_resource'
idany?Only to hold two listeners on one stat (the options may go here instead)
optstable?table = true: one table { source, key, value, old, reason }. now = true: also called straight away for every loaded player with the stat (old = nil, reason = 'now')
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
Clamping can't loop. A listener that sets its own stat isn't called again for that change; the value still lands.

Effects

ApplyEffect(source, name, config)SERVER

Applies a timed effect to a player. It's your resource's: removed without onRemove when your resource stops (a resource field is ignored). Ticks pause while dead and during the spawn guard.

FieldTypeDescription
durationnumber?Seconds until removed. nil: until RemoveEffect
magnitudenumber?Any value your callbacks read (default 1)
tickRatenumber?Seconds between onTick calls (default 1)
onTick / onApply / onRemovefunction?(source, player, effect). onRemove also runs on logout or disconnect (effect.reason 'logout' / 'disconnect')
damageModifier / meleeModifiernumber?Incoming damage multiplier: 0.5 takes half
replaceSilentlyboolean?On replacing an active effect of this name, skip its onRemove (default: it runs)
sheet'light'?Callbacks get the light player sheet (who, whether dead), not the full one, which reads the ped, pockets and two stats each tick
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: 'duration must be a positive number of seconds, or nil', 'Player not loaded'...
Nothing stacks. A second apply under the same name replaces the effect entirely. To stack, read GetEffects and apply the sum. stackable is refused.
RemoveEffect(source, name)SERVER

Removes an effect early: runs its onRemove, recalculates the damage modifiers if it carried one and tells the client. Any resource may remove any effect.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringThe name it was applied under
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: 'no effect named "x" on this player'
HasEffect(source, name) / GetEffects(source)SERVER

Whether an effect is active, and every active one keyed by name: duration, remaining, magnitude, tickRate, damageModifier, meleeModifier, resource. No callbacks.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
namestringEffect name (HasEffect only)
Returns: boolean / table: { [name] = effect }, empty when none
GetDamageModifier(source) / GetMeleeModifier(source)SERVER

The combined, clamped incoming weapon (or melee) multiplier from every active effect, for your own damage math.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
Returns: number: 1.0 with no modifier
-- A trap that respects armour buffs
exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'health', -25 * exports.whip_core:GetDamageModifier(source))

HUD Framework

Every status ring on the HUD is drawn from a stat's hud config. Give your stat a hud block when you register it and every player gets the ring, with no HTML, CSS or JS to write.

Adding a ring

Add a hud block to RegisterStat, such as hud = { icon = '...', color = '#e879f9', order = 5 }. The ring appears on every player's HUD at once, follows the stat, and comes off when your resource stops.

Below 20% the arc and icon turn red, unless noCritical is set. At 0% the ring ghosts out: a faded track and a dim icon.

Ring fields

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
iconstringYesAn SVG path's d, 24x24 viewBox, as in Material Design Icons, Lucide and Heroicons
colorstringYesHex colour of the arc; glow and haze shades are made from it
ordernumberNoPosition in the bar, lower further left (default 99), after the stats the server has placed in Config.StatOrder. Once your stat is placed on the Hunger, thirst and breath settings page, that wins
heartbeatbooleanNoHeartbeat animation on the icon when critical (below 20%), as health has
iconCriticalstringNoAlternate SVG paths, pipe-delimited, shown when critical: the first is the fill, the rest stroke lines. Armour's crack uses it
hideWhenEmptybooleanNoFade to 25% opacity at 0% instead of an empty ring, as armour does
noCriticalbooleanNoNo red warning below 20%, for stats where low isn't urgent (drunk, stress)
showAboveZerobooleanNoHidden at 0%; slides in above it. For situational stats (drunk)
showBelowFullbooleanNoHidden while full; slides in below full. For a reserve that is usually full, like oxygen
glidebooleanNoGlides to each new reading over the time between readings, so a stat moved once a tick drains smoothly (oxygen). Off for one that should snap to a hit (health)
showWhenPresentbooleanNoVehicle stats only: drawn whenever the vehicle carries the stat, whatever its value. For fittings that rest above zero, such as a turbo idling at 1
showAboveZero and showWhenPresent agree only when the default is zero. A car without the stat reads as its default, so showAboveZero on a stat that rests at 1 draws a gauge on every car on the server. Use showAboveZero for a quantity that runs out, showWhenPresent for a part that is fitted or not.

Built-in rings

Health is green (#34d399) with a heartbeat below 20%. Armour is purple (#818cf8), shows a cracked shield below 20% and fades out at 0% (hideWhenEmpty). Hunger (orange, #fb923c) and thirst (blue, #38bdf8) turn red below 20%.

Example: a drunk effect

A beer that makes the player drunk: a stat, a ring and an item. Drinking takes 5 seconds, adds 20 drunk and changes their walk; the ring shows only above 0 and never turns red. Put both files beside an fxmanifest.lua that loads @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua as a shared script.

-- server.lua
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterStat('drunk', {
        default = 0, min = 0, max = 100,
        persist = false,                -- sober again after a restart
        decay = -1, decayInterval = 2,  -- sobers up 1 point every 2 seconds
        hud = {
            icon = 'M10 1h4v1.5h-1v3h.5c1.5 0 2.5 1.5 2.5 3V21a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H9a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V8.5c0-1.5 1-3 2.5-3h.5v-3H10V1z',
            color = '#b8860b',          -- beer brown
            order = 5,
            noCritical = true,          -- low drunk isn't urgent: no red warning
            showAboveZero = true,       -- hidden when sober, slides in above 0
        },
    })

    Whip.core:RegisterItem('alcohol', { name = 'Beer', weight = 0.5, type = 'consumable', usable = true })

    -- A timed use (a table, not a function): WHIP runs the bar and takes the beer, then onComplete
    Whip.core:RegisterUseHandler('alcohol', {
        label = 'Drinking...',
        duration = 5000,
        anim = { dict = 'mp_player_intdrink', clip = 'loop_bottle', flag = 49 },  -- upper body
        prop = { model = 'prop_amb_beer_bottle', bone = 18905 },                 -- left hand
        disable = { move = false },   -- they can walk while they drink
        reason = 'drunk',             -- for the item log
        onComplete = function(source)   -- false, why gives the beer back
            return exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'drunk', 20, 'item:alcohol')
        end,
    })
end)
-- client.lua: the walk, one clipset per tier. No drinking code: the bar is whip_core's.
local walk
local function setWalk(value)
    value = value or 0
    local clipset = value >= 60 and 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@VERYDRUNK'
        or value >= 40 and 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@MODERATEDRUNK'
        or value >= 20 and 'MOVE_M@DRUNK@SLIGHTLYDRUNK' or nil
    if clipset ~= walk then
        exports.whip_core:SetWalkOverride(clipset)   -- on top of their own /walk; nil gives it back
        walk = clipset
    end
end

-- a listener is a registration; now = true calls it at once
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:OnStatChanged('drunk', setWalk, nil, { now = true })
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:player:logout', function() setWalk(0) end)   -- logging out ends the night

Death & Revive

When a player dies, WHIP puts them in the death state and shows the death screen until they respawn at a hospital or are revived. Your resource can hold a respawn while a medic is on the way, draw its own death screen, and react to deaths and revives.

The death state

WHIP does this by itself and fires whip_core:player:died. While dead:

  • They lie where they fell and take no more damage.
  • Every control is off except the camera (V and looking around), chat (T), push-to-talk (N) and E to respawn.
  • Other players can still escort (drag) them.
  • Hunger and thirst stop draining, low ones cost no health, and effects stop ticking.
  • Their health stat reads 100 (GTA's dead value) and their armour 0.
  • Leaving doesn't end it: they're still dead when they come back.

Dead in a vehicle. They stay slumped in the seat and the car can still be driven. Taken out of a seat, the body falls and lies as on the ground; put into one, it's dead there. A revive in a seat keeps them in it; a respawn takes them out.

Respawning and reviving

The death screen counts down Config.RespawnTime (10 seconds, also in /whip → Settings → Config), then shows Hold E to respawn (A on a controller). Holding it 1.5 seconds respawns them at a random hospital from Config.RespawnLocations (vector4s), with damage modifiers back to normal; the server refuses an earlier respawn.

H (Y on a controller) hides and shows the screen; respawning needs it showing. Themes recolour it with --ui-death-curtain.

Admins revive with /whip_revive <charId> (console, or in game with whip.devtools), or themselves with /whip_reviveme (in game, whip.devtools). No item is needed. Every revive and respawn sets health to 200 and armour to 0 and starts the 10-second spawn guard, when low hunger and thirst cost no health.

Holding a respawn

HoldRespawn(source, key, label?) · ReleaseRespawn(source, key?) · GetRespawnHold(source)SERVER

Keeps a dead player from respawning while your resource comes for them, such as an EMS call with a medic on the way. The server refuses a respawn until every hold goes: released, a revive, a logout, or the holding resource stopping. GetRespawnHold returns the words their screen shows, or nil.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe dead player's server ID
keystringNames your hold; the same key again changes its words
labelstring?Shown instead of "Hold E to respawn", up to 80 letters (default "Help is on the way")
Returns: HoldRespawn: true, or false, 'no such player' | 'they are not dead'. ReleaseRespawn: true when a hold went
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HoldRespawn(patient, 'call', 'A medic is on the way')
-- The call is dropped: they can respawn once the usual wait is over
exports.whip_core:ReleaseRespawn(patient, 'call')

Checking death state

-- client: the local player
if exports.whip_core:IsPlayerDead() then end

-- server
local player = exports.whip_core:GetPlayer(source)
if player and player.isDead then end

-- any client, any player: the statebag
local isDead = Player(serverId).state.whipDead

Events

EventSidePayload
whip_core:player:diedServer{ source, charId, killer, reported }: killer is the server id the server saw do it (a car's driver counts), or nil; reported is the victim's own game's description, for display only
whip_core:player:revivedServer{ source, charId, how, reason }: how is 'revived' or 'respawned'
whip_core:player:diedClient{ reconnected, respawnRefused }
whip_core:player:revivedClient{ how }
whip_core:death:screenChangedClientWhat the death screen shows: { state = 'count', left, total }, { state = 'ready', progress, key }, { state = 'held', label }, { state = 'off' } or { hidden }

For a death screen of your own, set Config.DeathScreen = false and draw from whip_core:death:screenChanged; WHIP still counts down and reads E. The console and Stats change log print what killed a player, marked "reported": [whip_core] John [3] has died — reported: Carbine Rifle by Jane (#5) (charId: 12). A player who dies of hunger or thirst reads Starvation or Dehydration; health a script or effect takes reads as its reason.

Never pay out on a server event alone. Any server resource can fire whip_core:player:died and whip_core:player:revived.

Escorting

A player can grab another player, alive or dead, and move them around. Your resource reads escort state, for example to block an action while someone is being dragged.

Controls

Left Arrow escorts a player who isn't in a vehicle or already escorted; Right Arrow releases them. The escorted player is attached beside the holder, and only their movement is off: they can still look around, open their inventory and chat.

The escort breaks when either player ragdolls (hit by a car, a fall) or disconnects, when the holder dies, or when they're more than 10 m apart.

Reading escort state

The controls use WHIP's own network messages and aren't an API. Read state with the client exports below, or for any player with the statebags:

local isEscorted = Player(serverId).state.whipEscorted     -- boolean
local escortedBy = Player(serverId).state.whipEscortedBy   -- server id of the holder
IsEscorting()CLIENT

Whether the local player is escorting someone.

Returns: boolean
IsBeingEscorted()CLIENT

Whether the local player is being escorted. Check it before letting them do anything being dragged along should prevent.

Returns: boolean
GetEscortTarget()CLIENT

Who the local player is escorting.

Returns: number|nil: the escorted player's server ID, or nil

Bank Accounts

Every character has a personal bank account and can hold savings, shared and business accounts. The exports are on Bank API, and running banks in game on Banks.

Accounts and roles

An account's type is 'personal', 'savings', 'business' or 'shared'. A new character gets a personal account with Config.StartingBalance ($1000) and isDefault = 1. Account numbers are WB- and six random digits.

view (1) < deposit (2) < withdraw (3) < manager (4) < owner (5)

Each role includes those before it. A granter can only give roles below their own, and owner access can't be revoked.

Moving money

Who decidesExports
A playerTheir role: deposit to pay in, withdraw to take out or transferBankDeposit, BankWithdraw, BankTransfer, passing the player's source or { charId = n } (a bare number is a server id, never a charId). Bank money only: no cash moves
The systemYour resource: no permission checkBankSystemDeposit (wages, takings), BankSystemWithdraw (fines, fees), BankSystemTransfer (payroll), logged with your resource's name

Ask CanUseBankAccount to decide what to offer, such as only the accounts a person can pay from. To charge a player, use ChargePlayer; to pay one, PayPlayer.

-- A fine out of a player's default account
local account = exports.whip_core:GetDefaultBankAccount(source)
if account then
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:BankSystemWithdraw(account.accountId, 250, { reason = 'Speeding fine' })
end

Good to know

  • Whole amounts only. A fraction, zero, a string or NaN is refused with 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more', never rounded.
  • Refused outright: anything on a frozen account, and a transfer to the same account.
  • No money between a player's own characters. With Config.BlockOwnCharacterTransfers on (the default), "That is another character of the same player: money cannot pass between them": no transfers, payments, withdrawals or shared accounts. It covers every way in (BankTransfer, BankDeposit, BankWithdraw, ChargePlayer, GrantBankAccess, ATMs, the phone) except BankSystem* moves.
  • Every transaction fires whip_core:bank:balanceChanged.
  • Reads wait for the database. Read when the player asks (opening an app, pressing an ATM), not every frame or on a timer. To show a balance, use GetBalance, which reads memory after its first call, or follow whip_core:bank:balanceChanged.

Charging a Player

ChargePlayer takes a payment in cash or from the bank and returns a receipt. If what was paid for then fails, RefundPlayer gives the money back the way it came. WHIP's fuel pumps, shops, ATMs and whip_autos all charge this way.

Charging

local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 500, {
    method = 'auto',     -- 'cash' | 'bank' | 'auto': cash if they carry enough, else the bank
    reason = 'Car wash', -- on their bank statement and the activity log
})
if not receipt then
    return exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, err, 'error')   -- 'Not enough cash (have $20, need $500)'
end

if not washTheCar() then
    exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt)   -- all of it; RefundPlayer(receipt, 200) for part
end

Bank payments come from their default account unless you pass accountId; the player's own withdraw permission is checked, so a job account they can only view can't pay. currency charges another item as money: a black market taking gold bars refunds the very bars it took. The card lists every option.

An amount of 0 takes nothing and still returns a receipt, so a free item needs no special case.

Refunding

The receipt remembers how they paid, and RefundPlayer sends the money back the same way with no permission check. A refused bank refund comes back as cash; cash for a player who has left goes to their bank. A refund that can't be delivered returns false and is printed as CRITICAL.

Receipts are checked against WHIP's own record. Only the resource that charged may refund, only up to what's left of the payment, and only within 30 minutes. Editing the receipt table changes nothing: a forged one is refused.

Inside a SecureEvent

The payment is taken at once, so it can't be spent twice, but written in the same transaction as your next WHIP write: the car CreateOwnedVehicle makes, the data SetVehicleData sets, the parts SetVehicleAppearance fits, or the end of your handler. A crash or whip_core restart between paying and delivering keeps neither.

If that write fails, nothing was taken, and your RefundPlayer lets the payment go. Outside a SecureEvent, in a thread of yours, the payment is written at once.

Metered services

For fuel, a taxi fare or anything measured as it runs, don't charge and refund the change: the change is lost if your resource or the server stops in between. Use Money holds instead.

Paying a player

PayPlayer goes the other way: a wage, a reward, a sale. Pass a server id, or { charId = n } for a character who may be offline (paid into the bank). Cash that doesn't fit their pockets lands at their feet.

exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(source, 250, { reason = 'Courier job' })
exports.whip_core:PayPlayer({ charId = 12 }, 250, { method = 'bank', reason = 'Wages' })

Bank API

Server exports for charging and paying players, money holds and bank accounts. Read Charging a Player for the common path and Bank Accounts for roles and rules.

Charging and paying

ChargePlayer(source, amount, opts?)SERVER

Takes a payment in cash or from the bank and returns a receipt RefundPlayer can undo. See Charging a Player.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server ID
amountnumberA whole number, 0 or more (0 takes nothing and still returns a receipt)
opts.methodstring?'cash', 'bank' or 'auto' (default: cash if they carry enough, else the bank)
opts.accountIdnumber?Bank: which account (default their default one); their withdraw permission is checked
opts.currencystring?Cash: the item that counts as money (default 'cash'). A refund returns the very items taken, with what they carry (a paid gun keeps its serial)
opts.reasonstring?On the statement and the activity log (default 'Payment')
Returns: receipt|false, string|nil: receipt { id, amount, method, accountId, currency, refunded }; the error is a sentence the player can read
RefundPlayer(receipt, amount?)SERVER

Gives back a payment ChargePlayer took, the way it came, with no permission check (see Refunding). Only the resource that charged may refund, up to what's left, within 30 minutes.

ParamTypeDescription
receipttable|numberThe receipt, or its id
amountnumber?How much (default: everything not yet refunded)
Returns: bool, string|nil: false when it couldn't be delivered (also printed as CRITICAL)
PayPlayer(who, amount, opts?)SERVER

Pays a player: a wage, a reward, a sale. Cash that doesn't fit their pockets lands at their feet, and every payment is on the activity log with your resource's name.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA server id, or { charId = n } for a character who may be offline
amountnumberA whole number, 0 or more (0 pays nothing)
opts.methodstring?'cash', 'bank' or 'auto' (default: cash while they're online, else their bank)
opts.accountIdnumber?Bank: which account (default their default one)
opts.currencystring?Cash: the item paid (default 'cash')
opts.reasonstring?On the statement and the activity log
Returns: { method, amount, currency?, placement?, accountId? } (placement: 'inventory' or 'ground'), or false, reason: as ChargePlayer returns its receipt

Money holds

For a metered service (fuel, a taxi fare), hold the most it could cost, report what's used as it runs, and settle: the rest goes back. whip_fuel's pumps work this way. Nothing is lost if your resource or the server stops first: the refund owed is noted on the character with the charge and paid at their next login. The payer leaving, or your resource or whip_core stopping, settles it for what was used. Cash change goes to their pockets (the bank if it doesn't fit). Only your resource can spend or settle its holds.

HoldMoney(source, amount, opts?)SERVER

Takes amount from the player now, cash or bank. opts = { method = 'cash' | 'bank', reason, vehicle? }: vehicle (a vehicleId) keeps that car's row unwritten until the settle, so fuel not yet paid for is never saved.

Returns: the hold's id, or false, why (not enough money, no bank account)
local holdId, why = exports.whip_core:HoldMoney(source, 100, { method = 'cash', reason = 'Car wash' })
if not holdId then return false, why end
-- each cycle: SpendMoneyHold(holdId, usedSoFar); at the end: SettleMoneyHold(holdId)
SpendMoneyHold(id, spent)SERVER

Reports how much of the hold is used so far (0 up to what was held): what a settle keeps if your resource or the server stops first.

Returns: true, or false, why when the hold is gone (the payer left) or isn't yours: stop the service then
SettleMoneyHold(id, spent?)SERVER

Ends the hold: spent (default: what SpendMoneyHold last said) is kept, the rest goes back, the note is cleared and a held vehicle's row is written, all together.

Returns: { spent, refunded, paidNow } (paidNow false: the change is paid at the next login), or false, why when already settled or not yours
GetMoneyHold(id)SERVER

One of your holds as it is now. Ask before giving more of the service.

Returns: { source, amount, spent, method }, or nil: it's over, or not yours

Reading accounts

GetBalance(who)SERVER

A balance from memory: only the first read of an account waits for the database, and every bank write keeps it true. A HUD, phone app or ATM prompt can ask as often as it shows it.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person for their main account, or { accountId = n }
Returns: integer, or false, why: no such person or account, no bank account, or it's closed
GetBankAccount(ref)SERVER

An account, by its ID or its number.

ParamTypeDescription
refnumber|tableA bank account ID, or { number = 'WB-XXXXXX' }
Returns: table|nil: { accountId, accountNumber, label, type, ownerCharId, jobId, balance, isDefault, frozen, createdAt }, as every account read; times are epoch seconds
GetDefaultBankAccount(who)SERVER

A person's default account: a database read every call. To show a balance, use GetBalance.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableServer id, or { charId = n }
Returns: table|nil
GetCharacterBankAccounts(charId)SERVER

Every account a character can use, each with their role on it. To offer accounts to pay from, keep withdraw, manager and owner: the others are refused at the till.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdnumberCharacter ID
Returns: table[]: accounts with a role field
GetJobBankAccounts(job)SERVER

A job's accounts. None yet means the job has no owner.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key ('police')
Returns: table: accounts; {}, 'No such job' for a job that doesn't exist
GetBankTransactions(accountId, limit?, offset?)SERVER

An account's history, newest first.

ParamTypeDescription
accountIdnumberBank account ID
limitnumber?Rows to return (default 50, at most 500)
offsetnumber?Rows to skip (default 0)
Returns: table: rows of { txId, fromAccountId, toAccountId, type, amount, fromBalance, toBalance, actorCharId, message, createdAt }; type is 'deposit', 'withdraw', 'transfer' or 'payment'. A row is money out when fromAccountId is this account
GetBankAccessList(accountId)SERVER

Who has access to an account, and their roles.

ParamTypeDescription
accountIdnumberBank account ID
Returns: table: array of { charId, role, grantedBy }

A player's moves

CanUseBankAccount(accountId, who, role)SERVER

Whether a person may act at role level on an account, by the bank's own rule: ask before offering accounts or menu options.

ParamTypeDescription

Returns: bool, string|nil: false, 'Needs withdraw access to this account', 'Account not found'

A player pays into an account. For the system paying in, use BankSystemDeposit.

No cash is taken. For a cash deposit, first take the notes with ChargePlayer(source, n, { method = 'cash' }), and refund that receipt if the deposit is refused. Otherwise a deposit makes money from nothing.

A player takes money out of an account. To charge for something, use ChargePlayer instead.

Your resource decides: no permission check, and the activity log records your resource's name.

Vehicle values

What your resource charges for vehicles. Banks values an owned car at this price, averaged across resources. Declare it in Whip.register; again replaces your list, and it goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription

Returns: true, or false, why

Inventory

Characters carry items in pockets, and everything they carry has weight. Your resource gives, takes and checks items with four calls; this page also covers weight, metadata and saving.

Pockets

PocketSlotsMax weightFor
player3080 kg, the strip includedThe main inventory. It takes anything, and items go here first
accessory510 kg of the 80The strip beside it. Each slot takes one kind of item

Sizes come from Config.ContainerSlots and Config.MaxWeight. Config.AccessoryStrip = false removes the strip (keys then go in the ignition by hand), and what a character had in it moves into player at login. Read the list with GetPockets() rather than typing it out.

Strip slotTakes
1 PhonePhones while whip_phone runs; it looks here for one first. Without whip_phone, anything
2 Moneycash or a wallet
3 to 5 KeyAny ignition key (RegisterIgnitionKey)

The server holds each slot to its rule on a drag, a StoreMove and an AddItem, and tells a player why ("Only Cash or Wallet can go there"). A reward too big for the main inventory only spills into a slot that takes it. What a slot held before its rule changed stays until it's moved. Reshape a slot with RegisterAccessorySlot.

A vehicle_key in the strip goes into the ignition by itself when its holder takes the driver's seat of the car it fits, and comes back when they leave the seat, so three Key slots carry three cars' keys. Keys in player never move by themselves.

More room is an item, not a pocket. A duffle bag holds 25 slots, and players find, drop, steal and lose it like anything else. See RegisterPanelItem.

The four calls

ExportDoes
AddItemPuts an item on the player, wherever it fits
RemoveItemTakes an item from wherever it is
HasItemDo they have at least this many, anywhere on them?
GetItemCountHow many they carry in total
if not exports.whip_core:HasItem(source, 'lockpick') then return false, 'You need a lockpick' end
exports.whip_core:RemoveItem(source, 'lockpick', 1, nil, { reason = 'snapped' })

To act on one slot, name it with an address and use the store calls. You rarely build one: a use handler and FindItem hand you the address of their item.

When an inventory is full

OperationMeansWhen it won't fit
GiveThe item enters the world: a reward, a purchase, a refund, an admin spawnDropped at the player's feet. Failing would destroy it
MoveThe item already exists: a pickup, a stash transfer, a drag, a tradeLeft where it is. A copy at their feet would duplicate it

AddItem is a give: it returns 'inventory' or 'ground', and both count as given.

Weight is nested

An item's weight is what it weighs empty. Its contents are added on top, at every level, with nothing for you to declare.

duffle_bag   1.5 kg (empty)
 └─ wallet   0.2 kg (empty)
     └─ 5,000 cash @ 0.0001 kg = 0.5 kg
The bag weighs 2.2 kg, and every container above it agrees.
  • Filling a bag makes its carrier heavier, and a tooltip's weight includes the contents.
  • Bags inside bags count 4 levels deep at most.
  • A read hook that throws falls back to the item's base weight rather than failing the move.
  • An item with no definition weighs 0 (see Panels).

Metadata

An item can carry any JSON metadata: a key's plate, a jerry can's fuel, a wallet's contents. It's saved with the item and travels with it everywhere.

exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'id_card', 1, { name = 'John Smith', number = 'A-10294' })

local found = exports.whip_core:FindItem(source, 'jerry_can')   -- { item, amount, metadata, addr }
if found then exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(found.addr, { fuel = 50 }) end   -- changes fuel only

For starting metadata on every new item of yours (a radio's frequency, a gun's serial), register a generator with RegisterItemDefaultMetadata.

Saving

Inventories save write-behind: a change is in memory at once and written within about a second (Config.FlushInterval). Only changed rows are written (none on the first save after a load), and both halves of a move share one transaction.

So a true from a change means "owed to disk", not "on disk": a hard crash can lose up to one flush interval. Data that can't afford that belongs on a store kind that writes through. See also Save System.

Durability is per store kind. Player inventories, containers and vehicle storage defer. Ground items and shop stock write through, and the bank writes immediately with whatever the running action has saved, so an ATM's cash and its bank write are one transaction. A move that touches any write-through store commits immediately.

Items

An item is a key and a definition: a name, a weight and whatever else it needs. Your resource registers its own items and gives them a use, right-click options, pictures and settings an admin can change.

Registering an item

whip_core's own items are in Config.Items. Register yours with RegisterItem; every field is under Item definition below.

-- server.lua (fxmanifest.lua: shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua')
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItem('myems_medkit', {
        name = 'Medical Kit', desc = 'Heals injuries', weight = 0.5, type = 'medical',
        stack = true, maxStack = 5, usable = true, cooldown = 10, prop = 'prop_ld_health_pack',
    })
end)

It works everywhere at once.

Item icons

Your item's picture lives in your resource:

  1. Add a WebP (preferred: every player downloads every icon) or PNG named after the key: html/img/items/myems_medkit.webp, or the item's image path. If both exist, WebP wins.
  2. Add files { 'html/img/items/*.webp', 'html/img/items/*.png' } (or just the one you use) to your fxmanifest.lua. Without it the inventory shows the "missing" picture.

A new picture shows after its resource restarts. whip_autos is a good one to copy.

Stacking

An item with stack = true and maxStack above 1 stacks in one slot. Adding tops up existing stacks first (lowest slot first), then fills empty slots; removing empties the highest slots first. Cash has maxStack = 999999 and weighs 0.0001 kg a note.

Using an item

When a player uses a usable item, the server checks it exists and is off cooldown, then calls your use handler. Its return decides the rest:

ReturnResult
true or nothingOne is used up (food, a bandage)
falseKept (a tool, a toggle). Still a use: the cooldown starts and whip_core:item:used fires
false, 'why'Refused: kept, no cooldown, no event, no use logged, and the player sees why. Use this for "not now"
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('myems_medkit', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetStat(source, 'health', 200, 'item:medkit')
    if not ok then return false, why end
    return true
end)

addr is the item's address, for SetItemMetadata and the store calls. For a use at the end of a progress bar (a drink, a car part), pass a table instead: see a use with a progress bar.

Right-click options

An item's defaultAction and contextOptions add options to its menu, under Use; Give, Place, Split and Destroy go below. Lowest order goes first, then options without one, as listed. Each action needs a handler from RegisterContextAction, named with your resource's prefix.

contextOptions = { { action = 'my_resource:inspect_serial', label = 'Inspect serial', order = 1 } },   -- the definition

exports.whip_core:RegisterContextAction('my_resource:inspect_serial', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    local serial = slotData.metadata and slotData.metadata.serial
    if not serial then return false, 'No serial' end   -- refused: the player sees why
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, 'Serial: ' .. serial)
end)

To add an option to another resource's item (police "Check for prints" on whip_gunny's guns), use AddItemOption.

Options that come and go

when tests the item's metadata; require tests the player, with an interaction's require words (job, onDuty, jobPermission, item, zone, charId, ace, vehicle, alive). A failing option is left off the menu, and the server checks both again before it runs.

{ action = 'my_guns:unload', label = 'Unload', when = { ammo = { above = 0 } } },
{ action = 'my_cops:prints', label = 'Check for prints', require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true } },

Every test in a when must pass; unknown words are refused at registration.

  • ammo = 0: equal. model = { 'adder', 't20' }: one of.
  • ammo = { above = 0 }: also below, atLeast, atMost.
  • slots = { empty = false }: not nothing, false, '', 0 or an empty table.
  • ammo = { below = 12, default = 0 }: default stands in for a missing field.

A double-click or hotbar key on a failing option shows whyNot ('Magazine is full'), or "Load Bullets isn't possible right now".

Options outside the pockets

Options show only while the player carries the item. anywhere = true also offers one in a boot, glovebox, stash, bag, wallet or panel the player has open (not on the ground, in an ignition or on a shop's shelf). The handler's addr is then that store's, such as { kind = 'vehicle', id, sub = 'trunk', slot }, so handle any address.

Options on the ground

A pile's 3D prompt says Pick up. groundOptions adds up to three of the item's own options: the item is picked up, then the option runs on its new slot, with the usual checks (a refusal leaves it on the ground). whip_gunny's weapons offer Equip.

groundOptions = { { action = 'whip_gunny:equip_weapon', label = 'Equip', icon = 'target' } },   -- "Equip Pump Shotgun"

label comes before the item's name (24 letters at most); icon is a glyph from html/js/glyphs.js.

Pictures that change

An item's images list gives it other pictures for other states: the first whose when passes is drawn, otherwise its own. Paths are inside your resource, and {field} is filled from metadata.

images = { { when = { slots = { empty = false } }, image = 'html/img/items/duffle_bag_full.webp' } }
images = { { image = 'html/img/items/keys/{make}.webp' } }   -- {make}: the maker of the car its model names
images = {                                                   -- by the slot's count, as WHIP's cash does
    { amount = { below = 100 },  image = 'html/img/items/coins_few.webp' },
    { amount = { atLeast = 100 }, image = 'html/img/items/coins_heap.webp' },
}

amount takes above, below, atLeast, atMost. With no slot to count (a shop's list) none fits, so the item's own image should suit any amount. A missing file shows the item's own picture.

Admins can change these on the Items page, choosing by count, metaFields, fields your pictures test, and pictureFields: { { key = 'mustard', label = 'Mustard', type = 'bool' } }, where type is 'bool', 'number' or 'text' (the default).

Item settings

Admins can change any item's name, description and weight on the Items page; your definition is the default, and an admin's change stays until Reset.

An item can declare its own settings too (a magazine's size, a gun's reload time), shown on its Items page. Each entry in its settings list is a setting entry: key, type ('int', 'number', 'bool', 'string' or 'enum'), default, label, and the min, max, step, unit, maxLen, nullable, options or help its type takes.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItem('my_guns_mag', {
        name = 'Pistol Magazine', weight = 0.2, stack = false,
        settings = {
            { key = 'capacity', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 100, default = 12, label = 'Rounds it holds' },
        },
    })
    Whip.core:OnItemSettingChanged('my_guns_mag', 'capacity', function(value, old)
        Config.Magazines.my_guns_mag.capacity = value   -- at once, on server and clients; Reset too
    end)
end)
local capacity = exports.whip_core:GetItemSetting('my_guns_mag', 'capacity')   -- server or client
  • Keep your own default. Save your config's value for default before you overwrite it, or the next registration declares the admin's value as the default.
  • Limits. Twenty; name, desc and weight are taken. A bad default or type refuses the item.
  • On a player's game it's nil until whip_core sends the values as they join; your hook runs then.
  • Saved in whip_settings, history in whip_settings_log.

Retiring an item

RetireItem(key, reason) takes one of your own items out of the game for good: RetireItem('mycafe_bagel', 'Bagels are off the menu'). Its definition goes, none can be made, and every one is taken away, logged as lost with your reason, not refunded. It returns true, or false and a reason.

  • When. At once from online players, open stashes, boots and the ground; elsewhere as each loads, bags and wallets included.
  • Not touched: another resource's items (refused), and items in a fixed-shape panel (a magazine) or your own store kinds: yours to clear.
  • UnretireItem(key) frees the key again (register it to bring the item back); what was taken stays taken.

In game: /whip → Economy → ItemsServer owners

Every item from every resource, searchable, with the ones an admin has changed. An item's page has:

  • What it is, with Give to me and Edit hand position: how it's held out to give or throw, pose by pose (H next pose, R move or turn), plus playerWalk and grab.
  • Its settings: name, description, weight (for config.lua's items also stacking, cooldown and kind) and its own, each with Reset. Apply saves for everyone (as Config does); only a permanent admin can.
  • What players see: its pictures and what shows each (pictures that change). Add picture takes a link from a site in Picture links accepted (Fivemanage by default).

Item definition

The fields of a RegisterItem definition and of Config.Items.

FieldTypeDescription
namestringRequired. Display name
descstringTooltip description
weightnumberRequired. kg per unit
typestringCategory label: 'consumable', 'weapon', 'tool'…
stackbooleanStacks in one slot
maxStacknumberUnits per stack: 1 if not stackable (more is refused), 100 if stackable and unset
usablebooleanUsable from the hotbar and right-click
cooldownnumberSeconds between uses (0 = none)
propstringProp model when dropped
grabstringPicked up with '1h' (default) or '2h' (a rifle, a duffel bag)
playerWalkbooleanHeld out to give or throw, the player keeps their own walk, not Config.GiveModeStyle. Default false
metaFieldstable[]Card rows from metadata: { { key='plate', label='Plate' } }; a value shows when the key is missing
fuelCapacitynumberMakes it a fuel can: how much of a car's tank (100) a full one holds, so 30 is 30%. Metadata fuel is how full it is, 0-100. Held (SetHeldItem), whip_fuel fills it at a pump and refuels cars from it. whip_gunny's jerry_can is one
defaultActionstringContext menu action key (an item that opens a panel, say)
contextOptionstable[]{ { action='open', label='Open', order=1 } }, with optional when, require, whyNot, anywhere. icon is ignored. See options that come and go
groundOptionstable[]Up to three: { { action, label, icon? } }. See options on the ground
images, pictureFieldstable[]See pictures that change
imagestringIcon path in your resource, if not html/img/items/<key>.webp or .png; '@resource/path' for another resource's. See Item icons
settingstable[]See Item settings

Inventory API

Server exports for a player's pockets, your items, the accessory strip and the player's hands. New here? Read Inventory and Items first; for one slot or another store, see Stores.

Giving and taking

AddItem(source, item, amount, metadata, opts)SERVER

Gives a player an item, pockets first, then the strip. If it fits nowhere it's dropped at their feet (why), unless Config.DropOnFullInventory = false or opts.noDrop: then nothing is given, so check before you charge.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringA registered item key
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
metadatatable?Its metadata; nil to skip it and still pass opts
optsstring|table?A reason for the activity log ('quest reward'), or { reason, noDrop = true, pocket = 'player'|'accessory', coords }: refuse rather than drop, only that pocket, drop there instead of at their feet
Returns: 'inventory', 'ground' (they're told), or false, reason with nothing created: 'Unknown item "drnk"', 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more', noDrop with no room, rarely no ped or a failed drop
local where, err = exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'drink', 2, nil, 'quest reward')
if not where then print('nothing was given: ' .. err) end

exports.whip_core:AddItem(source, 'cash', 100, nil, { pocket = 'accessory', noDrop = true })   -- the Money slot
A ground drop counts as given, so if not where then never refunds an item that exists. whip_core:item:added doesn't fire for it.
RemoveItem(source, item, amount?, metadata?, opts?)SERVER

Takes an item from the pockets, then the accessory strip, in AddItem's shape. Nothing is taken unless they have the full amount.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
metadatatable?Only the stacks whose metadata carries every one of these values ({ serial = 'AB12' })
optstable?{ reason = '...' }, for the activity log (a plain reason string works too)
Returns: bool, string|nil: false, 'Not enough items (have 0, need 1)'
A test's items. What a Director or Systems test hands out is marked (director or systest in its metadata), may only move within its players' pockets and the test's own cars and containers, and is taken back when the test ends (or at next login). A live Director run marks nothing: its items are real.
HasItem(source, item, amount)SERVER

Whether the player has at least amount, across both pockets.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?Minimum (default 1)
Returns: bool, string|nil
GetItemCount(source, item)SERVER

How many of an item the player carries, across both pockets.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
Returns: number, string|nil
CanFitItem(source, item, amount, metadata)SERVER

Whether an item fits in the pockets, by slots and weight.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
amountnumber?Quantity (default 1)
metadatatable?This instance's metadata, so its contents are weighed too
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'Only 3 fit', 'No room', 'Unknown item "x"', 'Amount must be a whole number of 1 or more', 'Player not loaded'

Finding and reading

FindItem(source, item, pocket)SERVER

The first stack of an item the player carries, with its address, as a copy. Within a pocket the lowest slot comes first (FindAllItems uses the same order).

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
pocketstring?'player' or 'accessory'; nil searches all. A pocket that doesn't exist finds nothing
Returns: { item, amount, metadata, addr } or nil
local found = exports.whip_core:FindItem(source, 'lockpick')
if found then exports.whip_core:StoreTake(found.addr, 1, { reason = 'lockpick snapped' }) end
FindAllItems(source, item, pocket)SERVER

Every stack of an item the player carries, each as a FindItem entry.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
itemstringItem key
pocketstring?Only this pocket; nil for all
Returns: an array of { item, amount, metadata, addr }, empty if none; {}, 'Player not loaded' before they load
GetInventory(source)SERVER

A deep copy of a player's whole inventory: editing it changes nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
Returns: { player = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }, accessory = { ... } }, or {}, 'Player not loaded'

Registering items

RegisterItem(key, definition)SERVER

Registers an item; it joins Config.Items. Declare it in Whip.register: the same definition again changes nothing, and another running resource can't redefine your key.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringLetters, digits, _ and -, 50 at most. No colon, unlike container, door and event names: prefix with an underscore ('mypd_evidence')
definitiontableSee Item definition
Returns: true, or false, reason
Items stay when your resource stops, since players still carry them, but the keys stop being yours and another resource may take them over.
RegisterItemDefaultMetadata(itemKey, generator, opts?)SERVER

Makes an item's metadata when it's created without any: given (AddItem, StoreGive), picked up, shown on an infinite shop's shelf, or bought.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key
generatorfunctionfunction(itemKey, ctx) → table. ctx.source, ctx.charId: the receiver, nil into a stash or boot. ctx.reason: 'given', 'pickup', 'shelf' or 'bought'. ctx may be nil (Director rewards)
optstable?{ forBuyer = true }: bought off an infinite shop's shelf, it's made again for the buyer. Stocked shops sell real items, which keep their metadata
Returns: true, or false, reason: another resource has a generator for that item
-- A SIM card with its buyer's new number (whip_phone)
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemDefaultMetadata('sim_card', function(itemKey, ctx)
    if not (ctx and ctx.charId) then return {} end   -- for nobody yet: blank
    return { phoneNumber = NewNumber(), owner = ctx.charId }
end, { forBuyer = true })
GetItemSetting(item, key) · OnItemSettingChanged(item, key, fn)SERVER CLIENT

GetItemSetting: an item's setting as in force; on the server also 'name', 'desc' and 'weight'. OnItemSettingChanged runs fn after a change (Reset included; on a client, also when values first arrive). One per resource per setting, replaced by calling again, gone when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
itemstringThe item's key
keystringThe setting's key
fnfunctionfunction(value, old, item, key)
Returns: GetItemSetting: the value, or nil (no such item or key; on a client, before the values arrive). OnItemSettingChanged: true, or false, reason

Using items and right-click options

RegisterUseHandler(itemKey, handler)SERVER

What happens when a player uses an item (hotbar or Use). The handler gets (source, player, slotData, addr): player is a data sheet (GetPlayer's table, less metadata), slotData is { item, amount, metadata }, addr its address. Return true or nothing to use one up, false to keep it, false, 'why' to refuse (Using an item).

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key; the item needs usable = true, or players only see "Item not usable" (the console warns)
handlerfunction|tablefunction(source, player, slotData, addr) → boolean, or a table for a progress bar (below)
Returns: true, or false, reason: no key or handler, a table without a positive duration, or an item another resource handles (the registration rule)
-- Wears out: keep the pick, and take a point of durability off THIS one
exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('pickaxe', function(source, player, slotData, addr)
    local left = (slotData.metadata and slotData.metadata.durability or 100) - 1
    exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(addr, { durability = left })
    return false
end)

A use with a progress bar: pass a table

WHIP runs canUse, the server-timed bar, checks the item is still there, takes it, then calls onComplete. false, 'why' or an error from onComplete gives it back. One timed use at a time per player.

exports.whip_core:RegisterUseHandler('field_dressing', {
    label = 'Bandaging...', duration = 4000,
    anim  = { dict = 'missheistdockssetup1clipboard@idle_a', clip = 'idle_a' },
    canUse = function(source)   -- 200 is full health
        if exports.whip_core:GetStat(source, 'health') >= 200 then return false, 'You are not hurt' end
        return true
    end,
    onComplete = function(source)   -- RETURN its answer: a failed heal gives the item back
        return exports.whip_core:AddStat(source, 'health', 25)
    end,
})
FieldTypeDescription
durationnumberRequired. ms
labelstring?Default 'Using <item name>...'
anim, prop, disable, cancelOnDeath, cancelOnExit, notWhiletable|booleanAs the client Progress; stopped, they keep the item. cancelOnExit: leaving the seat stops it. notWhile = { 'swimming', 'falling' }: won't start or go on there
iconstring?For an item with no picture ('eat', 'fuel'…)
canCancelboolean?Default true: X stops it, and they keep the item
consumeboolean?Default true; false keeps it (a tool)
reasonstring?For the item log. Default 'used'
canUsefunction?function(source, player, slotData, addr) → true, or false, 'why' before the bar
onCompletefunction?function(source, player, item, addr), after the item is taken. A bare false also gives it back (no message, no cooldown), unlike the function form

Examples: HUD Framework's drunk effect, whip_core/server/items/armour.lua.

Not an item? Call the server Progress(source, opts).
RegisterContextAction(actionKey, handler)SERVER

The handler for a right-click option, run when a player picks it from an item's menu.

ParamTypeDescription
actionKeystringAs named by an item's defaultAction or contextOptions; 32 characters at most. Prefix it with your resource's name ('my_bows:equip'): names are server-wide
handlerfunctionfunction(source, player, slotData, addr, how): a use handler's arguments, plus how = { from = 'ground' } right after a ground option's pick-up (skip your draw animation). Return false, 'why' to refuse
Returns: true, or false, reason: a name another resource holds, WHIP's own included (the registration rule)
AddItemOption(itemKey, option)SERVER

Adds a right-click option to any item, yours or another resource's. It goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringThe item; it needn't be registered yet
optiontableA contextOptions entry, { action, label, order?, when?, require? }, with your own action
Returns: true, or false, reason: a malformed option, an action the item already has, or one another resource added
exports.whip_core:AddItemOption('gunny_pistol', {
    action = 'my_cops:prints', label = 'Check for prints', require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
})
RemoveItemOption(itemKey, action)SERVER

Takes back an option you added. They all go anyway when your resource stops.

Returns: true, or false, reason

Item lookups

GetItemDef(key)SERVER CLIENT

An item's definition.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringItem key, such as 'food'
Returns: table|nil
GetItemDefs()SERVER CLIENT

Every item definition.

Returns: { [key] = definition }

Pockets and the accessory strip

GetPockets()SERVER

The pockets a character carries, in fallback order ({ 'player', 'accessory' }), as a copy. For a slot a client names, use the 'slot' SecureEvent param type instead: it checks the pocket, range and contents before your handler runs.

Returns: string[]
Read it inside Whip.register. Config.AccessoryStrip takes effect at whip_core's next start, so a list kept from your own start goes stale.
GetPocketSlots(pocket)SERVER

A pocket's slot count, or the whole table.

ParamTypeDescription
pocketstring?'player', 'accessory', or omit for all
Returns: number | table
GetPocketMaxWeight(pocket)SERVER

A pocket's weight limit, or the whole table. 'player''s covers everything carried, the strip included; 'accessory''s is the strip's own, inside it.

ParamTypeDescription
pocketstring?'player', 'accessory', or omit for all
Returns: number | table
RegisterAccessorySlot(def)SERVER

Reshapes one accessory slot: label, icon and what it accepts (server-enforced), until your resource stops. WHIP's own five slots (AccessoryStripSlots in shared/inventory_shape.lua: Phone, Money, then three Keys; whip_phone keeps the Phone slot to phones) are defaults any resource may replace; a slot another resource registered is refused, and so is everything with Config.AccessoryStrip off.

FieldTypeDescription
def.slotnumberRequired. 1 to Config.ContainerSlots.accessory
def.acceptsstring | string[]?The item key it takes, or a list ({ 'cash', 'wallet' }). With neither this nor keys: anything
def.keysboolean?true: it takes any ignition key too (RegisterIgnitionKey's items)
def.labelstring?Default 'Accessory'
def.iconstring?'accessory' (pouch), 'plus', 'phone', 'vehicle_key', 'cash'; default: the accepted item's, or the pouch
def.iconSvgstring?Inline SVG, over icon. Never from player input
def.tagstring?A run tag ('run:42'): ReleaseTag(tag) restores WHIP's slot. Use a new tag each run
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err: check it, as a refusal leaves the strip unchanged
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterAccessorySlot({ slot = 4, accepts = 'bandage', label = 'Medkit' })
end)
GetAccessorySlots()SERVER

The accessory strip as it is now. accepts is a list of item keys; a Key slot has keys = true; a slot that takes anything has neither.

Returns: { [slot] = { slot, accepts, keys, label, icon } }, a copy
RegisterIgnitionKey(itemName)SERVER

Makes an item an ignition key, for the ignition slot, the key checks and key sweeps; its metadata.vehicleId must still match the car. Declare it in Whip.register. It stays a key until the last resource that registered it stops.

ParamTypeDescription
itemNamestringA registered item key
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err

Hands

SetHeldItem(source, addr)SERVER

Records the item your resource just put in the player's hand (a weapon, a tool), or nil when it's put away. Others then act on that exact item: whip_fuel uses the jerry can in hand, never another. The record is your resource's, cleared when it stops, at logout and on leaving, and an item moved or swapped out of the slot stops counting. The client sees it as GetHeldItem() and require = { held = ... }.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
addrtable|nilOne of their pocket slots, { kind = 'player', id = source, sub, slot }; nil to clear
Returns: true, or false, reason (an empty slot, not their own pockets, another resource's record)
GetHeldItem(source)SERVER

What the player holds: nil when nothing is, or the item has left its slot.

Returns: { addr, item, amount, metadata } or nil
local held = exports.whip_core:GetHeldItem(source)
if held and held.item == 'jerry_can' then print('fuel:', held.metadata.fuel) end
BlockHands(source, id, opts) / UnblockHands(source, id)SERVER

The client's BlockHands, set from the server for one player: jail, an arrest. The server keeps it too, for AreHandsBlocked(source, what). Cleared at logout or drop, or when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumber | { charId }The player, online
idstringYour name for this block
optstable?As the client's: label, only = 'weapons'
Returns: true, or false, reason (not online, a bad id or opts)
exports.whip_core:BlockHands(target, 'cuffed', { label = 'You are handcuffed' })
exports.whip_core:UnblockHands(target, 'cuffed')
AreHandsBlocked(source, what) / FreeHands(source)SERVER

AreHandsBlocked: are the hands blocked by the server, for 'weapon' or (with nothing) for anything? Blocks the player's game set itself aren't seen here. FreeHands: have their game empty the hands now (a gun holstered), without blocking them.

Returns: AreHandsBlocked: true, words or false. FreeHands: true, or false, reason (not online)
local blocked, why = exports.whip_core:AreHandsBlocked(source, 'weapon')
if blocked then return false, why end

Another player's pockets

For admin tools and robberies: open a player's pockets beside the viewer's, online or offline, and drag items both ways.

OpenPlayerInventory(source, target, opts)SERVER

Opens the target's pockets as a second panel. An online target's inventory is locked meanwhile; an offline one is loaded from the database and saved on close.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe viewer
targetnumber|tableA person: server ID, or { charId = n } (offline too)
optstable?{ range? }: metres from an online target (default 5); false for none
Returns: true, or false, reason (not loaded, no such character, already open, too far…)
exports.whip_core:OpenPlayerInventory(adminSource, { charId = targetCharId }, { range = false })
Held to where it was opened. With a range, moves out of it are refused, and it closes when the viewer leaves it, the target leaves, or after five minutes. Without one it lasts until closed, and the target can't open their own inventory meanwhile.
ClosePlayerInventory(source)SERVER

Ends an inspection: unlocks an online target and saves both inventories.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe viewer
Returns: true, or false, reason (not loaded, or none open)
IsCharacterBeingInspected(charId)SERVER

Whether someone else (an admin, a robber) has this character's pockets open. Not whether they have their own inventory open.

ParamTypeDescription
charIdnumberCharacter ID
Returns: boolean

Inventory API (client)

Client exports for the player's own items and hands, item flags for your prompts, and replacing the inventory screen. The server's are on Inventory API.

Reading

HasItem(itemKey, [filter])CLIENT

Whether the player has an item, in either pocket.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key
filterfunction|number?function(metadata) → bool, or a minimum count (HasItem('bandage', 3))
Returns: bool
local hasGoldPick = exports.whip_core:HasItem('lockpick', function(meta) return meta and meta.tier == 'gold' end)
GetItemCount(itemKey, [filter])CLIENT

How many of an item the player has, across every pocket.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringItem key
filterfunction?function(metadata) → bool. A number is ignored: use HasItem(item, 5) for "at least 5"
Returns: number (0 if none)
local keys = exports.whip_core:GetItemCount('vehicle_key', function(meta) return meta and meta.vehicleId == vehicleId end)
GetHeldItem()CLIENT

What the player holds, as the server last said (SetHeldItem). No metadata: that's the server's GetHeldItem(source). For a prompt about one held thing, require = { held = 'jerry_can' } is cheaper: your canInteract isn't asked while the hand holds anything else.

Returns: { item, pocket, slot } (a copy) or nil
IsInventoryOpen()CLIENT

Whether the plain inventory screen is open. To ask whether the player is busy, use IsGameInputFree (Screens, input and controls).

Returns: bool
CloseInventory()CLIENT

Closes the inventory screen, with any open container, vehicle storage or panel.

Hands

FreeHands()CLIENT

Call it before putting something in the player's hands (a phone, a tool, a box): whatever they hold is put away first, through the 'freeHands' hook (whip_gunny holsters with its animation). It waits, so call it from a thread, through Whip.core.

Returns: true when the hands are free, false while a weapon is still in them, or false, words while they're blocked
local free, why = Whip.core:FreeHands()
if not free then return end
Whip.core:PlayEmote('clipboard')
BlockHands(id, opts) / UnblockHands(id)CLIENT

Stops the player using their hands, with words they're shown: everything (tied up, a cutscene) or weapons only (a hospital). A block of everything empties the hands at once, and FreeHands returns false while it lasts, so the phone, a tool or give mode won't start. Every block holsters a gun and stops a draw. Yours go when your resource stops; for one player from the server, see the server's.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringYour name for it; the same id replaces
optstable?label: the words shown; only = 'weapons'. Without only: everything
Returns: true, or false, reason (no id, a bad only or label; UnblockHands: none of yours by that id)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:entered', function(e)
    if e.key == 'pillbox' then
        exports.whip_core:BlockHands('pillbox', { only = 'weapons', label = 'No weapons in the hospital' })
    end
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:exited', function(e)
    if e.key == 'pillbox' then exports.whip_core:UnblockHands('pillbox') end
end)
AreHandsBlocked(what)CLIENT

Whether this game's blocks or the server's block the hands: 'weapon' for a draw (any block), nothing for anything in the hands (a block of everything). Listen for whip_core:hands:blocked to put away what you hold.

Returns: true, words, or false
local blocked, why = exports.whip_core:AreHandsBlocked('weapon')
if blocked then exports.whip_core:Notify(why, 'error') return end
RegisterClientHook(hookName, handler, id?)CLIENT

Runs your code at a moment in the client inventory flow. A handler may return a delay in ms; whip_core waits for the longest.

ParamTypeDescription
hookNamestring'beforeGiveMode', 'beforePlaceMode' (placing an item or an emote) or 'freeHands' (something needs the hands, such as the phone: put away what you hold)
handlerfunctionMay return a delay in ms
idstring?To hold two handlers on one hook; the same id replaces
