Returns: true, or false, reason: no handler, or an unknown hook
exports.whip_core:RegisterClientHook('beforeGiveMode', function()
    if MyWeaponEquipped() then Holster() return 200 end   -- WHIP waits 200 ms
end)
SetGiveModeStyle(style)CLIENT

How a player moves while holding an item out to give it. The default is Config.GiveModeStyle (the Trash walk, no faster than a jog); the latest resource's wins while it runs, and yours goes when it stops. An item with playerWalk keeps their own walk.

ParamTypeDescription
styletable|nilwalk: a /walk name or clipset; speed: 'jog' (no sprint) or 'walk' (no running). nil clears yours
Returns: true, or false, reason

Item flags

A flag says whether the player carries an item, read from a cache kept up to date on every inventory change. Use one in canInteract when the rule is about metadata (a charged battery, a key for this car); for a plain "carries one", require = { item = 'crowbar' } is enough.

RegisterItemFlag(flagName, [itemOrFilter], [filter])CLIENT

Registers a flag; declare it in Whip.register. Yours go when your resource stops; a filter that errors counts as "no" and is reported once in F8.

ParamTypeDescription
flagNamestringYour name for it; also the item key unless itemOrFilter names one
itemOrFilterstring|function?The item key, or a metadata filter
filterfunction?function(metadata) → bool, when itemOrFilter is a key
Returns: true, or false, reason: a name that isn't a string, or a flag name another resource holds (whip_core's lockpick included)
exports.whip_core:RegisterItemFlag('my_valet_key', 'vehicle_key', function(meta)
    return meta and meta.plate == 'ABC123'
end)
HasItemFlag(flagName)CLIENT

Whether the player has the flag's item now.

ParamTypeDescription
flagNamestringThe name you registered
Returns: bool
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItemFlag('my_crowbar', 'crowbar')
    Whip.core:AddAction({
        id = 'crowbar', at = { vehiclePart = 'door_dside_f' }, label = 'Pry Open',
        canInteract = function(ctx)
            return exports.whip_core:HasItemFlag('my_crowbar') and GetVehicleDoorLockStatus(ctx.entity) == 2
        end,
        onSelect = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('my_resource:pry', VehToNet(ctx.entity)) end,
    })
end)

Replacing the inventory UI

To restyle the inventory or draw a different screen, set Config.InventoryRenderer to your resource. It draws, and WHIP keeps running the inventory: your UI needs one function, render(), and each move is one call, checked like WHIP's own. Nothing in whip_core is edited, so it survives updates.

  1. Build it in Chrome with sample items: node whip_core/dev/inventory-preview/preview.js my_inventory_ui (reloads on save).
  2. Try it in game: /whip_inventory_ui my_inventory_ui (developer mode).

The contract is in whip_core/docs/nui-inventory.md. Config.EnableInventoryUI = false is only for a server with no inventory screen at all.

GetInventory()CLIENT

The player's whole inventory, for drawing your own UI, as a deep copy.

Returns: { [container] = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } } }, or {}, 'Player not loaded' before the first sync

Stores

A store is anything that holds items: pockets, a stash, a car's boot, a shop, a bag's panel. One address names any store, and the same server calls read, fill, empty and move between them, open on a screen or not.

How stores work

Each kind of store says how it's read, written and saved; WHIP does the checks, stacking, saving and screen updates for all. A move between any two kinds is a single step, never half done. Ground items aren't a store: they have their own exports.

A kind may declare beforeMove, which can refuse before anything changes, and afterMove, run once the move commits. Panels build on them; RegisterStoreKind declares your own.

A hook that errors refuses the move. An error in beforeMove never counts as a yes; the error is logged in your resource's console.

Addresses

A store is named by { kind, id, sub, slot }. Leave slot out when the call can choose one (or, for OpenStore, has no use for one).

KindAddressWhat it is
player{ kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player' }Pockets; sub = 'accessory' is the strip. sub defaults to 'player'
container{ kind = 'container', id = containerId }A world stash, loaded on demand
vehicle{ kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' }'trunk', 'glovebox' or 'key' (ignition). id may be a vehicle reference ({ plate = 'ABC 123' }). Loaded on demand
panel{ kind = 'panel', id = panelId }A panel open now (owner = source to name whose)
your own{ kind = 'mykind', id = ..., sub = ... }Registered with RegisterStoreKind

shop and basket exist only while a player has one open, so they have no server-side address.

Moving

StoreMove(fromAddr, toAddr, opts)SERVER

Moves a stack between stores, or within one, as a player's drag does: hooks asked, checked, saved, viewers updated. Use it instead of a remove-then-add pair, which can fail halfway and lose the item.

ParamTypeDescription
fromAddrtableThe source address, with its slot
toAddrtableThe destination; without a slot it goes wherever it fits
optstable?amount (0 or omitted: the whole slot), mode ('move', 'one' or 'split'), reason for the log
Returns: true, or false, reason
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:StoreMove(
    { kind = 'container', id = 12, slot = 3 },
    { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 1 }, { amount = 2 })
It's on the record. Each character it touched gets a "moved" row naming your resource (and reason), and whip_core:item:added / item:removed fire for players whose pockets changed.

Reading

StoreRead(addr)SERVER

What's in any store, as a copy keyed by slot number; a slot in the address is ignored. A stash or boot is loaded if needed. A panel exists only while open; an open, empty one has items = {}.

Returns: { kind, id, sub, label, slots, maxWeight, weight, items = { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } } }, or false, reason: 'No such container', 'Vehicle not found', 'that panel is not open'…
local stash = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'container', id = 12 })
if not stash then return end
for slot, it in pairs(stash.items) do print(slot, it.item, it.amount) end
StoreCount(addr, item)SERVER

How many of one item a store holds.

Returns: number, or false, reason
Check it before you compare it. An unreachable store returns false, not 0 (unlike GetItemCount's 0, reason), so StoreCount(addr, 'x') >= 5 throws. Write if n and n >= 5 then.
GetItemAt(addr)SERVER

What's in one slot of any store, as a copy. Empty is nil and a wrong address false, so if not item then covers both.

ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address with a slot
Returns: { item, amount, metadata }, nil, or false, reason (no such store, a slot past the end)
local item = exports.whip_core:GetItemAt(addr)   -- the item a use handler was given: still there?
if not item or item.item ~= 'alcohol' then return end

Creating and destroying

StoreGive(addr, item, amount, metadata, reason)SERVER

Creates an item in any store. With a slot, into exactly that slot (onto the same item if it stacks) or refused; without, wherever it fits, across slots if needed, all or nothing. For a player's reward use AddItem, which drops at their feet instead of refusing.

ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address; slot optional
itemstringA registered item
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
metadatatable?Left out, a default generator (a gun's serial) fills each slot
reasonstring|table?For the log, or { reason = '...' }
Returns: the (first) slot it landed in, or false, reason
exports.whip_core:StoreGive({ kind = 'vehicle', id = vanId, sub = 'trunk' }, 'delivery_package', 20, nil, 'delivery shift')
StoreTake(addr, amount, opts)SERVER

Destroys items in any store: materials used up, evidence confiscated. With a slot, from that slot (amount nil: the whole stack); without, from wherever opts.item is. All or nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address, with or without a slot
amountnumber?How many
optstable|string?{ item = 'drink' } without a slot; reason for the log. A string is the reason
Returns: { item, amount, metadata } taken (metadata only from one slot), or false, reason ('Empty slot', 'Not enough items'…)
local taken, err = exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'container', id = 12 }, 5, { item = 'drink' })
Taking isn't moving. What you take is gone; to put it elsewhere, use StoreMove.

Metadata

SetItemMetadata(addr, metadata, opts)SERVER

Changes the metadata of the item at an address. Only the keys you pass change. It's saved and shown to whoever has the store open. The item's uid (its activity log identity) survives even replace, unless you pass uid = false.

ParamTypeDescription
addrtableAn address with a slot
metadatatable|nilThe keys to change. nil only with replace (clears all) or remove; a bare nil is refused
optstable?replace = true: the table becomes the whole metadata. remove = { 'key', ... }. quiet = true (pockets only): don't resend their inventory, for a value that changes many times a second (a round count)
Returns: true once changed (even if the save is retried), or false, reason ('Empty slot', a wrong address, unsaveable metadata)
exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata({ kind = 'container', id = 12, slot = 3 }, { evidence = true }, { remove = { 'label' } })
Plain data, and players can read it. Anything json.encode can't write is refused (false, 'metadata cannot be saved: ...'). Metadata goes whole to whoever sees the item, so keep secrets (a safe's code) server-side and store an id.

Finding one item

FindItemByUid(uid)SERVER

Where one item is, by the uid every logged item has in its metadata: its address with a slot, or { kind = 'ground', id }.

Returns: table|nil
local at = exports.whip_core:FindItemByUid(uid)
if at and at.kind == 'player' then exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(at.id, 'The police want a word', 'warning') end
It searches what's loaded: online players, stashes, boots and panels in memory, and the ground. Not a stash untouched since the restart, nor inside a bag.
FindItemByMetadata(key, value)SERVER

Where the first item whose metadata key holds value is, searching the same places as FindItemByUid: FindItemByMetadata('serial', 'AB12CD34EF56') runs a gun's serial.

Returns: an address or nil

Opening a store for a player

GetOpenStores(source)SERVER

Every store the player has open, as addresses in a stable order. Their pockets are never listed; a shop is { kind = 'shop' }. A panel comes with its label, which is how you learn the id of one an item opened: { kind = 'panel', id = 'wallet_...', owner = source, label = 'Wallet' }.

Returns: table[], empty when nothing is open
OpenStore(source, addr, opts)SERVER

Puts a stash, a boot or your own store kind on a player's screen, with the checks of a player's own open (access, distance, lock) unless opts skips them. Players share one stash; the loser of a race is told the slot is empty. Refused: pockets (OpenPlayerInventory), panels (OpenPanel), a glovebox or ignition, and a player with a screen already open.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
addrtable{ kind = 'container', id }, { kind = 'vehicle', id, sub = 'trunk' } or { kind = 'mykind', id, sub }
optstable?skipDistance (a stash; a boot always needs it), skipAccess (a stash's lock and owner, a boot's lock), coords + range (your kind: stay within, default 3 m), readOnly (your kind: every move refused)
Returns: true, or false, reason
local ok, reason = exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'container', id = containerId }, { skipAccess = true })
if not ok then exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, reason, 'error') end
Close what you open. The player stays a viewer, whose drags count, until CloseStore. Inside a SecureEvent handler that errors, WHIP releases the view; elsewhere, you must.
CloseStore(source, addr)SERVER

Takes a store away from a player, wherever they stand, even after they've disconnected. Other viewers keep it. A stash or boot is saved, and unloaded if nobody else uses it. A panel closes with ClosePanel.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
addrtableThe address you opened it with
Returns: true, or false, 'That is not open'

Ground items

Items lying in the world: dropped or thrown by players, or left by your resource. Players pick them up; your server code creates, finds and deletes them.

Dropping, throwing and picking up

  • Drop: drag an item to the Ground panel and it lands in front of the player.
  • Throw: in give mode, aim and release. It's a ground item as it leaves the hand: anyone in reach can grab it from the air, and it settles where it lands.
  • Pick up: E puts it in the best slot, or drag it from the Ground panel. If two players grab one item at once, one gets it.

The pockets lose an item only as its ground item is made, so nothing is lost or copied. Players are sent the items in the Config.GroundItemCellSize (50 m) cells around them as they move, and their game draws props within Config.GroundItemStreamRange.

API

CreateGroundItem({ item, amount?, coords, metadata?, heading?, reason? })SERVER

Puts an item on the ground. It syncs to nearby players by itself.

FieldTypeDescription
itemstringA registered item key
amountnumber?A whole number, 1 or more (default 1)
coordsvector3|vector4World position (a vector4's w is the heading)
metadatatable?Custom metadata
headingnumber?Degrees
reasonstring?For the activity log, beside your resource's name
Returns: table: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, createdAt }, or false, reason (not a table, an unknown item, a bad amount, no coordinates)
DeleteGroundItem(id)SERVER

Removes a ground item.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberGround item ID
Returns: bool, string|nil
GetGroundItemsNearby(x, y, z, range?)SERVER

Every ground item within a 3D radius.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberCentre, or a vector3 first and the range second
rangenumber?Metres (default 10)
Returns: table[]: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, ... }
-- A street sweeper
for _, row in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetGroundItemsNearby(vector3(x, y, z), 5.0)) do
    exports.whip_core:DeleteGroundItem(row.id)
end
GetGroundItem(id)SERVER

One ground item by id, or nil once it's picked up or deleted.

Returns: table|nil: { id, item, amount, metadata, x, y, z, heading, ... }

Containers

A container is a stash in the world: a prop with an E prompt that opens beside the player's inventory. Declare one with EnsureContainer, decide who may open it, and fill or read it with the store calls.

Opening one

The prop appears within 100 m. E opens it in place of the Ground panel when it isn't locked, the player may open it and they stand within 4.5 m. Several players can share it at once.

Who may open it

FieldEffect
locked = trueNobody (an admin can override)
accessCharId = charIdOnly that character
requirements = { jobs = 'police', onDuty = true }Anyone meeting any one rule: jobs (with onDuty, on duty there), charIds, items (carrying a keycard), ace, or property (its owner and keyholders, by id or key)
none of theseAnyone
allowedItems = { 'item1', 'item2' }Only these items go in. A keyed table ({ item1 = true }) works too; nil allows all

Requirements hold on every move, so going off duty, losing a property's key or the stash being locked stops the looting there. A required item can never go into the container it opens.

Reading and filling

A stash is a store at { kind = 'container', id = containerId }: read it with StoreRead (.items, by slot), fill it with StoreGive and StoreTake, and show it with OpenStore. Nobody needs it open. Closing or disconnecting saves it, and contents are in memory only while it's open, so thousands of containers cost little.

Declaring and creating

Use EnsureContainer for a stash your resource always has. CreateContainer makes a new one on every call: in your resource's start, that's a twin with separate contents on every restart.
EnsureContainer(key, data)SERVER

A container declared by key, the same rule as EnsureShop and EnsureZone. The same declaration again changes nothing, so an admin's edits stand; a changed one applies your fields, clears an allowedItems or requirements you dropped, and refuses fewer slots while an item sits above the new count. Another running resource's key is refused.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringLetters, digits, _ - . :, at most 100. Prefix it: 'pd:weapon_locker'
datatable{ x, y, z, heading?, name?, type?, slots?, maxWeight?, prop?, locked?, allowedItems?, requirements? }. An unread field is reported in the console. Not ownerCharId / accessCharId: use UpdateContainer
data.requirementstable?{ jobs?, onDuty?, charIds?, items?, ace?, property? }, any one lets a player in; checked on open and every move
Returns: table with containerId, key and declared (your declaration), or false, reason. While whip_core starts it waits up to 60 s, then returns false, 'whip_core has not finished starting …' (so do EnsureZone, EnsureDoors, EnsureJob).
-- Officers on duty only. Without `requirements` anyone could loot it.
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureContainer('pd:weapon_locker', {
        name = 'Weapon Locker', slots = 30, maxWeight = 200.0,
        x = 441.5, y = -982.3, z = 30.7, heading = 90.0,
        allowedItems = { gunny_pistol = true, gunny_mag_pistol = true },
        requirements = { jobs = 'police', onDuty = true },
    })
end)
Door and action rules. A door's lockpick is refused. An action's require is taken when it names one rule and refused when it names more: containers, like doors, read rules as any one, actions as all.
CreateContainer(data)SERVER

Creates a container on every call. accessCharId makes it one character's; requirements is as in EnsureContainer (a house stash: { property = 'pinklady_flat' }).

persist = false makes one that's never saved, for a job or a heist, which only your resource can change or delete. It goes when your resource stops or its tag is released (ReleaseTag): screens it's open on close, and what's left is logged as lost. It takes items (starting contents, all or nothing), prop = false (only a prompt) and placed = true with rx/ry (no snap to the ground).

Returns: table with containerId, or false, reason (no x/y/z, a key taken, a requirements shape it won't take such as a lockpick rule or an unknown property, an item that can't go in, a run whose tag has ended, a database error)
-- The vault's safe: never saved, gone with the job, the money already inside
local safe = exports.whip_core:CreateContainer({
    persist = false, tag = 'heist:' .. jobId, name = 'Safe',
    x = 255.1, y = 225.4, z = 101.9, prop = false,
    items = { { item = 'cash', amount = 5000 } },
    requirements = { charIds = crewCharIds },   -- only the crew
})

Finding

GetContainer(ref)SERVER

What a container is (name, size, position, owner), from cache. What it holds is StoreRead.

ParamTypeDescription
refnumber|tableA container id, or { key = } (the key it was declared by)
Returns: table|nil
local locker = exports.whip_core:GetContainer({ key = 'pd:weapon_locker' })

Changing and deleting

UpdateContainer(containerId, data)SERVER

Changes only the fields in data, saves them and re-sends them to clients. Players who have it open are held to the change on their next move.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumberContainer ID
datatableAny of name, type, slots, maxWeight, ownerCharId, accessCharId, locked, x, y, z, heading, prop, allowedItems, requirements, key. Fewer slots are refused while an item sits above the new count
data.accessCharIdnumber?The only way to change it after creation (a tradeable key, a handover). 0 makes it public; nil leaves it
data.requirementstable|false?As in EnsureContainer; false clears it
data.keystring|false?Gives it a key, so EnsureContainer finds it; false removes it
Returns: true, or false, reason: no such container, a slot above a smaller slots isn't empty, the key is another container's, or the write failed
-- Hand a stash to whoever used the key
exports.whip_core:UpdateContainer(containerId, { accessCharId = player.charId, locked = false })
DeleteContainer(containerId)SERVER

Deletes a container and its inventory. Refused while a shop sells from it.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumberContainer ID
Returns: true, or false, reason

Store kinds

A store is anything items sit in: pockets, a stash, a car boot, a panel. For your own kind you write how it's read, written and saved; weight, stacking, metadata merging, the transaction and client sync come with it.

Do you need one?

A store kind is for storage that persists, authorises itself and behaves like a first-class container. For a slot grid open for one session, OpenPanel is simpler, with no persistence to write; for an item that holds items, use RegisterPanelItem.

Registering a kind

RegisterStoreKind(kindId, kindDef)SERVER

Declares a kind of store: once per kind, never per instance. The name is yours once registered (the registration rule): another resource's kind is refused, and registering yours again swaps the definition quietly.

FunctionSignaturePurpose
resolve(key) → handle|nilRequired. Instance key to something to operate on. nil means "cannot proceed", never "empty"
instanceId(key, handle) → stringRequired. This store's stable identity, starting with your kind's name and a colon ('my_safe:3') or OpenStore refuses it
unitKey(key, handle) → stringWhat persists together. Default instanceId, right for almost every kind
slots / maxWeight(handle) → numberRequired. Capacity
get(handle, slot) → slotData|nilRequired. { item, amount, metadata }
set / clear(handle, slot, …)Required. Write and empty a slot
authorize(src, addr) → booleanLets players drag in a kind that decides "has it open" itself. Not needed while it's open with OpenStore
allows(handle, itemKey, metadata) → booleanItem filter for the whole store
allowsAt(handle, slot, itemKey, metadata) → boolean, reason?Per-slot filter (a tool rack, a magazine slot), checked wherever an item lands
persist(handle) → queries[]|nilnil means "cannot persist right now"
durability'writeThrough' | 'writeBehind'Default write-through
beforeMove / afterMove(handle, ctx)Veto; side effect after the commit. ctx: direction, slot, otherSlot, item, amount, metadata, swap, other (an address, { kind, id, sub, slot, label }). Destroying: direction = 'out', destroyed = true, no other
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err. Never throws, so a malformed definition can't kill your resource.
local lockers = { [3] = { slots = {} } }   -- yours, in memory; save it from persist

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterStoreKind('my_locker', {
        resolve    = function(key) return lockers[key.id] and { id = key.id } or nil end,
        instanceId = function(key, h) return 'my_locker:' .. h.id end,
        slots      = function(h) return 20 end,
        maxWeight  = function(h) return 100.0 end,
        get        = function(h, slot) return lockers[h.id].slots[slot] end,
        set        = function(h, slot, item, amount, metadata)
            lockers[h.id].slots[slot] = { item = item, amount = amount, metadata = metadata }
            return true
        end,
        clear      = function(h, slot) lockers[h.id].slots[slot] = nil; return true end,
    })
end)

exports.whip_core:OpenStore(source, { kind = 'my_locker', id = 3 })   -- beside their pockets
A handle carries an id, never a live table. FiveM copies what resolve returns, so a set on a handle holding your rows writes into a copy: the move succeeds, the item leaves the player and never arrives. Return { id = id } and look your storage up in get, set and clear.

Good to know

  • Every store call works with it (StoreRead, StoreGive, StoreMove, GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata...), with { kind = 'mykind', id, sub } resolved as resolve({ id, sub }).
  • Players touch it only when you let them: while it's open on their screen with OpenStore (held to opts.coords / opts.range; never if readOnly), or when authorize returns a literal true (an error refuses). Your resource can always move items.
  • id and sub come from the client when a player drags. resolve must look them up and return nil for anything unknown.
  • resolve, get, set and clear must not yield (no Wait, no database await): a refused write is undone with a plain set. Keep storage in memory; save from persist.
  • Reserved names: player, rawInventory, container, vehicle, panel, and client-addressable names such as target and accessory. Two resources can't claim one kind; the first wins. Your kinds go when your resource stops.

Panels

A panel is a slot grid that opens beside the player's inventory, with drag and drop and no NUI of your own. The server holds its items and checks every move.

OpenPanel opens a standalone panel, such as a crafting station; you save what's left from its onClose. RegisterPanelItem makes an item hold items, such as a wallet, saved in its metadata as they change.

Opening a panel

Everything goes in one config table, hooks included; every field is on the OpenPanel card.

local ok, err = exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id           = 'refine:input_' .. refineryId,   -- its address: { kind = 'panel', id = id }
    label        = 'Crusher — Input',
    slots        = 6,
    items        = r.input,                         -- what it held last time
    allowedItems = { 'old_radio', 'broken_phone' },

    -- The last person has walked away: keep what's left
    onClose = function(ctx)
        r.input = ctx.items   -- { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }
    end,
})
if not ok then print(err) end

The three hooks

All optional, all in the OpenPanel config, each handed one table, ctx.

HookRunsDoes
onValidate(ctx)Before a player's move into, out of or within the panel, or a Split or Destroy on its slotsReturn false, 'reason' to refuse; the player sees the reason. Anything else allows it; an error refuses
onChange(ctx)After a player's move, Split or Destroy has landedReacts: pay for it, start a machine. ctx.items is what the panel holds now
onClose(ctx)Once, when the last viewer leavesSaves what was left. ctx is { panel, source, items }. Without one, players get back what they put in, and your stock goes

ctx for onValidate and onChange:

FieldWhat it is
source, panelThe player moving the item, and the panel's id
direction'in', 'out', or 'within' (panel slot to panel slot; a Split is one)
slot, otherSlotThe panel's slot, and the slot at the other end
otherThe store at the other end, as an address: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }. nil when destroying
destroyedtrue when a developer in developer mode uses Destroy: direction is 'out', no other
item, amount, metadataWhat is moving
swaponValidate only: true on the returning half of a swap, inside one panel too
replacingonValidate only: on a swap's forward half, { item, amount, metadata } of what will go back, so "one magazine at a time" can allow a swap. nil when nothing is displaced
itemsonChange only: what the panel holds now, a copy keyed by slot
hostRegisterPanelItem only: the item the panel belongs to

Act on what a player drags in from onChange: by then the move has happened, so you never pay for something that didn't arrive.

-- A pawn counter: whatever is dragged in is bought on the spot
local PRICES = { gold_ring = 150, old_watch = 80 }

exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id = 'pawn:' .. source, label = 'Sell to the pawn shop', slots = 1,
    allowedItems = { 'gold_ring', 'old_watch' },
    onChange = function(ctx)
        if ctx.direction ~= 'in' then return end
        local taken = exports.whip_core:StoreTake({ kind = 'panel', id = ctx.panel, slot = ctx.slot })
        if taken then   -- PayPlayer drops cash that won't fit at their feet
            exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(ctx.source, PRICES[taken.item] * taken.amount, { method = 'cash', reason = 'pawn shop' })
        end
    end,
})
The hooks belong to the panel, not to one player. Several players can share a panel id. The first OpenPanel for it that brings hooks sets them for every viewer; later openers' hooks are ignored while it's open.

Filling it from the server

A panel is a store at { kind = 'panel', id = id, slot = n }. Your own writes skip onValidate and onChange, but its slots, maxWeight, allowedItems and stack sizes apply.

exports.whip_core:StoreGive({ kind = 'panel', id = 'refine:output_1', slot = 1 }, 'steel_ingot', 4)
local panel = exports.whip_core:StoreRead({ kind = 'panel', id = 'refine:output_1' })   -- panel.items
exports.whip_core:ClosePanel(source, 'refine:output_1')

Items that hold items

The panel hangs off the item's defaultAction, or the context action named in action, which RegisterPanelItem registers for you. Contents live in metadata.slots (or storageKey), so they travel with the item.

-- The item first: a panel for an item whip_core doesn't know is refused
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterItem('mymech_toolbox', {
        name = 'Toolbox', weight = 2.0, stack = false,
        defaultAction  = 'mytools:open_toolbox',
        contextOptions = { { action = 'mytools:open_toolbox', label = 'Open' } },
    })
    Whip.core:RegisterPanelItem('mymech_toolbox', {
        slots = 6, label = 'Toolbox', allowedItems = { 'wrench', 'screwdriver' },
    })
end)

whip_core's wallet is the same declaration: 3 slots, allowedItems = { 'cash', 'id_card' }.

Custom storage shapes

A magazine is one record { item, ammo, serial }; a revolver's chamber is a number. Five optional RegisterPanelItem hooks handle such shapes; leave them out for a plain slot list.

  • canOpen(host) may refuse to open. It runs before read, so a locked box never shows its contents; an error keeps it shut.
  • read(host) projects the item's metadata into slots, and write(host, items) folds them back. write only builds and returns the metadata: it's also run on a copy to check each move, and a move it errors on is refused.
  • onValidate(ctx) and onChange(ctx) are the hooks above, with ctx.host, the item (read after the fold, in onChange).

host is { source, container, slot, addr, item, amount, metadata }, read fresh each time, so it's right even if the item moves while its panel is open. addr is ready for GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata and StoreTake.

Example: whip_gunny's magazine slot

Condensed from whip_gunny/server/magpanel.lua: the magazine slot of every gun, in one declaration. The real file also covers guns with no magazine (revolvers, pump shotguns), where read shows a round count and write saves a number.

exports.whip_core:RegisterPanelItem(weaponItem, {
    action = 'whip_gunny:open_weapon',   -- a named context option, not the item's use action
    slots  = 1,
    label  = weaponCfg.label .. ' Mag',

    -- What the panel shows: the weapon's magazine, rendered as one slot. The gun keeps the
    -- magazine's WHOLE metadata (its uid and the rest), so it comes out as it went in.
    read = function(host)
        local mag = host.metadata.magazine
        if not mag then return {} end
        local item, metadata = GunnyMagazineOut(mag)   -- the record without its item name
        return { [1] = { item = item, amount = 1, metadata = metadata } }
    end,

    -- The rule allowedItems can't express: it depends on WHICH weapon, and what
    -- is already in it. The weapon is ctx.host. The reason is shown to the player.
    onValidate = function(ctx)
        local host = ctx.host
        -- Either way, not while the gun is loaded a shell at a time: the client is counting the shells.
        if GunnyLoopedReloadOpen(host.source, host.slot, host.addr.sub) then
            return false, 'Finish reloading first'
        end
        if ctx.direction ~= 'in' then return true end
        if not Config.IsMagCompatible(host.item, ctx.item) then
            return false, 'That magazine does not fit this weapon'
        end
        -- On a swap the fitted magazine is the one leaving (ctx.replacing dropping a new one onto it,
        -- ctx.swap dragging it out onto a new one), so only a SECOND one is refused.
        if host.metadata.magazine and not ctx.swap and not ctx.replacing then
            return false, 'Remove the current magazine first'
        end
        return true
    end,

    -- Fold the slot back into the weapon's own shape.
    write = function(host, items)
        local held = items[1]
        -- The magazine's whole metadata, plus its item name (server/main.lua)
        host.metadata.magazine = held and GunnyMagazineIn(held.item, held.metadata) or nil
        return host.metadata
    end,

    -- Post-commit only, never speculative: the right place to touch the ped. Swapping the
    -- visible magazine for a move that then failed would leave the model disagreeing with the inventory.
    onChange = function(ctx)
        local mag = ctx.host.metadata.magazine
        -- The rounds changed here, not by a shot: gunny numbers the change, and a count the game sent
        -- for the old magazine is then ignored (GunnyCountChanged, server/weapons.lua).
        -- Nil when this isn't the gun in the hand: then there's nothing on the ped to change.
        local version = GunnyCountChanged(ctx.host.source, ctx.host.addr, ctx.host.metadata.serial)
        if not version then return end
        if mag then
            TriggerClientEvent('whip_gunny:client:magazineInserted', ctx.host.source, ctx.host.slot, mag.ammo, version, mag.item)
        else
            TriggerClientEvent('whip_gunny:client:magazineRemoved', ctx.host.source, ctx.host.slot, version)
        end
    end,
})

Many items can share one action: every gun uses whip_gunny:open_weapon, and the handler gets whichever gun was used.

Example: a refinery

The input panel above plus a take-only output tray, each opened from a SecureEvent with near; refuse the input while it's busy. The input's onClose runs the crusher:

-- r is this refinery's state: { input = {}, output = {}, busy = false }
onClose = function(ctx)
    r.input = ctx.items
    if r.busy or next(ctx.items) == nil then return end
    r.busy = true
    SetTimeout(15000, function()
        r.output = Crush(r.input, r.output)   -- your recipes: 1 old_radio makes 3 copper_wire
        r.input, r.busy = {}, false
    end)
end,

-- The output tray
exports.whip_core:OpenPanel(source, {
    id = 'refine:output_' .. refineryId, label = 'Crusher — Output', slots = 12, items = r.output,
    onValidate = function(ctx)
        if ctx.direction == 'in' then return false, 'This tray is output only' end
    end,
    onClose = function(ctx) r.output = ctx.items end,
})

Cleanup

Panels close when a player disconnects or the resource stops, running onClose if that was the last viewer. With nothing to keep the contents (no onClose, or your resource or whip_core stopped), each character gets back what they put in and didn't take out; your stock goes, logged. A player can have several panels open: name one in ClosePanel.

Panels API

Server exports for panels. How panels and their hooks work is in Panels.

Opening and closing

OpenPanel(source, config)SERVER

Opens a panel for a player, with their inventory beside it. The server keeps its contents, checks every player move against its rules and calls its hooks.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
configtableThe fields below
Config fieldTypeRequiredDescription
idstring|numberYesAddress { kind = 'panel', id = id }. Opened again for the same player, nothing happens. Ids are shared, so prefix yours ('myres:bench_' .. src): one another resource has open returns false, 'Panel id "…" is already open by …'
labelstringNoHeader text (default 'Panel')
slotsnumberNoDefault 10, at most 5 per row
itemstableNo{ [slot] = { item, amount, metadata } }, used only when the panel isn't already open
maxWeightnumberNokg (nil = unlimited)
allowedItemstableNo{ 'food', 'drink' } or { food = true } (nil = any)
readOnlybooleanNoThe player can look; every move is refused, rearranging included
onValidatefunctionNo(ctx) → ok, reason, before a player's move; false or an error refuses
onChangefunctionNo(ctx), after a player's move landed
onClosefunctionNo(ctx), once the last viewer has left: { panel, source, items }. Give one to keep the contents. Without one (or if it errors), each player gets back what they put in and didn't take out, at their feet if their pockets are full (unless dropping is off). The rest goes, logged as lost. A readOnly panel without one gives nothing back
Returns: true, or false, reason
Contents live in memory until you take them. WHIP saves the player's side of a move, not the panel's, so a crash before onChange or onClose hands them to you loses them. To survive a crash, save in onChange, or use a store kind with persist.
ClosePanel(source, panelId?)SERVER

Closes a panel for one player. If they were its last viewer, onClose runs and the panel is gone.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberServer player ID
panelIdstring|number?Leave it out to close every panel they have open
Returns: true, or false, 'No such panel open'
A panel's id. A RegisterPanelItem panel's id is made up by WHIP, in an internal format. GetOpenStores(source) lists each open panel as { kind = 'panel', id, owner, label }, ready for StoreRead.

Items that hold items

RegisterPanelItem(itemKey, config)SERVER

Makes an item open a panel from its context action, like a wallet or toolbox. It registers the action and a metadata generator (adding the empty-slots default only when the item has none), and folds the contents into the item's metadata as they change. The custom hooks are in Panels.

ParamTypeDescription
itemKeystringRegistered, with a defaultAction unless the config names an action
configtableThe fields below
Config fieldTypeRequiredDescription
slotsnumberNoDefault 3
labelstring | functionNoHeader text, or (host) → string (a magazine's round count)
storageKeystringNoMetadata key for the items (default 'slots')
allowedItemstableNo{ 'cash', 'id_card' } or { cash = true }, fixed at registration
actionstringNoDefault the item's defaultAction; several items may share one
canOpenfunctionNo(host) → ok, reason, before read; fails closed
readfunctionNo(host) → items. Default metadata[storageKey]
onValidatefunctionNo(ctx) → ok, reason: OpenPanel's ctx, plus host
writefunctionNo(host, items) → metadata, no side effects: it's also run on a copy to check each move. Default metadata[storageKey]
onChangefunctionNo(ctx), after the move landed; never speculative
Returns: true, or false, reason, changing nothing, when the item isn't registered or has no action, another resource has a panel for it, or another resource holds the action.
Not taken here: maxWeight, readOnly, or a per-item maxPerSlot in allowedItems (only keys count, in OpenPanel too). They're ignored silently; enforce caps and read-only views in onValidate.

Vehicles & Keys

How WHIP's cars work: their states, keys that are items, the ignition, locks, seats, storage and the damage they keep. Read it before you write a script that touches a car; the calls are in the Vehicles API.

Vehicle states

StateMeaningEntity exists?
'out'In the world, position trackedYes
'garaged'Stored in a garageNo
'impounded'Seized (admin), retrievableNo

Cars that are out stay in the world when their player leaves or drives off, and come back where they stood after a restart.

Keys and the ignition

A key is an item, vehicle_key, with metadata { vehicleId, plate, model }, and a token when the car's locks have been changed. It doesn't stack and weighs 0.1 kg.

  • Getting one. GiveVehicleKey, or CreateOwnedVehicle with { giveKey = true } (without it, no key). SpawnTempVehicle with forSource gives that player one unless giveKey = false; keyInIgnition = true puts one in the ignition instead.
  • Starting the engine. The driver drags the key into the car's one-slot ignition in the inventory; only a key whose metadata.vehicleId matches fits, and after a change of locks only one cut since. Mouse wheel up starts the engine, down stops it.
  • No key in the ignition: the engine stays off and wheel up shows "No key in ignition!".
  • A spare. GiveVehicleKey refuses a player who already holds a key of the car, unless you pass { spare = true }, which cuts another one to hand to a friend.
  • Changing the locks. ChangeVehicleLocks makes every key of an owned car cut so far stop fitting, wherever it is, so a lost or copied key is worthless; keys cut after fit. CountVehicleKeys says how many keys fit the car now.
Stopping an engine (an overheat, a breakdown): HoldVehicleEngine keeps it off and shows the driver your reason until ReleaseVehicleEngine. Otherwise a running engine stays on while its key is in the ignition.

Locking

Players lock with L, or Lock / Unlock on a door's prompt; the lock is saved with the car. From the driver's seat the key may be in the ignition or the inventory; on foot it must be in the inventory, within Config.VehicleLockRange (8 m). Players nearby see two flashes for lock, one for unlock.

Street cars

KindComes fromSaved?vehicleId
OwnedCreateOwnedVehicle, or a street car claimed with ClaimVehicleYesDatabase id (1, 2, 3...)
SessionNPC cars, registered on first useNo1,000,000,000 and up

A street car is registered when a player takes its driver's seat, lockpicks it, opens its boot or refuels it, or a script calls ResolveVehicle. It then has a vehicleId, boot, glovebox, ignition, lock and fuel; if its engine was running, a key is put in its ignition.

Street cars stay locked until lockpicked, then stay unlocked. The rule's range is Config.NpcVehicleLockRange (10 m); 0 turns it off. A resource's local, non-networked car is left alone: its prompts work on that one game and it has no boot.

Seats

Passengers stay in their seat: no sliding into an empty driver's seat, and GTA's shuffle button (H, D-pad right) does nothing. Config.Seats.NoAutoShuffle = false brings GTA's behaviour back. Players change seat with Seats on the F1 wheel or /seats. Read a seat with GetPlayerSeat; whip_core:vehicle:entered fires again on a seat change.

Storage

Each car's boot (trunk), glovebox and ignition are stores. Their sizes come from the first that is set: the car's own (given when it was made), its model's, its category's (a GTA vehicle class), then the config (VehicleTrunkSlots and the rest). Set models and categories in /whip → Vehicles → Vehicle Adjustments, where either can also turn off its boot or glovebox. Shrinking or turning off slots is refused while a car still has items in them.

Naming a car: vehicle references

Every vehicle, stat and data export takes the car first, on both sides, in any of these forms:

vehicleId    { id = vehicleId }    { entity = veh }    { plate = 'ABC123' }    { netId = netId }
  • A bare number is always a vehicleId. Pass an entity handle as { entity = veh }: both are integers, so guessing could pick a different car. Only GetVehicleId(entity) and ResolveVehicle(entity) take a handle.
  • A snapshot from GetVehicle is a reference too.
  • On the server, a reference to no car returns 'Vehicle not found'; a table naming nothing returns 'Invalid vehicle reference'. A client returns nil for a car not streamed in near it.

Writing a vehicle script

On the client, GetVehicleId(entity) returns a car's id from the cache, or nil for a car WHIP hasn't met; ResolveVehicle(entity) then registers it. Send the id to the server. This tow hook works on any car:

-- client.lua
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:AddAction({
        id    = 'hook',
        at    = { vehiclePart = 'trunk' },
        label = 'Hook Vehicle',
        canInteract = function(ctx) return exports.whip_core:HasItemFlag('tow_hook') end,
        onSelect = function(ctx)   -- runs once, in its own thread: may wait
            local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleId(ctx.entity), nil
            if not vehicleId then vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:ResolveVehicle(ctx.entity) end
            if not vehicleId then return ctx.refuse(why) end
            TriggerServerEvent('tow:hookVehicle', vehicleId)
        end,
    })
end)

-- server.lua, inside Whip.register
Whip.core:SecureEvent('tow:hookVehicle', {
    rateLimit = 2000,
    params = { {'vehicle', 'vehicle', { anyOwner = true, session = true }} },   -- anybody's car, street cars too
    near   = { at = 'vehicle', range = 8.0 },   -- where the car is now
}, function(source, player, v)
    print(('Towing %s (%s)'):format(v.model, v.plate))
end)
ResolveVehicle waits for the server. Call it in onSelect, a command or another one-off, never in canInteract, a label, a loop or per-frame code. Use GetVehicleId or GetVehicle({ entity = entity }) there.

The other client reads are in the Client vehicles API. On the server, GetVehicle returns one snapshot with the owner, lock, state, netId, stats and storage. Sell a car with TransferVehicle and remove one with DeleteVehicle.

Damage a car keeps

An owned car keeps its engine and body health, torn-off doors and burst tyres, but not its dents. It's saved when the driver gets out, every VehiclePositionSaveInterval, and when the car is stored or leaves the world. It's put back when the car leaves a garage, or after a restart when a player comes near, and only ever adds damage. Config.VehicleDamage.remember = false turns it off.

A wreck comes back with its engine at Config.VehicleDamage.engineFloor (100): smoking, never on fire. The damage is five stats, read with GetVehicleStat:

StatValue
engineHealth, bodyHealth0 to 1000, GTA's scale; below 400 the engine smokes
doorsOffBit n is door n: 0 front left, 1 front right, 2 rear left, 3 rear right, 4 bonnet, 5 boot
tyresFlat, tyresRimBits over GTA's tyre numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 45, 47
A repair must clear the damage, or the next spawn puts it back. Call ClearVehicleDamage as you fix the car.

Vehicle data

SetVehicleData attaches anything that should stick to a car and isn't a gauge, a mod or an item: a part's grade, a finance flag. Values are anything JSON-encodable, never clamped or drawn. The calls are in Vehicle data & handling.

exports.whip_core:SetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo', { grade = 'A' })     -- server
local turbo = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleData(vehicleId, 'turbo')        -- any client
If it is...Use
a number with a range a player should watch movea vehicle stat
items in slotsa store
a GTA mod: colour, extra, wheelproperties
anything else that should stick to the carvehicle data
  • A key belongs to the resource that wrote it. Anyone can read it; only the writer can change or clear it.
  • It follows the car, not the entity, through garaging, despawning and restarts, and is deleted with the car.
  • It isn't a database: 32 keys per resource per car, not indexed. To query it or keep history, build your own table.
  • Every player near the car can read it, so keep no secrets in it.

Events

Server events, for AddEventHandler; a client can't send them. Don't fire them yourself: listeners would hear something that didn't happen.

EventPayloadFires when
whip_core:vehicle:created{ vehicleId, ownerCharId }Any path makes a vehicle
whip_core:vehicle:ownerChanged{ vehicleId, from, to }A vehicle changes character
whip_core:vehicle:deleted{ vehicleId, ownerCharId, wasOut }A vehicle stops existing. Remove your own per-car data here
whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged{ vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, resource }Vehicle data is set or removed, by resource
whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged{ vehicleId, plate, locked, source }A car is locked or unlocked by anything; source when a player did it
whip_core:vehicle:spawned{ vehicleId, entity, netId, plate, model, session, temp? }An owned car comes out, or a temp car is made (temp = true)
whip_core:vehicle:despawned{ vehicleId, netId }An owned car leaves the world; the record stays. Its next spawn has a new netId
whip_core:vehicle:released{ vehicleId, reason, temp }WHIP lets go of a street car or removes a temp car; the vehicleId then means nothing. reason: 'expired', 'idle', 'gone', 'stopped', 'despawned', 'deleted', 'released' (ReleaseTag) or 'failed'
whip_core:vehicle:registered{ vehicleId, plate, model, session, source }WHIP takes on a street car (driven, lockpicked, at a pump, AdoptVehicle); session is always true, source the reporting player if any
whip_core:vehicle:claimed{ vehicleId, from, ownerCharId }A street car becomes owned; from is its session id
whip_core:vehicle:plateChanged{ vehicleId, from, to }A car's plate changed
whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked{ vehicleId, plate, source }A player lockpicked a car open
AddEventHandler('whip_core:vehicle:lockpicked', function(data)
    local coords = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(data.source))
    TriggerClientEvent('dispatch:alert', -1, 'Vehicle Break-In', coords)
end)

Full lists: Server Events and Client Events.

Hearing a stat change

A stat changing has no event. On the server, OnVehicleStatChanged calls you when a named stat moves on any car, whoever registered it. It's called on a change, not on a clock: "full for ten seconds" needs your own timer.

-- A coolant add-on reacting to whip_autos' boost
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChanged('boost', function(vehicleId, value, previous)
    if value >= 20 then --[[ flat out ]] end
end)

Vehicles API

Calls for a car's whole life: reading it, keys and locks, making, spawning and garaging cars, ownership, appearance and the catalog. Every call names the car with a vehicle reference. New to vehicles? Read Vehicles & Keys first.

Reading a car

GetVehicle(vehicleId, opts?)SERVER

A copy of everything the server knows about a vehicle, or nil if WHIP doesn't know it. Editing the copy changes nothing.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicleId or a vehicle reference: { plate = }, { netId = }, { entity = }
optstable?{ occupants = true } adds who is sitting in it (slower: it checks every player)
Returns: table|nil
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle(vehicleId)   -- or GetVehicle({ plate = 'ABC123' })
if not v then return false, 'No such vehicle' end
print(v.plate, v.model, v.owner.charId, v.state, v.locked)

Also on it: displayName and class (nil for a model the catalog lacks), vehType, owner.name, owner.online, garage, coords, heading, temp, session, secure, spawned, entity, netId, stats, data, properties, occupants when asked, and storage once the car's storage is loaded (storage.trunk = { slots, maxWeight, used }).

Rental or street car? session = true means nobody owns it, rentals included. temp = true means a SpawnTempVehicle car only.
GetVehicle(vehicleId)CLIENT

Everything this client knows about a vehicle, or nil when it isn't streamed in here: live damage, colours, lock and engine state and every occupant, but not ownership or the garage. Takes a vehicleId or a vehicle reference.

Returns: table|nil: vehicleId, plate, mine, hasKey, entity, netId, model, modelHash, class (GTA's number), vehType, session, keyInIgnition (your car only), coords, heading, locked, engineOn, engineHealth, bodyHealth, colorPrimary, colorSecondary, occupants ({ seat, ped, isPlayer, serverId }), stats (a copy, defaults filled in), data
local v = exports.whip_core:GetVehicle({ entity = GetVehiclePedIsIn(PlayerPedId(), false) })
GetVehiclesOf(who)SERVER

Every vehicle a person owns, as full snapshots.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: a server id, or { charId = n }, online or not
Returns: table[], or {}, why when who names nobody
IsPlayerDrivingVehicle / IsPlayerInVehicleSERVER

Is this player driving this vehicle, or in it at all? Three natives and no copy, so prefer these to GetVehicle on a hot path.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
Returns: boolean
GetVehicleDriver(vehicle)SERVER

Whose game drives this car: the player at the wheel, or the one whose game plays a Director take (a recorded drive) on it. Ask before moving a car to another game to pull it: a take's game reclaims its car every two seconds.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicleId, { netId } / { entity } (any networked car, WHIP's or not), or { plate }
Returns: source, 'seat' | 'take', or nil when nobody drives it (parked, an NPC at the wheel)
GetPlayerVehicle(source, opts)SERVER

Which WHIP car this player sits in, from the server's view, not the client's word. An in-car item (nitrous, a part fitted from inside) starts here.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
optstable?{ driver = true }: only the driver's seat counts
Returns: vehicleId, or false, why, a sentence for the player: not in a vehicle, not driving, or a car WHIP doesn't look after
GetPlayerSeat(source)SERVER

Which seat this player is in, as the server sees it, in any vehicle including street cars. Seat -1 is the driver's, 0 the front passenger's, then the rear seats.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
Returns: { seat, driver, vehicleId, netId } (vehicleId is nil for a street car), or false, why: not in a vehicle, or still getting in
GetVehiclePosition(vehicleId)SERVER

Where a vehicle is right now, for a distance check or a blip. A garaged, despawned or lost car returns nil, so a near check fails. Last seen: GetVehicle(id).coords. A SecureEvent with a 'vehicle' param checks distance with near = { at = 'vehicle' }.

Returns: x, y, z, or nil if the car isn't in the world
IsVehicleWrecked(vehicle)SERVER

Is this car blown up or sunk? A job's "car lost" check. The game running the car reports a sinking.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: boolean: false for a car not out in the world

Keys and locks

A car's boot, glovebox and ignition are stores: address them as { kind = 'vehicle', id = vehicleId, sub = 'trunk' } (or 'glovebox', 'key'), where id may be a reference such as { plate = 'ABC 123' }. Use StoreRead, StoreCount, GetItemAt, StoreGive, StoreTake, StoreMove, OpenStore and CloseStore.

SetVehicleLocked(vehicleId, locked)SERVER

Lock or unlock a vehicle; saved, and whip_core:vehicle:lockChanged fires when the state changes. After a restart a car is as it was left, except one locked with its own key in the ignition, which is unlocked. A car leaving a garage is locked unless its own key is in the ignition.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
lockedbooltrue = locked
Returns: bool, string|nil
GiveVehicleKey(who, vehicleId, opts?)SERVER

Put a vehicle_key for the car in a player's inventory. A player who already holds one is refused, unless opts.spare asks for another.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person who is playing: server id, or { charId = n }
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
opts.sparebooltrue cuts a key even when they hold one, a second key to hand to someone
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Already has a key for this vehicle', no room, not online)
ChangeVehicleLocks(vehicleId)SERVER

Change an owned car's locks. Every key of it cut so far stops fitting, wherever it is: someone's pockets (playing or not), a stash, a boot, its own ignition or the ground. Keys cut after fit, and the change lasts through a restart. A car running on an old key in its ignition stops. Old keys stay where they are as items that no longer open anything. A street car or a temporary one is refused; a temporary car takes secure = true instead.

-- The owner lost a key: new locks, and one new key for them
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:ChangeVehicleLocks(vehicleId)
if ok then exports.whip_core:GiveVehicleKey(source, vehicleId) end
ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Only a car someone owns', 'Vehicle not found', a save that failed)
CountVehicleKeys(vehicleId)SERVER

How many keys fit the car now, wherever they are: every character's pockets (playing or not), every stash, every car's boot, glovebox and ignition, and the ground. A key inside another item (a bag), a resource's own stores and an open panel's slots aren't counted. Keys from before a ChangeVehicleLocks don't fit, so they aren't counted either.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: number, or false, reason (no such vehicle, the database couldn't be read)
RemoveVehicleKey(who, vehicleId)SERVER

Take every key that fits this car from all of a player's containers: an impound confiscating keys.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person who is playing: server id, or { charId = n }
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
Returns: bool, string?: true if any key was removed, else false and why ('They have no key for that vehicle', 'Player not loaded', ...)
HasVehicleKey(who, vehicleId)SERVER

Whether a person has a key for the vehicle in their pockets. A character who isn't playing is read from the database.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: a server id, or { charId = n }
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: bool, string?: false and why when it couldn't ask (no such person, a bad reference)
GetPlayerVehicleKeys(who)SERVER

Every vehicle key in a person's pockets. A character who isn't playing is read from the database.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: a server id, or { charId = n }
Returns: { [vehicleId] = plateText }; {}, why for no such person

Engine holds

HoldVehicleEngine(vehicleId, key, reason)SERVER

Keep a car's engine off and tell the driver why: no fuel, a flat battery, an immobiliser. While any hold is on, the engine won't start and a running one stops; the car still rolls. A hold ends when you release it, your resource stops, or the car's id goes for good.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
keystringNames your hold; the same key again replaces its reason
reasonstringShown to the driver, 80 letters at most
Returns: true, or false, why (no such vehicle)
ReleaseVehicleEngine(vehicleId, key?)SERVER

Release your hold key; with no key, all your holds on the car.

Returns: true when one went, false, why when you had none
GetVehicleEngineHold(vehicleId)SERVER

Whether anything holds the car's engine off, whoever's hold it is.

Returns: the reason shown, or nil

Making cars

CreateOwnedVehicle(source, data, opts)SERVER

Make a car owned by a player's character, the only way a resource mints one. With opts it also spawns the car and gives the key; if either fails the car is removed and you get false, reason. The owner comes from the player record, never from data.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe receiving player
datatable{ model, plate?, garage?, stats?, properties?, vehType?, trunkSlots?, trunkMaxWeight?, gloveboxSlots?, gloveboxMaxWeight? }
data.statstable?Starting values, { fuel = 100 }; one left out reads its registered default
data.garagestring?An existing garage (GetNearestGarage, GetGarage); default the default garage
data.vehTypestring?Left out, the catalog's class picks bike, boat, heli or plane
optstable?{ giveKey?, spawnAt? }: spawnAt (vector4, vector3 or { x, y, z, heading }) makes it out there; else it starts garaged. data.state = 'out' without it is refused; data.x/y/z aren't read
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err, boolean|nil saved. Read the plate from GetVehicle(vehicleId).plate. Refused before any car is made: an occupied spawnAt ('Something is already parked in that spot'), or a builder in Isolate world ('Leave Isolate world first: cars come out in the shared world')
local canOut, outWhy = exports.whip_core:CanBringOutVehicleFor(source)
if not canOut then return false, outWhy end
local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, 250000, { reason = 'Adder' })
if not receipt then return false, err end

local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:CreateOwnedVehicle(source, { model = 'adder' }, {
    giveKey = true, spawnAt = vector4(-56.7, -1097.2, 26.4, 160.0),
})
if not vehicleId then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) return false, why end
Don't refund on false, err, true. saved means a database fault after the car was saved with the payment; it reaches their garage with its key once it reads back. Refund only on a plain false.
CanBringOutVehicleFor(source)SERVER

Whether a car can be brought out for this player now. Ask before charging for a car with spawnAt: a builder in the Director's Isolate world is refused, since cars come out in the shared world.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player the car is for
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil why
VehicleModelExists(model)SERVER

Whether this game has a vehicle called model, add-ons included. Players' games report their lists at the character screen; the server saves them per platform and game build and drops a name unreported for 14 days. Spawning a missing model is refused with 'There is no vehicle called "x" in this game'.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringThe model name, like 'sultan'
Returns: boolean|nil: nil before any game has reported, or for a model not on a full list (20,000 names); nothing is refused then, so test == false
SpawnTempVehicle(model, coords, opts)SERVER

A temporary car: a rental, a job van, a test drive. Nobody owns it and it's never saved, but it has an id, stats, data, a boot and keys. It's removed when your resource stops, despawnAfter runs out, nobody is near for ten minutes, or DespawnVehicle; its key goes too and whip_core:vehicle:released fires.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringVehicle model name
coordsvector4|vector3|tableWhere; { x, y, z, heading } works too
opts.forSourcenumber?Who it's for; they get a key unless giveKey = false
opts.despawnAfternumber?Seconds until it's removed
opts.lockedboolean?Spawns locked; false stands open
opts.keyInIgnitionboolean?A key in the ignition, so anyone at the wheel can start it
opts.idleDespawnboolean?false: never removed for being left alone
opts.tagstring?One of your tags: ReleaseTag removes the car and stops new spawns
opts.secureboolean?No lockpick or hack; only a key cut for this car works
opts.forceboolean?Spawn on an occupied spot (GTA pushes things aside); else refused
opts.plate, opts.vehTypeanyNormally left out
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err
local vehicleId, err = exports.whip_core:SpawnTempVehicle('blista', vector4(x, y, z, h), {
    forSource = source, despawnAfter = 1800,   -- a rental, gone in half an hour
})
despawnAfter removes the car even while driven. Warn the driver first.
ClaimVehicle(vehicle, who, opts) · SetVehiclePlate(vehicle, plate)SERVER

ClaimVehicle makes a car nobody owns (temp or street) an owned one: the end of a boosting job. The new car (new id, new plate unless given) keeps the model, look, fuel, boot and glovebox, and takes the old one's place with the driver still in it. A failure changes nothing; a model the catalog doesn't know is refused. SetVehiclePlate changes any car's plate; old keys still fit.

ParamTypeDescription
whonumber|tableA person: server id, or { charId = n }
opts.platestring?Its new plate (8 characters at most, unused); default a new one
opts.hereboolean?false: put away in their garage instead
opts.garagestring?Its garage (default the default garage)
opts.keyboolean?false: no key for them
opts.reasonstring?For their activity log
opts.leavefunction?function(metadata, item): true leaves that stack in the old car
Returns: ClaimVehicle: the new vehicleId (plus a note when it waits in its garage), or false, reason; fires whip_core:vehicle:claimed. SetVehiclePlate: true, or false, reason; fires whip_core:vehicle:plateChanged
AdoptVehicle(plate | { entity } | { netId })SERVER

Register a car already in the world as a session vehicle; a car WHIP knows returns its id. It never creates a car. On the client, ResolveVehicle does this from an entity.

ParamTypeDescription
refstring|table{ entity = vehicle }, { netId = networkId }, or a plate (the first car wearing it). Prefer the car
ref.playernumber?When a player's action brings it in: counts against their street-car limit (20)
Returns: number|false vehicleId, string|nil err
Not a lookup. It searches every car and pins the one it finds (GTA can't clear it), without the player limits (20 m, 20 cars). To read by plate, use GetVehicle({ plate = }).

In and out of the world

SpawnVehicle(vehicleId, coords?)SERVER

Put a vehicle in the world; the server creates the entity. A car already out is moved, not cloned.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberThe vehicle to place
coordsvector3|vector4?Default its saved position; a vector4's w is the heading. Refused if occupied: 'Something is already parked in that spot', 'Someone is standing in that spot'
Returns: number|false: the network ID, or false and an error
DespawnVehicle(vehicleId, opts?)SERVER

Take a vehicle out of the world into the garage it's filed under, even with somebody inside; storage is flushed first. It stays put away after a restart. A temp car is removed for good.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
opts.garagestring?Put it away in this garage instead (an impound). Only an owned car that is out: 'A street car cannot be put in a garage', 'A temporary car cannot be put in a garage', 'Vehicle is already stored', 'No such garage: …'
opts.refuseOccupiedboolean?Refuse a car with somebody inside: 'Somebody is still in that vehicle'. On by default with a garage, off without one
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err: success if already out of the world; false, 'Vehicle is busy' mid-spawn, store or delete (retry shortly)
A street car stays in the world. WHIP hands it back to GTA and forgets it: its id means nothing, its boot and glovebox items are logged as lost, and released fires.
RetrieveVehicle(vehicleId, garageKey)SERVER

Take a vehicle out of a garage: marks it out and locked. Then spawn it where you choose.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
garageKeystring?Default: its own garage
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
local ok, err = exports.whip_core:RetrieveVehicle(vehicleId)
if ok then exports.whip_core:SpawnVehicle(vehicleId, vector4(x, y, z, heading)) end

Ownership

TransferVehicle(vehicleId, newOwner, opts)SERVER

Sell a vehicle to another player. Writes the owner, re-syncs both players' lists and fires whip_core:vehicle:ownerChanged.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
newOwnernumber|tableThe buyer, online: server id, or { charId = n }
optstable?{ giveKey, revokeOldKeys }, both default true
Returns: boolean, string|nil: 'The new owner must be online', 'Session vehicles have no owner' (use ClaimVehicle), 'Already owned by that character'
The seller can keep a working key. revokeOldKeys only empties their pockets while online; keys in a stash, a boot, on the ground or in the ignition still work. With full pockets the buyer gets no key and this still returns true.
DeleteVehicle(vehicleId)SERVER

Destroy an owned car for good, with its boot, glovebox, ignition and entity, in one transaction. Items are logged as lost; fires whip_core:vehicle:deleted. Any resource may call it, so check who may first.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
Returns: boolean, string|nil
A street car stays in the world, forgotten; a temp car is removed. To make a street car vanish, read its entity first, then DeleteVehicle and DeleteEntity.

Appearance

Properties are GTA's look on an entity, set on the client (SetVehicleProperties). Appearance is the look WHIP stores for a vehicleId, on the server. A shop holds the car, previews with properties, saves what was paid for with SetVehicleAppearance, strips the rest with RestoreVehicleAppearance, then releases the hold.

SetVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, props, opts?)SERVER

Change and store how a vehicle looks. Props merge over the current look, one level into mods, so setting mod 11 keeps mod 23. Performance mods are allowed; plate and model are never written.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
propstableFields to apply ({} for none)
optstable?data = { key = value }, clearData = { 'key' }: your vehicle data, in the same write
Returns: true, or false, why with nothing changed. A session car (street, rental) keeps the look only while it exists
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, { mods = { ['23'] = 4 }, color1 = 27 },
    { data = { myStance = { height = -0.05 } } })
RestoreVehicleAppearance(vehicleId)SERVER

Push the stored look back onto the car for everyone: the undo for a client's preview.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: boolean, string|nil
Previews replicate. Mods set by the client in control show to everyone, so an abandoned preview leaves unpaid parts on until this runs.
HoldVehicleAppearance(vehicleId, held)CLIENT

Mark a car as being previewed, so WHIP doesn't report or log the preview. If your resource stops while holding it, WHIP restores the stored look.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumberVehicle ID
heldbooleantrue to hold, false to release
Returns: true, or false, reason: another resource holds it, or the hold isn't yours. Releasing an unheld car is true
Always release it, on close and on death, or this client never reports the car again.

Catalog and pictures

GetVehicleCatalog()SERVER

The vehicle catalog, keyed by model: 930 cars from server/vehicle_catalog_list.lua, plus packs' cars from RegisterVehicles. A car has a picture when a media pack has its img/vehicles/<model>.webp.

Returns: a copy, { [model] = { model, displayName, class, hasImage, image, inGame } }: image is a URL for your NUI or false; don't sell inGame == false
RegisterVehicles(list)SERVER

Add a car pack's cars to the catalog while the pack runs. The list is the whole list: a car left out later goes, and all go when the pack stops. A model WHIP lists already keeps its name and class and takes your picture. List pictures in your files { }.

ParamTypeDescription
listtable[]{ model, name, class, image }; class is a name below or GetVehicleClass's number
Returns: true, or false, why and nothing added (missing model, unknown class, picture not in your resource, another pack's model)
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterVehicles({
        { model = 'mypack_gt', name = 'Velo GT', class = 'sports', image = 'img/mypack_gt.webp' },
    })
end)

Classes: compacts sedans suvs coupes muscle sportsclassics sports super motorcycles offroad industrial utility vans cycles boats helicopters planes service emergency military commercial trains openwheel.

GetVehicleImage(model)SERVER

The URL of a vehicle's picture, from a media pack over cfx-nui, for any resource's NUI.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringModel name, any case
Returns: string|nil: e.g. https://cfx-nui-whip_media_previews/img/vehicles/sultan.webp
HasVehicleImage(model)SERVER

Whether a model has a picture.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringModel name, any case
Returns: boolean

Client vehicles API

Client calls for finding cars, checking keys, previewing a look, taking network control, and the points and prompts on a car. All are instant cache reads except ResolveVehicle and TakeVehicleControl, which wait.

Finding cars

GetVehicleId(entity)CLIENT

A car's vehicleId from the cache, or nil for a car WHIP has never seen (ResolveVehicle registers it).

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumber|tableEntity handle, or { entity = veh }
Returns: number|nil
GetVehicleEntity(vehicleId)CLIENT

The entity handle for a vehicleId, for GTA natives, or nil when the car isn't streamed in nearby. WHIP's own exports take the id itself.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: number|nil: entity handle
ResolveVehicle(entity)CLIENT

A car's vehicleId, registering it as a session vehicle first if WHIP doesn't know it, which costs a server round trip.

ParamTypeDescription
entitynumber|tableEntity handle, or { entity = veh }
Returns: number, or false, why, a sentence for the player: not there or not a vehicle, no plate, the plate belongs to an owned car elsewhere, or too many street cars held
local vehicleId, why = exports.whip_core:ResolveVehicle(ctx.entity)   -- in onSelect
if not vehicleId then return ctx.refuse(why) end
It waits. Use it in onSelect, never in canInteract, a label, a loop or frequent code.
GetNearbyVehicles(radius)CLIENT

Every vehicle near the local player, closest first, from GetGamePool('CVehicle').

ParamTypeDescription
radiusnumber?Metres; default 25, max 100
Returns: table[]: { entity, plate, vehicleId, distance, model }
HasVehicleKey(vehicleId)CLIENT

Whether the local player has a key for a vehicle, from the cache. { plate = } finds a car that isn't streamed in here too.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: bool
if exports.whip_core:HasVehicleKey({ plate = plate }) then ... end

Look and network control

These change the entity now, unsaved; the server stores a look with SetVehicleAppearance (see Appearance). Each needs network control first, or the natives silently do nothing.

GetVehicleProperties(vehicle)CLIENT

How a vehicle looks now, in the shape SetVehicleProperties takes. Toggle mods 18, 20 and 22 come back as turbo, smokeEnabled and xenon, not in mods (slots 0–49).

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: { model, plate, plateIndex, color1, color2, customColor1, customColor2, pearlescent, wheelColor, mods, wheelType, turbo, smokeEnabled, xenon, tyreSmoke, neonColor, neonEnabled, windowTint, livery, extras, dirtLevel, headlightColor, interiorColor, dashboardColor }; empty for an invalid handle
SetVehicleProperties(vehicle, props)CLIENT

Apply a look, unsaved: right for previews. Mods are networked, so everyone sees it; the car reverts when the server next pushes its appearance.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
propstableAs GetVehicleProperties returns; absent fields are left alone
Returns: true, or false, why: no such car here, or a bare entity handle (unlike QBCore and ox_lib, pass { entity = veh })
local before = exports.whip_core:GetVehicleProperties({ entity = veh })
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleProperties({ entity = veh }, { livery = 3 })   -- preview
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleProperties({ entity = veh }, before)          -- undo
SetVehicleExtras(vehicle, extras)CLIENT

Switch a vehicle's extras (light bars, roof racks) and keep its damage. Unsaved; the server stores them with SetVehicleAppearance's extras.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
extrastable{ [n] = true } on, false off, extras 1 to 14; missing ones are left alone
Returns: how many were switched
Use this, not SetVehicleExtra, which repairs the car (health, doors, tyres, fuel, dirt). Dents still can't be kept.
TakeVehicleControl(vehicle, opts)CLIENT

Take network control of a vehicle: ask, wait, retry. It waits, so call it from a thread or handler through Whip.core. Refused while another player drives, since the car would rubber-band: make the change on the driver's client.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
optstable?{ attempts = 3, wait = 500 }: tries, and milliseconds per try
Returns: true, or false, why: 'no such vehicle', 'another player is driving it', 'control was not granted'
if Whip.core:TakeVehicleControl({ entity = veh }) then
    Whip.core:SetVehicleExtras({ entity = veh }, { [1] = true, [2] = false })
end

Points on a car

GetVehiclePoint(vehicle, action)CLIENT

Where a named point on a vehicle is, on the side nearest the player: 'fuel' (the filler), 'engine', 'storage' (boot), 'mount' (bike), 'board' (boat), or yours. A car's filler is its petrol cap, else above a rear wheel, on the side in Config.VehicleFillers, else its side tank's, else one picked per model.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
actionstringThe point's name
Returns: { x, y, z, heading, side, fixed }, or nil if the model has none. side: 'left', 'right', 'front', 'rear'; heading faces out of it; fixed: the side doesn't follow the player
SetVehiclePointRules(action, rules)CLIENT

Define a point of your own (a charging port). WHIP's and other resources' points can't be taken; yours go when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
actionstringYour point's name
rulestable{ default = { place, … }, bike = { … }, boat = { … } }, tried in order. A place: a bone name or list, 'entry', 'box', 'box:rear', 'box:front' or 'filler'
Returns: true, or false, why
exports.whip_core:SetVehiclePointRules('charge', { default = { 'petrolcap', 'box:front' } })

Adding options to a vehicle part

Add a choice to a part's prompt with AddAction and at = { vehiclePart = ... }; ctx.entity is the car. The parts are 'hood', 'trunk', 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r', 'door_pside_r', and the one prompt of a 'bike', 'bicycle' or 'boat'. A 'hood' option shows only while the bonnet is open or torn off: put engine work there.

Whip.register(function()
    for _, door in ipairs({ 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r', 'door_pside_r' }) do
        exports.whip_core:AddAction({
            id = 'jerrycan:' .. door,   -- one action per part
            at = { vehiclePart = door },
            icon = 'fuel', label = 'Refuel (jerry can)',
            canInteract = function(ctx) return JerryCanInHand() and not TankFull(ctx.entity) end,
            onSelect = function(ctx)
                TriggerServerEvent('myfuel:pourCan', NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(ctx.entity))
            end,
        })
    end
end)

Vehicle data & handling API

Attach your own data to a car, react to it on every client, and change how the car drives and how its dial reads. For when to use data, see Vehicle data.

Vehicle data

SetVehicleData / GetVehicleData / ClearVehicleDataSERVERCLIENT

Attach data to a vehicle by name: saved in the car's row and replicated to every client with the car in scope. Set and Clear are server only; Get works on both sides, and with no key returns a copy of everything the car carries.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference ({ entity = veh } for a handle)
keystring1–40 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_]
valueanyAnything JSON-encodable, false included; nil removes it
Returns: writes boolean, string|nil; reads the value (a stored false reads as false) or a copy of the block
A key belongs to the resource that wrote it first. Writing or clearing another resource's key is refused, naming the owner. Each resource gets 32 keys per car.
SetVehicleData(vehicleId, values)SERVER

A table in place of the key sets several keys in one replication and one database write, for installing a kit. Each key still fires its own whip_core:vehicle:dataChanged after the commit.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
valuestable{ [key] = value }, keys as for one
Returns: number written, or false, reason when nothing was written
A batch can't remove keys (use ClearVehicleData). Keys past your 32 are skipped and logged; a batch that would take the block past 8 KB, or touches another resource's key, is refused whole.
ClearAllVehicleData(vehicleId)SERVER

Remove every key your resource put on a car: uninstalling a kit. Other resources' keys stay. Fires one dataChanged per key removed. Stats are untouched (see ClearVehicleStat).

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: boolean, string|nil: why not is no such vehicle, or the write failed
OnVehicleDataChanged(key, callback, id, opts)SERVER

Be called when one data key changes, on any vehicle: the server half of the client export, and cheaper than handling every dataChanged broadcast. Dropped when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe data key to watch
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, cleared, old), or one table with table = true
idstring?Only for two listeners on one key; the same id replaces
optstable?{ table = true, now = true }; may go third, in place of id
Returns: boolean registered
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:OnVehicleDataChanged('kit', function(change)
        if change.cleared then --[[ the kit came off; change.old is what it was ]] end
    end, { table = true, now = true })
end)
Use table = true: { vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, resource } (plus entity on the client).
