Positional order differs: the client's callback gets (vehicleId, value, old, entity), and OnVehicleStatChanged's (vehicleId, value, previous, cleared, source). now = true also calls it at once for every car with the key.
WatchVehicleData(key, data)CLIENT

Run code while a car in scope carries a data key: the data twin of WatchVehicleStat. For what each client must do to a car itself because GTA doesn't replicate it: an engine sound, wheel stance, handling.

FieldTypeDescription
onGainedfunction?(entity, value, vehicleId): a car in scope has the key (cars already in scope are announced on registration)
onChangedfunction?(entity, value, old, vehicleId): a new value; without it, onLost(old) then onGained(new)
onLostfunction?(entity, value, vehicleId): the key went or the car left scope; value is what it was
onStartfunction?(entity, value, vehicleId): starts for the car (with driverOnly: you now drive it)
onStopfunction?(entity, value, vehicleId): you got out, the key or car went. A new value while started fires onStop(old), onStart(new)
driverOnlybool?Narrow onStart/onStop to the car you drive, for handling. Default false
idstring?Only for two watchers on one key; the same id replaces (with onStop)
Returns: string|false, string|nil: watcher id, or false and why
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleData('engine', {
    onGained = function(entity, value) ForceUseAudioGameObject(entity, value.audio) end,   -- every car in scope
    onStart  = function(entity, value) --[[ apply handling ]] end,                        -- you drive it
    onStop   = function(entity, value) --[[ restore handling ]] end,
    driverOnly = true,
})
Your resource stopping never reaches onStop. Put things back in your own onResourceStop too; a resource without dependency 'whip_core' also does it in Whip.onCoreLost. Values are compared by content, so another key changing doesn't re-fire you.
UnwatchVehicleData(watcherId)CLIENT

Stop one of your data watchers. Fires onStop for what it started, not onLost. Watchers also go when their resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id WatchVehicleData returned
Returns: boolean removed

Handling and power

Physics belongs to the driver, so set these from a driverOnly watcher's onStart (WatchVehicleStat or WatchVehicleData) and clear them in its onStop. They apply to one car at a time: asking for a different car puts the previous one back first.

SetVehicleHandlingLayer(vehicle, name, spec) · ClearVehicleHandlingLayer(name) · GetVehicleHandlingBase(vehicle, field)CLIENT

Never write handling yourself: declare a layer. WHIP captures each field's stock value, applies every resource's layers, and restores the car on every way out (layer cleared, another car, car gone, a resource stopping). Two features writing a field directly undo each other. Drivetrain changes are committed for you.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference
namestringYour layer's name, one per feature; setting it again replaces it
spec.settable?{ field = value }: absolute, in handling.meta units; CHandlingData floats (f…) and whole numbers (n…); gears kept to 1–7
spec.addtable?{ field = amount } (−1000 to 1000), added after every layer's set; layers' adds sum
spec.scaletable?{ field = factor } (0.01–100), applied after every set and add
spec.ordernumber?When two layers set one field, the higher wins. Default 0
Returns: Set → boolean, string|nil; Clear → boolean removed; GetVehicleHandlingBase → a field's value after every set and add, before scale
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = veh }, 'engine', { set = { fInitialDriveForce = 0.34 } })
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = veh }, 'tune', { scale = { fSuspensionForce = 1.2 } })
exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleHandlingLayer('tune')
More power is SetVehiclePower, not a layer. fInitialDriveMaxFlatVel is the gearing (speed at redline in top gear), so scaling it with a turbo stretches every gear.
SetVehiclePower(vehicle, name, multiplier) · ClearVehiclePower(name)CLIENT

Ask for more (or less) torque on the car this player drives: a turbo's boost, nitrous. Gearing is untouched, so more torque is more speed only where drag held the car back. Ask again as the amount changes; the car gets the product of every resource's ask each frame, and is normal again when nothing is asked.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference
namestringYour ask's name, one per feature; asking again replaces it
multipliernumber0 to 10: 1.25 is a quarter more torque, 1.0 the engine as it is
Returns: Set → boolean, string|nil; Clear → boolean removed
exports.whip_core:SetVehiclePower({ entity = veh }, 'turbo', 1.0 + 0.25 * boost)
Don't call SetVehicleCheatPowerIncrease yourself. The last write in a frame wins, so it undoes WHIP's.

The rev dial

SetVehicleRevRange(vehicle, engine)CLIENT

Say which engine a vehicle's rev dial follows, on this player's game. The dial uses the engine's model in Config.VehicleHud.rpmByModel, else rpmElectric for an electric motor, else its kind in rpmByClass. After an engine swap, name the donor: a dump truck with an F1 engine then revs to 15k.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference
enginestring|table|nilA model's spawn name; { max, idle? } in thousands of rpm (max 2–20, idle 0 or more, under max); or nil for its own engine
Returns: boolean, string|nil: why not is no such vehicle, not a vehicle model, a range out of bounds, or another running resource set it
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleRevRange({ entity = veh }, 'formula')   -- or { max = 11, idle = 1.2 }
Set it on every client, like the swap: in a WatchVehicleData watcher for every car in view, cleared in onLost. The car you're in updates at once; your settings go when your resource stops.
IsVehicleElectric(vehicle)CLIENT

Is the vehicle's engine electric? GTA's flag on its engine's model, its own or the one SetVehicleRevRange names. whip_fuel gives electric cars no fuel.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference
Returns: boolean: false for a vehicle not here, or a game build without the flag
SetVehicleDialGear(vehicle, gear)CLIENT

Set the forward gear the dial shows when your resource drives the gears (whip_autos keeps GTA in gear 1 and changes its ratio). Use 'speed' when you move the car yourself, as a recorded drive does: the dial works the gear out from speed and ratios, and shows R going backwards. Reverse and N stay the game's. This player's dial only; cleared when your resource stops. Clear it when you hand the car back: GTA's gearbox is put in the gear the dial showed.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicletable|numberA vehicle reference
gearnumber|string|nil1 to 20; 'speed'; or nil for the game's gear again
Returns: boolean, string|nil: why not is no such vehicle, a gear out of bounds, or another running resource set it
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleDialGear({ entity = veh }, 3)

Vehicle stats API

A vehicle stat is a number a car carries: fuel, nitrous, wear, boost. Register it once and WHIP saves it, replicates it to everyone in the car, draws its gauge and checks what clients report.

Registering a stat

RegisterVehicleStat(name, config)SERVER

Register a stat every vehicle can carry. It's saved with the car and replicated to everyone sitting in it. A hud block makes it a gauge around the rev dial (five at most are shown, by order).

FieldTypeDescription
defaultnumberWhat a vehicle starts on
min / maxnumberIts range
persistboolean|stringtrue (default): the value survives a restart. false: nothing does. 'presence': that the car has it, at its fitted value; written only when it appears or goes, for live fittings such as a turbo
decaynumber?Points changed every decayInterval; negative drains. Leave it out to disable: 0 still ticks
decayIntervalnumber?Seconds between decay steps. Default 10
hudtable?{ label, icon, color, order, iconOnly, showAboveZero, showWhenPresent, hideWhenEmpty, noCritical }. icon: an SVG path in a 24x24 box; order: lower first (fuel is 1); below 20% it flashes red unless noCritical. The dial draws gauges white, so color isn't used there; an iconOnly stat (an on/off light) gets no gauge
consumetable?{ maxRate, driverOnly, clearAtMin, interval, slack }: the client reports what it used. See consume and live
livetable?{ maxRate, driverOnly, interval, slack }: the client reports the current value
displaytable?How the value reads on its gauge and in /whip, instead of a percentage: { unit = 'psi', range = { -3, 30 } } (what min and max read); { unit = '°C', points = { { 0, 20 }, { 50, 90 }, { 100, 130 } } } (a curve, percent of range to reading); { ends = { 'E', 'F' } } (end labels, no number); decimals 0-2. The stat's range is unchanged
Returns: boolean, string|nil: ok, and why not
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterVehicleStat('nos', {
        default = 0, min = 0, max = 100,
        hud = { label = 'NOS', icon = 'M6 2h6v20H6z', color = '#60a5fa', order = 2 },
    })
end)
-- later, once a car has a bottle fitted
exports.whip_core:AddVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'nos', -10, 'mynos:boost')
clearAtMin requires default == min, or registration is refused: a cleared stat reads as its default, so it would refill itself by running out. Use it for installables, not for something every car has, like fuel.
  • Names are letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit, up to 32 characters. 'turbo-boost' or '2step' is refused.
  • Register before you write. Writes to an unregistered name are refused with 'unknown vehicle stat "x" — RegisterVehicleStat it first'.
  • The registration is your resource's and is dropped when it stops; stored values stay. WHIP's names (engine, the damage stats) can't be taken; fuel is whip_fuel's.
  • A car only carries what it has. An absent stat reads as its default, so registering costs nothing on cars without it.

Reading and writing

GetVehicleStat / SetVehicleStat / AddVehicleStat / GetVehicleStatsSERVER

Read and write stats. Writes are clamped to the stat's range, saved and replicated. GetVehicleStat and GetVehicleStats also work on the client, for a car streamed in nearby.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
namestringA registered stat name
value / deltanumberWhat to set it to, or add to it
changeSourcestring?A label for the change, e.g. 'refuel:pump'
Returns: GetVehicleStat → number|nil; GetVehicleStats → { [name] = value }, defaults filled in (stored only: below); writes → boolean, string|nil (no such car, not a number, unregistered stat)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStat(vehicleId, 'fuel', 100.0, 'refuel:pump')
SetVehicleStats(vehicleId, values, changeSource)SERVER

Write several stats to one car in a single replication: fitting a kit, resetting a car. Each single write re-sends the car's whole block.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
valuestable{ [statName] = value }: unregistered names and non-numbers are skipped and logged
changeSourcestring?A label for the change events
Returns: number written, or false, reason when none took
HasVehicleStat(vehicle, name)CLIENTSERVER

Does this car actually carry the stat, rather than read as its default? Use it whenever you mean "is one fitted". In a loop, prefer WatchVehicleStat.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
namestringRegistered stat name
Returns: boolean
GetVehicleStat(veh, name) > 0 isn't the same. An absent stat reads as its default, so a stat resting above zero would read as fitted on every car.
GetVehicleStats(vehicleId, { stored = true })SERVER

Only the stats a car actually stores, no defaults: nil for an installable means not fitted. The vehicle-list payloads send this, so a garage card can tell a spent bottle from none.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
opts.storedbooleantrue: stored values only
Returns: { [name] = value }, a copy; empty for an unknown vehicle
ClearVehicleStat(vehicleId, name)SERVER

Take a stat off one car: the part comes off. Reads fall back to the default, and the change is announced with cleared = true. It also resets a live stat's rate check, so a refit starts from idle.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
namestringRegistered stat name
Returns: boolean, string|nil: true includes already absent; false with the reason (no such vehicle, a bad name)
Setting it to zero isn't the same. Zero leaves the stat on the car (a bottle fitted and empty); this is the only call that removes it.
PurgeVehicleStat(name)SERVER

Delete a stat's values from every car, for good, each as ClearVehicleStat does: for retiring a stat. Stopping a resource never does this, so a restart never wipes a fitted part.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe stat to retire
Returns: number of cars that had a value, or false, reason when another running resource registered it (anyone may purge a stat with no running owner)
ClearVehicleDamage(vehicle)SERVER

Forget the damage a car keeps, so its next spawn is like new. Call it with a repair: it doesn't fix the car in the world, which only the game running it can do.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
Returns: boolean, string|nil (no such vehicle)

Listening for changes

OnVehicleStatChanged(name, callback, id, opts)SERVER

Be called when one stat changes, on any car, yours or another resource's. Declare it in Whip.register with your stats, so it comes back after a whip_core restart; it's dropped when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringA stat's name, or '*' for every stat (server only, and the costly one)
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, previous, cleared, source); for '*', (vehicleId, name, value, previous, cleared, source); or one table with table = true (change.key is the stat)
idany?Only for two listeners on one stat; the same id replaces
optstable?{ table = true, now = true }; may go third. now reports every car carrying the stat at once, with source = 'now'. now = 'all' (named stat) visits every car WHIP has, defaults included, for decisions from the value (an engine hold); registering again after the default changed visits them again
Returns: boolean registered
exports.whip_core:OnVehicleStatChanged('fuel', function(change)
    -- change.vehicleId, change.key, change.value, change.old, change.cleared, change.source
end, { table = true, now = true })
The callback must not wait. It runs inside the stat write: put slow work (a database write) in a CreateThread.
OnVehicleStatChanged(name, callback, id, opts)CLIENT

Be called when a stat's value changes on any car in scope. Use it for the number; use WatchVehicleStat for a car having the stat. Takes the server's table and now options, third or after an id.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringRegistered stat name
callbackfunction(vehicleId, value, old, entity), or with table = true: { vehicleId, key, value, old, cleared, entity }
Returns: boolean registered

Reacting to a stat: WatchVehicleStat

WatchVehicleStat runs your code while a car carries a stat. WHIP is already told when a stat appears or goes on any car in scope, so you never poll or cache. Pick the right pair of callbacks:

onGained / onLostonStart / onStop
Tells youwhat's true in the worldwhat this watcher is doing
Fires forevery car in scope, ignoring driverOnlyonly what whileHeld runs for
Getting outnothing: the car still has itonStop
Use fora badge, a sound, an effect on any car nearbysetting up and undoing your own work

If you change a car and must put it back, use onStart/onStop: onStop covers getting out, losing the stat, the car despawning and the part being pulled. Set driverOnly for anything touching handling or physics: you only own the car you drive.

-- A turbo resource, in full: no loop, no cache
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleStat('boost', {
    onStart   = function(entity)             captureHandling(entity) end,
    whileHeld = function(entity, value, dt) simulate(entity, dt)     end,
    onStop    = function()                   restoreHandling()        end,
    interval   = 50,     -- ms between whileHeld calls; 0 is every frame
    driverOnly = true,
})

-- The one end onStop never hears: this resource stopping. restoreHandling must be safe twice.
AddEventHandler('onResourceStop', function(res)
    if res == GetCurrentResourceName() then restoreHandling() end
end)
Start interval at 50. 0 runs every frame: 120 calls a second at 120 fps. A resource without dependency 'whip_core' also restores in Whip.onCoreLost.
WatchVehicleStat(name, data)CLIENT

Run code while a car in scope carries a stat. Cars already carrying it are announced on registration. name may be a list: then every callback gets the stat's name second (onGained(entity, name, value)), and one id covers them all.

FieldTypeDescription
onGainedfunction?(entity, value): a car in scope gained the stat
onLostfunction?(entity): a car in scope lost it
onStartfunction?(entity, value): whileHeld is about to run for this car
onStopfunction?(entity): whileHeld stopped for this car
whileHeldfunction?(entity, value, dt), repeatedly; dt is real seconds, a stall clamped to 0.25 s (or twice your interval). Return a number to show it on this client's gauge until onStop
intervalnumber?ms between whileHeld calls. Default 0 (every frame)
driverOnlybool?Narrow whileHeld, onStart, onStop to the car you drive. Default false
Returns: string|false, string|nil: watcher id, or false and why (a bad name or table)
With a list, whileHeld runs once per stat. For one job per car, track what's fitted with onStart/onStop and run your own loop only while something is.
UnwatchVehicleStat(watcherId)CLIENT

Stop one of your watchers. Fires onStop for what it was running, not onLost. Watchers also go when their resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id from WatchVehicleStat; a list's id stops every stat in it
Returns: boolean removed
SetVehicleStatWatchInterval(watcherId, ms)CLIENT

Change how often one of your watchers' whileHeld runs. 0 is every frame; tens of milliseconds is plenty for most.

ParamTypeDescription
watcherIdstringThe id from WatchVehicleStat; a list's id sets every stat in it
msnumberMilliseconds between runs
Returns: boolean: false for the same interval again, or an id that isn't yours

Stats the client drives: consume and live

Some values only the client knows: nitrous burned, boost, engine heat. A stat declared consume or live lets the client report them, and WHIP does the rest: one batched event per car, the driver check (driverOnly, default true), and a cap measured against the wall clock, so a modified client gets the same ramp as an honest one. A report lost to the rate limit costs nothing: the next carries the current picture.

consumelive
The valueonly fallsrises and falls
Client reportshow much was usedwhat it's worth now
Client callsConsumeVehicleStat, ConsumeVehicleStatsReportVehicleStat
Server capshow fast it drainshow fast it rises
Forfuel, nitrous, tyre wearturbo boost, engine heat, charge
FieldDefaultMeaning
maxRaterequiredUnits per second, flat out: the ceiling the server believes
driverOnlytrueOnly the driver may report
interval1.0 / 0.5 sHow often the client sends (consume / live); at least 0.25 s
slack1.25Headroom over maxRate for network jitter
clearAtMinfalseconsume only: take the stat off the car when it bottoms out
-- Server: declare it. Nothing else handles the reporting.
exports.whip_core:RegisterVehicleStat('boost', {
    default = 1, min = 1, max = 100,
    persist = 'presence',                       -- the turbo is fitted; the number is momentary
    live = { maxRate = 33.3, interval = 0.25 }, -- nothing to full in three seconds
    hud  = { label = 'Boost', color = '#facc15', order = 6, showWhenPresent = true },
})

-- Client: work out the value, and say what it is
exports.whip_core:ReportVehicleStat({ entity = veh }, 'boost', level)
  • One or the other. A stat with both consume and live is refused.
  • Reporting never creates a stat. A report for a stat the car doesn't carry is refused, or reporting boost would fit a turbo.
  • interval is for other people. It sets how often passengers' gauges and the server hear; apply the value locally every frame, and show it on your own gauge from whileHeld. Reporting is the costliest thing WHIP does on the server, so slower is cheaper.
  • Read stats through the exports, never the statebag: a live value rides its own key.
ReportVehicleStat(vehicle, name, value)CLIENT

Tell WHIP what a live stat is worth now. The newest value wins and is sent at the stat's interval; the server caps how fast it rises.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
namestringA stat registered with live
valuenumberWhat it's worth now
Returns: boolean: whether the value was taken
Not every frame. Each call costs about 20µs. Call when the value has moved by enough, no more often than interval, and compare on difference so a refused send is retried and the final value gets across.
ConsumeVehicleStat(vehicle, name, delta)CLIENT

Report that this client used some of a consume stat. Deltas add up locally and the total is sent at the stat's interval. Safe every frame; for several stats, use ConsumeVehicleStats.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
namestringA stat registered with consume
deltanumberAmount used since the last call; positive
Returns: boolean: false when the vehicle didn't resolve or the delta wasn't positive
It doesn't check the tank. The server clamps at the minimum; to stop at empty, read GetVehicleStat yourself.
ConsumeVehicleStats(vehicle, deltas)CLIENT

Report several stats used on one car in a single call: the same as ConsumeVehicleStat for each, at a fraction of the cost.

ParamTypeDescription
vehiclenumber|tableA vehicle reference
deltastable{ [statName] = amountUsed } since the last call, positive
Returns: boolean ok, number accepted
Check ok, not the count. (true, 0) means nothing in the table was usable; (false, 0) means the vehicle didn't resolve.

Gauges

These change only this player's dial, never the stat. Each stat has one rule, its setter's, dropped when that resource stops.

SetVehicleStatDisplay(name, fn)CLIENT

Draw a local reading for a stat on this client's gauges instead of the replicated one, for a value you compute in real time. It changes the number, never whether the gauge shows. Without a watcher the needle moves about once a second; with one, after each whileHeld tick.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringRegistered stat name
fnfunction(entity, replicated) → a number, or nil for the replicated value
Returns: true, or false, reason when another resource provides this stat
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatDisplay('boost', function(entity, replicated)
    if entity ~= myTunedVehicle then return nil end   -- passengers get the replicated value
    return liveBoost
end)
Running a watcher? Return the reading from whileHeld instead: it's cheaper and wins over a provider.
ClearVehicleStatDisplay(name)CLIENT

Stop drawing your local reading; the gauge shows the replicated value again.

Returns: true, or false, reason (not set, or another resource's)
SetVehicleStatShown(name, fn) · ClearVehicleStatShown(name)CLIENT

Whether a stat's gauge is drawn on a car. fn(entity) returns false to hide it; it's asked once per car the player sits in, so answer from what the car is.

Returns: true, or false, reason (no name or rule, or another resource's rule)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatShown('fuel', function(entity)   -- no fuel gauge on an electric car
    return not exports.whip_core:IsVehicleElectric({ entity = entity })
end)
SetVehicleStatIcon(name, fn) · ClearVehicleStatIcon(name)CLIENT

A stat's gauge icon per car. fn(entity) returns one of the dial's icons ('fuel', 'fuel_left', 'fuel_right', 'turbo', 'nitro', 'coolant', 'hack', 'weapon'), an SVG path in a 24x24 viewBox, or nil for the stat's own. Asked once per car.

Returns: true, or false, reason (no name or rule, or another resource's rule)
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleStatIcon('fuel', function(entity)   -- point to the filler's side
    local p = exports.whip_core:GetVehiclePoint({ entity = entity }, 'fuel')
    if p and p.fixed and p.side == 'left' then return 'fuel_left' end
end)

Garages

A garage is a place on the map with parking bays. Players take a car out at an empty bay and store it from the car's doors; server owners set garages and bays up in /whip.

Taking a car out and storing it

  • Out. An empty bay's prompt shows the garage's name. E expands it into one option per car garaged there, and E on a car brings it out into this bay with its colours and parts. Looking away folds the list.
  • In. A bay with a car in it has no prompt; the car's doors get Store instead. The server checks the player may store it (and says why not) and that the car is in the bay, within Config.GarageSpotRadius + 2 m.
  • One garage at a time. A bay lists only the cars garaged at its own garage.

The bay outline

Prompts are off while driving, so a driver sees bays marked on the ground; the mark changes once they're parked in one. It's a hint only: nothing to press, no events.

  • From a car, only free bays draw (and the one you're in), for the driver only. Any car they drive gets it; Config.GaragePositionHelper.requireStorable = true limits it to cars they own.
  • On foot, every bay of garages you may use draws within onFootRange (10 m); 0 keeps the outline for drivers.
  • A parked car hides the outline. Its size is Config.GaragePositionHelper: keep length and width at 2:1, or the ring goes oval.

Setting a garage upServer owners

/whip → Vehicles → Garages → + New Garage. Nothing is made until the last step:

  1. Name: shown on the map and over the bays. Its key is made from it (or typed); cars are filed under the key, so it can't change later.
  2. Bays: Set out bays in the world opens the bay tool. Up to 40.
  3. Map: the blip's place (the middle of the bays, or where you stand), icon and colour.
  4. Create: a summary with Change on each part.

To change a garage, pick it in the list and press Change on Name, Bays or Map: the same wizard opens, filled in, and Save changes writes only what changed. Bays keep their numbers and a garage keeps at least one. A property's private garage is changed in Properties.

Do it at the car park. A new or moved bay or marker further than Config.GarageWizardReach (250 m) from you is refused. Needs the whip.devtools ACE.

The bay toolServer owners

One tool sets out every garage's bays: a new garage's Bays step, Place & Edit Garage Locations on a saved garage (up to 40), or on a property's Garage in /whip → World → Properties (up to 8). Nothing is written while it's open: the wizard's Create or Save changes, or the property's Save, sends every bay at once.

ENTER (A) puts a bay down on flat ground where you aim, or picks up the one you aim at and puts it down again. Q / E (LT / RT) turn it to the heading a car comes out facing; ↑ / ↓ (D-pad) raise or lower it up to 5 m; hold ALT for slowly. X removes a bay, C (B) puts a carried bay back or undoes the whole visit, and ESC (Menu) finishes.

Garages API

Server exports for garages. A garage is a place and its bays; which cars are in it is each vehicle's own garage field. New to garages? Read Garages first.

Reading

GetGarage(key) / GetGarages()SERVER

One garage by key, or every garage. Both return copies.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe garage's key (GetGarage only)
Returns: GetGarage → { garageId, key, resource, name, x, y, z, heading, spawnX, spawnY, spawnZ, spawnHeading, blipSprite, blipColor } or nil, plus private = true and managedBy for a property's garage. GetGarages → { [key] = garage }
Get garage keys from here, not from config.lua: a hardcoded key fails with "Wrong garage" once someone renames a garage.
GetNearestGarage(x, y, z, maxRange)SERVER

The garage closest to a point, measured to its marker or nearest bay, so a far bay of a big car park still counts. Never returns a private garage.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberThe point
maxRangenumber?Only a garage within this many metres
Returns: string|nil key, number|nil distance
local c = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source))
local key = exports.whip_core:GetNearestGarage(c.x, c.y, c.z, 15.0)
if key then exports.whip_core:DespawnVehicle(vehicleId, { garage = key, refuseOccupied = true }) end
GetGarageVehicles(key)SERVER

The vehicles stored in one garage, as GetVehicle snapshots.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe garage's key
Returns: table[]; {} for a key that names no garage

Managing garages

CreateGarage / UpdateGarage / DeleteGarageSERVER

Make, change and remove garages at runtime; blips and markers update on every client. A new garage gets one bay, at the spawn point; add more in /whip → Vehicles → Garages. Update changes only the fields you send.

FieldTypeDescription
keystringUnique; set at creation, never changed
namestringShown on the blip
x, y, z, headingnumberThe garage marker
spawnX, spawnY, spawnZ, spawnHeadingnumberThe first bay (default the marker)
blipSprite, blipColornumberMap blip style
Returns: CreateGarage(data) → table|false, string|nil; UpdateGarage(key, data), DeleteGarage(key) → boolean, string|nil. A garage another running resource made is refused; one made in /whip, by a property, or by a stopped resource is open to any
local garage, err = exports.whip_core:CreateGarage({
    key = 'impound', name = 'Impound Lot', x = 409.3, y = -1623.1, z = 29.3, heading = 230.0,
})
exports.whip_core:UpdateGarage('impound', { name = 'City Impound' })
exports.whip_core:DeleteGarage('impound')
Deleting a garage keeps its cars. DeleteGarage moves them to the nearest other garage (or the default one) and tells online owners where. In /whip, a garage with cars can't be deleted until the admin picks the public garage they move to.
SetVehicleGarage(vehicleId, garageKey)SERVER

Move a stored vehicle to another garage: an impound releasing a car, a dealer delivering to the buyer's garage. DespawnVehicle with a garage refuses a car already put away ("Vehicle is already stored"); this moves it.

ParamTypeDescription
vehicleIdnumber|tableA vehicle reference
garageKeystringThe garage it now belongs to
Returns: boolean ok, string|nil err
It doesn't check access. Ask CanUseGarage before moving a player's car into a property garage; if they can't use it, WHIP moves the car to a public garage the next time access changes.
CanUseGarage(key, who)SERVER

May this person use this garage? Always true for a public one. A private garage (a property's, keyed property:<id>) is for its owner and keyholders only: hidden bays, no blip, and its bay events refuse anyone else.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe garage
whonumber|tableA person: server id, or { charId = n }
Returns: true, or false, why ('No such garage', 'That garage belongs to …')
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanUseGarage(garageKey, source)
if not ok then return false, why end
exports.whip_core:SetVehicleGarage(vehicleId, garageKey)

Jobs

A job is a business with ranks, staff and a bank account. Players clock on and off; your resource declares the job and checks duty and permissions.

Declaring a job

A job has a key, roles with levels and permissions, and employees; its owner holds the top role and the business account. Declare it with EnsureJob, in Whip.register:

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureJob('police', {
        name  = 'Police Department',
        icon  = 'shield',
        roles = {
            { name = 'Chief',    level = 100 },
            { name = 'Sergeant', level = 50, permissions = { canHire = true, canFire = true, cuff = true } },
            { name = 'Officer',  level = 20, permissions = { cuff = true, bankAccess = 'view' } },
            { name = 'Cadet',    level = 1 },
        },
        permissions = { cuff = 'Cuff suspects' },   -- the job's own, beside the built-ins
    })
end)

The first call makes the job, with your roles or Config.JobDefaultRoles. Later calls update the name, icon, permissions and selfClockOn, and add new roles; a role that exists (a server owner may have edited it) and the owner are never changed.

Roles and permissions

Levels run 1–100; level 100 has every permission. Built-ins are canHire, canFire, canPromote / canDemote and canManage (roles, shop stock and prices). A job's own show as toggles on each role on the Jobs page. HasJobPermission checks both, on duty or off unless you pass { onDuty = true }.

A role's bankAccess ('none', 'view', 'deposit', 'withdraw', 'manager') is its access to the business account, kept in step as people are hired, promoted and fired.

Pass { by = source } and WHIP checks the player's rank on HirePlayer, FirePlayer, SetPlayerRole and the role exports: they outrank the person's role and the role given, and hold the permission. Below level 100, nobody gives what they don't have. Leave by out when your code or an admin decides.

-- A boss menu
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:HirePlayer(target, 'police', 'Cadet', { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end   -- 'They (or that role) outrank you'...

Clocking on and off

Duty isn't saved: logging out or a restart ends it. A player can be on duty at several jobs; their current job is the latest clock-on, which GetPlayerJob and the whipJob statebag name. Config.JobDutyOneAtATime = true makes a clock-on end every other.

Players clock on in the phone's Business app; your resource can add a command or a prompt. For duty at the station only, declare selfClockOn = false (the app's clock-on is refused) and call ClockOn from your server code.

exports.whip_core:ClockOn(source, 'police')            -- server: a prompt at the station
exports.whip_core:IsPlayerClockedOn(source, 'police')  -- server: on duty?
exports.whip_core:ClockOn('burgershot')                -- client, from a thread: waits for the server
Only need "works here"? Skip clocking: GetPlayerRole(source, 'police') ~= nil.

In game: /whip → Economy → JobsServer owners

+ New Job asks for a name (the key, used by doors, shops and scripts, is made from it, then fixed), ranks from a template, an owner (without one, no bank account) and staff. A job's page shows its staff on duty, account and shops; Change reopens the wizard, and nothing is written before Save changes.

Events

Server events pass one table: { jobId, key }, and for a person { charId, source } (source only while online).

EventExtra fields
whip_core:job:createdname
whip_core:job:updatedname, icon, ownerCharId, oldOwnerCharId
whip_core:job:deleted—
whip_core:job:hiredcharId, source, roleId, role, by
whip_core:job:firedcharId, source
whip_core:job:roleChangedcharId, source, roleId, role, oldRoleId
whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOffcharId, source

Client, for the local player: whip_core:job:clockedOn / clockedOff with { jobId, key }, and whip_core:job:listChanged with { jobs }.

Data shapes

ObjectFields
JobjobId, key, name, icon, ownerCharId, settings
RoleroleId, jobId, name, level, permissions
EmployeejobId, charId, roleId, hiredAt, hiredBy
Job list entry (GetPlayerJobs)jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, clockedOn, permissions

Jobs API

Server and client exports for jobs. New to jobs? Read Jobs first.

Every job export names things the same way. A job is a jobId or key; a person a source or { charId = 42 } (offline too); a role a roleId or name (any capitals). Each returns a value, or false and a reason a player can read. opts.by names the player acting, and WHIP checks their rank; leave it out when your code or an admin decides.

Reading jobs

GetJob(job)SERVER

A job by jobId or key.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table|nil: { jobId, key, name, icon, ownerCharId, settings }
GetJobs()SERVER

Every job, in jobId order.

Returns: table[]: job objects
GetJobRoles(job)SERVER

A job's roles, highest level first.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table[]: { roleId, name, level, permissions }, or false, 'No such job'

Declaring and changing jobs

EnsureJob(key, data)SERVER

Finds or creates your job; declare it in Whip.register (example). Later calls update the name, icon, permissions and selfClockOn and add new roles; existing roles and the owner stay (UpdateJob changes the owner). Another running resource's key is refused. While whip_core starts, it waits up to 60 seconds.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringLetters, numbers and _ ('police')
data.namestringDisplay name
data.iconstring?Icon
data.rolestable?{ { name, level, permissions } }, level 1–100. Default Config.JobDefaultRoles
data.permissionstable?The job's own, beside the built-in five: { cuff = 'Cuff suspects' }
data.ownerperson?Used only when the job is made: holds the top role and the business account
data.selfClockOnboolean?false: the client's ClockOn is refused; your server code puts them on duty. Going off duty always works
Returns: table: the job, or false, why (a bad key, 'roles[2] (Cadet): level must be...'). A new owned job whose business account couldn't be opened is still returned; the console says so.
UpdateJob(job, patch)SERVER

Changes a job's name, icon or owner. The business account follows a new owner; the old owner keeps what their role gives, or nothing if they don't work there.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
patchtable{ name?, icon?, owner? }. owner = false removes the owner (refused while there's a business account)
Returns: true (even if the account couldn't follow the new owner; the console says so), or false, why. Refused for a job another running resource declares; one made on the Jobs page, or whose resource is stopped, is open to any.
DeleteJob(job)SERVER

Deletes a job, its roles and staff list, and closes its business accounts.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why: 'Empty the job's business account first' while one holds money. Refused for a job another running resource declares, as UpdateJob.

Who works where

GetPlayerJob(who)SERVER

The job they clocked on at most recently, as the whipJob statebag and the client's GetPlayerJob name it. nil off duty.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
Returns: table|nil: { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel }
GetPlayerJobs(who)SERVER

Every job they have a role at (employed, or the owner), on duty or not.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
Returns: table, by jobId: { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, clockedOn, permissions }; {}, why for nobody
IsPlayerClockedOn(who, job?)SERVER

On duty at this job, or, with no job, at any.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
Returns: boolean; with false, a reason when there's no such player or job, so "off duty" and "asked about nobody" differ
GetPlayerRole(who, job)SERVER

Their role at a job. The owner holds the top role, hired or not.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table|nil: { roleId, name, level, permissions }
HasJobPermission(who, job, permission, opts?)SERVER

May they do this at this job? Level 100 holds every permission. Permissions hold on duty or off.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
permissionstringcanHire, canFire, canPromote, canDemote, canManage, or the job's own
optstable?{ onDuty = true } also requires being on duty there
Returns: true, or false, why ('Not on duty at Police', 'Not allowed at Police', no such player or job)
if not exports.whip_core:HasJobPermission(source, 'police', 'cuff', { onDuty = true }) then
    return false, 'Only an officer on duty can do that'
end
GetJobEmployees(job)SERVER

Everyone on the payroll, online or not, by charId. The owner is listed only if also hired.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table, by charId: { charId, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, hiredAt, hiredBy, onDuty, source } (hiredAt in epoch seconds; source only while online), or false, 'No such job'
GetClockedOnEmployees(job)SERVER

Everyone on duty at a job, the owner included. Each has a source, as duty ends at logout.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: table[]: { charId, source }, or false, reason for no such job (hence the or {})
for _, cop in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetClockedOnEmployees('police') or {}) do
    exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(cop.source, '10-31 in progress at the bank')
end

Hiring and roles

HirePlayer(who, job, role?, opts?)SERVER

Hires someone. Their business-account access follows the role; their client's job list updates itself.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId } (offline too)
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|string?roleId or name; default the lowest role
optstable?{ by = person }, recorded and checked: they outrank the role, hold canHire, and hold all it can do (its permissions, at least its account access)
Returns: true, or false, why ('They already work there', 'No such role at that job', 'No such character', 'Your role is not allowed to do that', 'They (or that role) outrank you'...)
One character per account. Config.JobOneCharacterPerAccount (on by default) refuses hiring a character whose account already has one there, the owner included, so an alt can't keep a fired character's access. Trusted code obeys it too; false turns it off.
CanHirePlayer(who, job, role?, opts?)SERVER

Would HirePlayer allow it? Nothing is written: for a step that waits on someone, like the phone's job offer, which hires (checking again) once accepted.

Returns: true, or false, why (as HirePlayer)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:CanHirePlayer({ charId = typedId }, jobId, roleId, { by = source })
if not ok then return false, why end   -- say why now, before asking them
FirePlayer(who, job, opts?)SERVER

Fires someone. They go off duty and lose their business-account access.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
optstable?{ by = person }, checked: they outrank the person and hold canFire
Returns: true, or false, why ('They do not work there'...)
SetPlayerRole(who, job, role, opts?)SERVER

Changes someone's role. Their business-account access follows it.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
optstable?{ by = person }, checked: they outrank the old and new role and hold canPromote (up) or canDemote (down); the new role gives nothing theirs can't do; nobody promotes themselves
Returns: true, or false, why
CreateJobRole(job, data, opts?)SERVER

Adds a role. Role names are unique within a job, ignoring case.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
datatable{ name, level, permissions? }, level 1–100; permissions are built-ins, the job's own and bankAccess. One the job lacks is refused
optstable?{ by = person }, checked: canManage; below level 100, the role sits below theirs and does no more (no permission they lack, no more account access)
Returns: table: { roleId, name, level, permissions }, or false, why ('There is already a role called Shift Lead', 'They (or that role) outrank you', 'That rank can do more than yours: you cannot give more than you have'...)
UpdateJobRole(job, role, patch, opts?)SERVER

Changes a role's name, level or permissions. Unnamed permissions keep their value; false removes one. Its holders' account access follows.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
patchtable{ name?, level?, permissions? }
optstable?{ by = person }, checked: canManage; below level 100, the role and its new level sit below theirs and gain nothing their role lacks. Nobody may leave the job without a level 100 role
Returns: true, or false, why
DeleteJobRole(job, role, opts?)SERVER

Deletes a role. Refused while anyone holds it.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
rolenumber|stringroleId or name
optstable?{ by = person }, checked as for UpdateJobRole
Returns: true, or false, why ('Move the people in that role to another role first')

Duty

ClockOn(who, job, opts?)SERVER

Puts an online player on duty, until logout or a restart. With Config.JobDutyOneAtATime, every other job clocks off first.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }; online
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
optstable?{ by = person }, checked like the client's ClockOn: only themselves, at a job that allows it (selfClockOn)
Returns: true, or false, why ('They do not work there', 'They are not online'...)
ClockOff(who, job?)SERVER

Takes someone off duty at a job, or, with no job, at every job.

ParamTypeDescription
whopersonsource or { charId }
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why ('They are not on duty'...)

Client

The local player's job state, cached: no server round trip except ClockOn and ClockOff. Client events are in Jobs.

GetPlayerJobs()CLIENT

Every job the local player has a role at.

Returns: table: { [jobId] = { jobId, key, name, icon, roleId, roleName, roleLevel, clockedOn, permissions } }
IsPlayerClockedOn(job?)CLIENT

On duty at this job, or, with no job, at any?

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|string?jobId or key; nil for any
Returns: boolean
HasJobPermission(job, permission)CLIENT

What the job list says the player may do: a hint for what to offer, such as a "Manage Stock" option. The server checks again when it's used.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
permissionstringA built-in or the job's own
Returns: boolean
GetPlayerJob()CLIENT

The job of the most recent clock-on, as the server's GetPlayerJob names it. nil off duty.

Returns: table|nil: an entry of GetPlayerJobs
ClockOn(job)CLIENT

Goes on duty. It waits for the server, so call it from a thread (a command, a key binding, an interaction callback). Refused ('This job puts people on duty itself') when the job has selfClockOn = false.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|stringjobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why
ClockOff(job?)CLIENT

Goes off duty at a job, or, with none, at every job. Always allowed, even while dead. Waits for the server.

ParamTypeDescription
jobnumber|string?jobId or key
Returns: true, or false, why

Shops

A shop sells items from a shopkeeper or an object in the world, through a prompt. It's the server's own money sink, or a job's business with unlimited goods or real stock its staff fill.

Three modes

ModeStockPricingRevenue
npcUnlimitedThe shop's catalogNone: a money sink
infiniteUnlimitedThe shop's catalogThe job's business account
stockedA container its staff stock by handOne price per item, set by staffThe job's business account; a shop priced in an item puts that payment in its stock room

Declaring a shop

Declare a shop your resource always has with EnsureShop, in Whip.register: it's made once and found on every start. The other calls are in the Shops API.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureShop('my_gunshop', {
        name = 'Ammu-Nation', mode = 'npc', npcModel = 's_m_m_ammucountry',
        x = -330.2, y = 6084.3, z = 31.5, heading = 228.0,
        blipSprite = 110,
        catalog = { gunny_pistol = 2500, gunny_mag_pistol = 150 },
    })
end)

-- Hear every sale
AddEventHandler('whip_core:shop:purchased', function(e)
    print(('charId %s bought %d line(s) for $%d'):format(e.charId, #e.items, e.total))
end)

Business shops

infinite and stocked shops link to a job with jobId. The customer pays through ChargePlayer, and the job's business account gets a system deposit (BankSystemDeposit) logging the buyer's charId. A line that can't be handed over is refunded in the currency paid.

No owner, no account. A job's business account exists once it has an owner (/whip → Economy → Jobs). Until then GetJobBankAccounts returns nothing, so a resource paying a job needs a fallback.

For a stocked shop, set containerId to a container. Staff with canManage choose Manage Stock on the prompt, drag items in, and right-click them to Set Price and Mark For Sale. A buyer gets the exact item, metadata and serial number included.

Buying

E on the prompt swaps the inventory for the shop's cards and a basket. The server has the last word on the basket (a shelf ran out, a full basket), and Buy waits for it. Payment is Cash or Bank, or only the item a shop is priced in.

Shop talk

Everyone nearby sees the shopping: the shopper says each step in a /me bubble, and the shopkeeper answers a moment later; the shop's header shows the conversation too, with faces. Lines and timings are Config.ShopTalk (Configuration).

Every line
  • Opening: "What do you got?" / "Welcome in."
  • Adding: "I'll take x3 Water" / "Coming right up."
  • Changing how many: "Actually, I want x5 Water instead" / "No problem, changed."
  • Taking it out: "I changed my mind on x3 Water" / "No worries."
  • Paying: "Paid $1,170 for x10 Burger and x1 Phone" / "$1,170 received. Enjoy your x10 Burger and x1 Phone!"
  • Can't afford it (once in 8 s): "Uh... can I owe you?" / "Come back when you can afford it, cheapskate."
  • Leaving: "Nevermind, I'll shop elsewhere" / "Suit yourself."

Basket changes are said once it's left alone for a second, each item once. Nothing is said by someone who is down, when a death, logout or walking away shuts the shop, or on reopening it within 15 seconds. A shop with an object has nobody to answer.

Shops in config.lua

WHIP ships with no shops. A shop in Config.Shops is made at start-up whenever no shop has its key, then managed in /whip; deleted there, it comes back at the next restart while it's listed.

Config.Shops = {
    convenience_1 = {
        name = '24/7 Store', mode = 'npc', npcModel = 'mp_m_shopkeep_01',
        pos = vector4(25.7, -1347.3, 29.5, 271.0),
        blipSprite = 52, blipColor = 2,
        catalog = { food = 50, drink = 30, bandage = 100 },
    },
}

In game: /whip → Economy → ShopsServer owners

+ New Shop walks through the mode (and job), where it stands (walk there, press E), the shopkeeper (an NPC, a prop or nobody), the stock room, goods and prices, and the blip. A shop's page has Change on each part, Teleport there and Delete; nothing is written until Save changes, and removing a stocked shop's item from Prices takes it off sale. Arrange the shelf and tabs in game with Edit Shelf.

Shops API

Server and client exports for shops. New to shops? Read Shops first.

Finding shops

GetShop(ref)SERVER

One shop, by id or by what you hold, as GetVehicle takes a reference.

ParamTypeDescription
refnumber|tableA shop id, { key = }, or { containerId = } (the shop whose stock that container is)
Returns: table|nil: { shopId, key, name, mode, jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, x, y, z, heading, blipSprite, blipColor, catalog, settings }
local shop = exports.whip_core:GetShop({ key = 'burgershot' })
GetShops(filter?)SERVER

Every shop, sorted by shopId, or one job's: a job can own several.

ParamTypeDescription
filtertable?{ job = }, by key or jobId
Returns: table[]; {}, 'No such job' for an unknown job
GetShopViewers(shopId)SERVER

The players browsing a shop now.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
Returns: number[]: sources

Creating and changing shops

EnsureShop(key, data)SERVER

A shop declared by key, safe on every start (example). The same declaration again changes nothing, so an admin's edits stand; a changed one applies your fields and clears a link you dropped (jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, blipSprite). Another running resource's key is refused.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringStable shop id
datatable{ name, mode, npcModel?, prop?, x, y, z, heading, catalog?, jobId?, containerId?, blipSprite?, blipColor?, settings? }; jobId takes a jobId or key
Returns: table: the shop, its declaration in settings.ensured; or false, reason (a bad catalog, no x/y/z, no such job or container, another resource's key, a database error)
CreateShop(data)SERVER

Creates a shop on every call, without a key check: a pop-up stall for one event, say. Fires whip_core:shop:created with { shopId, shop }.

ParamTypeDescription
datatableAs EnsureShop's
Returns: table: the shop with shopId, or false, reason
UpdateShop(shopId, data)SERVER

Changes the fields you include; false clears jobId, containerId, npcModel, prop, blipSprite or key. Fires whip_core:shop:updated with { shopId, shop }.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
datatableShop fields. catalog ({ [itemKey] = price }) replaces an infinite or npc shop's whole catalog; for one price, use AddCatalogItem
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false, 'Shop not found' for an unknown id. Refused for another running resource's shop, as DeleteShop
DeleteShop(shopId)SERVER

Deletes a shop, closes it for anyone browsing and despawns its entity. Fires whip_core:shop:deleted with { shopId }.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false, 'Shop not found' for an unknown id. Refused for a shop another running resource made or declares; one made in /whip, or whose resource isn't running, is open to any
SetShopLayout(shopId, { categories, layout })SERVER

Sets a shop's tabs and where its goods sit, as Edit Shelf does for its managers and WHIP's admins. Lower order comes first; unplaced goods follow, A to Z. Both fields can also sit in a shop's settings (config.lua §9, EnsureShop).

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID (any mode)
categoriesstring[]?The tabs in order: 1–24 letters each, at most 12. Omitted: kept
layouttable?{ [itemKey] = { category, order } }. Each entry replaces that item's place; one with neither removes it; others keep theirs
Returns: boolean, string|nil: false for an unknown item, a tab the shop doesn't have, a tab name too long or too many tabs

Catalog (infinite and npc shops)

GetShopCatalog(shopId)SERVER

An infinite or npc shop's catalog.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
Returns: table|nil: { [itemKey] = price }, nil for no such shop
AddCatalogItem(shopId, itemKey, price)SERVER

Adds or reprices one registered item in an infinite or npc shop's catalog, and saves it.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
itemKeystringItem key
pricenumber≥ 0
Returns: boolean, string|nil
RemoveCatalogItem(shopId, itemKey)SERVER

Removes one item from an infinite or npc shop's catalog, and saves it.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberShop ID
itemKeystringItem key
Returns: boolean, string|nil

Stock and prices (stocked shops)

GetShopStock(shopId)SERVER

A stocked shop's shelf, each slot with its item's price. Loaded from the database if not cached.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberA stocked shop
Returns: table: { [slot] = { item, amount, metadata, price, forSale } }, or false, reason (not stocked, no such shop)
GetShopPrices(shopId)SERVER

Every item price a stocked shop has, for sale or not.

ParamTypeDescription
shopIdnumberA stocked shop
Returns: table: { [itemKey] = { price, forSale } }, or false, reason (not stocked, no such shop)
SetShopItemPrice(containerId, itemKey, price, forSale)SERVER

Prices an item on a stocked shop's shelf, or takes it off sale. One price per item, for every slot holding it; customers see it at once. Fires whip_core:shop:priceChanged with { containerId, item, price, forSale }.

ParamTypeDescription
containerIdnumber|tableThe stock container ID, or { shopId = n }, as every shop export takes
itemKeystringA registered item
pricenumberDollars (0 = free; negative becomes 0)
forSalebooleanfalse keeps the price but hides the item
Returns: boolean, string|nil: 'Unknown container', 'Unknown item', 'Invalid price' (not a number)
exports.whip_core:SetShopItemPrice({ shopId = shopId }, 'drink', 5, true)   -- water at $5

Client

IsShopOpen()CLIENT

Whether the shop screen is open.

Returns: boolean
GetActiveShopId()CLIENT

The shop the player is browsing, or nil.

Returns: number|nil

Properties & Homes

A property is a home a player can own: a house, a flat, a studio. Server owners set them up in game; your resource reads them and sets owners and keys with the Properties API.

Templates, units and properties

  • Template: one per interior (MLO archetype), such as a half-floor of Mega Tower B.
  • Unit: one home inside that interior (its space, doors, signs, garage), measured from the interior's origin: flat 5 of the four on that half-floor.
  • Property: one unit at one place the interior stands in the world: B805.

Every copy of an interior shares its units: set up one Mega floor's four flats and the other 35 floors are a button each.

Setting one upServer owners

Stand inside the MLO and open /whip → World → Properties → New property, then step through Interior, Space, Doors, Signs, Garage, Name & settings and Review; nothing is saved until Save. Entrance and garage doors lock to the owner and keyholders; an inner door locks only if you say so. Until a manager sign is placed inside, Keys stand at the outside sign and Furnish isn't offered (the owner can type /furnish in the home).

A whole buildingServer owners

Register here, in another copy of a templated interior, registers its free units from a name pattern: {b} building, {u} / {k} unit label / key, {f} floor, {n} / {nn} a number counting up from the start number. B{f}{nn} on floor 8 from 5 gives B805 to B808. Stamp mode flies you through the building: E registers the copy you're in, PgUp / PgDn change floor, Tab / Q change the block of numbers, Esc is done.

Checking themServer owners

Verify takes you to each property and checks its interior, position, rooms, doorways and doors; Quick check re-checks on the server without moving you. A property's status is ok, unverified (never checked, or changed since) or attention (with a reason).

Buying and owning

  • Buying. A priced property is sold at its outside sign, for cash or from any account the buyer can pay from (their own, or a shared or job account with withdraw access). Price 0 means not for sale: only an admin, or SetPropertyOwner, hands it over.
  • Doors are managed doors that open for the owner and keyholders; unowned, for nobody.
  • Keys are given face to face at the manager sign, within Config.PropertyKeyGrantRange. A new owner takes every key back.
  • Furniture and the theme are chosen at the manager sign. A sale keeps the theme.
  • Private garage. A unit with bays gives each property a garage only the owner and keyholders see, with no blip; GetNearestGarage never returns it. Lose access and your cars inside move to the nearest public garage.

Stashes

Furniture listed in Config.PropertyStashProps becomes a stash once placed. Only the owner and keyholders can open it; admins open any from /whip → Economy → Containers.

-- config.lua: model = { label, slots, most kg }
Config.PropertyStashProps = {
    ['v_res_tre_wardrobe'] = { label = 'Wardrobe', slots = 40, weight = 150.0 },
    ['prop_ld_int_safe_01'] = { label = 'Safe', slots = 10, weight = 40.0 },
}
  • It moves with its furniture, contents and all, and passes to a new owner full.
  • A save or Clear that would remove a stash with anything in it is refused.
  • Deleting the property deletes its stashes, logging the contents as lost.
  • At most Config.PropertyStashLimit per property; lowering it takes none away.

Interior themes

An interior resource can give its homes several looks (one entity set each) with whip_interior_themes 'v1' in its fxmanifest.lua and four server exports, read when either resource starts. A property whose interior and origin match a home's within 2 m gets a Theme option on its sign.

Your exportWhat it returns or does
GetThemes(){ { id = 0, name = 'Original', walls = '#rrggbb', trim = '#rrggbb', floor = '#rrggbb' }, ... }: ids 0 to 255, 0 the default; the colours are the swatch
GetHomes(){ { key, archetype, designArchetype?, position }, ... }: archetype name and instance origin. designArchetype is the interior a replaced home used to place
SetAllThemes(map){ [key] = themeId }, every home (one left out is 0), sent when either resource starts
SetHomeTheme(key, themeId)One home changed. Return true, or false, why

Your client draws the look: switch the entity set before a fresh interior is ready, or on one already showing, refresh it and tell WHIP to remake the furniture:

ActivateInteriorEntitySet(interiorId, 'wh_theme_2')
RefreshInterior(interiorId)
TriggerEvent('whip_core:interiorRefreshed', interiorId)

Shipping it with an MLOServer owners

Templates & packs → Export writes an interior and its copies as whip_properties.lua. Put it in the MLO's resource with whip_property_pack 'whip_properties.lua' in the manifest, and every server running the MLO gets its homes. The format is in whip_core/docs/properties.md.

Config

ConfigDefaultWhat it does
PropertyMaxObjects150Furniture limit, unless the property says otherwise
PropertyKeyGrantRange5.0How close someone must be to be handed a key
PropertyStreamRange60.0How close a sign appears from
PropertyFurnitureDistance20.0How close to the walls furniture appears (it goes 2 m further out). 0 = only inside
PropertyFurnitureRooms4Properties furnished at once: yours, then the nearest
PropertySignPlaceRange12.0How far an admin can aim a sign from
PropertyStashProps4 piecesFurniture that becomes a stash
PropertyStashLimit6Most stashes per property

Properties API

Exports for properties, their furniture and the placeable-prop catalogue. New to properties? Read Properties & Homes first. A who is a person: a server id, or { charId = n }.

Reading

GetProperty(propertyId)SERVER

One property: name, owner, placement, space, signs, keyholders (keys), doors (doorIds), settings, private garage (garageKey) and status ('ok' | 'unverified' | 'attention', with statusReason). WhipProperty in types/server.lua lists every field.

Returns: table|nil
GetProperties()SERVER

Every property, as clients see them (no keyholders, doors or settings).

Returns: table[]
GetPropertyAt(x, y, z)SERVER

The property whose space holds this point, or nil. Takes a vector3 too.

Returns: table|nil
GetCharacterProperties(charId)SERVER

The property ids a character owns and holds keys to.

Returns: { owned = {...}, keys = {...} }

Owners and keys

HasPropertyAccess(propertyId, who)SERVER

Whether a person is the property's owner or a keyholder.

Returns: true, or false, why ('No key to that property', 'No such property')
SetPropertyOwner(propertyId, who)SERVER

Gives a property to a person; nil or false makes it unowned. A new owner takes back every key and locks the doors.

Returns: boolean, string|nil
-- A sale: the money first, then the house, or the money back
local receipt, err = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(buyerSource, price, { method = 'bank', reason = 'House' })
if not receipt then return false, err end
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetPropertyOwner(propertyId, buyerSource)
if not ok then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) return false, why end
GivePropertyKey / RemovePropertyKey(propertyId, who)SERVER

Gives a person a key, or takes it back, without the in-game face-to-face rule.

Returns: boolean, string|nil ('They already have a key')

Furniture and stashes

GetPropertyStashes(propertyId)SERVER

A property's stashes in the order they were made, each { containerId, name, slots, maxWeight, x, y, z }. containerId works with the container calls.

Returns: table[], empty for none

Themes

GetPropertyThemes(propertyId)SERVER

A property's looks, or nil when its interior has none. label names the resource they come from.

Returns: { label, current, themes = { { id, name, walls, trim, floor }, ... } } or nil
SetPropertyTheme(propertyId, themeId)SERVER

Gives a property one of its looks, with no check on who asks. It's saved, then the interior's resource redraws the home.

Returns: boolean, string|nil ('That is not one of its themes')

Property packs

RegisterPropertyPack(pack)SERVER

Registers an MLO's homes from a script, from the table a whip_property_pack file returns (format in whip_core/docs/properties.md); most MLOs only need the manifest line. The pack belongs to your resource and is checked whole: the first mistake refuses it.

Returns: boolean ok, string: 'applied', 'unchanged', 'queued' (WHIP still starting), or 'path: why'
Applying it again is free. An identical pack writes nothing; a changed one only moves what the pack set. Owners, keys, furniture and admin changes are never touched, and a home an admin deleted isn't remade.
GetPropertyPacks()SERVER

The packs WHIP knows (id, resource, version, label, running) and the pack files it refused (file, error).

Returns: { packs = {...}, problems = {...} }

Client

GetCurrentProperty()CLIENT

The property the local player stands in, or nil; key means this character holds a key. whip_core:property:entered and :exited fire as it changes.

Returns: { id, name, label, building, ownerCharId, mine, key } or nil
GetInteriorFurnishState(interiorId)CLIENT

How far along WHIP's furniture is for the property an interior stands on, for a resource that covers the windows until the room is finished. Ask a few times a second, or listen for whip_core:property:furnishStateChanged.

  • 'pending': WHIP will make it, or remake it after whip_core:interiorRefreshed, and it isn't up yet.
  • 'done': it's up, or the furnisher has the room open.
  • 'none': nothing to wait for (no saved furniture, or not a property's interior).
  • 'idle': it has furniture, but beyond PropertyFurnitureDistance or not among the PropertyFurnitureRooms nearest.
Returns: 'pending' | 'done' | 'none' | 'idle'
local ok, state = pcall(function() return exports.whip_core:GetInteriorFurnishState(interiorId) end)
if not ok or state == 'done' or state == 'none' then
    -- reveal the room
end

Prop catalogue

RegisterProps(list)SERVER

Adds a pack's props to the furnisher while it runs, with your pictures (list them in your files { }). Each call is the whole list; all go when the pack stops. A model WHIP already lists keeps its row and admin choices, and takes your picture.

Returns: true, or false, why (a category not in Config.PropCategories, a picture not in your resource, a model another pack registered)
exports.whip_core:RegisterProps({
    { model = 'mypack_armchair', name = 'Velvet armchair', category = 'seating', image = 'img/armchair.webp' },
})
IsPlaceableProp(model)SERVER

Whether a prop may be placed: false for an unknown model or one marked unavailable. Check it before placing a model a client named.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstringProp model name, any case
Returns: boolean

Doors

Take control of any door in the game world: save it, lock it and decide who may open it. Each saved door has an E prompt on its handles within Config.DoorInteractRange (3 m), and the server decides every lock and unlock.

Declaring your resource's doors

A map, MLO or job resource declares its doors with EnsureDoors: the list is your whole set, each door named by a key. Every start, new keys are made, changed ones updated and dropped ones released.

-- Server, inside Whip.register
Whip.core:EnsureDoors({
    { key = 'front', label = 'PD Front Door', folder = 'Mission Row PD',
      model = 631614199, coords = vector4(434.7, -980.6, 30.7, 180.0),
      requirements = { jobs = { 'police', 'ems' }, lockpick = true } },
}, { label = 'Mission Row PD' })

exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked({ key = 'front' }, false)

To save one door and leave it to admins, use CreateDoor; to hold one only while a heist runs, HoldDoor. Link two leaves of a double door with link, LinkDoors or the Door Editor, and they lock together.

Who may open a door

A door's requirements are any-of: one match lets a player in. A door with none opens for anyone.

RequirementOpens for
jobs = { 'police' }Anyone with a role at one of these jobs (employed or owner), on duty or not
onDuty = trueWith jobs: only while on duty there
charIds = { 12 }These characters
items = { { key = 'keycard' } }Anyone carrying one of these (count = 2: at least that many)
ace = 'whip.admin'Anyone with this ACE
lockpick = trueA locked door offers a lockpick skill check
The opposite of an action's require. On AddAction every rule must pass: { job = 'police', item = 'pd_keycard' } there means an officer holding the keycard; on a door, any officer or anyone with the keycard.

The Door EditorServer owners

/whip → World → Doors lists every saved door by folder, and Open the editor flies you around with saved doors lit (grey when a property manages them). Aim at a door and press G to save it, E to link two, R to delete. + New Door walks you through picking both leaves, a name, locking and access, and saves nothing until the last step.

Doors API

Server and client exports for doors. New to doors? Read Doors first. A server export that takes a door also takes { key = 'office' } for one your resource declared (add set = '…' with more than one set); a key reaches only your own doors.

Declaring and saving

EnsureDoors(list, opts)SERVER

Declares your resource's doors, instead of a door script that fights WHIP's locks. The list is your whole set, keyed: a new key makes its door or adopts the one on that spot; a known key follows the list; a key that left the list is released (deleted if the list made it, put back if adopted).

FieldTypeDescription
keystringRequired. Letters, digits, _ - . :, at most 60
modelstring | numberRequired. A name, or a hash (signed or not)
coordsvector3 | vector4 | tableRequired. A vector4's w is the heading (or x, y, z, heading)
label, folderstring?What the Doors page shows. The label defaults to the key
requirementstable?Who may open it. Left out: anyone
autolock, autolockDelayboolean?, number?Lock again this many seconds (default 10) after any unlock. A picked lock stays open
linkstring?The key of the other half of a double door
optstable?id (the set, default 'doors'), label (the Doors page's name for the set), prune (default true; false keeps dropped doors)
Returns: { doors = { [key] = doorId }, failed = { [key] = why }, released = n }, or false, reason
Whip.register(function()
    local res, why = exports.whip_core:EnsureDoors({
        { key = 'lobby_l', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor004', coords = vector4(-868.84, -1275.53, 5.10, 110.0), link = 'lobby_r' },
        { key = 'lobby_r', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor004', coords = vector4(-867.60, -1273.20, 5.10, 110.0) },
        { key = 'office', model = 'v_ilev_ph_gendoor', coords = vector3(-870.1, -1280.4, 5.1),
          requirements = { jobs = { 'realestate' }, onDuty = true }, autolock = true },
    }, { label = 'Pink Lady' })
    if not res then print('doors: ' .. why) return end
    for key, reason in pairs(res.failed) do print('door ' .. key .. ': ' .. reason) end
end)
The list wins. By key you can lock, read, and change label and folder (a Doors page rename lasts until your next start). Requirements, auto-lock, the link and the door's existence belong to the list, and the other exports refuse them. One bad entry and nothing changes; a door that can't be placed goes in failed. Declared doors stay when your resource stops.
EnsureDoor(key, data, opts)SERVER

EnsureDoors for one door, never releasing any. It's kept in its own set, 'door:<key>' (or opts.id), so an EnsureDoors call neither prunes nor undoes it. data takes an entry's fields without key and link: declare a pair with EnsureDoors.

Returns: door, or false, reason
CreateDoor(data)SERVER

Saves a door, always locked, and leaves it to admins. Waits up to 60 s for whip_core to finish starting.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ label, folder, model, x, y, z, heading, requirements, metadata }
Returns: the door, or false, reason, plus the id of a door already within half a metre

Locking and access

SetDoorLocked(doorId, locked)SERVER

Locks or unlocks a door and its linked door, and tells the players near it.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … }
lockedbooleantrue locks
Returns: true, or false, reason
IsDoorLocked(doorId)SERVER

Whether a door is locked.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … } for a door you declared
Returns: boolean, or nil for no such door
CanUseDoor(source, doorId)SERVER

Whether this player may open this door, by its any-of requirements, and if not, the reason they're shown.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … }
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Requires job: police (on duty)', 'Door not found')
A door or stash given require (not requirements) takes it when it names one rule and refuses it when it names more. A field it doesn't read is reported in the server console.

Finding doors

GetDoor(doorId)SERVER

A door's full data.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … } for a door you declared
Returns: table|nil
GetDoors()SERVER

Every door on the server (a client only knows the doors it streamed in).

Returns: table[]
GetDoorsNearby(x, y, z, range) · GetDoorsNearby(coords, range)SERVER

Every saved door within a range of a point.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, z / coordsnumber / vector3Centre
rangenumberMetres (default 25)
Returns: table[]
GetDoorByPosition(x, y, z, range)SERVER

A saved door near a point, when you know where it is but not its id.

ParamTypeDescription
x, y, znumberWorld position
rangenumber?Metres (default 1). The first door found wins, not the nearest: keep it small
Returns: table|nil

Changing doors

UpdateDoor(doorId, updates, manager)SERVER

Changes label, folder, locked (linked door too), requirements, autolock, autolockDelay, linkedDoorId and metadata (not its managedBy). Other fields are refused: position and model are fixed. Every door starts locked when the server starts.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … } for a door you declared
updatestableFields to change. Clear requirements with {}, not nil
managertable?For a door you manage: its set, { id = 'doors' } (or your opts.id, or 'door:<key>')
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Door not found', someone else's managed door, bad fields)
DeleteDoor(doorId, manager)SERVER

Deletes a saved door.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableDoor id, or { key = … } for a door you declared
managertable?As for UpdateDoor
Returns: true, or false, reason
LinkDoors(doorId1, doorId2, manager?)SERVER

Links two doors so they lock together, unlinking each one's old partner.

ParamTypeDescription
doorId1numberFirst door id
doorId2numberSecond door id
managertable?As for UpdateDoor
Returns: true, or false, reason
UnlinkDoors(doorId, manager?)SERVER

Unlinks both halves of a pair; true if it wasn't linked. linkedDoorId = nil in UpdateDoor can't do this (a nil is no key in Lua).

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumber|tableEither door of the pair (id, or { key = … })
managertable?As for UpdateDoor
Returns: true, or false, reason

Managed and held doors

A managed door belongs to one resource, as the doors you declare with EnsureDoors do: the Doors page and other resources can't change its requirements, link or auto-lock. A held door is yours only while a job runs.

A declared door sits in a set: 'doors' for EnsureDoors with no opts.id, your opts.id otherwise, and 'door:<key>' for one from EnsureDoor. That set is the manager that UpdateDoor, DeleteDoor, LinkDoors and UnlinkDoors take: { id = 'doors' }. To give a door back, declare its set without it; for one from EnsureDoor, EnsureDoors({}, { id = 'door:<key>' }). It is deleted if it was made for you and restored if you adopted it.

GetManagedDoors(id)SERVER

The doors your resource manages, to reconcile against when it starts.

ParamTypeDescription
idany?A manager id, or nil for all
Returns: table[]
HoldDoor(data, opts)SERVER

Holds the door within half a metre of a spot (a heist's vault), making a temporary unsaved door for everyone if there's none. While held, nobody may press it until you say who and it never relocks itself; both leaves of a pair are held. When the hold ends (ReleaseDoor, ReleaseTag, or your resource stopping) it returns to its old lock. A property's door, another resource's managed door and an already held door are refused.

ParamTypeDescription
datatable{ model, x, y, z, heading?, label? }, as the Door Editor reads them
optstable?{ tag?, requirements? }: tag releases it with your run; requirements is who may press it (nobody if left out)
Returns: doorId, how ('held', 'made', 'already'), or false, reason. Also SetHeldDoorAccess(doorId, requirements) (nil = nobody, {} = anyone), ReleaseDoor(doorId) and GetDoorHold(doorId) → { owner, tag, doorId, made } or nil.
local vault = exports.whip_core:HoldDoor({ model = vaultModel, x = pos.x, y = pos.y, z = pos.z }, { tag = 'heist:' .. jobId })
exports.whip_core:SetDoorLocked(vault, false)
exports.whip_core:SetHeldDoorAccess(vault, { charIds = crewCharIds })

Client

The client knows only the doors it has streamed in, as of its last visit: ask the server for anything that matters.

IsDoorLocked(doorId)CLIENT

Whether a door is locked, from the client's cache. A far door catches up as it comes back into range.

ParamTypeDescription
doorIdnumberDoor id
Returns: boolean, or nil for a door the client doesn't know
GetDoorsNearby(range) · GetDoorsNearby(coords, range) · GetDoorsNearby(x, y, z, range)CLIENT

Every saved door within a range of the player, or of a point.

ParamTypeDescription
coords / x, y, zvector3? / number?Left out, the player's position
rangenumberMetres (default 25)
Returns: table[]
GetLoadedDoors()CLIENT

Every door the client has streamed in, not every door: the server's GetDoors has those.

Returns: table[]
GetDoor(ref)CLIENT

A door's full data, from the client cache: by id, or the saved door a world entity is (by model and position).

ParamTypeDescription
refnumber|tableA door id, or { entity = }
Returns: table|nil
local door = exports.whip_core:GetDoor({ entity = entity })

Zones

A zone is an area of the world (a box, sphere or polygon) that knows when players enter and leave, and can enforce rules inside with no code of your own.

Making a zone

On the client, make one with RegisterZone: a 'box', a 'sphere' or a 'poly' (an outline with a min and max Z). The client checks its zones every Config.ZonePollInterval (300 ms). A zone every player shares, or the server must trust, is declared on the server with EnsureZone or drawn in the Zone Editor; it's saved, and you use its key everywhere (require = { zone = 'mrpd' } on an action).

-- Client, in Whip.register: a safe zone
exports.whip_core:RegisterZone({
    type = 'box', id = 'myres_station', pos = vec3(440, -980, 30), size = vec3(20, 20, 10),
    label = 'Police Station', group = 'police', notify = true,
    rules = { noPvP = true, noWeapons = true, heal = true },
    onEnter = function(zone) end,
    onExit = function(zone) end,
})

Rules

RuleTypeInside the zone
noWeaponsboolWeapons removed on entry, re-equipping blocked
noPvPboolThe player can't be hurt, fire or melee
noMeleeboolNo punching or melee
disableFiringboolNo firing; carrying is fine
speedLimitnumberVehicle speed cap (km/h)
noVehiclesboolEjected from the vehicle on entry
heal, healRatebool, numberGradual health regen, HP per tick (default 2)
noWantedLevelboolWanted level cleared and prevented
noCollisionboolNo ped-to-ped collision
noFallDamageboolNo fall damage; the player is collision-proof, so crashes and being run over do none either
jobWhitelist, aceWhitelist, charWhitelisttable, string, tableWho's authorised; meeting any one is enough
ejectUnauthorizedboolTeleports unauthorised players out

Events

Any client resource hears the local player cross any zone. On the server, give a zone trackPlayers = true and listen for the server events of the same names.

AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:entered', function(zone)
    if zone.group == 'police' then --[[ zone.zoneId, zone.label ]] end
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:zone:exited', function(zone) end)

The Zone EditorServer owners

/whip → World → Zones → Open the editor gives you a free camera: 1 / 2 / 3 draw a box, sphere or poly, scroll sizes it.

  • Room scanner. Inside a room, press H and fly: WHIP traces the walls, smoothing over doorways and windows. H previews, scroll sets height, G confirms.
