  • Vertex editor. 4 moves a poly's points and 5 sets each point's own height (E grabs, G confirms, Esc reverts), so one zone can cover a garage lower than the house.

Zones API (server)

The server holds saved zones (EnsureZone and the Zone Editor, synced to every client) and server zones a resource registers with RegisterZone. Every lookup takes a saved zone's key as well as its 'dbzone_<n>' id. New to zones? Read Zones.

The server also knows client zones, as most players report them. One modified client is outvoted, but a zone only one player has is whatever they say. Use EnsureZone or RegisterZone for a zone the server must trust, and trusted = true on IsPointInZone. A client zone id needs letters, digits, _ and -, 60 at most, to reach the server.

Server events

Give a zone of either kind trackPlayers = true and the server checks it every Config.ZoneTrackInterval ms (1000), firing local server events. A player in the character creator or logging out is in no zone; one in another routing bucket still counts.

EventPayload
whip_core:zone:entered{ zoneId, key?, source }
whip_core:zone:exitedThe same, plus dropped = true (left the server inside it) or removed = true (the zone went)

Saved zones

EnsureZone(key, data)SERVER

A saved zone declared by your key; declare it in Whip.register, so it runs at every start. It's made once and updated only when your declaration changes, so an admin's edits stand until then. A different type makes a new zone under the key.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringLetters, digits, _ - . :, at most 60. Refused if another running resource declared it
datatabletype ('box' | 'sphere' | 'poly'), pos, size + heading (box), radius (sphere), points (poly, 3+), minZ, maxZ, label, group, priority, rules, notify, trackVehicles, trackPlayers
Returns: zone, or false, reason
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:EnsureZone('mrpd', {
        type = 'box', pos = vector3(441.0, -982.0, 30.7), size = vector3(60, 50, 20), heading = 0,
        label = 'Mission Row PD', trackPlayers = true,
    })
end)
DeleteZone(keyOrId)SERVER

Deletes a saved zone for everyone. Refused for a zone a running resource declares, and for a server zone (use RemoveZone).

ParamTypeDescription
keyOrIdstringKey, or 'dbzone_<n>' id
Returns: true, or false, reason

Server zones

RegisterZone(id, data)SERVER

Registers a zone for server-side checks, with no tick unless trackPlayers. The id is yours (the registration rule), and your zones go when your resource stops. A bad shape is refused, saying what's wrong.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id
datatabletype, pos, size, heading, radius, points, minZ, maxZ, group, label, trackPlayers, tag (for ReleaseTag). A sphere needs pos + radius, a box pos + size, a poly 3+ points
Returns: true, or false, reason
RemoveZone(id)SERVER

Removes one of your server zones. A client zone of the same id is separate and stays.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id
Returns: true, or false, reason

Queries

IsPointInZone(id, point, trusted)SERVER

Whether a point is inside a zone.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
pointvector3Point to test
trustedboolean?true: only server-held zones answer; a client-made one is false. For anti-cheat
Returns: boolean
if not exports.whip_core:IsPointInZone('mrpd', GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source)), true) then
    return false, 'You need to be at the station'
end
GetPlayersInZone(id)SERVER

The server ids of every player inside a zone. It tests every player: to react as they come and go, use trackPlayers instead of a loop. Players in the character creator or logging out are left out; routing buckets don't matter.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: number[]
GetVehiclesInZone(id)SERVER

The vehicles inside a zone. vehicleId is nil for a car WHIP doesn't track; entity is always set.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: { vehicleId, entity }[]
GetZones()SERVER

Every zone the server knows, as a list: GetZones()[id] is always nil, so use GetZone.

Returns: { zoneDef, zoneDef, … }
GetZone(id)SERVER

One zone's definition.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id, or a saved zone's key
Returns: table|nil

Zones API (client)

Client exports to make zones, ask where the player is and change a zone's rules. New to zones? Read Zones.

Making and removing zones

RegisterZone(data)CLIENT

Makes a zone: type is 'box', 'sphere' or 'poly'. Give it an id (letters, digits, _ and -, 60 at most): the same id again replaces it, and the server only learns of a zone with an id like that.

FieldTypeDescription
typestring'box', 'sphere' or 'poly'
pos, size, headingvector3, vector3, numberA box: its centre, size and heading
pos, radiusvector3, numberA sphere
points, minZ, maxZvec2[], number, numberA poly: its outline and heights
the restanyid, onEnter, onExit, inside, condition, priority, group, label, debug, rules, notify, weather, trackVehicles, onVehicleEnter, onVehicleExit
Returns: string zone id, or false, why (no type, or the id is another resource's)
local id = exports.whip_core:RegisterZone({ type = 'sphere', pos = vec3(200, -800, 30), radius = 8.0,
    onEnter = function(zone) end })
RemoveZone(id)CLIENT

Deletes one of your zones (another resource's is refused), firing onExit if the player was inside.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id
Returns: true, or false, why
RemoveZoneGroup(group)CLIENT

Deletes all your zones in a group; other resources' stay.

ParamTypeDescription
groupstringGroup name
Returns: true, count, or false, why

Where the player is

These take a zone id or a saved zone's key.

IsPointInZone(id, point)CLIENT

Whether a point is inside a zone: instant maths, no polling.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id or key
pointvector3Point to test
Returns: boolean
IsInZone(id)CLIENT

Whether the local player is inside, as of the last poll.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id or key
Returns: boolean
GetZonesInside()CLIENT

Every zone id the local player is inside.

Returns: string[]
GetZonesNearby(pos, radius)CLIENT

Every zone within a radius of a point, nearest first.

ParamTypeDescription
posvector3Centre
radiusnumberMetres (default 50)
Returns: { id, type, label, pos, dist }[]
GetZone(id)CLIENT

A zone as the client holds it: shape, size, rules, label, priority, inside, debug and hasCondition (the function itself isn't returned).

ParamTypeDescription
idstringZone id
Returns: table|nil

Changing a zone

UpdateZone(id, patch)CLIENT

Changes one of your zones: only the keys in patch. A key it doesn't know is refused and nothing changes.

KeyTypeDescription
posvector3Moves the zone (a poly's points move with it)
sizenumber | vector3A sphere's radius, or a box's dimensions. A poly is resized by its points
rulestable|falseReplaces the rules; false for none. To turn one rule off, send the rules without it
conditionfunction|false() → boolean: while it returns false, the player counts as outside (rules off, no events). false takes it off
labelstringThe name shown on entry
prioritynumberWhere zones overlap, all their rules apply; priority settles only the speed limit (highest priority that sets one; ties take the lower), the weather layer, and callback order (enters highest first, exits lowest first). A car park's 20 km/h inside a district's 60 needs the higher priority
notifybooleanThe on-screen enter and exit notice; events fire either way
trackVehiclesbooleanTests the player's vehicle position instead of the ped's, which at speed can skip over a thin zone
debugbooleanDraws the outline every frame. For development only
Returns: true, or false, why ('no zone "x"', 'zone "x" belongs to …', a size its shape doesn't take)
exports.whip_core:UpdateZone('myres_station', { label = 'Closed', rules = { noWeapons = true } })

Time & Weather

The server keeps one clock and one weather for everyone, and every player's game follows it. Layers show one player something else: night in a club, fog in a zone, a storm during a mission.

The world's clock and weather

Read and set them from the server with the Time & Weather API: local h, m = exports.whip_core:GetTime(). Time, weather, freeze, blackout and time scale are saved, so a restart picks up where it left off; a new server starts from Config.StartTime.

-- config.lua
Config.TimeScale    = 1.0     -- 1.0 = normal GTA speed (48 min real = 24 h game)
Config.StartTime    = { hour = 12, minute = 0 }
Config.StartWeather = 'CLEAR'
Config.WeatherTypes = { 'CLEAR', 'EXTRASUNNY', 'CLOUDS', 'OVERCAST', 'RAIN', 'CLEARING', 'THUNDER',
    'SMOG', 'FOGGY', 'XMAS', 'SNOWLIGHT', 'BLIZZARD', 'HALLOWEEN', 'NEUTRAL' }

One player's sky: layers

A layer is a named change to what one player sees, and layers stack. Each field comes from the highest-priority layer that sets it (ties break by name), or else the server. Each source clears only its own layer, so what was under it comes back; yours come off when your resource stops.

FieldTypeMeaning
prioritynumberHigher wins. Default 0
weatherstringA name from Config.WeatherTypes
hour, minutenumberWhere the clock starts; it runs unless frozen
frozenbooleanHolds the clock
blackoutbooleanTurns off the city lights
-- Server: 1am and clear skies inside the club, clock held still
exports.whip_core:SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub', {
    hour = 1, minute = 0, weather = 'CLEAR', frozen = true, priority = 50,
})
exports.whip_core:ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, 'nightclub')

-- Client: no round trip needed, a layer only affects this machine
exports.whip_core:SetWeatherLayer('zone:swamp', { weather = 'FOGGY', priority = 10 })

A zone with a weather field (a weather name, or a layer table such as { weather = 'FOGGY', hour = 3 }) pushes a layer named after itself on enter and pops it on exit; the layer's priority defaults to a little above the zone's own.

frozen = false isn't the same as leaving it out. Left out, it comes from the layer below; false un-freezes a lower layer's clock. blackout works the same. Don't build layers with x and y or nil, which turns false into "no opinion".

Changing it in gameServer owners

/whip → World → Time & Weather sets the time (or Dawn, Noon, Sunset, Midnight), the weather, freeze, blackout and time scale (0 to 10). Changes apply to the whole server at once.

Time & Weather API

Exports for the world's clock and weather, and for per-player layers. New to them? Read Time & Weather.

Reading

GetTime()SERVER

The server time, exact at the moment you call it.

Returns: number hour, number minute
GetWeather()SERVER

The server weather, in upper case.

Returns: string
GetTimeScale()SERVER

The time scale multiplier.

Returns: number
IsTimeFrozen()SERVER

Whether the world's clock is frozen.

Returns: boolean
IsBlackout()SERVER

Whether the city is blacked out.

Returns: boolean

Setting

Each change reaches every client at once and is saved.

SetTime(hour, minute)SERVER

Sets the time and fires whip_core:time:changed { hour, minute }. Out-of-range values wrap, each on its own (25:61 is 01:01).

ParamTypeDescription
hournumber0–23
minutenumber?0–59, default 0
Returns: true, or false, reason for a value that isn't a number
SetWeather(weather)SERVER

Sets the weather and fires whip_core:weather:changed { weather }.

ParamTypeDescription
weatherstringOne of Config.WeatherTypes, any case
Returns: true, or false, reason ('Invalid weather type', or not a string)
SetTimeFrozen(frozen)SERVER

Freezes or unfreezes the clock for everyone, and fires whip_core:time:freezeChanged { frozen }.

ParamTypeDescription
frozenbooleantrue freezes
Returns: true
SetBlackout(blackout)SERVER

Turns every artificial light off or back on.

ParamTypeDescription
blackoutbooleantrue = blackout
Returns: true
SetTimeScale(scale)SERVER

Sets how fast the clock runs: 1.0 is normal (48 min real = 24 h game), 2.0 twice as fast.

ParamTypeDescription
scalenumber0.0–10.0, clamped
Returns: true, or false, reason for a scale that isn't a number

Layers

A layer is yours: another resource can't replace or clear it, and it comes off when your resource stops. Numbers must be numbers and weather one of Config.WeatherTypes.

SetPlayerWeatherLayer(source, name, opts)SERVER

Pushes a layer onto one player.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberPlayer server id
namestringAt most 64 characters. The player sees it as 'server:' .. name, apart from client layers
optstable|nil{ priority?, hour?, minute?, weather?, frozen?, blackout? }, nothing else; nil clears
Returns: true, or false, reason
ClearPlayerWeatherLayer(source, name)SERVER

Removes one of your layers from one player.

Returns: true, or false, reason
GetPlayerWeatherLayers(source)SERVER

The layers the server pushed to this player, not the ones the client set itself (such as its zone's): the client's GetWeatherLayers has the whole picture.

Returns: { [name] = opts }
SetWeatherLayer(name, opts)CLIENT

Adds or replaces a layer on this client; nil opts removes it.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringUnique per source, e.g. 'zone:swamp'
optstable|nil{ priority?, hour?, minute?, weather?, frozen?, blackout? }
Returns: true, or false, why ('Invalid weather type', 'layer "x" belongs to …')
ClearWeatherLayer(name)CLIENT

Removes one of your layers; the others stay.

Returns: true, or false, why (none, or another resource's)
GetWeatherLayers()CLIENT

Every active layer in priority order, and which owns each field: for debugging a stack.

Returns: { layers = { {name, priority} }, owners = { weather = 'zone:swamp', hour = 'server', ... } }

Client

What this player sees, layers included.

GetTime()CLIENT

The time as the local player sees it.

Returns: number hour, number minute
GetWeather()CLIENT

The weather as the local player sees it.

Returns: string
IsTimeFrozen()CLIENT

Whether the clock is frozen for this player, by the server or by a layer.

Returns: boolean
IsTimeOverridden()CLIENT

Whether any layer is active for this player; GetWeatherLayers says which.

Returns: boolean

NPCs

NPCs the server makes and looks after: guards, hostages, targets. WHIP keeps each doing what you set, so it never wanders off; yours go when your resource stops, or with a run's ReleaseTag.

Spawning

SpawnNpc(def, opts)SERVER

Makes an NPC. It exists at once, and the first nearby player's game takes it over within about half a second.

FieldTypeDescription
modelstringA ped model name
coordsvector3|vector4|tableWhere; a vector4's w (or heading) faces it
behaviour'stand'|'guard'?stand (default) stays put; guard wanders near its spot. Either walks back after a fight
conditionstable?{ invincible, canMove, reacts, flees }, default false, true, false, false. flees (run, not fight) needs reacts = true
weaponstring|table?A weapon name (GTA's or a streamed add-on), or { name, ammo }
armournumber?0–100
looktable?A character editor look, checked like a character's save (10,000 bytes of JSON at most). The ped becomes the look's freemode model
interior, gateAtboolean?, coords?It stands inside an MLO: kept frozen until the interior loads. gateAt: where to look for the MLO, if not at its spot
opts.tagstring?Your run tag (ReleaseTag)
opts.hostileTotable?{ people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }: fights the nearest of them online and not down. { except = { ... } }: everyone else, only with opts.range
opts.fightBackboolean?Fights its attacker (default true) until they go down or a minute after their last hit
opts.corpseMsnumber?How long a body stays (default 60000; 0 = until removed)
opts.rangenumber?1–500 m: fights hostileTo only this near its spot, chases a shooter up to three times as far, then walks back. Left out, anywhere
opts.groupstring?Up to 128 characters: hurt one (even with one fatal shot) and every NPC of yours in the group fights back
Returns: npcId, netId, or false, reason
local npcId, netId = exports.whip_core:SpawnNpc({
    model = 's_m_y_dealer_01', coords = vector4(x, y, z, heading),
    behaviour = 'guard', weapon = 'WEAPON_PISTOL',
}, { tag = 'run:42', hostileTo = { people = { source } } })
DespawnNpc(npcId)SERVER

Removes one of your NPCs; its owner's game deletes the ped.

Returns: true, or false, reason

Changing what it does

SetNpcState(npcId, patch)SERVER

Changes what one of your NPCs does; whichever game runs it next carries on. patch also takes behaviour, hostileTo (false calms it and forgets its attackers), fightBack, conditions, interior and range (false: anywhere again).

patchTypeDescription
attacktable | false?What it attacks when it has nobody to fight: { net = a car's netId } or { at = coords } (a prop). Shoots, or walks up without a weapon; leaves a burnt-out car
postcoords?A new spot to walk to and stand or guard at. With interior = true it's inside an MLO
gateAtcoords?Where to look for that MLO, if not at the post (the spot a group gathers round)
pacestring?'walk' (default) or 'run'
followserverId | falseWalks after that player, waiting while they're gone or down. false stops it: set post too, or it walks back
fleeserverId | falseRuns from that player, fighting nobody
animtable | false{ dict, clip } or { scenario }, looped where it stands
Returns: true, or false, reason
exports.whip_core:SetNpcState(npcId, { hostileTo = { people = { source } } })   -- the alarm tripped
exports.whip_core:SetNpcState(hostageId, { follow = source, pace = 'run' })    -- the rescue

Reading and events

Events: whip_core:npc:spawned, :despawned { reason }, :damaged { amount, attacker }, :killed { killer, weapon, coords }.

GetNpc(ref) · GetNpcs({ tag })SERVER

GetNpc returns a copy or nil: { npcId, owner, tag, model, netId, alive, health, armour, behaviour, conditions, targets, focus, range, group, killer, killedAt, weapon, coords, post, pace, follow, flee, interior }. killer is the server's reading (a car's driver for a run-over). ref is an npcId, or { entity = } or { netId = } while that is still the NPC's ped. GetNpcs returns yours, or one tag's.

local paid = {}
AddEventHandler('whip_core:npc:killed', function(e)
    local npc = exports.whip_core:GetNpc(e.npcId)   -- the server's reading, not the event's
    if not npc or npc.owner ~= GetCurrentResourceName() or paid[npc.npcId] then return end
    if not npc.alive and npc.killer then
        paid[npc.npcId] = true
        exports.whip_core:PayPlayer(npc.killer, 500, { reason = 'Bounty' })
    end
end)
Check a kill before paying. Any server resource can fire an event: ask GetNpc.

Interactions

Everything a player does with E, a car part's prompt or the F1 wheel is one client call: AddAction. Server code adds prompts with AddPoint and NPC conversations with StartConversation.

A first prompt

Declare actions in Whip.register, so they come back when whip_core restarts. An action is yours by id: the same id again replaces it, and it goes when your resource stops.

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:AddAction({
        id = 'stash',
        at = { coords = vector3(200.0, -800.0, 30.0) },
        label = 'Open Stash',
        onSelect = function(ctx)
            TriggerServerEvent('myres:openStash')   -- its own thread: waiting is fine
        end,
    })
end)

A prompt shows within Config.InteractVisibleRange (5 m) and works within Config.InteractActiveRange (2 m); E acts on the one nearest the centre of view, inside Config.InteractFocusCone (40°). Prompts hide while a screen or bar has the input, and while the player is dead or in a vehicle unless require says alive = false or vehicle = 'in'. Ground items, containers and doors make their own. Later examples show AddAction alone.

AddAction

AddAction(def)CLIENT

Puts an action in the world. at says where; every other field reads the same wherever that is. "World prompts" below means every at but the wheel and car parts.

FieldTypeDescription
idstring?Yours: another resource's 'bench' is another action. Left out, one is made from the rest, the same every time
attableRequired. See at
labelstring | function(ctx)What it says; a function is asked at every draw, so it mustn't wait. The wheel needs one
iconstring?A glyph, or text drawn as is. On the wheel, no icon or text over 3 letters draws the label's first letter
imagestring | function(ctx)?World prompts: a picture above the label, a path under whip_core's html/ ('img/vehicles/<model>.webp') or a https://cfx-nui-<resource>/… URL
descriptionstring | function(ctx)?Wheel only: shown beside the name while aimed at. A function is asked as the wheel opens
requiretable?See require
canInteractfunction(ctx)?Your own rule on top of require: return true to offer it. Asked often; mustn't wait
onSelectfunction(ctx)Required, here or on each option (an option takes the nearest one above it; with none, F8 says so). Runs in its own thread, so it may wait
optionstable?See options
reachnumber?Metres to use it (default Config.InteractActiveRange). Match your server's distance check
seeFromnumber?World prompts: how far it appears. Clamped to Config.InteractVisibleRange (the default); raise that to go further
scalenumber?World prompts: size against other prompts (1.5, 0.75), 0.25 to 4
sizeRangenumber?World prompts: the distance its size is designed at (default its reach, so changing the reach resizes it; set the first reach here to stop that)
focusMode'aim' | 'near'World prompts: 'aim' (default) picks the one looked at, for things side by side; 'near' the closest in a wide cone, for a door or counter
onBlurfunction?World prompts: called when it stops being the one E acts on, to fold an opened menu
stylestring | table?World prompts: see Styles
holdMsnumber?World prompts: hold E (A on a pad) this long instead of a press (1500 to plant a charge); letting go, looking away or scrolling cancels. Per option too (0 is a press). Your server still checks it like any press
pressboolean | vector3 | table?World prompts and car parts: the hand reaches towards true (the prompt's point), a point, or { coords | offset, normal }, for looks only; onSelect runs at once. Too far, seated or no clips installed: a plain press. Per option too (false for one with its own animation). See PlayPress
firstboolean?vehiclePart: above the part's own options (Open Door, Lock), so E does it while canInteract says yes. Per option too
onGonefunction(ctx)?entity: called once the entity and the action have gone (ctx.id, ctx.owner); add it again from here
onFound, onLostfunction(ctx)?model: told as every prop of the model comes within 50 m and leaves (60 m, or gone), with ctx = { id, owner, entity, model, prop, coords }, each in its own thread. In onLost use ctx.coords
groupstring?For RemoveActionGroup
enabledboolean?false hides it
Returns: id, false, warnings, or false, reason, warnings (no at, an at naming nothing, no onSelect, a wheel entry with no label, an unknown require word). warnings lists what was wrong but not refused, or is nil; the false on success carries it through the export.
exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id = 'bench',
    at = { coords = vector3(12.1, -1105.3, 29.8), heading = 90.0 },
    label = 'Weapon Bench', icon = 'store',
    require = { job = 'gunsmith', item = 'toolkit' },
    onSelect = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('mygunsmith:openBench') end,
})
Misspellings are warned about, not refused. An unknown field (lable, canUse), a wrong type or an out-of-range number is reported in F8 with its likely meaning, then left out or clamped; so is a field the place doesn't read. Only require is strict. ox_target's and qb-target's distance is read as reach.

at: where it lives

atWhat it is
{ coords = vector3, heading? }A prompt at a point. With heading it stands like a sign (not drawn from behind); without, it faces you. follow = function() return x, y, z, heading end moves it
{ entity = handle, offset?, bone?, heading? }On a local entity. Removed a few seconds after the entity goes (see onGone). offset is in the entity's own frame. heading stands it like a sign at that turn from the entity's facing, turning as it turns (180: on its back); without one it faces the player. For anything networked use netId
{ netId = n, offset?, bone?, heading? }On a networked NPC or car, shown whenever it's streamed in, whatever its handle; nothing to re-add. The id can come from the server before it streams in
{ model = 'prop_vend_soda_01', offset?, heading?, faces?, perModel? }On every prop of that model nearby (or a list of models), offered on the nearest, never from a car. offset: x across, y out of its face, z up. heading stands it like a sign at that turn from the prop's facing (try 0, 90, 180). faces = 2 for two-sided props. perModel = { ['prop_x'] = { offset, heading } } overrides one model
{ vehiclePart = 'hood' }A choice on a car part: 'hood' (shown only while open; engine work goes here), 'trunk', 'door_dside_f', 'door_pside_f', 'door_dside_r', 'door_pside_r', or the Get On / Board prompt of a 'bike', 'bicycle' or 'boat'
{ radial = true }An F1 wheel entry with its icon and label, sorted by label. Aimed with mouse or stick, then click or A
{ aimBox = 'vehicle' | 'object' | 'ped' | 'world' }Where the player looks on the car, prop or person (or a list of kinds) within reach, on its bounding box (or body, for a helicopter's rotor span); a wall in front hides it. 'world' is the map itself: ctx.entity is nil, ctx.world true, ctx.normal the surface's facing, and a car or prop in front wins
An aimBox casts a ray every frame. Add it only while it means something (a rope in hand, an officer on duty) and remove it after.

require: who may use it

Every key given must pass. The client uses it to decide what to offer, so check again on the server. Any other key (a door's jobs) refuses the whole action.

KeyExamplePasses when
alivealive = falseAlso offered to the downed (by default, nobody downed is)
vehicle'in' / 'out'In a vehicle / on foot. World prompts default to on foot; the wheel to either
job'police' or { 'police', 'ems' }A role at one of these jobs (key or jobId)
onDutytrue…on duty there; with no job, anywhere
jobPermission'canManage'…with this permission; with no job, at any job
item'toolkit', { item = 'lockpick', count = 2 }, { 'toolkit', 'gloves' }Carrying all of them
held'jerry_can' or a listThe item in hand is one of these (SetHeldItem)
zone'mrpd' or a listStanding in one of these zones
charId12 or a listOne of these characters
ace'whip.devtools'Holds this ACE (asked once, then remembered)

A vehiclePart action refuses alive = false and vehicle = 'in': it's always used on foot and alive.

require is free; canInteract isn't. canInteract crosses into your resource on every pass, about 95 times a second per option near a car. Say what you can with require, checked first, and for a state only you know, add the action while it holds and remove it after.

ctx: what your functions get

label, canInteract and onSelect get one table; only onSelect's has the functions.

FieldDescription
id, owner, optionYour action's id, your resource, and which option
underIn a menu: the option it was chosen under ('repair'); nil at the top
entity, coordsThe entity aimed at, ridden or the part's car (nil for aimBox = 'world'), and the prompt's point
model, face, propat = { model }: model name, face (1, or 2), and the prop's id
playerOn a person who is a real player: { serverId, playerIdx, activeJob, isDead }; nil for an NPC. Name: GetPlayerFullName(ctx.player.serverId)
flash(r, g, b), status(text, ms), refuse(why)Tint the prompt, say something on it, or flash amber with a reason (a notification off world prompts)
beginInput(opts), cancelInput(), inputText()See typing into a prompt
typedWhat's typed so far with a caret, or false, for your label
exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id = 'frisk', at = { aimBox = 'ped' }, label = 'Frisk', reach = 2.0,
    require = { job = 'police', onDuty = true },
    canInteract = function(ctx) return ctx.player ~= nil and not ctx.player.isDead end,
    onSelect = function(ctx) TriggerServerEvent('police:frisk', ctx.player.serverId) end,
})

options: several choices on one action

Each option has its own id, label, icon, image, description, require, canInteract and onSelect, and takes the action's for what it leaves out. A world prompt shows them as a stack the player scrolls; the wheel, as entries.

exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id = 'counter', at = { coords = vector3(25.7, -1346.7, 29.5) }, icon = 'store',
    options = {
        { id = 'buy', label = 'Buy', onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('shop:buy') end },
        { id = 'stock', label = 'Restock', require = { job = 'shopkeep', onDuty = true },
          onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('shop:restock') end },
    },
})
An option's require and canInteract add to the action's. An option can only narrow who sees it. The exception is alive: the option's own wins, else the action's.

Menus

On a world prompt, an option can have options of its own, any levels deep. Its label gets a ›, and choosing it shows them on the same prompt with a Back; pressing one, or looking away, folds back. A nested option must also pass every option above it and takes what it leaves out from them; ids need only differ within one menu. Car parts and the wheel have no menus (F8 warns, and leaves them out).

options = {
    { id = 'repair', label = 'Repair', options = {
        { id = 'engine', label = 'Engine', onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mech:fix', 'engine') end },
        { id = 'body', label = 'Body', onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mech:fix', 'body') end },
    } },
    { id = 'wash', label = 'Wash', onSelect = function() TriggerServerEvent('mech:wash') end },
}

A menu whose options depend on the player (the cars they own, the orders waiting for them) is filled when it opens: give options a function returning the list. It's called each time the menu opens, with the same ctx as onSelect, in a thread of its own, so it can wait for a server callback. The prompt shows "One moment…" until it returns and "Nothing here" for an empty list. What it returns is read like any options, menus of either kind included. Going Back to a filled menu shows the list it had, without asking again.

An option with stay = true keeps the prompt on its menu after onSelect, instead of folding back to the top, and a filled menu is filled again once onSelect has finished. Use it for something a player may press twice, or that changes what the menu shows.

{ id = 'orders', label = 'My orders', options = function(ctx)
    local orders = exports.whip_core:Callback('mycafe:myOrders') or {}
    local list = {}
    for _, o in ipairs(orders) do
        list[#list + 1] = { id = 'order' .. o.id, label = o.name, stay = true, onSelect = function()
            exports.whip_core:Callback('mycafe:collect', o.id)
        end }
    end
    return list
end }

Changing and removing actions

UpdateAction(id, patch)CLIENT

Lays patch over one of your actions; an at in it replaces the old one whole. A refused change leaves it as it was.

Returns: true, false, warnings, or false, reason, warnings
SetActionStyle(id, style)CLIENT

Restyles one of your world prompts in place, without fading or losing its place, so it can turn red as a timer runs out. style is a name, a table or nil for the default.

Returns: true, false, warnings, or false, reason
RemoveAction(id)CLIENT

Takes out one of your actions; another resource's is refused.

Returns: true, or false, reason
RemoveActionGroup(group)CLIENT

Takes out all your actions in a group, not another resource's of the same name.

Returns: true, count, or false, reason
GetAction(id)CLIENT

One of your actions as data, with whether each option is offered to this player now and why not. The first thing to check when an action never shows.

Returns: { id, owner, key, group, reach, seeFrom, enabled, at, label, icon, mounted, engineIds, options = { { id, label, offered, why } } } or nil. mounted: 'prompt', 'aimbox', 'props', 'radial', 'part', or false if it failed (F8 says why)
for _, opt in ipairs((exports.whip_core:GetAction('bench') or {}).options or {}) do
    print(opt.id, opt.offered, opt.why)
end

The hand: press and held props

Put a torch or clipboard in a player's hand with HoldProps from your server, never your own CreateObject and attach, so everyone sees it in the hand. The hand holds one set, shared with WHIP's own (an emote's cup, a progress bar's tool), and a new set replaces the old. Yours go when your resource stops, and whip_core:heldProps:lost says why when yours leave without you asking.

PlayPress(target, opts)CLIENT

The player's hand reaches out to a point and back, for looks only: it never moves the player or takes control. It returns at once, so do the real thing yourself, before or after.

ParamTypeDescription
targetvector3 | tableA point, or { entity, offset?, bone? }
opts.normalvector3?The surface's facing: the hand stops where it meets it. Pass one for walls, doors and panels
opts.onContactfunction?Runs once as the hand arrives, or as a press is cut short (a ragdoll, a car, an emote). Never when it returns false
Returns: true, or false, why: 'off' (disabled, too far, seated, falling, swimming, aiming, already against the surface, or no animation reaches), 'busy', 'dead'
ringTheBell()
exports.whip_core:PlayPress(vector3(x, y, z), { normal = vector3(0, -1, 0) })
Server owners. Config.InteractPress: enabled (Hand press in /whip → Settings → Config), maxDistance (2.5 m), followHand. Picking up from the ground always plays GTA's own grab.
HoldProps(source, props, tag)SERVER

Puts props in a player's hand for everyone. At most one new set a second per player; faster calls wait, and only the newest is made.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
propstable[]One or two { model, bone?, offset? = { x, y, z }, rot? = { x, y, z } }; bone defaults to the left hand (18905)
tagstring?Default 'held', kept as '<resource>:<tag>'
Returns: true, or false, why
exports.whip_core:HoldProps(source, { { model = 'prop_cs_police_torch', offset = { 0.1, 0.0, 0.0 } } }, 'torch')
DropHeldProps(source, tag)SERVER

Takes your props of tag, or all of yours, out of the player's hand. Never anyone else's.

Returns: true, or false, why when they held none of yours
GetHeldPropsTag(source)SERVER

What the hands hold or are about to: '<resource>:<tag>', WHIP's 'emote', 'bar', 'give', 'take', or nil.

Returns: string|nil
GetOwnHeldProp(model, tag) · DropOwnHeldProp(model, tag) · SetOwnHeldPropPose(model, tag, pose)CLIENT

Your held prop (your tag, its model) on this player's game, while it holds it. GetOwnHeldProp returns its entity; DropOwnHeldProp lets go here at once (still tell your server's DropHeldProps); SetOwnHeldPropPose sets another grip for a while, pose = { bone?, offset = { x, y, z }, rot = { x, y, z } }, or nil for the server's.

Returns: entity|nil; the other two boolean, whether it was done
AimDot(on)CLIENT

true shows the aim dot while you aim something that isn't a weapon, false after (weapons get it from Config.AimDot). Removed if your resource stops.

Returns: nothing

Typing into a prompt

A world prompt can ask for a value: start it from onSelect with ctx.beginInput. The prompt steps aside, and what stands in its place depends on what the player is holding:

  • A keyboard: a capsule in the chat capsule's look, with the option's glyph and words, saying "Start typing". The keys go to it while the mouse still looks round. Enter gives the value, Esc (or Backspace on nothing) leaves it.
  • A pad: WHIP's on-screen keyboard, in 3D. The left stick moves a circle over the keys, the D-pad steps from key to key and A types; X deletes, Y is a space, LT turns to the symbols, RB or Done gives the value, B or Cancel leaves it. The right stick still looks round; walking is held off until it is done. A number gets the number pad.

Both stand where the prompt was, facing the player, and stay there while they look round. Picking up a pad or putting it down while typing swaps them, keeping what was typed. By default the value is a number (digits only, no leading zero); numeric = false takes any text.

exports.whip_core:AddAction({
    id = 'deposit', at = { coords = vector3(150.2, -1040.1, 29.4) }, icon = 'deposit', label = 'Deposit',
    onSelect = function(ctx)
        ctx.beginInput({
            max = 6,            -- most characters (default 9 for a number, 64 for text)
            prefix = '$', commas = true,   -- shown as $1,250
            onSubmit = function(text) TriggerServerEvent('bank:deposit', tonumber(text)) end,
            onCancel = function() end,   -- left, or replaced by another input
        })
    end,
})
optsTypeDescription
maxnumber?The most characters: default 9 for a number, 64 for text
numericboolean?true (default): digits only, the number pad on a controller. false: any text, the whole keyboard
titlestring?What is being typed, over the text. Default: the option's own words
prefixstring?Shown before the text, such as '$'
commasboolean?A number shown in groups of three (1,250); what onSubmit gets stays digits
placeholderstring?What shows until something is typed. Default 'Start typing'
valuestring?The text it starts with
onSubmitfunction(text)The value was given
onCancelfunction?It was left, the player walked off, or another input replaced it
onChangefunction(text)?Each change of the text

Styles

A style sets a world prompt's size, colour, visibility and motion, by name or as a table. What it leaves out comes from its base, then 'default' (Config.Interact3D). WHIP ships subtle (smaller, hidden until in reach) and lively; server owners add styles in Config.Interact3D.styles and set every prompt under styles.default. WHIP's own prompts take one per group from groupStyles: doors, vehicles, ground_items, garages, containers, properties, conversation, atm, and actions for every AddAction and AddPoint. A prompt's own style wins; a misspelt one is warned about in F8.

style = 'subtle'
style = { base = 'subtle', badgeScale = 1.3, tint = '#ffc850', fadeMs = 250 }
FieldDescription
baseStart from this named style
badgeScale, labelScaleCircle or label size, 0.25 to 4, on top of scale
opacity{ seen = 0.35, inReach = 0.85, focused = 1.0 }; seen = 0 hides it until in reach
tint, labelTint'#ffc850' or { 255, 200, 80 }; white is no change
fadeMs, crossfadeMs, slideMs, appearMsFades (default 100), ring to key, stack slide, arrival (220), in ms
flash, flashMsThe ctx.flash answer: 'blink' (default) or 'fade', back to tint; flashMs defaults to Config.Interact3D.flashMs
gap, stackGap, stackAlpha, previewScaleSpacing, unselected-option alpha and picture size
cullBehindfalse draws a sign-like prompt from behind too
easing'smooth' (default), 'linear', 'out', 'inOut', 'back'; or fadeEasing, crossfadeEasing, slideEasing
appear, focus, idle, pressMotion: 'fade' (default) 'pop' 'slide' 'none'; 'none' 'pop' 'pulse'; 'none' 'pulse' 'bob'; 'none' 'pop'
labelWeight, labelOutline, labelOutlineColour, labelCase, labelShadow400–800 (700); width 0–8 (3); colour (black); 'upper' or 'none'; false removes it
theme'keycap', 'classic', 'glass', 'rim' or 'dot'. Left out, the player's Prompt shape setting in the pause menu's Map & HUD (default Config.Interact3D.theme)
darkBlack and white swapped. Left out, the player's Dark prompts setting (default Config.Interact3D.dark)

Glyphs

lock unlock lockpick door hood_closed hood_open trunk_closed trunk_open trunk_lid garage car store turbo furnish house pickup bank deposit withdraw back fuel nozzle cash talk phone bag emote id power headlights seat devtools place give eat respawn objective target pin star timer, and mfr_<brand> for a car maker's badge. Other text is drawn as is ('$'). The default, 'E', shows the player's Interact key, or A on a pad.

Points from the server: AddPoint

A prompt your server adds while it runs (a Talk on an NPC, a hand-in spot), for everyone or named players. Pressing it runs onUse on the server after WHIP checks distance, audience and requirements. It's gone when your resource stops, and isn't saved.

AddPoint(def)SERVER

Adds a prompt from the server.

FieldTypeDescription
attable{ coords, heading? }; { netId, offset?, bone? } (while each game has it); { vehicle = id | { plate }, offset?, bone? } (a WHIP car while it's out); { ground = groundItemId, offset? } (until picked up); or { container = containerId, offset? }. On a car, pile or container it sits above their own prompts
label, iconstring?Text and glyph
optionstable?Up to 6 { id, label?, icon?, require?, options? }; none means use.option = 'default'. Nested options make a menu with a Back: 3 deep, 6 a level, 40 in all. Only a leaf is pressed, named by use.path ('tools/hack/firewall'), and the server checks every require on the path. What a menu requires, its options and Back need too
requiretable?AddAction's words, checked again on the server. An unknown word is refused; a zone must be a saved one
audiencetable|'everyone'?{ people = { serverId | { charId = n } } }: only they see and use it. Default 'everyone'
reach, seeFrom, focusMode, enabled, style, holdMs?As AddAction's; false clears style or holdMs. In a menu only leaves are held. A hold is the player's game asking: onUse is still the check
talkboolean?A Talk on its NPC (icon talk). While the NPC talks to someone else it shows Config.Conversations.speakingText; while disabled, busyText. Pressing it then only says so again
quietForaudience?With talk: who sees nothing, not "busy", while it's disabled
tagstring?Your run tag (ReleaseTag)
onUsefunction(source, use)use = { pointId, option, path, useId, coords, netId }. Return false, 'why' to refuse; the player is told why. Keep it quick: start a thread for slow work
Returns: pointId, false, warnings, or false, reason, warnings: warnings lists unknown fields (onSelect, lable) and a clamped reach or seeFrom, also in the server console; a wrong value is refused. Also UpdatePoint(pointId, patch) (false clears a field; the tag stays), RemovePoint(pointId), GetPoints({ tag }).
local pointId = exports.whip_core:AddPoint({
    at = { netId = npcNetId, offset = vector3(0.0, 0.0, 0.3) },
    label = 'Talk',
    options = { { id = 'work', label = 'Got work?' }, { id = 'bye', label = 'Leave' } },
    audience = { people = { source } },
    tag = 'run:42',
    onUse = function(source, use)
        if use.option == 'work' then StartJob(source) end
    end,
})

Conversations: StartConversation

An NPC talks and the player picks one of up to four answers with the scroll wheel and E, in the dialog capsule. It opens only from a point's onUse, and the server checks each answer before onChoose hears it. It ends when you end it, an ends answer is chosen, the player leaves, opens a screen, goes down or logs out, or the NPC dies, goes or turns hostile. Others nearby see it as /me bubbles (Config.Conversations.watcherBubbles).

StartConversation(source, spec)SERVER

Opens a conversation for the player who pressed your point; a new one replaces theirs.

FieldTypeDescription
fromUsenumberuse.useId, within 10 s. A point on an NPC opens only with that NPC
npcId / netIdnumberThe speaker: a living SpawnNpc NPC or a networked entity
speaker, linestringName, and what they say (440 characters at most)
optionstable1 to 4 { id, label, ends?, input?, cost? }. input = { min, max, prefix }: the answer becomes a field for an amount, checked against min and max (Backspace on an empty field goes back). cost = { amount, currency?, method?, reason? }: charged like ChargePlayer before onChoose (method auto/cash/bank, or currency an item key); unpaid, it's refused with the reason and the answers stay up
nexttable?{ [answerId] = { line, options } }: replies sent ahead. Without one the capsule dims until UpdateConversation (15 s, then it ends). A costed answer's reply waits for payment
layout'grid'|'stack'?2x2 grid (default) or a column
onChoosefunction(source, answerId, convId, amount)?A checked (and paid) answer; amount for input
canChoosefunction(source, answerId, convId)?Return false, 'why' to refuse an answer before it's taken or paid
onEndfunction(source, why)?'ended', 'chose', 'left', 'blocked', 'downed', 'logout', 'killed', 'gone', 'hostile', 'no answer', 'replaced', 'released', 'stopped'
tagstring?Your run tag
Returns: convId, or false, reason. Also UpdateConversation(convId, { line, options, next, speaker, canChoose }) (canChoose = false removes it), EndConversation(convId), GetConversation(convId).
onUse = function(source, use)
    exports.whip_core:StartConversation(source, {
        fromUse = use.useId, npcId = npcId, speaker = 'Fence', line = 'Got the goods?',
        options = { { id = 'yes', label = 'Here.' }, { id = 'bye', label = 'Leave', ends = true } },
        next = { yes = { line = 'Let me see.', options = { { id = 'deal', label = 'Deal?' } } } },
        onChoose = function(source, answer, convId)
            if answer == 'deal' then PayFor(source); exports.whip_core:EndConversation(convId) end
        end,
    })
end

Good to know

  • Functions cross as references. Calling one works; type(fn) == 'function' on the other side doesn't.
  • Doors read rules the other way round: any one passes. See Who may open a door.

UI Library

Toasts, progress bars, dialogs, skill checks, on-screen text and a one-line text field, plus the calls that keep your screen, hotkeys and controls from fighting WHIP's. The exports are the client's, except the cards marked SERVER.

I want to...

I want to...Call
Show a short messageNotify
Load a model or animation and wait for itLoadModel, LoadAnimDict...
Run a timed bar with an animationProgress; if finishing hands something out, the server's Progress(source, opts)
Ask for a form, a yes or no, or an OKInput, Confirm, Alert
Run a minigameSkillCheck; your own game: Whip.skillCheckGame
Show a mode's controls, or an objectiveShowText, ShowObjective
Let the player type one lineOpenComposer (which input?)
Know if the player is busy, or a hotkey may actIsGameInputFree
Open your own NUI screenSetScreenOpen
Let the player put a prop down where they want itPlaceObject
Hold controls off, or freeze or hide the pedBlockControls, HoldPlayerPed
Show WHIP's yes or no questions on your own screenRegisterAskChannel

Blocking components

A progress bar, Input, Confirm, Alert, SkillCheck and PlaceObject wait for the player, so call them from a command or your own thread. They share these rules:

  • One at a time. A call while another is up returns false, 'busy'. Other reasons come second the same way: 'cancelled', 'timeout', 'failed' (SkillCheck).
  • Other screens. It closes the inventory, and is 'busy' over another resource's SetScreenOpen screen. A dialog is also 'busy' over the chat composer, radial wheel, /whip panel, character screen, appearance creator or furnisher.
  • Your own screen doesn't block your dialogs, but a dialog drops the focus when it closes: call SetNuiFocus(true, true) when it returns.
  • It's yours. When your resource stops, WHIP cancels your bar or dialog and hides your text.
  • Positional or one table: Confirm('Sell?', 'Sure?') or Confirm({ title = 'Sell?', message = 'Sure?' }). While one is up, IsGameInputFree() is false.

Messages and loading

Notify(text, type?, duration?)CLIENT

Shows a toast. Doesn't block; several can show at once.

ParamTypeDescription
textstringThe message
typestring?'success', 'error', 'info' (default) or 'warning'
durationnumber?Milliseconds, default 3000
exports.whip_core:Notify('Inventory full', 'error', 5000)
LoadModel(model, timeoutMs?) · LoadAnimDict(dict, timeoutMs?) · LoadTextureDict(dict, timeoutMs?) · LoadAnimSet(set, timeoutMs?) · LoadPtfxAsset(asset, timeoutMs?)CLIENT

Loads something the game streams and waits, up to timeoutMs (default 5000). LoadModel takes a name or hash and returns the hash, or nil (at once for a model the game lacks); the others return a boolean. LoadAnimSet is a walk style's clip set, LoadPtfxAsset a particle asset. Call from a thread; from a satellite, Whip.core:LoadModel(...) returns false if whip_core restarts.

local hash = exports.whip_core:LoadModel('prop_beer_bottle')
if not hash then return end
local obj = CreateObject(hash, x, y, z, true, true, false)
SetModelAsNoLongerNeeded(hash)

Progress bars

Progress(label, duration?, opts?) · Progress(opts)CLIENT

Shows a progress bar and waits, with an optional animation, a prop in hand, and controls held off.

ParamTypeDescription
labelstringText above the bar
durationnumber?Milliseconds, default 3000
opts.canCancelboolean?X or Escape stops it. Default false (also on the server), true in a use with a progress bar
opts.animtable?{ dict, clip, flag }; flag default 49 (upper body). Or { scenario = 'WORLD_HUMAN_VEHICLE_MECHANIC' }
opts.proptable?{ model, bone, offset, rot }; bone default 18905 (left hand); offset, rot are {x, y, z}
opts.disabletable?{ move, combat, car }. Default: walking and fighting off, driving on. move = false frees movement; move = 'walk' allows a walk, and running cancels
opts.cancelOnDeathboolean?Default true: dying or ragdolling (a long fall too) cancels it, shown red. false: a bar for the downed
opts.cancelOnExitboolean?Default false. Leaving the vehicle cancels it; out of one, it ends at once. The server's refuses 'not in a vehicle' and 'left the vehicle'
opts.notWhiletable?Any of 'swimming' (covers under water), 'underwater', 'falling'. Already so: 'refused'; becoming so: cancelled, and the capsule says why. A sunk car is under water, a skydive falling (GetBodyState)
opts.iconstring?The capsule disc's icon: a prompt glyph name ('eat', 'fuel'... in html/js/glyphs.js). Default an hourglass
opts.itemstring|table?An item key ('jerry_can') or a slot's { item, metadata }: the disc shows its picture
Returns: true, or false, why, words: 'cancelled', 'busy', 'timeout' or 'refused'; words is what the capsule said
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:Progress({
    label = 'Drinking...', duration = 5000, canCancel = true,
    anim = { dict = 'mp_player_intdrink', clip = 'loop_bottle' },
    prop = { model = 'prop_amb_beer_bottle' },
    disable = { move = false },
})
A client bar is the player's word. A modified client can skip it. If finishing hands out anything, use the server Progress or a declared timed use.
IsProgressActive() · CancelProgress()CLIENT

IsProgressActive: is any bar running? CancelProgress stops the bar your resource started (its caller gets false, 'cancelled'), never another's.

Returns: boolean (false: nothing of yours to cancel)
InterruptProgress(why) · ShowInterrupted(why, what?)CLIENT

For a bar or mode stopped by something the player didn't choose: the capsule turns red with why, then goes. WHIP's own already do this. InterruptProgress ends your bar (its caller gets false, 'cancelled', why). ShowInterrupted is for your own mode: call it, then HideText, which won't cut it short. Not shown while a bar is up.

ParamTypeDescription
whystring'You were knocked down'; for a long fall, use GetBodyState's words
whatstring?ShowInterrupted only: what it stopped, 'Placing the sign'
Returns: boolean: interrupted (false: no bar of yours), or shown
Progress(source, opts)SERVER

Shows a bar on a player's screen and waits; true only if it really ran. The server keeps the clock (a one-shot token; an answer before 90% of duration is 'too fast' and logged). Takes the client options as one table; duration is required. Call it from a SecureEvent, not a SecureCallback (the client gives up on those after 10 s). For an item, use a declared timed use: it also checks, takes and refunds the item.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
opts.neartable?{ coords = vector3, range = 3.0 } or { vehicle = vehicleId, range = 5.0 }, checked at start and finish ('too far')
opts.tagany?Your run tag: ReleaseTag(tag) cancels it; a released tag is 'run ended'
opts.notWhiletable?Checked by the player's game; never started is 'refused'
Returns: true, or false, why: 'cancelled', 'refused', 'busy', 'timeout', 'too fast', 'too far', 'dead' (unless cancelOnDeath = false), 'not in a vehicle', 'left the vehicle', 'player left', 'run ended', or a refusal (no duration, a bad near)
local done = Whip.core:Progress(source, {
    label = 'Picking the lock...', duration = 8000,
    anim = { dict = 'mini@safe_cracking', clip = 'idle_base' },
    near = { coords = doorCoords, range = 3.0 },
})
if not done then return end
Call waiting exports through Whip.core. Without dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart leaves exports.whip_core:Progress waiting forever; Whip.core returns false, 'whip_core stopped'. Do the same for SkillCheck, ChargePlayer, Callback and database reads when you hold a flag across the call.

Dialogs and text input

You wantUse
A form: fields, a dropdown, limits. A centred dialog that waitsInput(title, fields)
One line of text without leaving the game view; keyboard onlyOpenComposer(opts)
A code typed into a 3D prompt: a keypad, a safectx.beginInput(opts) (Interactions)
Input(title, fields) · Input({ title, fields })CLIENT

Shows a form with mouse focus and waits. required = true blocks an empty field; min/max are checked on Submit. An empty optional number returns 0.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringThe title
fieldstableA list of { label, type, ... }, by type:
text→ stringplaceholder, default
number→ numberplaceholder, default, min, max
select→ stringoptions = { {value, label}, ... }, default; returns the value
checkbox→ booleanplaceholder (its label), default
textarea→ stringplaceholder, default, rows (1-12, default 3)
Returns: { [1] = firstValue, ... }, or false, why
local r = exports.whip_core:Input('Create Report', {
    { label = 'Title', type = 'text' },
    { label = 'Urgent', type = 'checkbox', placeholder = 'Mark as urgent' },
})
if r then TriggerServerEvent('reports:create', r[1], r[2]) end
Not from a prompt or vehicle-part callback. Waiting there freezes every prompt; use a command or CreateThread.
Alert(title, message, btnText?) · Alert({ title, message, button })CLIENT

A dialog with one button; waits.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringThe title
messagestringBody text
btnTextstring?Default 'OK' (button in a table)
Returns: true, or false, why ('cancelled': Escape)
Confirm(title, message, confirmText?, cancelText?) · Confirm({ title, message, yes, no })CLIENT

A dialog with two buttons; waits.

ParamTypeDescription
titlestringThe title
messagestringBody text
confirmTextstring?Default 'Confirm' (yes in a table)
cancelTextstring?Default 'Cancel' (no in a table)
Returns: true if confirmed, or false, why ('cancelled': no, or Escape)
local sell = exports.whip_core:Confirm({ title = 'Sell car', message = 'Sell it for $4,000?', yes = 'Sell', no = 'Keep it' })
RegisterAskChannel(name, deliver) / AnswerAsk(source, token, yes)SERVER

Offers whip_core's yes or no questions for your channel (the Director's job invite) to your own screen first; whip_phone registers 'phone'. Unless deliver returns true, whip_core asks on screen. If whip_core gives up (timeout, run end, player left), whip_core:ask:cancelled ({ token }) fires on the player's game. When your resource stops, open questions go back on screen.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringLetters, digits, _, -; not another running resource's name
deliverfunction(source, token, kind, payload) → true when shown; never waits. payload: title, message, yes, no
tokennumberAs deliver got it; only you may answer it
yesbooleantrue Accept, false Decline
Returns: true, or false, why: a bad or taken name; 'That question is gone', 'That question was not asked through you', 'That question was for another character'
exports.whip_core:RegisterAskChannel('phone', function(source, token, kind, payload)
    if not playerHasPhone(source) then return false end
    TriggerClientEvent('my_phone:invite', source, token, payload)
    return true
end)
exports.whip_core:AnswerAsk(source, token, true)   -- later, they pressed Accept

Skill checks

SkillCheck(difficulty?) · SkillCheck({ difficulty }) · SkillCheck({ difficulty, game })CLIENT

The ring: the player pushes the centre dot onto the lit part and holds it until it fills (Config.SkillCheckHoldMs), part after narrower part. Touching outside it, or the clock running out, fails. Mouse (Config.SkillCheckMouseSpeed) or right stick, not keyboard.

ParamTypeDescription
difficultystring?A name in Config.SkillCheckDifficulty (servers can add their own). Default 'medium'
gamestring?A game instead of the ring ('phone.reroute'); its canStart is asked first
NamePartsRing cut intoLit partClock (msPerPart)
easy643/4 to 1/43.9 s (0.65 s a part)
medium1281/2 to 1/87.2 s (0.6 s a part)
hard16161/4 to 1/169.2 s (0.575 s a part)
Returns: true, or false, why: 'failed', 'cancelled', 'busy', 'timeout'; with a game, 'not started' (not a fail) or 'unavailable'; or a sentence naming an unknown difficulty
A client skill check is the player's word. If passing hands something out, use the server SkillCheck(source, difficulty).
SkillCheck(source, difficulty?, opts?)SERVER

The ring from the server, with a one-shot token, a minimum time and a timeout; waits, then clears their screen. Run medium and hard from a SecureEvent: they can outlast a SecureCallback's 10 s.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player
difficultystring?Default 'medium'
opts.timeoutMsnumber?Default the check's clock plus 2 s
opts.minMsnumber?Fastest believable answer (default parts × fill time); must be under the timeout
opts.tagany?Your run tag: ReleaseTag(tag) cancels it
opts.gamestring?A game at one of its levels, on its own timings unless you pass yours
opts.quietboolean?Don't tell a player why a game couldn't start
Returns: true, or false, why: 'failed', 'busy', 'cancelled', 'timeout', 'too fast', 'dead', 'run ended', 'Player not loaded', 'not started', 'unavailable', or a sentence naming a bad argument
local passed, why = Whip.core:SkillCheck(source, 'medium')
if not passed then return false, why == 'busy' and 'Finish what you are doing first' or 'You slipped' end
A patient cheater still passes by waiting the honest time. Don't gate an outcome that must be uncheatable on a minigame.
Whip.skillCheckGame(id, def) · GetSkillCheckGames()SERVERCLIENT

Your own game for the server and client SkillCheck and the Director's Skill Check card; whip_core keeps the token, timings and answer. Call it in a file both sides load, or once per side with the same id, '<yours>.<name>'. whip_phone adds phone.bruteforce, phone.coderecall, phone.fragmentmatch, phone.override, phone.reroute, phone.safecrack and phone.stabilise.

FieldSideDescription
labelserverIts Director name (40 characters)
descserverOptional: a line about it
levelsserver{ easy = { minMs, timeoutMs }, ... }; timeoutMs up to 120 s
canStart(source)serverOptional: true, or false, words (they're told; 'not started')
canStart()clientOptional: the same for the client SkillCheck; must not wait
run(difficulty, token)clientPlay it (may wait); return passed, why. Holds WHIP's blocking slot
cancel(token)clientOptional: called off; make run return

Re-sent when whip_core restarts; removed when your resource stops (a running check is 'cancelled') or by Whip.removeSkillCheckGame(id). GetSkillCheckGames() (server) returns { id, label, desc, levels, needs, owner } each.

Whip.skillCheckGame('mygame.wires', {
    label = 'Cut the Wires',
    levels = { easy = { minMs = 2000, timeoutMs = 30000 } },
    canStart = function(source) return HasCutters(source) or false, 'You need wire cutters' end,
    run = function(difficulty) return PlayWires(difficulty) end,
})

Placing a prop

PlaceObject(model, opts?)CLIENT

The item placer for a prop of yours: a see-through ghost of model follows where the player looks and sits on the surface. The mouse wheel turns it (triggers on a pad), the arrow keys raise and lower it (the D-pad), Ctrl makes both fine, E places it and C cancels. Nothing is made: it returns where, and your resource puts the prop there (with ShowPropSet or an object of its own). Waits.

ParamTypeDescription
modelstring|numberThe prop's model
opts.labelstring?What the hint calls it: "Place Speaker" (default "it")
opts.vehiclesboolean?true: it may go on a car (its roof, its bed). Otherwise a car is refused
opts.reachnumber?Metres from the camera (1 to 10; default an item's)
Returns: { coords, rot }, rot as vector3(tiltForward, tiltSideways, heading). On a car, also netId, offset and offsetRot in the car's frame, as attach, attachOffset and attachRot take them. Or false, why: 'cancelled', 'busy', 'model' (it won't load) or 'dead'
CreateThread(function()
    local spot = Whip.core:PlaceObject('prop_speaker_06', { label = 'Speaker', vehicles = true })
    if not spot then return end                       -- cancelled, busy, ...
    TriggerServerEvent('myres:server:placed', spot.coords, spot.rot, spot.netId, spot.offset, spot.offsetRot)
end)
The answer is the player's word. Check it on the server: near them, and somewhere you allow.

On-screen text

ShowText(text, position?, progress?)CLIENT

Shows text in the hint capsule until HideText() or the next call; doesn't block. One slot: the newest caller wins. Split controls with |: '[E] Place | [C] Cancel'; the first part is the title, [Key] draws a keycap, {pad:a} a pad button.

ParamTypeDescription
textstring'[E] Open Door'
positionstring|table?'bottom' (default), 'top', or { position, progress, icon, tone }
progressnumber?0-100: a bar you update by calling again (unlike Progress(), never waits)
iconstring?Table only: a glyph name for the disc ('place', 'give', 'fuel'...). Default the first key
tone'warn'?Table only: an amber ring, "can't be done here"
exports.whip_core:ShowText('[E] Plant seed  |  [C] Cancel', { icon = 'place' })
HideText()CLIENT

Hides the ShowText() text if it's yours.

Returns: boolean: false when it's another resource's
ShowObjective(id, text, opts?) · HideObjective(id)CLIENT

A Director-style objective card, top right, for something your client runs (server-run work goes through the Director). The same id updates it; cards stack, newest on top.

ParamTypeDescription
idstring64 characters at most
textstring200 characters at most; colour codes removed
opts.iconstring?A glyph: 'target', 'star', 'car'... Default the flag
opts.namestring?The small line under it
opts.countdownnumber?Seconds counted down; opts.countdownTotal is the full length
opts.filmboolean?Stays up on a clean screen
Returns: ShowObjective: true or false, why. HideObjective: true
exports.whip_core:ShowObjective('escape', 'Lose the cops', { icon = 'star' })
IsRadialOpen()CLIENT

Is the F1 wheel on screen? Add options with AddAction and at = { radial = true } (a label is required; give an icon and description). Players open it with F1 or by holding D-pad down.

Returns: boolean

The composer

Turns the player capsule into a one-line text field that takes the keyboard but not the mouse, so the camera stays put. whip_chat uses it. It closes when its resource stops; /resetcomposer in F8 (developer mode) frees a stuck keyboard.

RegisterCommand('+myinput', function()   -- open on the press...
    exports.whip_core:OpenComposer({ placeholder = 'Say something', deferFocus = true,
        onSubmit = function(text, mode) print(text) end })
end, false)
RegisterCommand('-myinput', function() exports.whip_core:FocusComposer() end, false)   -- ...type on the release
RegisterKeyMapping('+myinput', 'Type something', 'keyboard', 'T')
OpenComposer(opts)CLIENT

Opens the composer. One at a time: it won't replace a half-typed line.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.onSubmitfunctionRequired. (text, mode); mode is the active mode's name or nil
opts.placeholderstring?Ghost text
opts.prefillstring?Starting text
opts.maxLengthnumber?Default 256
opts.modestable?{ name, displayName?, color? } list, cycled with Tab
opts.suggestionstable?{ name, help?, params? } list, filtered as they type
opts.onCancelfunction?Escape, an empty line, or CloseComposer
opts.onScrollfunction?(delta): PageUp -1, PageDown 1
opts.deferFocusboolean?Don't take the keyboard yet: needed from a key binding, or the key gets typed in
opts.padboolean?Type on WHIP's pad keyboard instead; Done submits, B cancels; no modes or suggestions
opts.titlestring?With pad: the keyboard's heading
Returns: boolean: false if one is open or onSubmit is missing
FocusComposer()CLIENT

Takes the keyboard for a deferFocus composer. Skipping it is safe: it takes it after a quarter of a second.

Returns: boolean
CloseComposer()CLIENT

Closes your composer without submitting; onCancel runs.

Returns: boolean: false when none is open or it's another resource's
IsComposerOpen()CLIENT

Is any composer open, not only yours?

Returns: boolean

Screens, input and controls

These keep two resources' screens, keys and HUDs from fighting.

IsAnyScreenOpen()CLIENT

Is a screen or a dialog up (a bare progress bar does not count)? Ask it to decide whether to hide an overlay, as the HUD, radar and whip_chat do; whip_core:ui:stateChanged follows it.

Returns: boolean
local hidden = exports.whip_core:IsAnyScreenOpen()
AddEventHandler('whip_core:ui:stateChanged', function(e) hidden = e.open end)
IsGameInputFree()CLIENT

May a hotkey act, or the player start something? false while a WHIP screen, a bar or a dialog is up, while anything holds the NUI focus (the wheel, chat, /whip, any resource's screen), and while a mode owns the keys (placing, give mode, throwing). E prompts close while it's false.

Returns: boolean
RegisterCommand('+my_horn', function()
    if not exports.whip_core:IsGameInputFree() then return end
end, false)
A key mapping fires under a screen. Disabled controls don't stop it, and SetNuiFocusKeepInput screens (the furnisher, whip_autos) pass every key. Check this once per press in every world-acting key command.
SetScreenOpen(open, key?, opts?)CLIENT

Declares your NUI open or closed, so the HUD and chat hide, prompts stop and nothing opens on top. Other resources' dialogs are 'busy' over it; after one of your own, or OpenComposer, call SetNuiFocus(true, true) again.

ParamTypeDescription
openbooleanShown or hidden
keystring?Which of your screens, so closing one leaves another held
opts.keepHudboolean?Leave the status HUD, minimap and dial up (the phone does); chat and prompts still hide
Returns: boolean: false only with no calling resource
SetNuiFocus(true, true)
exports.whip_core:SetScreenOpen(true)
-- on every close path:
SetNuiFocus(false, false)
exports.whip_core:SetScreenOpen(false)
Call both halves. Skip the open and the HUD and prompts stay over your UI; skip the close and they stay hidden. A stopped resource's claim is dropped.
SetScreenArea(area, key?)CLIENT

Says where your UI sits; the vehicle dial slides up or left out of it (or fades). Hides nothing. Send it when it changes, not every frame, and from Whip.register: whip_core forgets areas on restart.

ParamTypeDescription
areatable|nil{ left, top, right, bottom }, fractions from the top left; nil or false when gone
keystring?Which of your UIs
Returns: boolean, or false, reason for a bad area
HoldCleanScreen(id?) / ReleaseCleanScreen(id?)CLIENT

Nothing on screen but the game, for filming (chat stays; F6 hides it). Screens opened meanwhile work unseen, so release soon. Holds are per resource; others hear whip_core:ui:cleanScreen (Client Events).

ParamTypeDescription
idstring?Your name for the hold
Returns: boolean: false only with no calling resource
BlockControls(id, spec) / UnblockControls(id)CLIENT

Holds controls off until you let go, in WHIP's one shared loop instead of your own DisableControlAction loop. Swept when your resource stops; the same id replaces a block. Read blocked controls with IsDisabledControlPressed and its siblings.

ParamTypeDescription
idstring|numberYour name for the block
spec.groupsstring[]?move (walk, sprint, jump, duck, cover), combat (attack, aim, weapon select, melee), driving (steer, throttle, brake, get out), vehicleCombat, look, radio, weaponWheel, and the switch driveBy
spec.controlsinteger[]?GTA control ids; 200 keeps Esc from the pause menu
spec.all / spec.exceptboolean? / integer[]?Every control but the exceptions
spec.walkboolean?A walk at most
spec.jogboolean?A jog at most, never sprint; a walk wins
spec.modeboolean?Your own mode: E prompts, hotbar and wheels stand down (IsGameInputFree is false), so E is yours. HUD stays
spec.hotbarboolean?With mode: the hotbar still works; see whip_core:hotbar:slotUsed
Returns: boolean ok, string? why: an unknown group, a bad id, except without all, or nothing named
exports.whip_core:BlockControls('shop', { groups = { 'move', 'combat', 'radio', 'driveBy' }, controls = { 75 } })
exports.whip_core:UnblockControls('shop')
HoldPlayerPed(id, flags) / ReleasePlayerPed(id)CLIENT

Holds the ped invincible, frozen, hidden or without collision. Every resource's holds combine, so your release never reveals an invisible admin. Kept across death, swept when you stop.

ParamTypeDescription
idstring|numberYour name for the hold
flagstableinvincible, frozen, hidden (to others too), noCollision
Returns: boolean ok, string? why
exports.whip_core:HoldPlayerPed('hang', { hidden = true, noCollision = true })
PermitNativeWeapon(weapon, on)CLIENT

WHIP removes GTA weapons no resource permits (Config.WeaponGuard). Permit yours (hash or name) before giving it; permits go when you stop.

Returns: boolean: false for a bad weapon
exports.whip_core:PermitNativeWeapon('WEAPON_PETROLCAN', true)

Controller support

A player on a gamepad gets most of WHIP without you writing anything for it. Beyond that, you can put an action on a button, drive your own screen with the pad, and give a mode WHIP's confirm and cancel.

What you get free

  • Prompts (AddAction): A uses the one in view; D-pad up and down step its options.
  • The F1 wheel: holding D-pad down opens it.
  • Bars and dialogs: Progress, Input, Confirm, SkillCheck and WHIP's panels read the pad themselves.
  • Typing: OpenKeyboard, an on-screen keyboard.
  • Hints: {pad:a} in ShowText draws the A button. Also b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, ls, rs, l3, r3, dpad, dpad_up ... dpad_right, view, menu; as images at https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/img/pad/a.svg.
LB is WHIP's combo key. LB + A talks, LB + X is the radio, and players can put other actions on LB + a button. Everything here leaves those presses to WHIP.

An action on a button

FiveM's pad key bindings never fire, so put your action on WHIP's buttons: it shows on the pause menu's Controller screen, players can move it, and WHIP reads the button. The phone, talk, the radio and nitrous work this way.

RegisterPadAction(id, def) / RemovePadAction(id)CLIENT

Puts your action on the button it asks for, if that button is free in WHIP's default (or a player's layout never set it). Registering again replaces it; it goes when your resource stops.

ParamTypeDescription
idstringA letter, then letters, digits, _; up to 32. Layouts save it by this
def.labelstringIts name on the Controller screen, up to 32 characters
def.commandstring?A key command ('+my_action'; its - half runs on release). This or onPress
def.onPress / def.onReleasefunction?On button down and (optionally) up. Must not wait
def.slotstring?dpad_up, dpad_down, dpad_left, dpad_right, l3, veh_a (A in a vehicle), foot_b (B on foot), lb_a, lb_b, lb_x, lb_y, lb_dpad_up ... lb_dpad_right. None: players place it
def.wherestring?'car' or 'foot'. A ready 'car' action shows over the dial, so keep it not ready where it does nothing
def.menusboolean?true: works with a screen open (talk). Otherwise it waits for IsGameInputFree
def.readyboolean?Default true; see SetPadActionReady
Returns: boolean ok, string? why: a bad field (named), one of WHIP's ids, or an id another resource holds
Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterPadAction('mycafe_menu', { label = 'Cafe menu', command = 'mycafe_menu', slot = 'lb_y' })
end)

Config.Controller.Layout holds WHIP's own (D-pad up phone, LB + A talk, LB + B Gunny ammo check, LB + X radio, A in a vehicle nitrous, B on foot Gunny reload), so LB + Y and LB + D-pad are yours. A taken slot leaves the action registered on no button, and F8 says once what has it. Two resources asking for one free button: the id first alphabetically wins.

SetPadActionReady(id, ready)CLIENT

While your action isn't ready it keeps its button, but presses reach GTA: nitrous is ready only with a bottle, so a motorbike keeps A for ducking.

Returns: boolean ok, string? why (not your id)
exports.whip_core:SetPadActionReady('nitrous', true)
GetPadActionButton(id)CLIENT

Which button any action is on in this player's layout (yours, another resource's, or WHIP's 'radial', 'inventory', 'engine', 'sprint'). Ask each time you show a hint.

Returns: slot ('lb_y'), pictures for ShowText ('{pad:lb}{pad:y}'), name ('LB+Y'); nil on no button or no such action
local slot, pictures = Whip.core:GetPadActionButton('mycafe_menu')
if type(slot) == 'string' then exports.whip_core:ShowText(pictures .. ' Cafe menu') end

A pad on your own screen

The browser can't read a gamepad in FiveM. Whip.padScreen (in @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua) reads it while your screen is open, sends presses to your page, owns your NUI focus (no cursor while a pad drives) and holds the pad's world actions off.

Whip.padScreen(def?)CLIENT

Make one at file scope; screen:open() when your screen opens, screen:close() on every close. Your page gets { action = 'pad', cmd, down, rep } per press (rep: a held D-pad's repeats) and { action = 'padDevice', pad } when the player swaps devices.

FieldTypeDescription
buttonsstring[]?Default up, down, left, right, a, b, x, y; also lb (on release without a combo), rb, menu
stickboolean?false: the left stick doesn't step like the D-pad
releasestable?{ a = true }: also send down = false on release
keepInputstring?'always': the game keeps its input with the mouse too (an orbit camera). Default 'pad'
blocktable|false?Held off while a pad drives, in BlockControls form. Default: walking, looking, fighting, wheels, jump, getting in, cover, reload, Start / Esc
onButton / onDevicefunction?(cmd, down, rep) and (pad), instead of the messages
onFramefunction?Every frame a pad drives, for a stick of your own
Returns: the screen: :open() (returns whether a pad is in use), :close(), :typing(on) (your text field has the keyboard), :pause(on) (another screen of yours has the pad), :isPad()
local screen = Whip.padScreen()
SendNUIMessage({ action = 'open', pad = screen:open() })   -- on open
screen:close()                                             -- on every close
OpenKeyboard(opts?)CLIENT

WHIP's on-screen keyboard for a pad player; open it only on a pad (IsControllerActive). It opens over any page and waits, so call it from a thread. It suggests word endings in the player's language (Config.Keyboard), learning their words. While it's up the pad is its alone: your own pad reader waits between whip_core:keyboard:opened and whip_core:keyboard:closed.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.titlestring?Shown over the keys: 'Search'
opts.valuestring?Starting text
opts.placeholderstring?Ghost text
opts.numericboolean?A number pad (digits, minus, point)
opts.maxLengthinteger?Character limit
opts.predictboolean?false: no suggestions, nothing learned (a plate, a code)
Returns: string, or nil when left (B) or replaced by another keyboard
local text = Whip.core:OpenKeyboard({ title = 'Search', value = current, maxLength = 40 })

A mode's confirm and cancel

A mode of your own (placing, aiming, a minigame) confirms with Interact (E, or wherever the player moved it) and cancels with C; on a pad, A and B, never with LB.

IsAcceptPressed() / IsAcceptHeld() / IsCancelPressed() · AcceptHint() / CancelHint()CLIENT

Read the first three every frame; they follow whichever device is in use and read through a block. The hints return '[E]' / '[C]' or '{pad:a}' / '{pad:b}'. Hold a BlockControls block with mode = true, naming what the keys also do in GTA: C look behind (26), B reload and melee (45, 140).

Returns: boolean for the readers, string for the hints
exports.whip_core:BlockControls('placing', { controls = { 26, 45, 140 }, mode = true })
while placing do
    if exports.whip_core:IsAcceptPressed() then place() end
    if exports.whip_core:IsCancelPressed() then placing = false end
    Wait(0)
end
IsKeyPressed(key, button) / IsKeyHeld(key, button) · KeyHint(keyText, button)CLIENT

Any other key, by the same rules: key on a keyboard, button on a pad, never both, never with LB. Either may be nil. GTA control numbers; a pad's are frontend ones: 201 A, 202 B, 203 X, 204 Y, 206 RB, 199 Start, D-pad 187-190, never LB (205). KeyHint takes a key name and a picture name, or a list of them.

Returns: boolean; KeyHint: '[Space]', '{pad:x}' or ''
if exports.whip_core:IsKeyPressed(22, 203) then flip() end   -- Space, or X
local hint = exports.whip_core:KeyHint('Scroll', { 'lt', 'rt' }) .. ' Turn'

Reading the pad yourself

IsControllerActive()CLIENT

Is the player on a gamepad? Use it to pick hint pictures, not to change controls. Ask once, then listen for whip_core:pad:deviceChanged ({ pad }).

Returns: boolean
AddEventHandler('whip_core:pad:deviceChanged', function(e) onPad = e.pad == true end)

A pad screen of your own: Whip.padScreen leaves a press with LB held to WHIP's combos for you.

Camera System

Scripted cameras for cutscenes, intros, showrooms and cinematics. One camera plays at a time, and it belongs to the resource that started it: when that resource stops, WHIP hands the view back.

Three ways to use it

  • A sequence made in the Camera Creator: a timeline of shots and the moves between them. Play it by name, or paste it as code: PlayCameraSequence.
  • An orbit round anything, up until you stop it, which the player can turn and zoom: OrbitCamera.
  • One fixed shot (PlayCamera), or a simple path through points (PlayCameraPath, which plays as a sequence).

Every export is on the Camera API page. An orbit frames a bike and a bus alike, and a shot inside an MLO draws its interior.

Playing a sequence

-- Saved in the Camera Creator, by name (from a thread: the first time, it's fetched from the server)
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence('intro')

-- Round a car you hand it ('target' is the Creator's "picked thing")
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence('car_reveal', { subjects = { target = veh }, async = true })

-- Or written out (what Copy code gives you)
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraSequence({
    letterbox = true,
    keys = {
        { t = 0, move = 'glide', ease = 'smooth',
          shot = { kind = 'fixed', pos = { x = -75.2, y = -819.4, z = 326.1 }, rot = { x = -12, y = 0, z = 140 }, fov = 50 } },
        { t = 4000, move = 'orbit', around = 'left',
          shot = { kind = 'orbit', subject = 'vehicle', yaw = 30, pitch = 8, fit = 1.2, fov = 40, turn = 6 } },
        { t = 9000, shot = { kind = 'orbit', subject = 'vehicle', yaw = 160, pitch = 4, fit = 0.9, fov = 36 },
          shake = { amount = 0.3, freq = 6 } },
    },
})

A sequence is checked before anything goes up; a mistake returns false, why naming the key and field. 'player' and 'vehicle' need nothing; any other subject name is one you pass in subjects, as an entity or a place { x, y, z, h }. A subject that goes away mid-sequence holds the last picture.

Orbiting anything

-- A showroom: the player turns it with the mouse (or right stick) and zooms with the wheel
exports.whip_core:OrbitCamera(veh, { yaw = 35, pitch = 12, fit = 1.3, fov = 40, turn = 6 })
-- ...when they're done
exports.whip_core:StopCamera()

Stopping

StopCamera() stops the camera your resource started; you don't need it in onResourceStop.

Cameras wait unless you pass async = true. PlayCamera (with its default exitKey), paths and sequences hold your thread until they end; a loop path, until StopCamera.

The Camera CreatorServer owners

  • Turn it on in /whip → Settings → Config → Experimental features (an unfinished prototype, off by default). It's a row at the end of the /w dev menu.
  • Fly with the right mouse button held, then WASD, Space and Ctrl; on a controller the sticks fly. G adds a key at the playhead; Space plays.
