  • Each key is a shot (Fixed, Orbit, Chase, Mounted or Track) of you, your vehicle or a picked thing, and moves on to the next by Cut, Glide, Spring or Orbit.
  • Save keeps it on the server by name, for any admin to open and any script to play (PlayCameraSequence('intro')). Copy code copies it as a Lua call; your draft is kept on this PC.

Making a cinematicServer owners

Place your cameras in the Camera Creator (each key is one), press F9 to play in game as your character, and record the screen with OBS or any recorder. F5 rolls the timeline live (again to cut back), Page Down / Page Up or Num 1-Num 9 cut between cameras, and F9 returns to the editor. A rolling shot leaves a clean screen (F6 hides chat), and with Plays round set to your vehicle, the cameras are placed round the car wherever it is.

The driving cameraServer owners

A smooth chase camera for cars, motorbikes and quads, which each player switches on in the pause menu (Server Settings → Vehicles → Smooth driving camera); it's off unless you make it the default. It steps aside for aiming, GTA's cinematic camera, death and any other script's camera, then comes back, so nothing you write needs to know about it. Switch it off for everyone, change the default or set the shake in Config.DrivingCamera (/whip → Settings → Config → Vehicles).

Each player also picks its Camera style. Consistent stays behind the car the same way all the time. Cinematic frames the car by what it's doing: back and up in the air so the landing is in frame, further back on softer springs in a drift, lower and closer with a wider view in a burnout from a stop, and closer and much wider on nitrous (any pull harder than a launch). Config.DrivingCamera.Style ('consistent' or 'cinematic') is the style a player who never chose gets.

Camera API

Exports for scripted cameras. New to them? Read Camera System first. The play exports return false, 'busy' while another resource's camera is up; your own you may replace.

Playing

PlayCamera(opts)CLIENT

Plays one fixed camera.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.posvector3?Position. Default: the gameplay camera's
opts.rotvector3?Rotation (pitch, roll, yaw), default 0, 0, 0
opts.fovnumber?Field of view, default 60
opts.filterstring?Default 'none'; also 'scanline_cam', 'CAMERA_secuirity', 'CAMERA_secuirity_FUZZ', 'heliGunCam', 'NG_filmic04', 'NG_filmic08', 'cinema', 'underwater', 'Forest', 'Tunnel', 'phone_cam1', 'phone_cam2'
opts.canLookboolean?Mouse look, default false
opts.canMoveboolean?WASD movement, default false
opts.exitKeyboolean?Esc ends it, default true
opts.transitionIn / transitionOutnumber?Milliseconds to ease from and back to the gameplay camera, default 0
opts.asyncboolean?Return at once, default false
Returns: true, or false, 'busy', or false, why for a pos or rot that isn't a vector3
exports.whip_core:PlayCamera({
    pos    = vector3(-1042.0, -2745.0, 22.0),
    rot    = vector3(-10.0, 0.0, 180.0),
    fov    = 50.0,
    filter = 'cinema',
})
It waits unless async = true. With exitKey (the default), canLook or canMove, its controls run in your thread until the camera ends.
PlayCameraPath(opts)CLIENT

A path through points, played as a sequence: 'interpolate' is a smooth curve at one speed, 'cycle' jumps and holds.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.pointsarrayRequired: at least two { pos, rot, fov?, filter? }
opts.modestring?'interpolate' (default) or 'cycle'
opts.durationnumber?Whole path in ms, interpolate mode. Default 10000
opts.easingstring?Over the whole path: 'linear', 'smooth' (default), 'ease-in', 'ease-out'
opts.loopboolean?Loop the path, default false
opts.cycleDurationnumber?Hold per point in cycle mode, ms. Default 3000
opts.transitionIn / transitionOutnumber?As PlayCamera's
opts.asyncboolean?Return at once, default false
Returns: true, or false, why before any camera goes up: fewer than two points, a point without pos or rot, a duration or cycleDuration of 0, or 'busy'. A failure mid-path hands the player back to gameplay
exports.whip_core:PlayCameraPath({
    points = {
        { pos = vector3(100, 200, 30), rot = vector3(0, 0, 180), fov = 40 },
        { pos = vector3(105, 195, 30), rot = vector3(-10, 0, 90), fov = 50 },
    },
    duration = 8000,
    loop     = true,
    async    = true,   -- a loop never ends: without async this never returns
})
PlayCameraSequence(sequence, opts?)CLIENT

Plays a timeline of shots, the Camera Creator's. sequence is the name it was saved under (fetched from the server the first time, so call from a thread) or the table itself, as Copy code gives it.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.subjectstable?{ [name] = entity | { x, y, z, h } }. 'player' and 'vehicle' (the car the player is in, or was last in) need nothing
opts.asyncboolean?Return at once; otherwise it waits for the end
opts.loop, opts.letterboxboolean?Override the sequence's own
opts.speednumber?1 as made, 0.5 half speed (0.05 to 20)
opts.startAtnumber?Milliseconds into it to start
opts.holdboolean?Stay on the last moment until stopped
opts.controlboolean?The player turns and zooms its orbits (mouse and wheel, or right stick and triggers)
opts.exitKeyboolean?Esc (B) ends it. Off by default
opts.transitionIn, opts.transitionOutnumber?Milliseconds to ease from and back to the game's camera
Returns: true, or false, why before any camera goes up: what's wrong (the key and field), a missing subject or anchor, an unknown saved name, or 'busy'

A sequence is { keys, length?, anchor?, loop?, letterbox?, ease? }, times in ms. anchor names a subject its fixed places are kept round. ease ('linear', 'smooth', 'in', 'out', 'strong') bends the whole timeline; the Camera Creator doesn't use it.

A key is { t, shot, move?, ease?, rate?, around?, coast?, shake?, filter?, punch?, label? }. move to the next key: 'cut', 'glide' (default; ease its pace, default 'smooth'), 'spring' (rate 3 gentle to 8 brisk) or 'orbit' (between two orbits of one subject; around 'short', 'left' or 'right'). coast (0.2 to 50, a resistance) makes the camera drift past a key it stops at. shake = { amount, freq }, punch = { fov, decay } (a lens kick), filter from that key on.

A shot has a kind, a fov (default 50) and, all but fixed, a subject name:

kindFields
fixedpos = { x, y, z }, rot = { x = pitch, y = roll, z = yaw } (round the anchor if there is one)
orbityaw (0 behind, 180 in front), pitch (degrees above), fit (1 fills the screen) or dist (metres), aim = { x, y, z } (the point looked at, as a share of its box, -1 to 1; +y front, +z top), look = { pitch, yaw } off that point, turn (degrees a second), clear (metres off the ground, default 0.35), roll
chasedist, height, ahead (look-ahead), slip (0 follow its nose, 1 where it goes), stiff, turnRate, fovAdd and distAdd (at speed), collision (pull in at walls, default on)
mountedoffset = { x, y, z } in its metres (right, forward, up), rot relative to it
trackpos, plus an orbit's aim and look: stands still and keeps the subject in frame
OrbitCamera(target, opts?)CLIENT

An orbit round an entity or a place { x, y, z, h }, up until StopCamera. Returns at once.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.yaw, pitch, fit / dist, aim, look, fov, turn, clearnumber|table?As an orbit shot's. Defaults: yaw 35, pitch 12, fit 1.3, fov 40
opts.controlboolean?The player turns and zooms it. Default on
opts.exitKey, opts.letterboxboolean?Esc (B) ends it; cinema bars
opts.transitionIn, opts.transitionOutnumber?Milliseconds to ease from and back to the game's camera, default 500 each
Returns: true, or false, why

Stopping and reading

StopCamera()CLIENT

Stops the camera your resource started and eases back to the normal view over its transitionOut. Another resource's camera is left alone. Not needed when your resource stops.

Returns: boolean: false when none is playing, or it's another resource's
IsCameraActive()CLIENT

Returns whether a scripted camera is playing.

Returns: boolean

Theming & Skins

WHIP's colours, fonts, radii, shadows and spacing are CSS custom properties in whip_core/html/css/base.css. A skin is a resource of its own, an fxmanifest.lua and a theme.css that overrides them, so it survives every whip_core update.

Turning a skin on

  • Standing theme: Config.Theme = 'your_theme_resource' in whip_core's config, the server's permanent look.
  • Runtime skin: a resource that calls SetActiveTheme. start reskins every connected client live; stop reverts.

The full contract (every token, your own fonts, partial themes, what's locked) is whip_core/docs/nui-theming.md. Beside it, nui-architecture.md covers how the NUI modules talk to the client scripts, and nui-inventory.md how to replace the inventory's renderer outright.

SetActiveTheme(resource)SERVER

Sets, or clears with nil, the server-wide theme over Config.Theme. It belongs to the resource that set it (the registration rule): only it can change it, a second skin is refused, and when it stops the look reverts to Config.Theme. Connected clients swap live, late joiners get it on login, and a misnamed resource logs to F8 and falls back to the base look.

ParamTypeDescription
resourcestring|nilThe resource whose theme.css to apply, usually your own. nil clears it (only for the resource that set it)
Returns: bool ok, string|nil err: false, 'the active theme belongs to X — stop it first' when another resource's skin is active
-- A complete skin's server.lua (fxmanifest.lua: shared_script '@whip_core/lib/satellite.lua')
Whip.register(function()
    exports.whip_core:SetActiveTheme('my_skin')
end)
Call it inside Whip.register, not at file scope. The override dies with whip_core on a restart, and Whip.register runs again then. At file scope your skin vanishes after the first restart whip_core.
GetActiveTheme()SERVER

Which theme is in force, and who set it.

Returns: string|nil theme, string|nil owner: the resource whose theme.css applies and the one that set it. With no override, Config.Theme (nil for the stock look) and no owner
local theme, owner = exports.whip_core:GetActiveTheme()
print(('theme %s, set by %s'):format(tostring(theme), owner or 'config.lua'))

Browser features and tools

FiveM's in-game browser is moving from Chromium 103 to 144. WHIP's detector tells your page and your Lua which features it has, so you can use the new way where it can. Below that: client tools for tests, from reading screens to screenshots and the error log.

In your page

Load the detector before your scripts. It sets window.WhipCaps and a caps-... class on <html> per feature (caps-anchor, caps-game-view...).

<script src="https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/js/caps.js"></script>
FlagTrue when the browser has
chromeIts Chrome version, a number (0 if unknown)
has:has()
colorMix / relativeColorcolor-mix() / rgb(from var(--x) r g b / 50%)
textBalancetext-wrap: balance and pretty
startingStyle@starting-style, transition-behavior: allow-discrete
heightAutointerpolate-size: allow-keywords
anchorCSS anchor positioning
fieldSizingfield-sizing: content
viewTransitionsdocument.startViewTransition
schedulerYieldscheduler.yield()
webgpunavigator.gpu (the GPU may still be unusable)
zoomScreenPxgetBoundingClientRect in screen pixels inside a CSS zoom (103 returned them unzoomed); measured
gameViewFiveM's new game view (CfxGameViewRenderer, gl.CFX_BIND_GAME_VIEW), to draw or read the game's picture

@supports is safe for what 103 lacks entirely (text-wrap, anchor positioning, field-sizing, interpolate-size, @starting-style). Use the classes for :has(), zoomScreenPx and gameView. In script, WhipCaps.transition(fn) cross-fades where it can and WhipCaps.yieldToBrowser() lets a long job breathe; both fall back by themselves.

.caps-has .panel:has(.slot.selected) { border-color: var(--ui-accent); }
Trust the flags, not CSS.supports. FiveM's Chromium 103 has experimental features on, so @supports selector(:has(a)) is true there, and any test holding var() passes in every Chrome.
GetNuiCaps()CLIENT

A copy of the flags, as whip_core's page reported them; whip_core:nui:capsDetected fires with them when it does. From a satellite, Whip.core:GetNuiCaps(). /nuicaps prints them in F8; /nuicaps gameview shows the game view live (solid blue: it didn't bind).

Returns: table|false caps, string|nil err: false, 'not_detected_yet' before the page reports
local caps = exports.whip_core:GetNuiCaps()
if caps and caps.gameView then print('the page can have the game picture') end

Reading and pressing screens

For tests, in developer mode only (else false, 'developer mode is off'). They reach whip_core's page and any page that loads https://cfx-nui-whip_core/html/js/page-tools.js in its <head>, which also sends its errors to GetErrorLog. A keyboard-only menu can be pressed if its rows carry data-probe-press and handle a click.

ReadScreen(opts?)CLIENT

The words on screen in reading order, and every pressable control with its id, words, kind, near (heading above), row (its row's words), state and position.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.textboolean?false: no words
opts.controlsboolean?false: no controls
opts.understring?Only controls under this heading
opts.pagesboolean?false: not other resources' pages
Returns: { view, focus, text, controls, pages }|false, why
PressScreen(target, opts?)CLIENT

Presses one control at its middle. target is an id from the last ReadScreen or its words (exact, then starts-with, then contains), narrowed by near, kind, index or page. Several matches press nothing. Read again after a press: ids change.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.buttonstring?'left' (default), 'right', 'double'
opts.textstring?Type this into the field
opts.enterboolean?With text: then Enter
opts.choosestring?Pick this list choice
Returns: { pressed, kind, chose, typed, covered }, { ambiguous } or false, why
exports.whip_core:PressScreen({ label = 'Change', near = 'Who can open it' })
exports.whip_core:PressScreen('Weather', { choose = 'Rain' })

Screenshots

These replace screenshot-basic, which halved the frame rate on GTA V Enhanced; they cost nothing until asked. A shot is the game alone, with what it draws (DUI screens, 3D prompts). ui = true adds whip_core's screens and HUD, not other resources' pages.

TakeScreenshot(opts?)CLIENT

This player's game picture. Waits up to 15 s.

ParamTypeDescription
opts.formatstring?'jpg' (default), 'png', 'webp'
opts.qualitynumber?0 to 1 (0.92)
opts.width, opts.heightnumber?Default the screen's; one alone keeps its shape
opts.uiboolean?Draw WHIP's interface over it
opts.frames, opts.everynumber?A burst of 2-24 frames every 33-1000 ms in one grid, 640 wide each; no ui
opts.uploadtable?{ url, field }: post it to a helper on this PC instead
Returns: dataUrl|false, why (with upload, the answer's text)
RequestScreenshot(source, opts?)SERVER

A player's picture, with TakeScreenshot's options but upload. Waits up to 30 s. A game can send a fake picture: for tools, not catching cheats.

Returns: dataUrl|false, why

Errors, frame rate and reviving

GetErrorLog(opts?)SERVERCLIENT

The last 200 errors on this side: in threads, handlers, NUI callbacks, commands and statebag handlers of whip_core and every satellite (unless its fxmanifest says whip_error_tap 'no': the satellite helper), whip_core's own caught errors, red (^1) warnings, and on the client, pages with the page tools. Repeats are counted; an export's error goes to its caller instead.

Returns: { entries = { { seq, at, side, resource, kind, text, count } }, last, side }; kind: 'error', 'warning', 'page'
local before = exports.whip_core:GetErrorLog().last
-- ... do the thing being tested ...
local after = exports.whip_core:GetErrorLog({ since = before })
MeasureFrames(opts?)CLIENT

Frame timing over the next seconds (1-30, default 5); waits that long. Compare standing still in one place.

Returns: { seconds, frames, fps, fpsWorst1, medianMs, worstMs, over33, over50 }
RevivePlayer(source, reason?)SERVER

Revives a downed player where they lie, as /w Restore does: full health, no armour. reason is logged after revive: (default your resource's name).

Returns: true, or false, 'Player not loaded' | 'not down'

Screens in the world (DUI)

A DUI is a page from your resource, drawn by a browser of its own into a texture the game can draw in the world: over a head, on a wall, on the ground. WHIP draws its prompts, /me bubbles, NPC conversations, garage bays and the Director's marks this way.

The rules

Each DUI is a whole browser that keeps rendering whether or not anything draws it. WHIP's own keep these rules, and yours should too:

  1. One browser per system, not per thing. Lay the page out as an atlas of cells: thirty garage bays are thirty quads from one texture.
  2. A change is a message, never a new browser. Send one only when a cell's content changes, never every frame.
  3. Made on first use, given back when idle. Create it the first time something draws from it; destroy it a while after the last.
  4. A still page. Animate only while something is happening; an endless animation renders all the time.

Your own DUI

One browser for every sign your resource shows, made on the first draw, sent a sign's words only when they change, and destroyed a minute after the last draw.

local PAGE = ('nui://%s/html/signs.html'):format(GetCurrentResourceName())
local TXD, TEX = 'mysigns', 'signs'
local IDLE_MS = 60000

local dui, up, waiting, painted, lastUsed = nil, false, {}, {}, 0

local function release()
    if not dui then return end
    DestroyDui(dui)
    dui, up, waiting, painted = nil, false, {}, {}
end

-- Given back IDLE_MS after the last draw: a timer, not a loop
local function checkIdle()
    if not dui then return end
    local left = lastUsed + IDLE_MS - GetGameTimer()
    if left > 0 then SetTimeout(left, checkIdle) else release() end
end

-- Every draw calls this: made the first time, and counted as used
local function ensure()
    lastUsed = GetGameTimer()
    if dui then return end
    dui = CreateDui(PAGE, 1024, 1024)
    CreateRuntimeTextureFromDuiHandle(CreateRuntimeTxd(TXD), TEX, GetDuiHandle(dui))
    local mine = dui
    CreateThread(function()
        while dui == mine and not IsDuiAvailable(mine) do Wait(50) end
        if dui ~= mine then return end
        up = true
        for _, msg in ipairs(waiting) do SendDuiMessage(dui, json.encode(msg)) end
        waiting = {}
    end)
    SetTimeout(IDLE_MS, checkIdle)
end

-- A sign's words, sent only when they change (held until the page is up)
local function paint(cell, text)
    ensure()
    if painted[cell] == text then return end
    painted[cell] = text
    local msg = { cell = cell, text = text }
    if up then SendDuiMessage(dui, json.encode(msg)) else waiting[#waiting + 1] = msg end
end

-- Each frame a sign is near: its cell of the 4 x 4 atlas, over that spot
local function drawSign(cell, x, y, z)
    ensure()
    if not up then return end
    local col, row = cell % 4, cell // 4
    SetDrawOrigin(x, y, z, 0)
    DrawSpriteUv(TXD, TEX, 0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.1, col / 4, row / 4, (col + 1) / 4, (row + 1) / 4, 0.0, 255, 255, 255, 255)
    ClearDrawOrigin()
end

The page reads each message as a JSON string and paints only the cell it names:

window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
    const d = typeof e.data === 'string' ? JSON.parse(e.data) : e.data;
    if (d && d.cell !== undefined) document.querySelectorAll('.cell')[d.cell].textContent = d.text;
});
Keep an atlas inside the game's limit. CreateDui throws for a page wider than the game allows: 8192 pixels on GTA V Enhanced. Pack cells into more rows rather than one long strip.

Settings pages for your resource

Put your resource's settings in /whip → Settings beside Config, so server owners never open your config file. You declare the settings; WHIP builds the page, checks and saves values, sends changes to every player and calls you back.

The page is named by your label, and only permanent admins see it. Declare it with Whip.configPage from WHIP's helper, in a shared script: the server checks and saves, and each player's game needs your defaults.

Values follow the folder name. Saved values are kept under the name the server runs your resource by. Renaming the folder (mycafe to mycafe-v2) starts from your defaults again, so tell owners to keep the name across updates.

Your config.lua as the page

Your resource reads a Config table, and Whip.configPage (from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua) puts chosen Config values on your page. Each key is a path in Config, its default is config.lua's value, and saved values are written into Config on both sides, so your code keeps reading Config.X.

Saved values arrive when whip_core is ready, after your files load. Code that reads Config at file scope sees config.lua's values first: rebuild what it works out with Whip.onConfigChanged. whip_autos's shared/settings.lua is a worked example.

Whip.configPage(def)SERVER CLIENT

Call once at file scope (not in Whip.register), in a shared script after config.lua; it declares the page on both sides whenever whip_core is ready. Entries are the setting entries below, without default; tables are changed in place, so a local copy of Config.Shop sees new values.

Saved values are checked again: one that no longer passes (you lowered a max) is dropped with a console line, and config.lua's value stands. The page goes when your resource stops; saved values stay.

Values are kept as their check returns them (text trimmed, keyKind = 'hash' maps keyed by hash). sides = 'server' values go into the server's Config only. Only data goes on a page: an entry holding a function, or an undeclared table or position field in a row, is left off with a console line.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe page's name in Settings
settingstableThe entries, in order; each key a path such as 'Tuning.EngineSwapPrice'
groupstable|nilInstead of settings, for a long page: { { label = 'Prices', settings = { … } }, … }, each a group on the left
configtable|nilThe table the keys are in. Default Config
Returns: boolean: false when def isn't a page (printed). whip_core's own refusal is printed when the page is declared
-- settings.lua (shared_script, after config.lua)
Whip.configPage({
    label = 'My Cafe',
    groups = {
        { label = 'Prices', settings = {
            { key = 'Prices.coffee', type = 'int', min = 1, max = 500, unit = '$', label = 'Coffee' },
        } },
        { label = 'Counter', settings = {
            { key = 'Counter.coords', type = 'vec3', here = true, label = 'Where it stands' },
            { key = 'Counter.open', type = 'bool', label = 'Open' },
        } },
    },
})
Clamp what you read. A config.lua value its own row would refuse leaves that row off the page, with the reason in the console, and your code keeps reading the raw value.
Whip.onConfigChanged(path, fn)SERVER CLIENT

Rebuilds what you worked out from Config at load. fn runs after a page value changes on this side, including saved values written in as the page is declared. It hears its path, anything under it, and changes to a table it's inside. Call it at file scope: inside Whip.register it would be added again at every whip_core restart.

ParamTypeDescription
pathstringA path in Config
fnfunctionfunction(value, old, key): key is the path that changed, so a hook on 'Counter.coords' hearing 'Counter' gets the whole table. Read Config when in doubt. Mustn't wait
Whip.onConfigChanged('Counter.coords', function()
    local c = Config.Counter.coords
    SetBlipCoords(counterBlip, c.x, c.y, c.z)
end)

Setting entries

Each entry of a page's settings, and of an item's own settings:

FieldTypeDescription
keystringLetters, digits, _ and ., starting with a letter or _, up to 64; unique on the page. A dot makes a path: a callback on 'prices' also hears 'prices.coffee'
typestring'int', 'number', 'bool', 'string', 'enum', 'vec3', 'vec4', 'list', 'records', 'map' or 'record' (one card of fields, each its own setting: 'turbo.gain', its default from the card's default table)
defaultanyThe value until an admin changes it: an item's setting gives one; on a Whip.configPage page it's config.lua's value. It must pass the entry's checks or the row is left off (the console says which); the page is refused only when none pass
shownWhentable|nil{ path = 'key', equals = value }: show the row (or whole card) only while that setting has that value
label / helpstringThe row's name, and the line under it
min / max / stepnumber|nilint and number: range, and the arrows' step
unitstring|nilint and number: '$' goes in front, anything else ('m', 'ms') after
optionstableenum: { { value = 'slow', label = 'Slow' }, … }
maxLen / pattern / patternWhynumber / stringstring: most characters; a Lua pattern it must match (use ^…$ for the whole text); the message when it doesn't
nullable / emptyLabelboolean / stringAn empty box is nil, and the row calls it this (default 'none')
offWhenEmptybooleanint, number, string: an empty box is false ("off"), for a cap that can be switched off
applystring|nil'live' (default): in force at once, everywhere. 'restart': in force when your resource or whip_core next starts; read it at start, Whip.onConfigChanged isn't called. 'readonly': shown, never changed
whystring|nilFor 'restart' or 'readonly': the reason shown on the row
sidesstring|nil'both' (default), or 'server': never sent to players, for a key or password. Admins still see it
crossfunction|nilfunction(get), run on the server when this setting is in a save; get(key) returns any setting as it will be saved. Return true, or false, 'why' to refuse. Give both entries of a two-setting rule the check
here / limitsboolean / tablevec3, vec4: a Use where I stand button, and { x = { min, max }, … } per ranged axis
itemtablelist: every entry's shape, as an entry with no key: { type = 'int', min = 1, max = 9 }. int, number, string or enum, edited as one comma-separated line. For positions, use records with a vec3 field
fieldstablerecords, a map of rows, or record: the fields, each an entry with a key
widget / markerstring / tablewidget = 'mapPoints': records with a vec3 and a string field show as map icons, dragged to move, clicked to rename or remove, added where the admin stands. marker = { sprite = 361, colour = 1, name = 'Gas Station' }: the blip and a new row's name
eachtablemap of single values: each value's shape, e.g. { type = 'string', maxLen = 20 }
minItems / maxItems / uniquenumber / stringHow many entries or rows (a map takes maxItems only), and for records a field no two rows share. Set them equal to fix a table's rows
keyKind / keyPattern / keyWhystring|nilmap: keyKind = 'hash' takes a model name and keeps its hash (as GetEntityModel returns). 'number' keeps a digits-only key as a number (a mod slot, a wheel type). Name keys are checked against keyPattern

Each player's own settings

A choice each player makes for their own screen (volume, units, shown or hidden) goes on the pause menu's Server Settings page, as a row of yours. Your resource stores the value (its own KVP, on the player's PC); the page calls your get and set. The row goes when your resource stops and comes back when whip_core restarts.

Whip.playerSetting(def)CLIENT

Adds a row to Settings, under Server. From WHIP's helper; call it at file scope, it registers inside Whip.register itself. A refusal is printed with the reason.

FieldTypeDescription
keystringUnique: letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, up to 64. Start with your resource's name ('mycafe.sounds')
labelstringThe row's name
typestring'toggle' (true / false), 'choice' (one of options) or 'slider' (a number)
getfunctionfunction() returns the current value
setfunctionfunction(value) stores the new value. The page keeps nothing of yours
defaultanyRequired. What "Reset this page to server defaults" restores: true, an option's value, a number in range
groupstring?The tab: 'Controller', 'Vehicles', 'Map & HUD', 'Chat & voice' or your own. Default 'Other'
helpstring?One line under the row
optionstable?A choice's options, each { value, label }: at least two
min, max, step, unitnumber?, string?A slider's range, step (default 1) and the text after the number
Returns: boolean: false (printed) when def has no key, get or set, or this is the server
local sounds = GetResourceKvpInt('sounds') ~= 2   -- 2 is off; unset reads 0, so on

Whip.playerSetting({
    key = 'mycafe.sounds', group = 'Map & HUD', type = 'toggle', default = true,
    label = 'Café sounds', help = 'The till and the coffee machine.',
    get = function() return sounds end,
    set = function(on)
        sounds = on
        SetResourceKvpInt('sounds', on and 1 or 2)
    end,
})
GetPlayerSetting(key)CLIENT

A row's value on this player's PC: their choice, else the default. Reads whip_core's own rows too.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe row's key
Returns: any, or nil for a key not on the page
local unit = exports.whip_core:GetPlayerSetting('dial.speedUnit')   -- 'mph' or 'kmh'
SetPlayerSetting(key, value)CLIENT

Changes a row's value on this player's PC, as the page does, for your own screen that shows the same setting. A resource's row goes through its set; out-of-range values are clamped. whip_phone's call volume is voice.callVolume this way.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe row's key
valueanyA value its type takes
Returns: true, or false, reason (no such setting, or a value its type doesn't take)
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:SetPlayerSetting('voice.callVolume', 75)

Activity Log

WHIP keeps two timelines: one per character and one per item instance, so an admin can answer "where did this rifle come from". The admin tools read both, and your resource can write to them.

The Item LogServer owners

/whip → Economy → Item Log has two tabs:

  • Everything. Every item event, newest first, filtered by person, item, what happened, when (up to Config.ActivityLogDays) and a minimum amount. Click a person, an item's whole life, or a place to teleport there.
  • Economy. One item at a time: how many are in the game now, what came in and went out by reason, and who holds or gained the most. Items inside other items, and a resource's own storage, aren't counted.

Rows that name no item (logins, dev tool use) stay on the person's timeline in the Player Manager. The reasons are the reason your resource passes to AddItem, PayPlayer and the rest.

Exports

LogActivity(source, event, opts?)SERVER

Writes a row to a player's timeline. Pass an item's address as opts.slotData to add the row to that item's own history too, which also gives the item its uid if it has none.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberWhose timeline
eventstringShort event name. Required
opts.detailstring?Free text shown alongside it
opts.slotDatatable?An address with a slot: { kind = 'player', id = source, sub = 'player', slot = 4 }, the addr a use handler or FindItem gives you, or any store's (a gun in a stash)
Returns: true, or false, reason (no event name, a wrong address, an empty slot)
-- On the player's timeline only
exports.whip_core:LogActivity(source, 'whiplash_entered', { detail = 'Bay 3' })

-- Inside a use handler: on the player's timeline and the used item's own history
exports.whip_core:LogActivity(source, 'lockpick_used', { detail = 'garage door', slotData = addr })
Pass the address, not the item. The table GetItemAt returns is a copy, so a uid given to it belongs to nothing (a copy works only if the item already has a uid). A { container, slot } table is refused with a reason.
FlushActivityLog()SERVER

Writes every pending log row now. Rows already save in the same transaction as the change they describe, so you only need this in tests and operations work.

Returns: boolean: false if the database refused the rows (they're kept and tried again)

Debug & internal exports

Exports that exist for WHIP's own tools and tests. Don't build on them: they may change without notice.

GetGarageHelperStatus()CLIENT

Internal: a test hook. What the garage position helper is doing right now, for a test or a tool.

FieldTypeDescription
enabledbooleanConfig.GaragePositionHelper.enabled
duiActivebooleanWhether the one browser this feature uses is up
drawingnumberHow many bay outlines are visible right now
drivingbooleanWhether the player is in a driver's seat
qualifiesbooleanWhether the driven vehicle passes the requireStorable test
Returns: table

Timing your loops (WhipCost)

What a loop of yours really costs on a player's PC, without a profiler's overhead. Mark the section with WhipCost, run /whipcost in game, and read the table it prints in F8, most expensive first.

WhipCost.start() / WhipCost.stop(name, started)CLIENTSERVER

Marks a section to time. Load client_script '@whip_core/lib/cost.lua', and server_script the same for server code. While /whipcost isn't running, start() returns nil and stop() returns at once.

ParamTypeDescription
namestringThe section's line in the table, as 'area: what'
startednumber|nilWhat start() returned
Returns: start(): number|nil; stop(): nothing
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        local cost = WhipCost.start()
        drawCafeMarkers()
        WhipCost.stop('mycafe: markers', cost)
        Wait(0)
    end
end)
Never Wait() between the two. A run that waited a frame is left out of the table.

Running it and reading the table

With developer mode on, type /whipcost (20 seconds) or /whipcost 60 (5 to 120) and play as usual. The server console's whipcost times server sections, by CPU time only.

  • us a frame: the section's share of every frame. Read this column. A section that ran under 100 times is marked "rough".
  • KB a second: memory made, which the garbage collector then clears. A second table gives it for every resource loading lib/satellite.lua or lib/cost.lua: the climb you see in resmon.
  • Calls into whip_core, and how often: one a frame from another resource costs both sides every frame. Then whip_core's own loops.
Collectors pause while it runs, so memory counts are exact. A resource making over 32 MB gets its collector back and its figure stops there; afterwards, collectors catch up, which can cause a small hitch.

Your page in /w

Add a page of your own to the /w menu, a debug tool switch, or Object Viewer options. They show only to a developer with developer mode on.

A page of your own

Your page is a row at the end of Panels; picked, it shows your rows, and its first row (or Backspace) goes back. whip_core draws the rows and asks for them again after every pick. For levels of your own, return a view with back, and the way back calls your onBack.

The menu only reads rows. Check anything a row does on the server there: exports.whip_core:HasDevTools(source).
RegisterDevPage(id, def)CLIENT

Adds your page to /w, or replaces yours with this id. Declare it in Whip.register: whip_core forgets every page when it restarts. The page goes when your resource stops, and /w reopens on the page it was shut on with Escape.

FieldTypeDescription
idstringLetters, digits, _ and -; another resource's page with the same id is another page
labelstringThe row in /w and the page's title
descstring|nilThe line under the list while your row is picked
rowsfunctionReturns a list of rows, or { title, back, select, rows } for a level (back names the level above, select the row picked first). Called on open, after every pick, and on RefreshDevPage
onSelectfunction(rowId)A row was picked. It must not wait: start a thread, then call RefreshDevPage
onBackfunction|nilThe way back on a level that returned back
onOpen / onClosefunction|nilThe page came on screen, or left it
Row fieldTypeDescription
idstring|numberWhat onSelect gets. Every row but a note needs one
labelstringThe row's text
kindstring|nil'run' (default), 'toggle' (lit by active), 'open' (a chevron into a level) or 'note' (never picked)
activeboolean|nilA toggle's switch
descstring|nilThe line under the list while the row is picked
closeboolean|nilShut the menu after onSelect, for an action that needs a clear screen
iconstring|nilOne of the prompts' glyphs by name ('target', 'car'...); an unknown name draws nothing
sepstringA group header instead of a row: { sep = 'Playback' }
Returns: true, or false, why (a bad id, no label, no rows or onSelect)
local open, level = false, 'top'

Whip.register(function()
    Whip.core:RegisterDevPage('cafe', {
        label = 'Café',
        rows = function()
            if level == 'menu' then
                return { title = 'Menu', back = 'Café', rows = { { id = 'coffee', label = 'Coffee' } } }
            end
            return { rows = {
                { id = 'open', label = 'Open', kind = 'toggle', active = open },
                { id = 'restock', label = 'Restock', desc = 'Fills every shelf.' },
                { id = 'menu', label = 'Menu', kind = 'open' },
            } }
        end,
        onSelect = function(rowId)
            if rowId == 'open' then open = not open
            elseif rowId == 'menu' then level = 'menu'
            else TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:devAction', rowId) end   -- the server checks HasDevTools
        end,
        onBack = function() level = 'top' end,
    })
end)
RefreshDevPage(id)CLIENT

Your rows changed without a pick (a list arrived from the server). If your page is on screen, whip_core calls rows again, keeping the same row picked; otherwise it costs nothing.

Returns: true, or false, why (no page of yours has that id)
exports.whip_core:RefreshDevPage('cafe')
RemoveDevPage(id)CLIENT

Takes your page out of /w while your resource keeps running; it goes by itself when your resource stops.

Returns: true, or false, why (no page of yours has that id)

Debug tools

RegisterDebugTool(id, def)CLIENT

A switch of your own among /w's debug tools, shown while its Debug row is on, after WHIP's own, by label. Turning it on checks with the server, as any dev tool does; the same id again replaces it. Declare it in Whip.register; it goes when your resource stops.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringIts row in /w (40 characters at most)
descstring?The line under the list while its row is picked
onTogglefunctiononToggle(on), also with false when Debug or developer mode goes off. Return false to stay off
Returns: true, or false, why
exports.whip_core:RegisterDebugTool('mine', {
    label = 'My Debug', desc = 'What my overlay shows.',
    onToggle = function(on) ShowMyOverlay(on) end,
})
RemoveDebugTool(id)CLIENT

Takes your debug tool out of /w (it goes by itself when your resource stops). One that's on isn't switched off: that's yours to do.

Returns: true, or false, why (no debug tool of yours has that id)

Object Viewer options

Whip.objectViewerOption(id, def)CLIENT

Adds or changes an option in the Object Viewer's options, the list G opens on what's picked out (whip_autos' Open Whiplash is one). The id is '<your namespace>.<name>'. From @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua, called at file scope; picked, your select runs in a thread of its own.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe option's line (48 characters at most)
kindsstring[]vehicle, player, npc, object
whipboolean?true: only WHIP's own (a saved car, a player). false: only the game's. Left out: both
groupstring?Its heading (24 characters); default your resource's name
tintstring?blue, teal, green, amber, red, violet or slate (default)
hintstring?The line under the list while it's pointed at (160 characters)
selectfunctionselect(target), with target = { kind, entity, netId, whip, vehicleId, serverId, model, name, coords = { x, y, z, heading } }
Returns: true, or false when it isn't valid (the reason is printed). Whip.removeObjectViewerOption(id) removes one; it goes by itself when your resource stops.
Whip.objectViewerOption('mycafe.refuel', {
    label = 'Fill the tank', group = 'My cafe', tint = 'amber', kinds = { 'vehicle' }, whip = true,
    select = function(target)
        TriggerServerEvent('mycafe:server:refuel', target.vehicleId)   -- the server checks HasDevTools
    end,
})
A Dungeon Master sees it too, in Dungeon Mode. Check anything it asks of your server: HasDevTools(source), or the permission it needs.

Weapon System

whip_gunny is WHIP's weapon system: guns, magazines, ammunition, melee weapons, throwables and the jerry can. It ships with WHIP and needs no setup: its items are in /whip → Economy → Items, ready to sell or hand out.

A resource that calls it adds dependency 'whip_gunny'. For gunny as a worked example, see Learning from gunny.

How it works

Weapons are inventory items with state, kept in whip_core's item metadata: gunny owns the rules, whip_core owns the data. A revolver or pump shotgun carries its rounds itself.

gun item ─ metadata ─┬─ serial          "AB12CD34EF56"
                     ├─ attachments     { muzzle = 'gunny_suppressor' }
                     ├─ attachmentMeta  { muzzle = { ... } }
                     └─ magazine ─┬─ item    'gunny_mag_rifle'
                                  ├─ serial  'GH78IJ90KL12'
                                  ├─ ammo    24
                                  └─ ...     the rest of the magazine's metadata (its uid)
  • Drawing. The server records where the gun was drawn from and its serial; shots, throws and holstering go by that record. When the gun leaves its slot (dragged, stashed, handed over), the server puts it away.
  • Shooting. The game reports the rounds each frame fires and the server takes them from the metadata. The game's own count is believed only when it's lower.
  • Reloading. R swaps in the fullest magazine carried, or loads loose rounds into a gun with no magazine. Firing stops until the reload is done, and the gun can't be put away or swapped meanwhile (Finish reloading first).
  • Loading magazines. Load Bullets runs a bar on the server's clock, 300 ms a round, not in water or while falling (notWhile). Unload puts the rounds back in the pockets.

Magazines and calibers

  • Magazine-fed guns take separate magazine items, several kinds per gun.
  • No magazine (magless): revolvers, tube-fed and break-action shotguns, launchers. R loads loose rounds at once, or a shell at a time for the pump, pump Mk II, sawed-off and combat shotguns (loopedReload), stopped by firing or running.
  • Calibers. Each is an ammo item: '9mm' is 'ammo_9mm', loose rounds. A magazine takes one caliber, and item cards show it as Ammo Type.

Controls

KeyControllerAction
RBReload, on foot only
GLB + BCheck the ammo; with sticky bombs out, set them all off
E at the benchAUse the weapon bench

Players can rebind R and G, and move the controller buttons in the pause menu. In a seat, reloading is automatic (the last round, or the trigger on an empty gun) and takes at least the weapon's reloadTime. On a controller, double-tap RB to start or stop aiming, then hold it to fire.

The magazine slot, throwables and the jerry can

  • The magazine slot. Open on a gun shows its magazine, or its rounds, as one slot to drag in and out of. It's a panel item (server/magpanel.lua, the panel guide's worked example).
  • Throwables: grenades, sticky bombs, mines, pipe bombs, molotovs, BZ and tear gas, flares, snowballs, acid packages and newspapers. Each is a stack held whole, and each throw comes off it. The acid package and newspaper need a recent game build.
  • The jerry can (jerry_can): its ammunition is its fuel (metadata fuel, 0-100%), poured on the ground and lit. Pouring it into a car and filling it at a pump are whip_fuel's, through fuelCapacity. A new can is empty.

The weapon benchServer owners

Attachments go on and come off at the weapon bench: E at it with a gun in hand. Each attachment is an item, and each weapon lists what it takes slot by slot (scope, muzzle, barrel, grip, flashlight) as GTA components in items/attachments.lua. The bench's place, model and label are Config.WeaponBench in gunny's config.lua; enabled = false removes it.

Adding weaponsServer owners

  • One entry per item in items/weapons.lua, magazines.lua, calibers.lua or attachments.lua, each headed by every field and its default. Then restart whip_gunny.
  • A gun needs hash (GTA's name in backticks, listed in whip_core's shared/gta_weapons.lua), a caliber from items/calibers.lua, and compatibleMags, or magless = true with internalCapacity. Its prop model is in shared/gta_weapon_models.lua. loopedReload = true needs looped reload animations in its weapon meta.
  • A melee weapon needs only weight, description, hash, label, prop and melee = true. Icons are html/img/items/<key>.webp (or .png).
  • A broken entry is left out, with a [GUNNY] WARNING console line saying why.
  • Sizes and reload times can be changed per item in /whip → Economy → Items, which wins over the file until you Reset.

To add guns without editing gunny's files, so updates never touch them, use a weapon pack.

From your resource

A gun is an ordinary item: AddItem gives one empty, RemoveItem takes one, and GiveWeapon adds a magazine, rounds or your own serial. The held gun is GetHeldItem(source) on the server and GetDrawnWeapon on the client.

Give a gun, and take that one back

For an armory or a mission's kit, note the serials you hand out and take back those. FindItemByMetadata finds each, and StoreTake takes it (a drawn gun is put away first, its magazine with it). A spare magazine put into a gun is inside it, so its serial finds nothing until it comes out.

local issued = {}   -- [source] = the serials handed out

local function issue(source)
    local ok, where, gunSerial = exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_carbinerifle', { loaded = true }, 'armory issue')
    if not ok then return false, where end
    local _, _, magSerial = exports.whip_gunny:GiveMagazine(source, 'gunny_mag_carbinerifle', 999, 'armory issue')
    issued[source] = { gunSerial, magSerial }
    return true
end

local function takeBack(source)   -- exactly what was issued
    for _, serial in ipairs(issued[source] or {}) do
        local at = exports.whip_core:FindItemByMetadata('serial', serial)
        if at and at.kind == 'player' and at.id == source then
            exports.whip_core:StoreTake(at, 1, { reason = 'returned to the armory' })
        end
    end
    issued[source] = nil
end

Every shot fired

whip_gunny:weapon:fired comes each time the server takes rounds off a gun: automatic fire is counted a frame at a time, so shots can be more than 1. It runs as often as anyone fires, so keep your handler short.

-- Server: a "shots fired" call, at most one a minute per shooter
local lastAlert = {}
AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:fired', function(e)
    local now = GetGameTimer()
    if e.coords and now - (lastAlert[e.source] or 0) > 60000 then   -- coords is nil once they've gone
        lastAlert[e.source] = now
        AlertPolice(e.coords, e.item)   -- your own
    end
end)

The rounds on your HUD

The client has no per-shot event: read GetDrawnWeapon a few times a second between whip_gunny:weapon:drawn and :holstered. Its count is live.

local following = 0   -- each draw and holster bumps it, ending the loop before
AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:drawn', function(w)
    following = following + 1
    local mine = following
    if w.kind ~= 'gun' then return end
    CreateThread(function()
        local gun = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
        while following == mine and gun do
            ShowAmmo(gun.ammo, gun.capacity)   -- your own
            Wait(150)
            gun = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
        end
    end)
end)
AddEventHandler('whip_gunny:weapon:holstered', function() following = following + 1; HideAmmo() end)

No weapons here

For a no-weapons zone, handcuffs or jail, call BlockHands with only = 'weapons', on the client for a place or the server for one player. gunny refuses a draw with the block's label and puts away a drawn gun until UnblockHands.

exports.whip_core:BlockHands(source, 'myjail', { only = 'weapons', label = 'No weapons in here' })

A zone's own Weapons away rule works on GTA's weapons, not gunny's.

Weapon packs

A weapon pack adds guns from your own resource without editing gunny. It streams the weapons, ships icons as html/img/items/<item>.webp, and registers each item inside Gunny.register (no dependency needed), magazines first, in a file both sides load. A pack's gun needs what any gun needs (Adding weapons), may use gunny's magazines and calibers, and gets gunny's menus, magazine slot, settings and bench.

-- fxmanifest.lua (models and textures go in stream/)
shared_script '@whip_gunny/lib/pack.lua'
shared_script 'gunny.lua'
data_file 'WEAPONCOMPONENTSINFO_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponcomponents.meta'   -- before the weapons that list them
data_file 'WEAPON_METADATA_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponarchetypes.meta'
data_file 'WEAPON_ANIMATIONS_FILE' 'data/mypack_weaponanimations.meta'
data_file 'WEAPONINFO_FILE' 'data/mypack_weapons.meta'
files { 'data/*.meta', 'html/img/items/*.webp' }

-- gunny.lua: runs when gunny is up, and again each time it starts
Gunny.register(function()
    exports.whip_gunny:RegisterMagazine('mypack_mag_m4', {
        weight = 0.2, label = 'M4 Magazine', prop = 'w_ar_mypack_m4_mag', caliber = '5.56x45', capacity = 30,
    })
    exports.whip_gunny:RegisterWeapon('mypack_m4', {
        weight = 3.2, label = 'M4', description = 'A carbine.', hash = `WEAPON_MYPACK_M4`,
        prop = 'w_ar_mypack_m4', caliber = '5.56x45', compatibleMags = { 'mypack_mag_m4' }, reloadTime = 2200,
        attachments = { scope = { medium = `COMPONENT_MYPACK_M4_SCOPE` } },
    })
end)
  • Print what each register returns while you build: a name already in use is refused, and an attachment kind no item in items/attachments.lua has is reported.
  • When the pack stops, its items leave gunny; players keep them, and they work again when it's back.
  • WHIP's weapon lists (the Director, the Object Viewer) show the guns once the pack calls Whip.weapons from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua.

gunny's own fxmanifest.lua streams its add-on guns the same way and is a full example.

Debugging

/w → Debug → Gunny Debug shows the drawn weapon's rounds as the game, gunny and the server count them, and the shot reports. /gunnydebugreset zeroes the counters; /gunnydebugserver says what's drawn. [GUNNY] WARNING lines always print: a failed write, or an undone change.

A gun that won't reload

The player seesWhy, and what to do
No magazines for this weapon on youNone of its compatibleMags is in their pockets
All your magazines for this weapon are emptyLoad Bullets on one, with its caliber's rounds carried
No ammunition for this weapon on youA gun with no magazine needs its caliber's loose rounds
No room for the old magazineThe old one had nowhere to go, not even the ground: the reload was undone
Nothing at allR does nothing in a vehicle, with a melee weapon, with a screen or bar up, or while the gun is being put away

Learning from gunny

whip_gunny is the worked example of a resource built on WHIP: each section is a pattern WHIP expects, with gunny's code for it. New to WHIP? Start with Your First Resource.

Every client message is declared

Everything a game may send gunny's server is a SecureEvent or SecureCallback, declared inside Whip.register: whip_core checks the rate limit and each parameter before the handler runs.

exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('myguns:server:shotFired', {
    whileDead = true,                   -- a round fired as the player dies is still spent
    rateLimit = 15, burst = 30,
    params = { {'shotsFired', 'int', 1, 10, 1} },
}, function(source, player, shotsFired) --[[ ... ]] end)

'int' holds a value in range (9999 counts as 10) instead of refusing it: the rounds were fired, so the count mustn't be refused. Use 'amount' for money or items, which refuses, and 'id' for an exact id. gunny's RegisterGunnyEvent and RegisterGunnyCallback wrap the same call only because a weapon pack changes what its 'slot' params accept.

Declare inside Whip.register

whip_core keeps items, callbacks, panels and hooks in memory. Declare them inside Whip.register (from @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua) and they're declared once whip_core is ready; with dependency 'whip_core', a whip_core restart restarts you too, so there's nothing to clean up (the satellite helper).

Name the item the player clicked with a 'slot' param

The client sends the slot; a 'slot' param checks the pocket is the player's and holds the right kind of item, and hands over { addr, item, amount, metadata }. An item that moved meanwhile is refused with a readable reason.

-- server/magazines.lua
RegisterGunnyCallback('whip_gunny:unloadBulletsFromMag', { params = {
    { 'mag',   'slot', { item = GunnyMagazineItems } },   -- one of the player's own magazines
    { 'count', 'int',  1, 9999, 9999 },
} }, function(source, player, mag, count)
    local ok, left, unloaded = GunnyUnloadMagazine(source, mag.addr, count)
    if not ok then return false, left end
    return true, { left = left, unloaded = unloaded }
end)

The game learns the slot from a right-click action (RegisterContextAction), which gets addr and tells the game addr.slot and addr.sub. Prefix every action, event and callback with your resource's name: names are server-wide, and an action's is at most 32 characters.

Declare a panel, don't handle one

The magazine slot (server/magpanel.lua) declares how it reads and writes the gun's metadata and what may go in (onValidate); whip_core performs the move and calls onChange. A panel that only holds items needs only allowedItems. Either way the item must not stack and needs an action that opens it (the worked example).

Take before you give, and check every result

A reload takes the new magazine before giving the old one back; unloading lowers the count before giving the rounds. A failed step gives back what was taken (GunnyGiveBack), and GunnyStillThere reads the slot again after any wait so the undo lands on the same item.

-- server/magazines.lua: unloading
meta.ammo = currentAmmo - toUnload                            -- take: the magazine lowered first
if not exports.whip_core:SetItemMetadata(magAddr, meta) then
    return false, 'Could not unload: the magazine was not changed'
end
local added = Whip.core:AddItem(source, caliber.ammoItem, toUnload,   -- then give
    nil, { reason = 'unloaded from a magazine', noDrop = true })
if not added then
    -- no room: the rounds go back into the magazine, if it's still the one lowered
end

A bar the server times

Loading a magazine runs the server Progress through Whip.core and loads only when it returns true; a finish sooner than the bar could fill is refused ('too fast'). It waits, so run it from a SecureEvent or right-click action, never a SecureCallback (the game gives up after 10 seconds), and read the item again after. To use an item at the end of a bar, give RegisterUseHandler a table instead (a use with a progress bar).

Go by the server's own record

Shots, throws and holstering go by where the server saw the gun drawn and its serial (GunnyDrawnWeapon), never a slot the client names. Every gun and magazine gets a serial as it's made (RegisterItemDefaultMetadata). Give your own findable items an id the same way: WHIP's uid only comes the first time an item is logged.

Calling whip_core

Call an export straight when it returns at once, inside a handler whip_core runs (GetItemAt, SetItemMetadata). Use Whip.core for a call that can wait (AddItem, Progress), for everything after such a wait, and outside whip_core's handlers; it returns false, why instead of throwing. The full rule is in Calling whip_core, and at the top of gunny's server/main.lua and client/main.lua.

Where to look

Read server/main.lua, server/items.lua, server/weapons.lua, server/magpanel.lua, then client/main.lua.

To see how toRead
Register items, right-click options and panelsserver/items.lua: registerWithWhip
Declare what the game may askserver/main.lua: RegisterGunnyCallback, RegisterGunnyEvent; server/shooting.lua
Act on the item the player clickedserver/magazines.lua: unloadBulletsFromMag; client/main.lua: GunnySlot
Run a bar the server timesserver/magazines.lua: runLoad
Take before you give, and undo on a failureserver/reload.lua: performReload; server/main.lua: GunnyGiveBack, GunnyStillThere
Keep a record the server trustsserver/weapons.lua: equipWeapon, GunnyDrawnWeapon
Ask the server and wait for the resultclient/main.lua: GunnyCallback; client/weapons.lua: DrawWeapon
Run a per-frame loop only while neededclient/main.lua: GunnyStartTick, RegisterGunnyTick
Hold controls off for a momentclient/reload.lua: holdFire (BlockControls)
Every file
FileWhat's in it
config.lua, items/*.luaThe weapon bench; every caliber, weapon, magazine and attachment
shared/catalog.lua, shared/whip_weapons.luaItem lookups and rules; gunny's guns in whip_core's weapon lists
shared/packs.lua, lib/pack.luaWeapon packs

server/items.luaItem registration; GiveWeapon, GiveMagazine
