server/magpanel.lua, */magazines.lua, */reload.luaThe magazine slot; loading and unloading; reloading
*/shooting.lua, */throwables.lua, client/ammo.lua, client/vehicle.luaShots and throws, the jerry can, sticky bombs; the one place ped ammo is written; shooting from a seat
*/attachments.lua, html/, */debug.luaThe weapon bench; Gunny Debug
data/, stream/, stream_enhanced/, audiodirectory/GTA weapon data, models and sounds (stream_enhanced/ for GTA V Enhanced); sources in anim_src/, audio_src/, props_src/

Gunny API

Server and client exports of exports.whip_gunny, and its events; add dependency 'whip_gunny' to your fxmanifest. New to it? Read Weapon System first.

Giving weapons

GiveWeapon(source, weaponName, overrides?, reason?)SERVER

Gives a player a weapon with a new serial, set up as you say. Rounds are held to what the gun or magazine holds.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player's server id
weaponNamestringThe weapon item ('gunny_pistol')
overridestable?serial; attachments ({ [slot] = attachment item }); a gun with magazines: magazine (one it takes) with ammo rounds in it; a gun without: ammo; either: loaded = true fills it (with its first magazine when none is named); the jerry can: fuel, 0-100; a throwable: amount
reasonstring?Why they got it, for the activity log ('shop purchase'), as AddItem takes
Returns: true, where, serial: where is 'inventory', or 'ground' at their feet when it didn't fit; serial finds it again (give and take back), nil for a throwable. Or false, reason: an unknown weapon or magazine, a magazine or attachment the gun doesn't take, or AddItem's own refusal (a player not loaded)
exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_pistol', { loaded = true })
exports.whip_gunny:GiveWeapon(source, 'gunny_pistol', { serial = 'LSPD00000042', magazine = 'gunny_mag_pistol_extended', ammo = 10 })
GiveMagazine(source, magName, ammo?, reason?)SERVER

Gives a player a magazine with rounds in it, held to what it holds.

ParamTypeDescription
sourcenumberThe player's server id
magNamestringThe magazine item ('gunny_mag_pistol')
ammonumber?Rounds in it: none is empty, and any number past its size fills it (its size can change on the Items page)
reasonstring?Why they got it, for the activity log
Returns: true, where, serial as GiveWeapon (the magazine's own serial), or false, reason: an unknown magazine, or AddItem's own refusal
exports.whip_gunny:GiveMagazine(source, 'gunny_mag_pistol', 999)   -- full, whatever its size

Weapon packs

RegisterWeapon(item, def) / RegisterMagazine(item, def)SERVERCLIENT

A weapon pack's gun or magazine, on both sides, inside Gunny.register (@whip_gunny/lib/pack.lua). def is an entry shaped like gunny's items/weapons.lua or items/magazines.lua, checked as gunny's own are; a weapon may add attachments ({ [slot] = { [kind] = component } }). Register its magazines first; the same pack registering again replaces its own.

Returns: true, or false, reason: a missing field, an unknown caliber or magazine, a name of gunny's own or another pack's

Client

There's no export to open a gun's magazine slot: it's a panel item, opened by the gun's whip_gunny:open_weapon action.

IsWeaponDrawn()CLIENT

Whether one of gunny's weapons is in the player's hands. To follow it rather than ask, listen for whip_gunny:weapon:drawn / :holstered.

Returns: boolean
GetDrawnWeapon()CLIENT

A copy of the weapon in the player's hands: { item, label, kind, slot, pocket, serial, ammo, capacity, magazine, attachments }, or nil. The count is live (a HUD).

FieldTypeDescription
kindstring'gun', 'melee', 'throwable' or 'fuelCan'
ammonumberA gun's rounds, a throwable's stack, the jerry can's petrol as GTA counts it (0 to 4500, not the item's 0-100%), 0 for melee
capacitynumber|nilThe most a gun holds: its magazine's size, or the rounds a gun with no magazine takes. nil with no magazine in, and for anything else
magazinestring|nilThe magazine's item name ('gunny_mag_pistol')
Returns: table|nil
local w = exports.whip_gunny:GetDrawnWeapon()
if w and w.kind == 'gun' and w.ammo == 0 then
    exports.whip_core:Notify(('Your %s is empty'):format(w.label), 'info')
end
DrawWeapon(slot, pocket?)CLIENT

Draws the weapon in a pocket slot, with its animation, putting away another drawn one first. Waits: call it from a thread. To put a weapon away, call whip_core's FreeHands().

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe slot
pocketstring?'player' (default) or 'accessory'
Returns: true (drawn, or already was), or false, reason: the hands blocked, a reload under way, the server refused
local ok, why = exports.whip_gunny:DrawWeapon(3)
Not during a reload. From the press until the reload ends (not only while the animation plays) it returns false and the gun stays out. A death, or BlockHands, still puts it away at once.
LoadBullets(slot, pocket?)CLIENT

Fills the magazine in a pocket slot from the rounds carried, behind the server's bar (300 ms a round), and tells the player how it went. One magazine at a time; waits, so call it from a thread.

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe magazine's slot
pocketstring?'player' (default) or 'accessory'
Returns: true, rounds loaded (a load stopped partway keeps what went in), or false, reason: 'Busy' (another bar is up), 'Magazine is full', no rounds carried, 'Loading cancelled'
UnloadBullets(slot, pocket?, count?)CLIENT

Empties the magazine in a pocket slot into the pockets as rounds, or count of them, and tells the player. Waits: call it from a thread.

ParamTypeDescription
slotnumberThe magazine's slot
pocketstring?'player' (default) or 'accessory'
countnumber?How many (default: all)
Returns: true, rounds unloaded, or false, reason: it's empty, no room for the rounds
ApplyWeaponAttachments(ped, hash, item, attachments)CLIENT

Fits a gun's attachments on any ped holding it (an NPC, a display), turning attachments as the gun's metadata has them ({ [slot] = attachment item }) into the GTA components that gun takes. The ped must hold the weapon first.

Returns: nothing
GiveWeaponToPed(npc, `WEAPON_PISTOL`, 12, false, true)
exports.whip_gunny:ApplyWeaponAttachments(npc, `WEAPON_PISTOL`, 'gunny_pistol', { muzzle = 'gunny_suppressor' })

Events

For a police alert, evidence or a Director card, listen with AddEventHandler rather than watching the ped (naming rule).

EventSidePayload
whip_gunny:weapon:drawnServer{ source, item, kind, serial, slot, pocket }: kind is 'gun', 'melee', 'throwable' or 'fuelCan'
whip_gunny:weapon:holsteredServer{ source, item, serial, slot, pocket, reason }, once however it went: reason is 'holstered', 'moved' (it left its slot), 'replaced', 'logout' or 'dropped'
whip_gunny:weapon:firedServer{ source, item, serial, shots, ammo, coords }, each time the server takes rounds off a drawn gun (every shot fired). ammo is what's left; coords is nil once the shooter has gone
whip_gunny:weapon:drawnClientThe GetDrawnWeapon() table
whip_gunny:weapon:holsteredClient{ item, slot, pocket }

The client has no per-shot event: see the rounds on your HUD.

Rope System

whip_rope is a physics rope. Players carry it as the rope item, tie it to cars, props and the map, tow with it and hang off it. Your resource can make ropes too, as whip_fuel's pump hose does.

It ships with WHIP and needs no setup. See Rope API for ropes from a script and Learning from rope for its code.

Using a rope

ToHow
Put one outUse the Rope item. One end is in your hand
Tie the end you holdLook at a car, a prop or the map within reach and press the prompt's key. You then hold the other end, if it was loose
Put it down, let go, coil it upThe wheel (F1). Coiling takes 3 seconds and puts the rope in your pockets
Pick up or untie an endThe prompt on the end
Hang onThe prompt on the rope. Jump lets go; a shot knocks a hanging player off, unhurt

Holding an end, you can't sprint (a setting). Walk a metre past the rope's easy stretch and it leaves your hands; if a car drives off with the other end, you're dragged for a few seconds.

How it pulls

A slack rope pulls nothing. Taut, it stretches easily up to 15% past its length, then harder: a weak car is pulled back, a strong one drags it. Both ends feel the same pull, so a light car moves more than a heavy truck.

The server keeps each rope's ends; every game near works out the rest, so a towed car follows at once, at any ping.

SettingsServer owners

  • /whip → Settings → Rope has the rules (who may handle a rope, tying, reach), length and node count, ropes per player, collisions, hanging and holding. How it pulls and looks is in whip_rope's config.lua.
  • A rope keeps the length and node count it was made with.
  • Players who leave with ropes out get them back at their next login, even after a restart.
  • With Config.Rules.AnyoneCanHandle on (the default), anyone can pick up, untie or coil up anyone's rope; coiling gives the item to whoever coils it.

Ropes in the Director

whip_rope adds a Ropes group to the Director's cards. A run's ropes are found by name (rope unless a scenario makes more than one), and go when the run ends, a Test's too.

  • Make a Rope, Move a Rope End, Change Rope Rules, Remove a Rope. Each end is tied to a placed car (front, back or middle), prop or spot, in the player's hand, or loose. The rules say whether players may pick it up and hang off it.
  • Goal: Tie a Rope: on once any rope (a player's too, unless it asks for the run's) is tied to a placed car, prop or spot, or between two. Goal: Hang on a Rope: a run player hangs off one for as long as it asks.
  • When a Rope Is Pulled Too Far: a run's rope is pulled past a stretch (default 35%); it can snap.

A rope never ties to an NPC (Check says so). A moving prop is tied to itself; a still one, and a spot, are tied to the map.

Debugging

All need developer mode on; /ropes and /clearropes also run from the server console.

  • /ropedebug: your overlay of each rope's ends, stretch, pull and rays cast a second.
  • /ropestatus: what your game has, in F8. /ropes: every rope out, in the server console.
  • /clearropes: takes every rope in. Owners get theirs back; a resource's rope is removed and its resource told (whip_rope:ropeRemoved).

Learning from rope

Most of whip_rope is rope physics (client/physics.lua, client/collision.lua, client/contact.lua), which teaches nothing about WHIP. These are the smaller parts worth reading; for the patterns gunny shows, see Learning from gunny.

The game acts first, the server corrects it

Picking up or tying an end changes the rope on the player's game at once, so it feels instant at any ping, then asks the server through a SecureEvent. A refusal, in the handler or before it (through the schema's onReject), sends that game the rope as the server has it. Every end change goes through Rope.ApplyEnd, which skips an unchanged end, so the server's echo does nothing.

-- client/interaction.lua: the end in the hand at once, then the ask
Rope.ApplyEnd(rope, which, { type = 'held', heldBy = Rope.MyServerId() })
TriggerServerEvent('whip_rope:take', rope.serverRopeId, which)

-- server/main.lua: a refusal, in the handler or before it, sends their game the rope as the server has it
local function refuse(source, ropeId, why)
    Ropes.correct(source, ropeId)
    return false, why                                 -- WHIP shows `why` to the player
end
-- in the SecureEvent's schema; `raw` is what the game sent, not checked yet
onReject = function(src, _, raw) Ropes.correct(src, tonumber(type(raw) == 'table' and raw[1])) end,

What a game tells the server is a claim

A report about something the server can't see is checked against what it can.

  • Node positions are passed on only near the rope's ends (believable).
  • A shot at someone hanging counts only from an armed player in range (onShot).
  • A stretched rope counts only when its ends really are far apart (onStretched).
  • A blown-up prop counts only with an explosion by it, which OneSync routes through the server (explosionEvent).

Nothing a player owns is lost

A rope still out when its owner leaves, or whip_rope stops, is owed back to their character in whip_rope's resource KVP, and paid as that character loads. The debt comes off the books before the give, so two loads can't both be paid, and goes back on if the give fails.

-- server/item.lua
local function payOwed(source, charId)
    local owed = Ropes.takeOwed(charId)               -- off the books first
    if owed <= 0 then return end
    if not Ropes.giveItem(source, owed, 'ropes you had out') then
        Ropes.owe(charId, owed)                       -- the give failed: owed again
    end
end

A bar the server times, and a look after it

Coiling up runs the server Progress through Whip.core from a SecureEvent handler, which may wait (a SecureCallback may not). The bar takes seconds, so the handler looks again after it: the rope may be gone or in someone else's hands. Pockets that won't take the item make it owed instead.

-- server/main.lua, onCoil (trimmed)
local done = Whip.core:Progress(source, { label = 'Coiling up the rope', duration = Config.Item.CoilDuration or 3000, canCancel = true })
if done ~= true then return false end             -- cancelled, or they left
if Ropes.all[ropeId] ~= rope or Ropes.heldBy(source, true) ~= rope then return false end   -- still there, still theirs?
Ropes.remove(ropeId)
if not Ropes.giveItem(source, 1, 'rope coiled up') then Ropes.owe(player and player.charId, 1) end

A prompt where the player looks

The tie prompt is a whip_core action with aimBox (at: where it lives): it sits where the player's look meets a car, prop or the map, and ctx.coords is that point. An aimBox action casts a ray every frame while it exists, so whip_rope adds it only while an end is in the hand.

-- client/ui.lua (trimmed)
local TIE = {
    id = 'tie', group = 'whip_rope', label = 'Tie the rope here', reach = Config.Rules.Reach,
    at = { aimBox = { 'vehicle', 'object', 'world' } },   -- a car, a prop, or the map itself
    onSelect = function(ctx) Rope.TieHeldEnd(ctx.entity, ctx.coords, ctx.world, ctx.normal) end,
}
-- five times a second: up only while an end is in the hand
local wantTie = Rope.MyHeld() ~= nil
if wantTie ~= tieUp then
    if wantTie then tieUp = Whip.core:AddAction(TIE) == true
    else Whip.core:RemoveAction('tie'); tieUp = false end
end
Without dependency 'whip_core', reset the flag. The action lives in whip_core's memory. A resource that keeps running through a whip_core restart must reset its "prompt is up" flag in Whip.onCoreLost, or the prompt never comes back.

Where to look

To see how toRead
Check what a game asks, and put it right on a refusalserver/main.lua: refuse, its Whip.register block
Change things on the player's game before the server repliesclient/interaction.lua: Rope.TakeEnd, Rope.TieHeldEnd, Rope.ApplyEnd
Put the game right when the server says noclient/sync.lua: whip_rope:correction
Check what a game tells you against what the server can seeserver/main.lua: believable, onShot; server/api.lua: onStretched, onEndBroken
Let go of what a player had when they die, log out or leaveserver/main.lua: its last event handlers; server/state.lua: Ropes.playerGone
Owe an item back, kept on diskserver/state.lua: Ropes.owe; server/item.lua: payOwed
Register an item whose use puts something in the worldserver/item.lua: registerItem, onUse
Run a bar the server timesserver/main.lua: onCoil
Prompts, wheel entries and the hint capsuleclient/ui.lua
A settings page that changes things at onceshared/settings.lua: Whip.configPage, Whip.onConfigChanged
Hold the player's ped and slow their walkclient/interaction.lua: HangPedOn, applyHoldWalk (HoldPlayerPed, BlockControls)
Offer an API to other resources, each owning what it madeserver/api.lua (keyed to GetInvokingResource(), cleaned up in onResourceStop); client/api.lua
Use the rope API from your own resourcewhip_fuel/server/hose.lua: draw; whip_fuel/client/pumps.lua
Loops that rest while there's nothing to doclient/main.lua, client/ui.lua (Rope.Const.IDLE_MS)

Rope API

Make ropes from your own resource (a tow line, a winch, a hose) with exports.whip_rope. New to ropes? Read Rope System first.

Add dependency 'whip_rope', or, if you can work without ropes, check GetResourceState('whip_rope') == 'started' before a call. whip_fuel's pump hose (whip_fuel/server/hose.lua) uses everything here.

Your ropes

Only your resource can move a rope it made with SetRopeEnd, or remove it. It stays when its player leaves, goes when your resource stops, is never an item and never counts against a player's ropes. Its length is fixed: for another, remove it and create it again.

With locked = true, nobody else moves it, and holding its end isn't holding a rope. Unlocked, players handle it like any rope and you aren't told (read GetRope): put its end in a player's hand and whip_rope's tie prompt lets them hook it to any car.

A rope's ends

Each end is a table, in the same shape for CreateRope, SetRopeEnd and GetRope.

EndFields
{ type = 'held' }heldBy: a player's server id. It ends at their right hand (or at heldAt's prop)
{ type = 'fixed' }pos: a spot in the world; tied = true: tied to the map there (players see Untie), not put down
{ type = 'vehicle' }netId: a networked car; offset: where on it, in the car's space (default its middle), or edge = 'front' / 'back'
{ type = 'object' }netId: a networked prop, or 0 for a map prop, which then needs model (a hash: `prop_gas_pump_1a`) and worldPos, and may give point (where it's tied, default worldPos); offset; still = true: never pulled loose; mass in kg (otherwise guessed from its size)
{ type = 'free' }Loose. GetRope also gives at, where it was let go, when the server knows
An end can come loose with no notice. On any rope when the car or prop it's tied to goes (garaged, deleted, despawned); on an unlocked rope also when its holder dies or leaves, or a player unties it. Check GetRope before you rely on it.

Server

CreateRope(spec)SERVER

Makes a rope between two things, built on every game near it.

spec fieldTypeDescription
origin, tailtableIts two ends. At least one must be held, fixed, or tied to a car or prop
lengthnumber?Metres, 0.5 to 100 (default: the item rope's length setting). Fixed for the rope's life
linknumber?Metres between nodes (default: the item rope's). At most 64 nodes: past that, links are made longer
playernumber?The player it's for: their game always has the rope
kindstring?A tag of your own, up to 32 characters, returned by GetRope
lockedboolean?true: nobody can grab, tie, put down, coil or hang off it. Left out, players handle it like any rope but can't coil it (locked or not)
take, hangboolean?On an unlocked rope: take = false, nobody picks up or unties its ends; hang = false, nobody hangs off it. Change with SetRopeRules
looktable?{ model, modelNoShadow, thickness }: its own rope pieces, modelled as whip_rope_seg (whip_rope/docs/whip_rope_seg.txt). Models are hashes; a quoted name is dropped
collidetable?{ spacing, vehicles, props }: every spacing'th node is checked (default 2), and whether cars and props count (default: the Rope settings). The map always counts
heldAttable?{ model, offset }: a held end sits at offset on the prop of that model in the hand (a pump's nozzle). This model may be a name or a hash
watchtable?{ stretch, holdMs, broken }: whip_rope:ropeStretched when pulled stretch past its length (0.35: 35%) for holdMs (default 250); broken = true: whip_rope:ropeEndBroken when a map prop it's tied to is blown up
maxStretchnumber?A hard length, 0 to 2 (0.2: 20% past it): past it, one pull draws both ends together, each moved by its weight. Left out, the rope is elastic with no hard end
Returns: number: the rope's id, or false, reason: what's wrong with an end ('tail: a vehicle end names netId'), or 'neither end is anywhere yet'
-- A 6 m tow line from a truck's back to the car behind it, that players can't take off
local id, why = exports.whip_rope:CreateRope({
    origin = { type = 'vehicle', netId = NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(truck), offset = vector3(0.0, -3.2, 0.6) },
    tail   = { type = 'vehicle', netId = NetworkGetNetworkIdFromEntity(car),   offset = vector3(0.0, 2.1, 0.3) },
    length = 6.0, locked = true, kind = 'towline',
})
if not id then print('no tow line: ' .. why) return end
How maxStretch holds

The pull is at most a very strong hose's: a snag jolts the car, and the rope stretches for a moment up to twice maxStretch (Config.Coupling.HardCeiling), where it holds. A car driving away from something that doesn't move is never held back. With watch.stretch above maxStretch, the notice comes only when neither end can follow: whip_fuel's hose (0.3 and 0.35) is told only when a car drives off with the nozzle in.

SetRopeEnd(id, which, end)SERVER

Moves one end of a rope your resource made. Every game is told.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id
whichstring'origin' or 'tail'
endtableWhere it goes: an end
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'not your rope' (another resource's, or gone), a bad which, or what's wrong with the end
exports.whip_rope:SetRopeEnd(id, 'tail', { type = 'held', heldBy = source })
A locked rope's held end is yours to move. whip_rope never lets it go for you: move it on whip_core:player:died, whip_core:player:logout and playerDropped, as whip_rope's server/main.lua does.
SetRopeRules(id, rules)SERVER

Changes what players may do with a rope your resource made, and its stretch notice, from now on. A field left out stays as it was.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id
rulestable{ take?, hang?, stretch? }: take and hang as CreateRope takes them; stretch is its watch.stretch, or false to stop it
Returns: true, or false, reason: 'not your rope', or a rule it can't read
exports.whip_rope:SetRopeRules(id, { take = false })   -- the winch is set: nobody unhooks it now
RemoveRope(id)SERVER

Removes a rope your resource made, on every game.

Returns: true, or false when it's another resource's or already gone
GetRope(id)SERVER

Any rope's tag, ends and length, a player's or a resource's.

Returns: { kind, origin, tail, length } (its ends as the server keeps them), or nil
local rope = exports.whip_rope:GetRope(id)
if rope and rope.tail.type == 'held' then print(rope.tail.heldBy, rope.length) end

Client

GetRopeEndEntity(id, which)CLIENT

The car or prop a rope's end is tied to on this game. A SetRopeEnd move has reached this game once this returns the new one.

ParamTypeDescription
idnumberThe rope's id
whichstring'origin' or 'tail'
Returns: the entity, or nil: not tied to one, not streamed in yet, or no such rope here

The notices

Every resource hears every rope's notices: check that resource is yours.

EventSideArgsWhen
whip_rope:ropeStretchedServerid, resourcePulled past watch.stretch for watch.holdMs, and again every 3 seconds while it stays so: act once. Believed only when the ends really are far apart and the reporting player is near
whip_rope:ropeEndBrokenServerid, which, resourceA map prop that end is tied to was blown up (watch.broken), with an explosion the server saw
whip_rope:ropeRemovedServerid, resource, whywhip_rope removed it (/clearropes): forget the id. Not sent for your own RemoveRope or when your resource stops
whip_rope:pulledFromHandClientid, which, resourceLocked ropes only, on the holder's game: the other end dragged them and they let go, or died. The end stays theirs until your server moves it
-- Client: a locked line pulled from this player's hand
AddEventHandler('whip_rope:pulledFromHand', function(id, which, resource)
    if resource ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then return end
    TriggerServerEvent('mytow:dropLine', id)
end)

-- Server, inside Whip.register: drop it at their feet
Whip.core:SecureEvent('mytow:dropLine', { params = { { 'id', 'id', 1, 2147483647 } } }, function(source, player, id)
    local rope = exports.whip_rope:GetRope(id)
    if not rope or rope.tail.type ~= 'held' or rope.tail.heldBy ~= source then return end   -- theirs to drop
    exports.whip_rope:SetRopeEnd(id, 'tail', { type = 'fixed', pos = GetEntityCoords(GetPlayerPed(source)) })
end)
When whip_rope restarts, your ropes go with it. No notice is sent, and ids start again from 1. Forget yours on its onResourceStop, and make them again on its onResourceStart, as whip_fuel's hoses do.

Learning from whip_autos

whip_autos is Whiplash, the car customisation shop, with turbos and nitrous. This page shows how a shop that takes money for work on a car is built on WHIP; server owners want whip_autos/README.md.

Skip the camera, the 3D page (html/js/view.js, kit.js), the gearbox computer and the stance maths: they teach nothing about WHIP. fxmanifest.lua lists every file and follows Calling whip_core.

The server prices the basket again

The page sends what was picked and the total it showed, never a price. The purchase is a SecureEvent: near keeps it to the shop floor, and onReject replies to the page even when it's refused early, so the pay button never hangs.

-- server/main.lua (trimmed)
exports.whip_core:SecureEvent('whip_autos:server:purchase', {
    rateLimit = 3000, burst = 2,
    near = SHOP_NEAR,   -- its `at` is a function: a /whiplash visit's floor is wherever its car is
    onReject = function(src, why)
        TriggerClientEvent('whip_autos:client:purchaseResult', src, false, tostring(why))
    end,
    params = {
        { 'vehicleId', 'id' },
        { 'method', 'enum', { 'cash', 'bank' } },
        { 'basket', 'list', { { 'slot', 'any' }, { 'index', 'id', -1, 255 } --[[ , ... ]] }, 40 },
        { 'shown', 'int', 0, 1000000000, -1 },
    },
}, onPurchase)

Paid and fitted in one write

The handler prices every line again from the server's Config, drops parts the car already has (ShopFitted), and refuses a total above the one shown. ChargePlayer, called straight inside the SecureEvent, lands in the same transaction as the car's new look, and a failed fit gives the money back (RefundPlayer).

-- server/main.lua, onPurchase (trimmed)
if shown >= 0 and total > shown then   -- a price raised in /whip mid-visit is refused, not charged
    return fail('The prices changed while you were here. Leave and come back to see them.')
end
local receipt
if total > 0 then
    local payErr
    receipt, payErr = exports.whip_core:ChargePlayer(source, total, { method = method, reason = 'Whiplash customisation' })
    if not receipt then return fail(payErr or 'Payment failed') end
end
if not TuningServer.write(vehicleId, tuningChanges, propsFromBasket(lines)) then   -- one SetVehicleAppearance
    if receipt then exports.whip_core:RefundPlayer(receipt) end
    return fail('Something went wrong fitting that')
end

A claim that every exit gives back

Trying parts on changes the real car for everyone near, so the server keeps one session per car and per player. Every way a visit ends puts the stored look back: the page closing, leaving the driver's seat (whip_core:vehicle:exited), playerDropped, whip_autos stopping. The client calls Whip.core:HoldVehicleAppearance(vId, true) so WHIP doesn't report the unpaid preview as the car's look.

Data on a car that every game applies

An engine swap, stance, handling setup and drivetrain aren't GTA mods, so the server writes them as vehicle data. Every game applies them with WatchVehicleData: onGained/onChanged/onLost for every car in view, or driverOnly with onStart/onStop for the driver alone (a handling layer).

-- client/tuning.lua (trimmed), inside Whip.register: the swapped engine's power, on the car this player drives
exports.whip_core:WatchVehicleData(TUNING_ENGINE_KEY, {
    id = 'enginePower', driverOnly = true,
    onStart = function(entity, value)
        local set = TuningEngineSet(value, GetVehicleHandlingFloat(entity, 'CHandlingData', 'fMass'))
        if set then exports.whip_core:SetVehicleHandlingLayer({ entity = entity }, 'engine', { set = set }) end
    end,
    onStop = function() exports.whip_core:ClearVehicleHandlingLayer('engine') end,
})

Two kinds of vehicle stat

The turbo's boost is a live stat (RegisterVehicleStat): the driver's game simulates it, whip_core caps how fast it rises, and the gauge reads it from whileHeld (Watching vehicle stats). Nitrous is a consume stat: the game bills what it burns, and whip_core caps it and clears the bottle when empty. Fitting a bottle is a declared timed use, on the car the server sees the player in (server/power/nitrous.lua).

Who may change a car

Config.WhoCanModify lets anyone work on a car, only the owner for performance and tuning, or only the owner at all (anyone may still repair). One function both sides load decides it. The server asks it at the claim, to hide shelves, and again at payment: hiding a shelf is for the player, the server is the rule.

-- shared/shop.lua
function ShopMayChange(charId, ownerCharId)
    local rule = Config.WhoCanModify
    if rule ~= 'ownerTuning' and rule ~= 'owner' then return 'all' end
    if ownerCharId == nil or ownerCharId == charId then return 'all' end
    if rule == 'owner' then return 'repair' end
    return 'looks'
end

A settings page, and what's worked out from it

shared/settings.lua puts the prices, power and slider ranges on a page in /whip (Whip.configPage), written into Config when saved. A lookup built from Config is rebuilt in place with Whip.onConfigChanged, so every file holding it sees the change.

-- shared/shop.lua
local function buildServices() refill(SHOP_SERVICES, Config.Services, function(t, _, x) t[x.id] = true end) end
buildServices()
Whip.onConfigChanged('Services', buildServices)

A page of its own

The shop is whip_autos' own NUI page. nui_callback_strict_mode 'true' lets only that page call its callbacks (the purchase spends money), and every callback replies, even on an error, or the page's fetch hangs (cb, client/ui.lua). Whip.padScreen gives it a controller and cursor, and SetScreenOpen stands WHIP's HUD down while it's up.

Director cards

whip_autos adds two Whip.cards, a car task and a builder button (tasks and buttons) to the Director; the files are in the table below.
