The Director

The Director builds missions, heists and stories in game from cards, with no code. Your resource can start and steer its runs, hear what they do, ship scenarios, and add cards of its own.

Scenarios, runs and cards

  • Scenario. A job or story: its placed things (NPCs, cars, props, spots, containers) and its cards, wired together in the editor. Every revision is kept, so the one switched on never changes under its players.
  • Card. One step: a line of dialogue, a goal, giving an item, waiting for an event. It goes on through one of its outcomes, along a wire to the next card. Resources can add their own: Cards of your own.
  • Run. One playing of a scenario, for its players. Your code reads it as a DirectorRunView (Runs from a script).
  • Test. A builder's private run from the editor. It changes nothing that lasts.

Scenarios are managed in /whip → Director (the /w menu's Director row opens it too) and built in game, in the world.

Who may build

LevelPermissionMay
Builderdirector.buildSee every scenario; make, edit, test, switch on and off; restore an old revision; stop a run
Director admindirector.adminAll a builder may, and delete scenarios, accept shipped packs, export packs, and give or take Director access
Dungeon Masterdirector.liveDungeon Mode: change the live world until a restart. Neither of the other two includes it, nor does it include them
Full adminwhip.devtoolsAll three, always, and the /director dev commands

Give access per account in /whip → Director → Access: pick a character, and every character on that account has it. A builder who isn't a full admin sees only the Director in /whip; a Dungeon Master sees only its Dungeon Mode page.

Builders see through walls. The world builder's camera goes anywhere. Give Director access only to people you trust.

How a scenario starts

Switching a scenario on makes it available. A run then begins the way its Scenario Enabled card's It starts says:

It startsHow
When it's switched onThe default for a new scenario. A run starts at once with nobody in it, and players join it (below)
Talk to an NPCTalk on a standing NPC. While its runs are full, others see "They're busy right now."
Press somethingAn E prompt, in your words, on a standing prop or a spot (a laptop, a keypad, a job board)
A player comes nearWithin the distance of a placed thing. Once a visit: still there when their run ends, they must leave and come back. One turned away by full runs gets one as soon as a place frees
Use an itemKept unless Used up. Only an item that does nothing else when used (Check refuses one that does); two scenarios can't start with the same item
On a timerEvery so many minutes, the first that long after switching on: one run for every player near a placed thing
From a scriptexports.whip_core:StartScenarioRun(key, source) from another resource (a phone app, a job menu)
By handOnly Start a run: admin-run events

When it's switched on, Scenario Enabled's cards play straight away and what they make (an NPC to talk to, cars, props) is out for everyone. The first player to talk to its NPC (a Dialog Line), press its prompt (Wait for Press, an Interaction Menu) or come near (Player Arrives) joins the run, and that card plays for them. The job starts at Scenario Started By Player (before it nothing counts), or as they join when there's no such card.

When that run ends, however it ended, a fresh one starts a couple of seconds later. One that ended before anyone joined (a Succeed with nobody there) waits until the scenario is switched off and on. Start a run and StartScenarioRun put the player into the waiting run.

With the other choices, a run starts for the player who does it, and Scenario Enabled's cards play then. Test starts one for you at once whatever it says, and anyone with Director access can press Start a run on its page in /whip. Started any other way, a player is never in two runs of the same scenario, and Runs at once and Players this close join apply.

For other resources

The Director tells other resources what its runs do, and its server exports start, read and steer runs. Two rules run through all of it:

  • A builder's Test is private. It sends none of these events, and every export leaves it out unless you pass { tests = true }. A script that pages officers when a heist starts doesn't fire on every Test.
  • You get copies. A run is a DirectorRunView, made when you ask: changing it changes nothing.

A builder fills in settings for you in Settings → For scripts: Kind (a few words, "heist, crime") and Where it happens (a placed thing: the bank, not the job giver) become a run's and a scenario's kinds and where. Scripts may switch it on and off allows SwitchScenario.

Server eventPayload
whip_core:run:started{ run, startedBy = { mode, by } }. mode: interaction · press · area · item · timer · script (by: the resource) · hand · enabled (When it's switched on: the run has nobody in it yet)
whip_core:run:ended{ run, outcome, reason, vars, payout, faultCard, stopping }. outcome: succeeded · failed · calledOff (a Call Off card) · aborted (an admin, the last player leaving, whip_core stopping) · faulted
whip_core:run:playerJoined{ run, source, charId, by }: AddPlayerToScenarioRun
whip_core:run:playerLeft{ run, source, charId, why, by, runEnds }. run is without them; sent before its run:ended; by: the resource that took them out
whip_core:run:signalled{ run, name, data = { value }, source }: a Send Signal card
whip_core:scenario:switchedOn / :switchedOff{ scenario, name, rev, replaced | why, by }. by: { source, name } (a person), { resource } (SwitchScenario) or nil (the server itself)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:run:started', function(e)
    if GetInvokingResource() ~= 'whip_core' then return end
    local run = e.run
    for _, k in ipairs(run.kinds) do
        if k == 'heist' and run.where then
            -- one mark for every on-duty officer, by character (it follows them through a relog)
            local people = {}
            for _, o in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetClockedOnEmployees('police') or {}) do
                people[#people + 1] = { charId = o.charId }
            end
            if #people > 0 then
                -- the run's tag: the mark goes when the run ends
                exports.whip_core:ShowBlip({ people = people }, 'heist:' .. run.id,
                    { coords = run.where.coords, label = 'Alarm: ' .. run.where.label, sprite = 161, color = 1, tag = run.tag })
            end
        end
    end
end)
  • Tag what you make. Anything you make for a run with tag = payload.run.tag (a blip, a point, an NPC, a skill check, a car) goes when the run ends. Anything made with it after that is refused.
  • Check the sender. Any server resource can fire these events. Before paying anything out, check GetInvokingResource() == 'whip_core' (for run:started you can also ask GetScenarioRun; an ended run is gone).
  • Wait for a player. An enabled run starts empty. Wait for run:playerJoined before treating it as a job going on (a heist being reported).
  • Never mid-run. Events are sent just after the Director's scheduler has done its work, so your handler never runs in the middle of a run's cards.

Two cards let a builder work with your script without a card of yours: Send Signal (you hear whip_core:run:signalled) and Wait for Script Event (the run carries on when you call SendDirectorEvent).

On the player's game (a phone's job screen, a HUD), exports.whip_core:GetPlayerScenarioRuns() returns the runs that player is in: { { runId, scenario, name, objective, countdown } }. The local events whip_core:run:joined, :updated (their objective or clock changed), :left and :ended ({ outcome, payout }) say when that changes. Never a Test.

Shipping scenarios in a resource

A resource can bring scenarios as data, with no scripts: one manifest line per file.

-- fxmanifest.lua of your pack
whip_director_scenario 'scenarios/bank_job.json'
whip_director_scenario 'scenarios/drug_run.json'

Each file is a scenario document as the editor saves it ("format": 2, at most 512 KB), with "key" (its key on every server) and "requires": { "items": [...], "models": [...], "resources": [...] }. Its "taskTimes": 2 says a task time of 0 is no end and a give-up of 0 is never; in a document without it, either 0 is a tenth of a second. Things it ships unplaced ("coords": "spot") are placed by each server in a copy. Export as a pack (a Director admin, on a scenario in /whip) writes one in exactly this shape to whip_core/pack_exports/, with its manifest beside it.

  • whip_core reads each file when the resource starts, checks it, and offers it to a Director admin to accept.
  • Accepted, it's a scenario like any other but read-only: Duplicate it to change it. It goes off while its resource is stopped and comes back on with it.
  • Deleted, it's never offered again. A file that changes is offered again; what was accepted stays as it was until then.

To offer scenarios or editor templates from code, use Whip.scenario and Whip.template (Cards of your own).

The Director in /whipServer owners

PageWhat it shows
OverviewNumbers for every scenario, or some, over 7, 14, 30 or 90 days: payouts, runs, successes, why runs fail, the newest runs. Tests left out
ScenariosEvery scenario. Its page has Active (its newest revision; edits made while on go live when you switch it off and on), Previous Versions with Restore, Duplicate, Open Editor, Start a run and Delete
Lore charactersThe people your stories come back to: picture, details, voice lines, where they're used
ShippedScenarios resources bring, and anything this server lacks to run one
Live runsRuns going now, with Stop; scenarios on from a file (/director load)
Access · Dungeon ModeWho has Director access (Director admins only) · what you made in Dungeon Mode, each with Remove

Building a scenarioServer owners

New scenario or Open Editor takes you into the world builder: place its people and things with Place, set each one up with Configure, and open Blueprint for its cards in a window over the world. Fullscreen opens the full editor (Cards, World, Variables and Settings tabs; Save, Test and Check); its ‹ or Esc goes back into the world.

  • Saving. Save writes the world into the scenario and saves it. The world builder also saves every five minutes, unless Auto-save in the world builder is off (World tab). Exit leaves the Director and throws away what you placed or moved since the last Save (it asks first). Other changes not saved stay with the scenario until you open it again.
  • Keys. In the world, R switches between moving and turning, G steps snapping, Ctrl+click selects several. On the grid, right-click adds a card, a drag from a pin draws a wire, C makes a comment box, and the usual Ctrl keys copy, paste, undo and save.
  • Wires. An outcome can have several: every card they lead to starts at the same moment, the first-drawn first.
  • Only once. A switch on every card that does something and goes on: it works the first time a run reaches it, then the run skips it through its first outcome. To stop the run the second time, use First Time Only.
  • Several things on one card. Most cards that name placed things take several, or a group: every NPC or prop whose page gives that Group name, as it is when the scenario plays. Talking cards, goals and cards about one car name one.
  • Watching. A scenario's live runs light each card they enter on the grid; after a test, the test plays back the same way. During a test, the test map's Free camera (H for the mouse first) flies round it, and G hides the test map.

Cards builders useServer owners

CardWhat it does
Dialog LineAn NPC's line with answers. Each answer can have rules: offered only if (an item, cash, a player flag, a variable), a cost, once a run or once ever, and a chance rolled on the server (a miss goes out of Answer N failed)
Sell to NPC · HaggleThe NPC buys an item at a price. Haggle agrees a price and moves no money: wire Deal to Sell to NPC, Pay or Take Item
Goal cardsShow Objective, Show Blip, the wait and Clear Objective in one: Go To, Deliver the Car, Kill Them All, Collect, Bring Item To, Steal the Car, Search, Speak To, Survive
Set Player Flag · If Player FlagRemember something about the player for good (Player flags), and branch on it
Claim Car · Give CarThe run's car made the player's own (ClaimVehicle), or a new car of their own
Fire WeaponA Fixed Weapon (a firearm placed as a prop) fires real shots that hurt, in a Test too
Play on Speakers · Stop SpeakersProps play a song from a Fivemanage link, in step, heard through walls like a voice, until stopped or the run ends (Speakers)
Send Signal · Wait for Script EventTalk to your scripts (For other resources)
Phone Call · Lore SaysA lore character phones a player or speaks (Lore phone calls, Lore characters speak)

Others give items, take money, show objectives and clocks, put up props, open menus and move NPCs. A card that waits on the server gives up out of Took too long.

What a run hands out

In a live run, items are real: what Give Item, Drop Item and Put in Car hand out, a heist's loot and a run car's keys are the player's to keep. A Test marks everything it hands out and takes it back when it ends, from its players and the ground (a test's items).

  • Run tags. An item one of a live run's cards looks for (Item Picked Up, Take Item, Collect, Bring Item To) carries a plain tag naming the run, so the run can tell its own package from anyone else's. Nothing else reads it, and it stays on the item.
  • A Test changes nothing that lasts. Costs, sales, Charge Player, Claim Car and Give Car are only said; flags it sets live on the test run alone; Send Signal sends nothing.

NPCs, cars and propsServer owners

Configure opens a thing's page, with these tabs among others:

  • Outfit. What an NPC wears, part by part. A freemode NPC (mp_m_freemode_01, mp_f_freemode_01) can open the players' character editor instead.
  • Tasks. What an NPC, car or prop does, top to bottom: go somewhere, take cover, shoot, drive, sound a siren, slide. Spawn cards start them (Start its tasks, on by default), or Start Tasks later. Play Tasks previews them on your screen only. A task's time (For, Gives up after) is hours, minutes and seconds, to a tenth. 0 is no end: the task goes on until its list is stopped or the run ends, and a new Shoot At, Aim At, Look At, Wander, Follow, Run Away From, fight, Play Emote, Cruise Around, Follow in a Car or Writhe starts there. A task that does one thing (Throw, Turn To Face, Sound the Horn, Flash the Lights, Brake, Speed Up To, and a prop's Slide To, Turn To and Fade) lasts its time, and its 0 is at once. A task that waits to be done gives up after its time; 0 is never.
  • Takes. Drives you record, up to three minutes, played back exactly by Play Scripted Driving Event, trailers included. Ride along puts the player at the wheel.
  • Eye sight. A guard notices the run's players in its cone, with nothing in between, as a meter fills (by default 2 s up close, 8 s at its full distance; sneaking halves the distance). Then Guard Spots You goes on. The server works out the cone and meter.

Routes (More, Route) are points an NPC walks with its Walk a Route task. Props have Physics on unless switched to static; a static one is made by each player's game (ShowPropSet). Config.ExperimentalDriveSync (off by default) has every game play recorded drives itself, smooth on every screen. /npcdebug shows each NPC's and car's task.

Dungeon ModeServer owners

The world builder with no scenario: what a Dungeon Master (director.live) makes goes into the live world, for everyone, with nothing to save. Open it from /whip → Director → Dungeon Mode → Start Dungeon Mode, or the Dungeon Mode row under Panels in /w (full admins).

  • Put down props, NPCs, cars or a Fixed Weapon (a gun as a prop). Click one of yours to move it, open its Options (an NPC attacks, follows or guards; a Fixed Weapon fires) or Remove it.
  • Click a player for Spawn a car for them (its key in their pocket) and Send NPCs after them, or anything else for the Object Viewer's options.
  • Cars are made unlocked with no key; their Dungeon car options set where the key is, Locked and Only its key opens it.
  • The map's own props, once changed, are hidden on every game until a restart, with Put back on the Dungeon Mode page.

What you make stays until a restart or until you remove it. It's yours by account, so it stays when you log off; only you or a full admin removes it. One account may have 150 things and 20 effects up at once; everyone together, 600 and 80. Everything is logged on the activity log as dungeon_mode.

Nothing that lasts past a restart. A Dungeon Master sees these greyed, Admins only, and the server refuses them: making a car someone's, changing a saved car (put away, delete, owner, stats, repairing a player's own), a player's stats, movement style or character editor, kick and ban, inventories, trunks and gloveboxes, getting into a player's locked car, and changing a ground item. Restore health and Restore armour stay open.

Director runs from a script

Server exports to start, read and steer the Director's runs. Any server script may steer any run, and the history says which did. Events, and the rules every export follows, are under For other resources.

Starting a run

StartScenarioRun(key, who, opts?)SERVER

Starts a run of a switched-on scenario for who (a server id, or { charId } online): a phone app's "take the job". For a scenario whose Settings say A run starts: From a script, or When it's switched on (the player joins its waiting run). The player becomes its starter; Players this close join applies. opts: the next card.

Returns: the run's id, or false, reason (not switched on, not "From a script", already in one, its runs full)
local runId, why = exports.whip_core:StartScenarioRun('bank_job', source)
if not runId then exports.whip_core:NotifyPlayer(source, why, 'error') end
StartScenarioRun(key, who, opts?) · optsSERVER

Crew, variables and places of its own: one scenario, played at today's gang territory.

FieldTypeDescription
withtable?More players, as crew; 16 at most. One who is down, in the character screen or already in a run of it is left out
varstable?Its variables, of the types the scenario declares
placestable?By placed thing, where this run's NPCs, car, items, containers and spots are: { x, y, z, heading } or a vector3 / vector4. Add interior = true inside an MLO. Refused for a Standing thing, a door or a prop
Returns: the run's id, or false, reason (a variable of the wrong type or one it doesn't have, a place it can't take, ...)
local runId, why = exports.whip_core:StartScenarioRun('turf_war', source, {
    with = { partner },
    vars = { reward = 2500, rival = 'Ballas' },
    places = { stash = { x = 102.4, y = -1940.2, z = 20.8, heading = 90 },
               boss  = vector4(-1150.2, -1520.6, 10.6, 35.0) },
})
When it's switched on. For a scenario that starts this way, the player and with join its waiting run: vars and places are refused.
CanStartScenarioRun(key, who)SERVER

StartScenarioRun's checks, starting nothing: switched on, "From a script" (or When it's switched on, its waiting run not taken), on a character and up, not already in one, runs not full. A phone app greys out the jobs a player can't take.

ParamTypeDescription
keystringThe scenario's key
whonumber | { charId }A server id, or an online character
Returns: true, or false, reason

Reading runs and scenarios

GetScenarioRun(runId, opts?) · GetScenarioRuns(filter?)SERVER

A run going now, or all of them, as a DirectorRunView: { id, tag, scenario, name, rev, test, kinds, where, players = { {source, charId, name} }, starter, startedAt, seconds, endsIn, vars, objectives = { {source, text, countdown} }, things = { [placedThingId] = { kind, netId, npcId, vehicleId, ... } } }. Give its tag to what you make for the run (ShowBlip, AddPoint, SpawnNpc's opts): it goes when the run ends.

ParamTypeDescription
filter.scenariostring?Runs of one scenario
filter.playernumber | { charId }?Runs a player is in
filter.kindstring?Runs of scenarios of that Kind (Settings)
filter.tests / opts.testsboolean?Include builders' Tests
Returns: GetScenarioRun: the view, or false, reason. GetScenarioRuns: a list (empty when none)
for _, run in ipairs(exports.whip_core:GetScenarioRuns({ kind = 'heist' })) do
    print(run.name, run.where and run.where.label, #run.players)
end
IsPlayerInScenarioRun(who, key?, opts?) · GetPlayerScenarioRuns(who, opts?)SERVER

Whether a player is in a run now (of that scenario, or any), and which. who: a server id or { charId } (online).

Returns: true | false · a list of DirectorRunViews
if exports.whip_core:IsPlayerInScenarioRun(source, 'bank_job') then
    return false, 'Finish the job you are on first'
end
GetScenarioRunOf(ref, opts?)SERVER

Which run a car, an NPC or a tag belongs to: { netId }, { vehicleId }, { npcId } or { tag }. Is this car a heist's getaway car?

Returns: the run's DirectorRunView, or false, reason (not part of a run going now)
GetScenario(key) · GetScenarios(filter?)SERVER

A scenario as a DirectorScenarioView: { key, name, description, kinds, where, on, rev, draftRev, startMode, source, runs }; GetScenario adds cards (the card types it uses), world (its placed things) and vars. It describes the revision switched on, or the draft when it's off, and never waits. filter: { on, kind, startMode }.

Returns: the view, or false, reason · a list
GetScenarioStats(key)SERVER

How a stored scenario's runs have gone, Tests left out: { runs, succeeded, stopped, lastAt } (stopped: called off, stopped by an admin, cut short). It waits on the database: call it from a thread.

Returns: the numbers, or false, reason
GetDirectorCards(filter?)SERVER

The editor's card types, each with its owner: { type, title, desc, category, inputs, outputs, labels, props, owner }. filter: { category }.

Returns: a list

Steering a run

EndScenarioRun(runId, outcome, reason?)SERVER

Ends a run as a card would: 'succeeded', 'failed' or 'calledOff' (no result, nobody told). The reason gets your resource's name ('the crew was arrested (by police_mdt)') in whip_core:run:ended and the history. The one control call that also takes a builder's Test.

Returns: true, or false, reason
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:EndScenarioRun(runId, 'failed', 'the crew was arrested')
AddPlayerToScenarioRun(runId, who) · RemovePlayerFromScenarioRun(runId, who, why?)SERVER

Puts a player into a run going now as crew, or takes one out. Crew get the run's doors, containers, payouts and items as the starter does, and what its cards gave "the run's players" (prompts, goals, the objective, guards' targets, blips); one taken out loses it all. Both are announced (run:playerJoined / :playerLeft, with by).

Adding is refused for a Test, a player down or with no character, one already in a run of it, and a full run (16). Police responding to a heist aren't crew: reach them with blips.

Returns: true, or false, reason
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:AddPlayerToScenarioRun(runId, friendSource)

CreateThread(function()   -- taking someone out waits
    exports.whip_core:RemovePlayerFromScenarioRun(runId, friendSource, 'left the crew')
end)
RemovePlayerFromScenarioRun waits. It takes back what the run handed them first: call it from a thread.
GetScenarioRunVar(runId, name) · SetScenarioRunVar(runId, name, value)SERVER

Reads or sets a run's variable, of the type the scenario declares (number, text, true/false). The next card that reads it sees your value. Not written into the history.

Returns: Get: true, value (true first: a variable can hold false or nothing), or false, reason. Set: true, or false, reason
local ok, score = exports.whip_core:GetScenarioRunVar(runId, 'score')
if ok then exports.whip_core:SetScenarioRunVar(runId, 'score', (score or 0) + 10) end
SendDirectorEvent(name, payload?, opts?)SERVER

Every Wait for Script Event card waiting for name carries on. name is in your namespace ('police.backupArrived'): the first running resource to send in one has it until it stops; whip_core's (npc., player. ...) are nobody's. payload.source is who it's about, and what follows acts for them (about none of its players: for whoever the card's branch was for). opts.runId: only that run hears it. At most 20 of one event a second, and 60 a second from one resource.

Returns: true, heardBy (how many runs heard it), or false, reason
-- an officer pressed "en route" on the MDT (checked in your own SecureEvent first)
exports.whip_core:SendDirectorEvent('police.backupArrived', { source = robber, unit = 'Adam-12' })
Testing a Wait card. A Test never hears a real script's event. /director send <event> [value] (any builder) puts one into your own Test, about you.
SwitchScenario(key, on, why?)SERVER

Switches a scenario on (true) or off by script: heists only at night. Only one whose Settings say Scripts may switch it on and off, never while a builder tests it, and on only at the revision a person last switched on (never a draft, never one a person switched off). Off calls off its runs, with your reason and resource name. It waits: call it from a thread.

In memory only: a reboot puts back what a person chose, and a person switching it forgets yours. An off while its pack restarts or the server starts is remembered. The switch events and /whip show by = { resource }.

Returns: true, or false, reason
CreateThread(function()
    local wasNight
    while true do
        local hour = exports.whip_core:GetTime()
        local night = hour >= 22 or hour < 5
        if night ~= wasNight then
            exports.whip_core:SwitchScenario('bank_job', night, 'night only')
            wasNight = night
        end
        Wait(60000)
    end
end)

Director: cards of your own

Put cards of your own in the Director's palette, and builders drag them into scenarios like whip_core's own. whip_core gets the card as data and calls your code through @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua, so an error reaches your console in its own words.

A minigame doesn't need a card. Add it as a skill check game and it's a choice in the Skill Check card, with Passed, Missed (out of time, or no answer) and Couldn't start (wire it back to a Wait for Press). whip_phone's seven phone games work this way.

Adding a card

Whip.card(type, def)SERVER

Adds a card, or changes one. type is '<your namespace>.<name>': the first running resource to use a namespace has it, for cards and events. Call it at file scope or in Whip.register: it's sent again whenever whip_core restarts. A refusal is printed with the reason.

FieldTypeDescription
titlestringIts name in the palette
desc, helpstring?One line under it, and the editor's longer help
category, categoryTitle, color, iconstring?Its palette group (default: your namespace) and the group's name; a colour (blue, teal, green, amber, red, violet, slate); an icon
outputsstring[]Its outcomes, one pin each. labels = { sent = 'Sent' } names them; bad lists the ones drawn as going wrong
propstable[]?Its fields, up to 40: { key, kind, label, default?, required?, hint?, unit?, group?, showIf? }. group (30 characters) heads this field and those after it; showIf names a bool field that must be on
props[n].kindstringtext (maxLength, lines 1–6), number or duration (min, max), bool, select (up to 200 options: text, or { value, label }), world (a placed thing; worldKind: 'spot', 'npc'…), item, var, job, players, lore, entries
props[n] of kind entries: button, add, maxstring, string, numberA list one of your Director buttons fills: button its id (kind 'card'), add the words to add one, max 1–12. Each entry is plain data, its text shown on its row
runfunction(card)?Its code; it may wait. Return an outcome, or nothing and answer later with Whip.answerCard
instantboolean?It returns at once and never waits
timeoutnumber?Seconds before Took Too Long (30; the builder can change it)
eventtable?{ name, match = 'player' | 'run' | 'any', once?, filter? } in place of run: it goes on when you send that event
failtable?A Fail Condition, in place of run and outputs: { event, match?, ends?, reason?, filter? }. It watches the whole run; when you send event about one of its players, the run fails for everyone or that player is taken out. ends ('everyone' or 'them') and reason are the defaults of its When it is broken and Why fields; match defaults to 'player'. filter(card, event): true or the words to tell them breaks it
checkfunction(props, doc)?Return a problem for the editor to show, and 'warning' if it doesn't stop a run. doc has the scenario's vars, world ({ id, kind, label } each) and data[worldId] (what your buttons saved)
onEndfunction(callId, why)?It ended without your answer: tidy up what it made
testSaysstring?What a Test says in place of running your code; {message} fills in a field
test'run'?Your code runs in a Test too, with card.test true: keep what it does to card.player
permissionstring?Only people with this permission may add it or change its fields
v, renamednumber?, table?Bumped when its fields change; its old names, { ['old.type'] = { pins = { old = 'new' } } }
once, onceOutboolean?, string?The Only once switch skips it on later visits, through onceOut (default: its first outcome). once = false removes the switch, for a card the run waits at for a player
Returns: true, or false (printed) when def isn't a card
Whip.card('mycafe.callStaff', {
    title = 'Call Staff', color = 'teal',
    desc = 'Tells the café staff on duty, with a message.',
    outputs = { 'sent', 'nobody' }, labels = { sent = 'Sent', nobody = 'Nobody on duty' }, bad = { 'nobody' },
    props = { { key = 'message', kind = 'text', label = 'Message', default = 'A customer is waiting', maxLength = 120 } },
    testSays = 'Would send "{message}" to the staff on duty',
    run = function(card)
        local staff = Whip.core:GetClockedOnEmployees('mycafe')
        if type(staff) ~= 'table' or #staff == 0 then return 'nobody' end
        for _, s in ipairs(staff) do
            if s.source then Whip.core:NotifyPlayer(s.source, card.props.message, 'info') end
        end
        card:record('called', { detail = card.props.message })
        return 'sent'
    end,
})
card: what your run is handedSERVER

A copy of what the card is doing, with methods into whip_core, refused once the card has finished. Give card.tag to what you make for the run: it goes when the run ends.

Field or methodDescription
callId, runId, cardIdThis call, its run, the card. Whip.answerCard takes callId to settle it later: never send it to a player's game
scenario, name, rev, tag, testThe scenario's key, name and revision; the run's tag; true in a Test
player, starter, players, triggerWho the run acts for now, who started it, its players (server ids), what started it
propsThe fields as the builder set them. A world field is the placed thing, { id, kind, label, coords = { x, y, z }, heading } (nil when not placed); a players field a list of server ids
card:var(name) · card:setVar(name, value)The run's variables
card:state() · card:setState(t)This card's own state, kept between its calls
card:place(id) · card:made(id)A placed thing's place, and what the run made for it
card:record(kind, { source?, detail? })A line in the run's history
card:objective(text, { who? }) · card:clearObjective()The objective band. It comes down by itself if the card ends without your answer; when you answer, take it down first
card:clock(seconds, label)A countdown on the band (0 stops it)
card:give(src, item, n, metadata?)Items, as Give Item gives them (a Test takes them back)
card:pay(src, amount, { method?, reason? }) · card:charge(src, amount, { method?, reason? })Money, with the run's protections: in a Test, Pay only says it and Charge charges nothing
card:finish('succeeded' | 'failed' | 'calledOff', reason?)Ends the run
card:log(fmt, …)A console line naming the run and the card
Returns: var, state, place, made: the value, or nil, why. The rest: true, or false, why
Whip.answerCard(callId, outcome, data?)SERVER

Answers a waiting card later: an officer pressing E at the place, a phone reply. outcome is one of the card's own; data.source is which of the run's players what follows acts for. Only the card's own resource may answer.

Returns: true, or false, reason (no longer waiting, or not one of its outcomes)
Whip.answerCard(callId, 'responded', { source = officer })
A wrong outcome doesn't retry. One the card lacks (a typo, 'timeout') ends it as Didn't Work, or stops the run if nothing is wired there.
Whip.removeCard(type) · Whip.scenario(key, doc) · Whip.template(name, doc)SERVER

Whip.removeCard takes one of your cards away (all go when your resource stops). Whip.scenario offers a scenario built in code to the Director admins: pending until one accepts it (unless they trust your resource), then read-only. Whip.template adds a starting point to the editor's New list. doc is a scenario document as the editor saves it; both are sent again when whip_core restarts.

Returns: removeCard: true, or false, reason. scenario, template: nothing (a refusal is printed)

Testing without the editor

Both run as a builder's Test: Give's items go back at the end, Pay and Charge only say it, and no script hears of the run. Both wait: call them from a thread.

TestDirectorCard(type, props?, opts)SERVER

Runs one of your cards once for a player, until it has an outcome, with card.test true.

ParamTypeDescription
typestringOne of your own cards
propstable?Its fields; a place field takes { x, y, z, heading? }
opts.playernumberWhose test run it is (required)
opts.secondsnumber?How long to wait, 1 to 120 (default: its Give up after, and 5 more)
opts.eventtable?An event card's payload, as SendDirectorEvent's
Returns: { outcome, data } ('timeout' when time ran out), or false, reason (Check's first problem, it failed, no answer in time)
CreateThread(function()
    local result, why = Whip.core:TestDirectorCard('mycafe.callStaff', { message = 'Test call' }, { player = source })
    print(result and result.outcome or why)
end)
TestDirectorScenario(doc, opts) · SteerDirectorTest(runId, op, ...) · GetDirectorTestResult(runId)SERVER

Runs a whole scenario document once as a Test for a player, until it ends, steering it as the test map does. It must pass Check (one that can never succeed is tested anyway). One per player at a time, three of yours at a time.

ParamTypeDescription
doctableA scenario document, as the editor saves it
opts.playernumberWhose test run it is (required, on a character)
opts.secondsnumber?1 to 600 (default 60): still going then, it's ended (late)
opts.varstable?{ name = value }, set before its first card
opts.steertable?Done in order: { op = 'take', node, pin } and { op = 'say', node, option, amount? } once their card waits; 'event', 'emit' and 'var' at once or once their when card waits; { op = 'end' }; { op = 'wait', ms }
opts.waitboolean?false: return at once, and steer it as it goes

SteerDirectorTest does one op now: 'take', nodeId, pin; 'say', nodeId, option, amount?; 'event', name, payload? (a script's event); 'emit', name, payload? (a Director event, to this run alone); 'var', name, value; 'end', outcome?, reason?. GetDirectorTestResult reads one of yours, kept ten minutes after its end.

Returns: { runId, status, reason, vars, steps, fired, entered, waiting, things, done, late } (fired[card][outcome] counts each way it went), or false, reason. SteerDirectorTest: true, or false, reason
CreateThread(function()
    local r = exports.whip_core:TestDirectorScenario(doc, { player = source, steer = {
        { op = 'say', node = 'offer', option = 'opt1' },   -- answer 1 of the Dialog Line 'offer'
    } })
    print(r and r.status, r and r.reason)
end)

Director: tasks and buttons of your own

Besides cards, your resource can add tasks to the Tasks list of NPCs and cars, buttons on placed things, and add-on weapons to every weapon list. They use your cards' namespace, and go away when your resource stops.

A button can keep data on a thing, saved with the scenario, and a run hands it back when it makes the thing. A tuning resource, say, adds a Customise button that saves paint and parts on a placed car, and applies them when it hears whip_core:run:thingMade.

Tasks

Whip.task(type, def)SERVER CLIENT

Adds a task, or changes one. Call it once, in a file both sides load: every game keeps your run, which plays the step on the game that owns the NPC or car. The world builder's Play here runs it on its own copy, with info.preview set.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringIts name in the + Task picker (40 letters at most)
descstring?One line about what it does
groupstring?The picker's group: move, look, fight, act, car, body, wait, or your own, named by groupTitle (default: your namespace)
kindsstring[]Who can do it: 'npc', 'vehicle'. A prop's tasks are whip_core's only
timingstring?'instant' (done once started), 'timed' (lasts sec seconds: the default), 'until' (until done, giving up after giveUp seconds), 'either' (the builder picks; next = 'done' or 'time' is the default)
secnumber?A timed step's seconds (3), up to 86399; 0 is no end: it lasts until its list is stopped. The builder can change it
giveUpnumber?An until step's limit in seconds (30), up to 86399; 0 is never: it waits until it's done. The builder can change it
lastingboolean?It keeps going after its slot: a Wait after it keeps the thing at it
onceboolean?A new owner never plays it again (it would happen twice: a line of speech, a throw)
standingboolean?false: a standing NPC passes it over (it needs a run)
fieldstable[]?Up to 8, each { key, kind, label, hint?, default?, required? }. Kinds: number (min, max, unit; slider = true with a step needs min and max), bool, select (1 to 200 options; look = 'seg' shows 2 to 4 as buttons), text (max), world (a placed thing; worldKind limits it), point (key 'at'), target (key 'target': the nearest player, who set the card off, a placed thing or a point)
runfunctionrun(entity, args, info), on the game that owns the thing, in a thread of its own (it may wait). In args, a world field is that thing's entity on this game (nil when it isn't here), a target { kind, entity, coords }, a point { x, y, z, heading }. info: { type, kind, timing, ms, preview }, ms being the step's time (a week for a step with no end)
donefunction?An until step's check, asked every quarter second: true done, 'failed' failed, anything else not yet. Without it, the step is done when run returns (false or an error: failed)
Returns: true, or false when it isn't a task (printed). whip_core's own answer is printed when it refuses one. Whip.removeTask(type) takes one away on the side it's called on.
-- shared/director.lua, in shared_scripts
Whip.task('mycafe.flash', {
    label = 'Flash the Lights', group = 'car', kinds = { 'vehicle' }, timing = 'timed', sec = 4,
    fields = { { key = 'times', kind = 'number', label = 'Times', min = 1, max = 20, default = 5 } },
    run = function(car, args)
        for _ = 1, args.times do
            SetVehicleLights(car, 2) Wait(200)
            SetVehicleLights(car, 1) Wait(200)
        end
        SetVehicleLights(car, 0)
    end,
})
The owner can change mid-step. The game that owns the thing changes as players move about, and the new owner runs a timed or lasting step again from its start. Keep run to what the entity itself does.

Buttons and their data

Whip.directorButton(id, def)CLIENT

Adds a button for a kind of placed thing, or changes one: under Tools on the thing's page, under the world builder's bubble, or both. Pressed, your press runs on that player's game, in a thread of its own. A thing not in the scenario yet is added first, as Configure does.

FieldTypeDescription
labelstringThe button's text (24 letters at most)
kindsstring[]Which placed things have it: npc, vehicle, prop, spot, groundItem, container, door, route
wherestring?'page', 'bubble' or 'both' (the default)
takesOverboolean?The Director steps aside first (the page hides, the mouse is let go) until you call thing:back(), your code throws, or your resource stops; then the world builder opens on the thing again
iconstring?One of WHIP's icons by its key, as AddAction's ('turbo', 'lock')
hintstring?Its tooltip
pressfunctionpress(thing): thing is { id, kind, label, model, models, coords, scenario, data, entity, builder }. data is what you keep on it; entity the world builder's copy while it's open (never for a button that takes over); builder whether it was pressed there
  • thing:save(t) keeps t on the thing: plain data, 4 KB of JSON at most; nil takes it away. It's an edit like any other, so Save keeps it and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
  • thing:back(t?) hands the screen back after a button that takes over, keeping t first when given.
  • A random vehicle has models, every model a run picks from, and is pressed for one of them: model.
  • A button for kind 'card' fills your card's entries field. Its thing is the card, with card = { type, field, entry, value, props, world } (entry nil for a new one), and thing:save(t) keeps t as that entry.
Returns: true, or false when it isn't a button (printed). Whip.removeDirectorButton(id) takes one away. thing:save and thing:back: true, or false, reason
-- client.lua
Whip.directorButton('mycafe.customise', {
    label = 'Customise', icon = 'turbo', kinds = { 'vehicle' }, takesOver = true,
    press = function(thing)
        local paint = OpenMyTuningScreen(thing.model, thing.coords, thing.data)   -- yours; waits until it closes
        thing:back(paint and { paint = paint } or nil)
    end,
})
GetDirectorThingData(where, worldId)SERVER

A copy of what your buttons saved on a placed thing. where is a run's id (that run's revision) or a scenario's key (the revision on now). A card reads it with card:made(id).data.

whip_core:run:thingMade brings it too, each time a run makes something for a placed thing: { run, world, kind, label, netId, npcId, vehicleId, containerId, groundId, doorId, data }, with yours in data[GetCurrentResourceName()]. An Always present thing fires it when the scenario is switched on (or a Test starts), with no run: { scenario, standing = true, test, world, kind, ... }. netId may be nil for a moment after a car is made.

Returns: a table, nil (nothing saved), or false, reason (no such run, scenario or thing)
AddEventHandler('whip_core:run:thingMade', function(e)
    if GetInvokingResource() ~= 'whip_core' then return end
    local mine = e.data[GetCurrentResourceName()]
    if e.kind == 'vehicle' and mine and mine.paint then PaintRunCar(e.vehicleId, mine.paint) end   -- yours
end)
It fires in a builder's Test too, so a Test shows how a thing comes out (Whiplash's look on a car). Check run.test if yours mustn't act on one.

Weapons

Whip.weapons(list, opts)SERVER CLIENT

Offers your add-on weapons (the WEAPON_* names in your weapons.meta) beside GTA's wherever WHIP lists weapons: an NPC's Weapon, the Hold a Weapon task, the world builder (a firearm with a world model can be a Fixed Weapon), Dungeon Mode, the Object Viewer. Each shows your tag: Pump Shotgun (gunny).

Call it once, in a file both sides load: the server's list decides what Check and a run accept, each game's what its editor offers. Calling it again replaces your list.

FieldTypeDescription
list[n].namestringWEAPON_ and capitals, digits or _ (64 at most); never GTA's own
list[n].labelstringIts name in the lists (40 letters at most)
list[n].groupstringpistol, smg, rifle, machine gun, shotgun, sniper, heavy, thrown, stun gun or melee
list[n].modelstring?A firearm's world model (its <Model>), so it can be a Fixed Weapon; never GTA's
opts.tagstring?What shows after each label (16 letters at most). Default: your resource's name
Returns: true, or false when it isn't a list (printed). When whip_core refuses one, its answer is printed and none of the list is added. Whip.removeWeapons() takes yours away on the side it's called on.
-- config/weapon_catalog.lua, in shared_scripts
Whip.weapons({
    { name = 'WEAPON_MY_PUMP', label = 'Pump Shotgun', group = 'shotgun', model = 'w_sg_my_pump' },
    { name = 'WEAPON_MY_KNIFE', label = 'Knife', group = 'melee' },
}, { tag = 'mine' })

A scenario using one of your weapons waits at server start until your resource adds it. An NPC given one carries the gun itself, never your item, so your ammo and reload code isn't on it.

Object Viewer options

Whip.objectViewerOption(id, def)CLIENT

An option of yours in the Object Viewer's list (the /w developer tool: G on what it has picked out opens its options), for the kinds you name. whip = true shows it for WHIP's own things only (a saved car, a player), false for the game's only (a street car, an NPC walking by), left out for both. id is '<your namespace>.<name>'; every field is in the full reference.

Returns: true, or false (printed). tint: blue, teal, green, amber, red, violet or slate. Whip.removeObjectViewerOption(id) takes one away; it goes when your resource stops
Check on the server. It shows to people with dev tools on, but anything select asks of your server must check for itself (HasDevTools).

Voice: keys, items, settings

whip_voice is WHIP's 3D voice chat. This page covers its keys, items, commands and settings; setup is under Setting up whip_voice, and your resource's calls under Voice for other resources.

Players hear the people near them in 3D: muffled through walls and doors, heard from the doorway or window between them, and different in cars and underwater. Outdoors, sound bends round what is in the way (over a low wall, round a building's corner, through a yard's gateway) and is heard from where it comes round, more muffled the sharper the bend: a post hardly at all, a right-angle corner about 6 dB, a building with no way round a lot. Music, such as a speaker's, comes round corners by two ways at once, so walking past a row of alleys it fades from one gap to the next rather than jumping. A phone call carries the phone's sound, and on speaker it works both ways. The radio is clear up close, then breaks up with static and fades out by its range. The server decides who hears whom, so a modified game can't listen in. whip_phone's calls, the radio, megaphone and speaker items, the HUD's voice light and your resources all go through it.

Keys

KeyBindingDoes
NVoice: push to talkTalk to the people near you. The HUD's voice circle lights blue
Caps LockVoice: radio push to talkTalk on your radio while it's on (the circle goes orange). The people next to you still hear you
ZCycle Voice RangeWhisper (3 m), normal (8 m), shout (20 m): whip_core's key
LB + A · LB + XA controller's talk and radioHeld, as the keys. Players move them on the pause menu's Controller screen

Players rebind them in Settings > Key Bindings > FiveM.

Items

whip_voice registers these. Give them like any item: Whip.core:AddItem(source, 'radio', 1).

  • megaphone: held up, your voice carries 6 times as far and sounds like a bullhorn. Use it again to put it away; it also goes down if you get in a car, draw a weapon, drop it or die.
  • radio: a 3D handheld radio in the bottom right, worked with the mouse (or a controller: its buttons show beside it). The right knob is power and volume; the middle knob is the channel, 100 to 999, which is the frequency. Everyone on the same frequency hears you on Caps Lock: clear up to 500 m, then cutting out with static, gone by 1.5 km. Esc puts it away and it keeps working; it turns off if you lose the radio. While you're down you still hear it but can't talk on it, open it or change it.
  • Radio on speaker: the grey button on top. The people near you hear your radio too, from where you stand, but not louder for you. Someone on the same frequency hears it on their own radio only, never twice.
  • speaker: put down anywhere, or on a car, it plays a song for everyone around. A prompt behind it picks the song and has Play, Stop, Volume and Range.

Commands

CommandWhoDoes
/voicecheckdeveloper mode, consoleChecks the voice system, the voice server (and Windows Firewall, for the built-in one) and every player's game, and says what to fix (Setting up whip_voice)
/voicestatusdeveloper mode, consoleThe voice address, the room, and each player connected, with how many voices they hear
/voicevolume 0-200everyoneHow loud the people around you are (100 normal, 0 mutes them). Kept on your PC
/voicedebugdeveloper modeWhat each voice goes through (muffled by what, heard from which doorway), and every door and window of the building you're in

Each player also sets Voice volume, Phone call volume (the phone's Settings > Sounds > Call volume too), Radio volume and Background noise suppression in the pause menu's Settings (Server → Chat & voice), kept on their PC. Noise suppression changes at once, with a moment's silence.

SettingsServer owners

In whip_voice/config.lua:

SettingDefaultChanges
Config.Ranges3 / 8 / 20How far whisper, normal and shout carry, in metres
Config.FullVolumeWithin1.0Full volume only this close; from there a voice fades steadily to silence at the edge of its range
Config.SideSeparation6dB quieter in the far ear, on top of the 3D: 0 the 3D alone, 12 strong
Config.Environment.headphone3DtrueFull 3D made for headphones. false for plain panning, if voices sound hollow
Config.MaxVoices100The most voices one player is connected to at once (the nearest)
Config.Megaphone.rangeMultiplier6How many times further a megaphone voice carries
Config.Megaphone.carMuffle4dB a closed car takes off a megaphone voice (a normal voice: Config.Muffle.car, 9)
Config.SpeakerFivemanage links, 100 %, 30 m (up to 300), 3 each, seen from 300 mThe speaker item: the links it plays, a new one's volume and range, the furthest a player may set it, how many one character may have out (64 on the server), and how far away it's seen (drawDistance)
Config.RadioCaps Lock, 500 / 1500 m, 100-999The radio's key, how far it's clear, how far it reaches, its frequencies
Config.Radio.staticVolume0.06Static in the gaps of a weak radio voice (0 none, 1 very loud)
Config.Radio.distortion1.0How garbled a weak radio voice gets (0 clean, 1.5 the most)
Config.Radio.speakerRange8How far, in metres, people hear a radio on speaker
Config.Radio.uiSoundstrueThe radio's key and power beeps. The talk and roger beeps stay either way
Config.Quality.bitrateKbps64Voice quality (Discord uses 64)
Config.Quality.noiseSuppressiontrueNoise suppression for players who haven't chosen
Config.CrowdQuality40 → 40 kbps, 80 → 24 kbpsVoices heard by big crowds send less, so a crowd doesn't swamp the voice server
Config.Quality.silentWhenQuietfalseSend nothing while the key is up: saves a little in huge crowds, but each press's first word comes ~30 ms later

Setting up whip_voice

whip_voice runs its own voice server (LiveKit) on the same machine as your FiveM server: one line in server.cfg and the voice ports open, and it works. The full guide, with every message explained, is whip_voice/docs/SETUP.md; the short version is whip_voice/README.md.

The permission lineServer owners

FXServer lets a resource start a program only with this line, above ensure whip_voice; WHIP's txAdmin recipe writes it. whip_voice uses it for the voice server and the voice bot, and Windows' tar and PowerShell to unpack them and read the firewall. Without it, the console says so.

add_unsafe_child_process_permission whip_voice
ensure whip_voice

The voice portsServer owners

UDP 7882 to 7893   voices
TCP 7881           voices, when a player's network blocks UDP
  • Windows Firewall. Click Allow when Windows asks about livekit-server.exe (on a server, tick Public networks too), or run whip_voice\service\Open voice ports.bat, which also lifts the block if someone clicked Cancel.
  • Your host's firewall or your router. Allow or forward the ports as you did 30120.
  • Linux with ufw: ufw allow 7882:7893/udp and ufw allow 7881/tcp.

Only the voices use these ports: the signalling goes through your FiveM server's own connection with each player. On rented hosting that can't open them, use a voice server of your own.

Checking itServer owners

The first start downloads LiveKit (about 20 MB) into whip_voice\bin, then the voice bot (about 100 MB) in the background; voice works meanwhile. /voicecheck in game (developer mode) or voicecheck in the console checks the voice server, Windows Firewall, every player's game and the voice bot, and says what to fix, top to bottom. voicestatus lists who is connected.

Can hear but not talk? FiveM asks each player to allow the microphone on their first join, and its box takes the mouse only with the F8 console open.

Ports, a fixed public IP and the voice bot are optional set lines in server.cfg (whip_voice_udp, whip_voice_tcp, whip_voice_ip, whip_voice_api, whip_voice_bot, whip_voicebot_url); SETUP.md lists them, and how to run two FiveM servers on one machine.

Your own voice serverServer owners

Instead of the built-in one: LiveKit on another machine, behind a domain name, or LiveKit Cloud. With whip_voice_url set (wss:// with a valid certificate), the built-in voice server stays off and needs no permission line. Use plain set, never setr: it would send the secret to every player.

set whip_voice_url    "wss://your-project.livekit.cloud"
set whip_voice_key    "API..."
set whip_voice_secret "..."
set whip_voice_api    "https://your-project.livekit.cloud"   # where this FiveM server reaches its API

The voice bot is then yours to run (whip_voice\service\voicebot, with whip_voicebot_url and whip_voicebot_token). On a Windows server, whip_voice\service\Setup voice server.bat installs LiveKit, Caddy (HTTPS with a free certificate) and the voice bot as services and writes the lines into server.cfg. SETUP.md walks through it.

Lore phone calls

A lore character (one of the Director's named NPCs) phones a player, and a recorded line plays into the call as them talking. It needs whip_voice and its voice bot (Setting up whip_voice).

1. Record the lineServer owners

Any recorder works. Save it as mp3, ogg or wav, up to 2 minutes and 15 MB (a minute of mp3 is about 1 MB).

2. Put it where the voice bot can reach itServer owners

WhereHowName it as
FivemanageDashboard → Storage → Upload. Tick Retention Exempt (else Fivemanage can delete it after a set time), upload, and copy the file's link. Anyone with the link can listenhttps://r2.fivemanage.com/abc123/irwin-intro.mp3
A resource of yoursPut the file in it and ensure the resource. Don't list it in files {}: the voice bot reads it on the server, and players never download it. This is how a story ships its voice lines@my_story/audio/irwin_intro.ogg

3. Hear itServer owners

With a lore character (/whip → Director → Lore characters), a phone with a SIM on you and dev tools on (/w):

/lorecall https://r2.fivemanage.com/abc123/irwin-intro.mp3
/lorecall @my_story/audio/irwin_intro.ogg mags      -- from the lore character whose key is mags

Your phone rings from their number. Answer: the line plays, they hang up, and chat says how it went.

4. In a scenarioServer owners

Add a Phone Call card (the green Lore group): From (the lore character; empty is the scenario's own), Recording (the link or @ name) and To (the players). It goes on by how the call went:

OutcomeWhen
Heard it allThey answered and heard it to the end
Hung up earlyThey hung up while it played
Declined · MissedThey declined it, or it rang out
Busy · No phoneAlready on a call, or no phone with a SIM on them
Didn't workIt couldn't ring at all; the run's log says why

Several players each get their own call, and the card goes on by the best outcome. In a Test it runs for real, but rings only you.

The caller's picture. In Lore characters, press Edit picture, paste a Fivemanage picture link, frame it and Save. It shows on the call screen and in Contacts, Messages and Recents. Accepted sites are Picture links accepted in /whip → Settings → Config → Server.

When it doesn't play

It saysDo
only links starting with https://r2.fivemanage.com/ are acceptedUse a Fivemanage link or an @ name. For another site, add its start to Config.VoiceBot.audioLinks in whip_voice's config.lua (with your own voice server, the bot's config.json)
the recording is over 120 seconds · over 15 MBShorten it, or save it as mp3
there is no irwin_intro.ogg · the resource my_story is not startedCheck the path inside the resource, and that the resource is ensured
You need a phone with a SIM on youThe call rings the phone you carry
needs whip_voice and its voice botwhip_voice isn't started, or its voice bot isn't set up (/voicecheck checks the bot)

Lore characters speak

A lore character says recorded lines out loud from its NPC, heard like a player's voice by the players near it, its mouth moving. It greets players, says goodbye, and reacts when bumped or threatened. It needs whip_voice and its voice bot, like Lore phone calls.

1. Give it linesServer owners

  1. Upload each recording as for a phone call.
  2. In /whip → Director → Lore characters, pick the character and open its Audio tab.
  3. Press + Variant on a line, paste the recording's link, and add a subtitle if you like. Add as many variants as you want: it takes them in turn, never the same twice running.
  4. Play hears one as it will sound. Then Save.
LineWhen it says it
HelloA player walks up (Hello when this close, 4 m). Once, until they've walked off and Greet again after (3 minutes) has passed
GoodbyeA player it met walks away (Goodbye when this far, 10 m)
React positive · React negativeA Lore Says card or a script asks: something went its way, or didn't
Bumped into · Hit by a car · Gun aimed at it · Gunfire nearby · Its car stolenA player does it. The same reaction again only after Same reaction again after (6 s); a reaction cuts in on whatever it was saying

A line with no variant isn't said. Its NPC must be in the world: a scenario NPC whose Lore character picker names it, standing or spawned by a card. A subtitle shows over its head as each player starts hearing the line (at once for a player too far to hear it).

2. In a scenarioServer owners

  • Lore Says (the green Lore group): Who (empty is the scenario's own), Line, and Wait until it has been said. It goes on by done or failed (no NPC in the world, no such line, or no voice bot; the run's log says why).
  • Play Custom Voice Line, for a line one scenario needs: Who, a Recording link (the same links accepted), an optional Subtitle, If it is already talking (say it after, the default; cut in; or skip it) and Wait until it has been said. It goes on by Said, Could not or Took too long.
  • Bonus range (both cards, 0 to 250 m): for a line said from a car ahead or across a yard. The character is heard at full volume that much further out, fading over the usual distance past it, and its subtitle is seen as far. It waits a second first, so players now in reach hear it from the start. The next line is back to normal.
  • Through a megaphone (both cards): its NPC holds one up as a player does, and the line carries further with the bullhorn sound. On the radio says it on a frequency as well as out loud: On the player's frequency (the one the radio of the player the card acts for is on; with their radio off it's said out loud only, and the run's log says so) or On a frequency (100 to 999). Everyone on that frequency hears it as a player's radio, breaking up with distance, while its NPC holds a radio to its mouth. Both last for that line only. The radio needs the voice bot from whip_voice 1.4.0 or newer.

3. The settingsServer owners

/whip → Settings → Config → Emotes, /me and talk has Lore characters speak (on/off) and Voice line links accepted (Fivemanage by default). The voice range (15 m) and the Hello, Goodbye and reaction timings are Config.LoreVoice in config.lua.

4. From your own resource

LoreSay(key, line, opts)SERVER

A lore character says one of its voice lines from its NPC, as the Lore Says card does. opts = { near = source, npcId, wait, busy, bonus, megaphone, radio }: near picks its NPC nearest that player (else npcId, else the first); wait = true returns once it's been said; busy ('skip', 'queue', 'cut') overrides the line's If talking; bonus is its Bonus range in metres; megaphone = true says it through a megaphone; radio is a frequency to say it on too, a whole number (whip_voice's GetPlayerRadio(source) gives a player's; one that isn't whole is refused, and one whip_voice won't take is said out loud only, with no radio in its hand, and named in the console). It waits while the recording is fetched: call it from a thread or a handler.

Returns: true (or true, 'queued'), or false, why: no such character, no NPC of it in the world, no such line, no voice bot. With wait, also when whip_voice stopped or the NPC went before it was said
local ok, why = exports.whip_core:LoreSay('irwin', 'positive', { near = source })
CheckPicture(url, frame)SERVER

Checks a profile picture as WHIP takes one, for a resource that keeps its own (whip_phone's contact card). The link must be on the accepted sites (Picture links accepted); an empty link is no picture. frame is { x, y, z } as Edit picture makes it: the middle, 0 to 100 across and down, and the zoom, 1 to 3. It comes back cleaned; the plain framing (the middle, no zoom) is none.

Returns: true, frame (frame nil for none, and for an empty link), or false, why

Speakers

A scenario's props play a song in the world: speakers on every wall of a gang's hideout as the players storm it, or a stack each side of a stage. Everyone near hears it from each speaker, in step, through walls and doorways as a voice carries. It needs whip_voice and its voice bot (1.5.0 or newer), which plays the song; players never download it.

More speakers add up as real ones do: two are a little louder than one, not twice as loud. Far off, the song is heard later and duller, and a speaker on a moving car rises and falls in pitch as it passes.

1. Place the speakersServer owners

Any prop placed on the World tab (+ Prop) can be one: prop_speaker_06, a boombox, a radio on a shelf. Give the ones that play together the same Group, and one card can name them all. A speaker attached to a car or an NPC plays from it as it moves.

2. Play a songServer owners

Upload the song to Fivemanage, as for a lore phone call, and add a Play on Speakers card (the World group):

SettingDoes
SpeakersThe props that play it, or a group (up to 32)
Song linkIts Fivemanage link: mp3, ogg or wav, up to 10 minutes. The play button beside it plays it to you
LoopOn: over and over until Stop Speakers or the run's end. Off: once
Volume0 to 200 %
Heard up toHow far from each speaker it carries (5 to 300 m)
Full volume withinFull volume this close to a speaker
Speaker sound0 % is clear. Higher sounds more like a cheap speaker: less bass and treble, a honk in the middle, grit when pushed. 100 % is tinny
ToneOn: Bass, Mids and Treble, each -12 to +12 dB
Fade inSeconds from silence to full
Wait until it has playedWith Loop off, the card goes on when the song ends instead of as it starts

It goes on by Done, Could not (no speakers, a link that isn't accepted, or no voice bot; the run's log says why) or Took too long. A speaker plays one song at a time: a new one stops the one playing there.

3. Stop itServer owners

Stop Speakers stops what its speakers play, over its Fade out (0 to 30 s; 0 is at once). Every song a run plays stops when the run ends.

Voice for other resources

Your resource can use voice (a call, an intercom, a dispatch channel, a bugged room) without knowing which voice system runs. Never call one by name: Whip.voice, in @whip_core/lib/satellite.lua, calls whichever is running.

A line is a set of players who hear each other wherever they are, through a sound you choose: with their talk key (a 'voice' line) or the radio key ('radio'). The people around them still hear them. A line is yours, and closes when your resource stops. Everything here is server side, except asking which voice system runs. Recordings played on a line or from an NPC are in whip_voice/docs/LINES.md.

Lines

Whip.voice(name, …) · Whip.voiceSystem()SERVER CLIENT

Whip.voice calls one of the running voice system's exports (below) and returns what it returns, or false, 'no voice system is running'. Whip.voiceSystem() returns which voice system runs (GetVoiceSystem's result), or false.

Returns: the export's result, or false, reason
local lineId, why = Whip.voice('OpenLine', { members = { visitor, guard } })   -- an intercom
if not lineId then return false, why end
OpenLine(spec)SERVER

Opens a line: Whip.voice('OpenLine', spec). Members are players with a character loaded; one not in voice yet is linked once they are.

FieldTypeDescription
membersnumber[]Server ids, at most 32. More later with AddLineMember
trackstring?'voice' (default: the talk key) or 'radio' (the radio key)
recipetable|string?How it sounds at the far end: a list of sound blocks, or a name from RegisterSound. None: the plain voice
speakerRangenumber?1-30 m (default 8): how far a member's device on speaker carries
pickupboolean?On speaker, the people near the device are heard on the line too, where the voice system has the pickup feature (whip_voice does)
qualitytable?{ clear = metres, range = metres }: worse with distance, gone past range
sameWorldboolean?Only members in the same routing bucket hear each other
minMembersnumber?Fewer members than this (default 2) and the line closes by itself
onEndfunction?(lineId, why): the line closed by itself ('empty'). Not called when you close it
onLeavefunction?(lineId, src, why): a member went ('left', 'logout', 'removed')
Returns: the line's id (yours to keep), or false, reason
-- A call between two players, sounding like a phone. With minMembers 2 it closes
-- by itself when either leaves or logs out.
local lineId, why = Whip.voice('OpenLine', {
    members = { caller, callee }, pickup = true, minMembers = 2,
    recipe  = { { 'band', low = 300, high = 3400 }, { 'compress', threshold = -24, ratio = 4 } },
    onEnd   = function(id, reason) print(('call %s over: %s'):format(id, reason)) end,
})
The other line callsSERVER

All through Whip.voice, and only on your own lines.

CallDoes
CloseLine(lineId)Everyone on it lets go at once. A line already closed returns true
AddLineMember(lineId, src) · RemoveLineMember(lineId, src)Puts a player on it, or takes one off
SetLineSpeaker(lineId, src, on)That member's device plays the line out loud to the people near it
SetLineMuted(lineId, src, on)The line stops hearing that member. The people near them still do
SetLineRecipe(lineId, recipe)A new sound for the line
GetLine(lineId){ id, track, members = { [src] = { speaker, muted } }, pickup, sameWorld, speakerRange, minMembers }
RegisterSound(name, recipe)Keeps a recipe under a name (letters, digits, -, _) for recipe = name. Returns its full name, '<your_resource>:<name>'
IsVoiceReady(src)Whether that player is connected to voice
Returns: true (GetLine: the table; RegisterSound: the name), or false, reason
Whip.voice('SetLineSpeaker', lineId, callee, true)   -- the callee's phone on speaker
Whip.voice('SetLineMuted', lineId, caller, true)     -- the far side stops hearing the caller
Whip.voice('CloseLine', lineId)                         -- hang up

Sound recipes

A recipe is a list of blocks, in order, each with its settings: { { 'band', low = 300, high = 3400 }, { 'drive', k = 1.5 } }. It's data, never code, checked before it plays: a setting left out takes its default, a number out of range is brought into it, and an unknown block is refused. At most 24 blocks, 4 of them ones that make sound of their own (noise, breakup, radio, hum, chorus, vibrato, tremolo, ringmod, reverb). whip_voice plays every block.

BlockSettings (default)Does
gaindb (0)Louder or quieter
lowpass · highpasshz (3000 · 300), q (0.7)Cuts the highs above, or the lows below, hz
bandpass · notchhz (1200 · 1000), q (0.7)Only a band around hz, or that band taken out
bandlow (300), high (3400), qKeeps low to high: a telephone
peak · lowshelf · highshelfhz, db (0), qBoosts or cuts a band, the lows, or the highs
drivek (2.5), oversampleSoft clipping: grit, harder the bigger k
crushsteps (32)A digital edge
compressthreshold (-24), ratio (4), knee, attack, releaseLoud and quiet squeezed together, like a phone line
noisekind (white, pink, brown), level (0.02), hz, qA hiss under the voice, only while they talk
humhz (50), level (0.02)A mains hum under the voice, only while they talk
breakupstatic (0.06)Drops out more the weaker the line (its quality), with static in the gaps
beepsup, down, down2 (Hz), levelA beep as they start and stop talking
panto (-1 left to 1 right)Towards one ear
echo · reverbtime, feedback, mix · size, mixRepeats, or a room around the device
chorus · vibrato · tremolorate, depth (mix)A wavering copy, a wavering pitch, a pulsing loudness
ringmodhz (50), mix (1)A robot
radiostatic (0.06), distortion (1)whip_voice's walkie-talkie, breaking up with distance

Voice systems

GetVoiceSystem()SERVER CLIENT

Which voice system runs, or false when none does. Offer only what its features say it can do. On the client, the local event whip_core:voice:systemChanged ({ resource, label, features }, all nil when none runs) says when it changes.

Featurewhip_voiceMeans
linestrueThe line calls above work
speakertrueSetLineSpeaker plays a line out loud near a device
pickuptrueOn speaker, the people near the device are heard on the line
qualitytrueA line's quality breaks up with distance
sounds'full''full': every sound block played. 'basic': a phone or radio filter at most
Returns: { resource, label, features }, or false
local v = Whip.voiceSystem()
if v and not v.features.pickup then
    -- on speaker, only the people near hear the other side: say so in your UI
end
RegisterVoiceSystem(info)SERVER

For a voice resource of your own: makes it the voice system. One at a time: refused, naming the other, while another runs; let go when your resource stops. A voice system handles the line calls above, with the same arguments, registers the radio and megaphone items, turns whip_core:voice:rangeChanged (the Z key) into metres, and lights the HUD with SetVoiceTalking(talking, mode?).

Returns: true, or false, reason
Whip.register(function()
    local ok, why = exports.whip_core:RegisterVoiceSystem({
        label = 'my_voice',
        features = { lines = true, speaker = true, pickup = false, quality = false, sounds = 'basic' },
    })
    if not ok then print('voice stays off: ' .. why) return end
    -- ... the rest of your registrations
end)

Running WHIP

What happens behind the Quick Start: the database, oxmysql, a player's first download, Legacy versus Enhanced, and update checks. When something goes wrong, the WHIP setup report in the server console says what to fix (whipsetup prints it again).

The database

WHIP needs MariaDB 10.2.3+ or MySQL 8.0.16+: older versions ignore the rules that stop a bank balance going below zero. The setup report says when yours is too old.

  • Waiting for the database. whip_core waits for oxmysql to connect. Meanwhile the console says what to check every 30 seconds, and joining players are told the server is still starting.
  • No connection string. With no mysql_connection_string, whip_core stops and prints the line to add.
  • No SQL to run. whip_core creates its tables on the first start and updates them on the next start after an update. whip_phone does the same for its own tables.
  • A broken table stops the start. If a table can't be created or read, whip_core stops and says why in the console. Players are told the server didn't start.

WHIPFX's oxmysql

The recipe installs WHIPFX's oxmysql: oxmysql 2.14.3 with one fix. A query made while the database is down returns an error at once, instead of waiting for ever (whip_core gives up after 65 seconds). Stock oxmysql works too; the setup report says which one you run.

To get the fix, replace the oxmysql folder with the latest release, or apply whip_core/dev/oxmysql-p001.diff by hand.

A player's first download

A first join downloads about 510 MB, mostly WHIP's pictures and videos in 5 media packs of up to 145 MB each. A pack downloads again only when it changes.

Enhanced cuts off slow downloads. An Enhanced server stops any one file after about two minutes, which cuts off players slower than about 1.2 MB/s. The Quick Start's sv_resourceFileDownloadTimeout 600000 raises it to ten minutes. Legacy has no limit.

Legacy and Enhanced

FiveM runs on Legacy (the FXServer server) and Enhanced (the cfx-server server). One WHIP runs on both, and almost everything works the same.

A script can't reliably tell which one it's on, so an Enhanced server declares it:

setr whip_platform enhanced

The setup report warns when the server looks like the other platform. To see what your game was told, turn developer mode on in /w and type whipplatform in F8. Developers: Writing for both platforms.

Update checks

Every 12 hours, whip_core asks GitHub whether WHIP's resources have a newer release, and any other resource that names its repository. A newer one shows in the server console, in the setup report, and to an admin turning developer mode on. whipupdates in the server console lists every resource it checks; whipupdates check asks again now.

It sends one request per repository to api.github.com. GitHub sees your server's address and which repositories it asked about, and nothing else. To turn it off:

set whip_update_check false

Your own resource takes part with one line in its fxmanifest.lua, next to its version:

version '1.0.0'
whip_updates 'you/mycafe'   -- the GitHub repository whose latest release is compared with version
GetUpdate(resource?) · GetUpdates()SERVER

A resource's update status, from the last check: your own when resource is left out, or nil when it names no repository. GetUpdates returns every resource that names one. Neither asks GitHub, so call them as often as you like.

Returns: { resource, repository, current, latest, url, newer, checkedAt, problem }|nil · table[]
local update = exports.whip_core:GetUpdate()
if update and update.newer then
    print(('mycafe %s is out: %s'):format(update.latest, update.url))
end

Configuration

whip_core's settings live in its config.lua, read by server and client. The ones an owner changes are also in /whip → Settings → Config; timings, reaches and fine tuning are config.lua only.

Most settings apply at once for every player; those marked Next restart wait for whip_core's next start. Another resource can't read whip_core's Config: use the export for the value, such as GetPockets().

Changing a setting in game

Only a permanent admin sees Config: whip.devtools from server.cfg, not dev tools given in the Player Manager. Pick a group, change values, press Apply.

  • Checked as you type. The server checks again, and an Apply is all or nothing: one refused value saves nothing, and the bar names it.
  • Each row shows its config.lua default, Reset, and who changed it last.
  • Positions and camera shots have Use where I stand, Place camera (a free camera; Enter keeps, Esc cancels) and Use my camera. Character hero shots are made with Edit in world.
  • Fixed rows, such as Garages and Shops, only seed the database; a button goes to where the real ones are edited.

A saved value wins over config.lua until you press Reset. Saved values live in whip_settings (history in whip_settings_log) and are copied to settings.json (read by players' games) and server_settings.json (never downloaded). Don't edit either: WHIP rewrites them from the database at every start.

Items are edited in /whip → Economy → Items. Resources add their own pages beside Config: Settings pages for your resource.

  • Players remap in the pause menu (saved on their PC). D-pad up/down, A and LB on prompts are fixed.

Dev Tools (/w & /whip)

/w is the quick menu: toggles that draw over the world. /whip is the Admin Panel: every manager in one window, grouped into Players, Vehicles, Economy, World, Director, System and Settings. Both need the whip.devtools ACE and developer mode.

Developer mode

whip.devtools alone isn't enough: /w opens to one switch, and until it's on the account is treated as an ordinary player everywhere (/whip, dev commands, admin-only doors, zones and every resource that asks HasDevTools).

  • Visible and logged. The HUD shows Developer Access Enabled. Each switch is printed in the console and logged (dev_mode_on / dev_mode_off, with position).
  • Off turns everything off. God Mode, Invisible, Noclip, overlays, open editors and /whip close with it. It's off at every join and after a whip_core restart; swapping character keeps it.
  • Ask HasDevTools. A resource checking IsPlayerAceAllowed(src, 'whip.devtools') itself skips developer mode: use exports.whip_core:HasDevTools(source).
  • Remote tools. exports.whip_core:SetDeveloperMode(source, on) (server) works as the switch: only for an account with dev tools, and logged with the resource that asked.

In chat or F8 with developer mode on; the console ones in the server console.

Open it with /whip, the /w entry, or the unbound key "Whip: Open Admin Panel" (Settings → Key Bindings → FiveM). Esc closes a dialog, then backs out of a section, then closes the panel. On a controller, LB / RB step through tabs; move the cursor to the top edge to fade the panel.
